stem: The attorney for a plaintiff in an action filed in federal district court served the defendant with the summons, the complaint, and 25 interrogatories asking questions about the defendant's contentions in the case. The interrogatories stated that they were to be answered within 30 days after service.
stemZh: 在联邦地区法院提起的诉讼中，原告的律师向被告送达了传票、诉状以及 25 个问题，要求被告说明其在本案中的主张。这些问题声明应在送达后 30 天内作答。
ask: The defendant is likely to succeed in obtaining a protective order on which of the following grounds?
askZh: 被告很可能基于以下哪一理由成功获得保护令？

options.en: Interrogatories are only proper to discover facts, not contentions.
options.zh: 问题仅适用于发现事实，而不适用于主张。

options.en: Interrogatories may not be served until an answer to the complaint is filed.
options.zh: 在提交诉状答复之前，不得送达问题。

options.en: Interrogatories may not be served until the parties have conferred to arrange for initial disclosures and prepare a discovery plan.
options.zh: 在当事人进行初步披露并制定证据开示计划之前，不得送达问题。

options.en: The interrogatories exceed the number permitted without permission from the court or an agreement between the parties.
options.zh: 这些问题的数量超过了法院许可或当事人之间达成协议所允许的范围。

explanation.en:
Methods of discovery

Depositions • Written or oral examination of party or witness under oath

• 10 per party Interrogatories • Written questions served on party

• Serve up to 25

• Written responses due within 30 days of service Request for production

• Request served on party (or subpoena served on nonparty) to produce & allow inspection of documents, electronic information, tangible items, or land

• No limit

• Written response due within 30 days of service Requests for admission

• Requests served on other party to admit truth of facts within scope of discovery

• No limit

• Written response due within 30 days of service Physical/mental exams

• Order by court or parties' agreement for physical or mental examination of party if those conditions are in controversy

Except in limited circumstances,* a party may not seek discovery (including interrogatories) until the parties have held an initial planning conference—ie, a meeting where the parties arrange for initial disclosures and prepare a plan for discovery. If a discovery request is submitted before this conference is held (as seen here), the court would likely grant a protective order. This shields the served party from the undue burden of responding to that request, especially since the disclosure of the requested information will likely be arranged at the initial planning conference.

*Discovery may be sought before an initial planning conference (1) in a proceeding exempt from initial disclosures or (2) if permitted by a court order, the parties' stipulation, or a procedural rule.

(Choice A) Interrogatories are written questions (served by one party on another party) that may inquire about any matter within the scope of discovery—including facts, opinions, and contentions that pertain to the case.

(Choice B) Interrogatories may be served after an initial planning conference has been held—not when an answer to the complaint has been filed.

(Choice D) A party may serve up to 25 interrogatories on any other party without the court's permission or an agreement between the parties (as seen here).

Educational objective:

Discovery requests generally cannot be served until the parties have held an initial planning conference to arrange for initial disclosures and prepare a discovery plan.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(d) (timing of discovery).

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 33 (interrogatories).

explanation.zh:
证据开示方法

• 对宣誓方或证人进行书面或口头检查

• 每方提出10个问题

• 最多25人

• 应在30天内作出书面答复

• 要求当事方(或向非当事方发出传票)提供文件、电子信息、有形物品或土地,并允许对其进行检查

• 无限制

• 应在送达后30天内作出书面答复

• 要求另一方承认证据开示范围内的事实真相

• 无限制

• 应在工作30天内作出书面答复

• 如果有争议,法院或当事方同意对当事方进行身体或精神检查

除有限的情况外,* 当事方在举行初步规划会议之前,不得寻求证据开示(包括询问),即当事方安排初步披露和拟订证据开示计划的会议。如果在举行这次会议之前提出证据开示请求(如此处所示),法院可能会下达保护令。这使受送达方免于因应这一请求而承担过重的负担,特别是因为可能将在初步规划会议上安排披露所要求的信息。

* 如果法院命令、当事人的规定或程序规则允许,则可以在初步规划会议之前(1)在免于初步披露的程序中寻求证据开示。

(选择A)审讯是书面问题(由一方向另一方提出),可以询问证据开示范围内的任何事项,包括与案件有关的事实、意见和争论。

(Choice B) 审讯可在举行初步规划会议之后进行,而不是在对起诉状提出答复之后。

(Choice D)一方未经法院许可或当事方之间达成协议(如此处所示),可对任何另一方进行多达25次审讯。

学习要点：

在当事人召开初步规划会议安排初步披露和编制证据开示计划之前,一般不能满足证据开示请求.

参考资料

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(d)(证据开示的时机)。

• Fed. R. Civ. P.33(审讯)。

stem:
A plastic surgeon left her business partner to open her own plastic surgery clinic in a neighboring state. The business partner brought a diversity action against the plastic surgeon in federal court for violating a noncompete clause in the partnership agreement. The business partner properly filed an ex parte application for a temporary restraining order (TRO) that would prohibit the plastic surgeon from operating her new clinic. After a hearing at which only the business partner was present, the court properly issued the ex parte TRO, finding that the partner would be immediately and irreparably harmed by the loss of goodwill caused by the plastic surgeon's violation of the noncompete clause. The TRO was served on the plastic surgeon the next day.

One week later, the business partner moved to convert the TRO into a preliminary injunction. He requested that the court grant the motion immediately without providing notice to the plastic surgeon.
stemZh:
一名整形外科医生离开她的商业合作伙伴，前往邻州开设自己的整形外科诊所。商业合作伙伴在联邦法院提起了一项基于不同州籍管辖权的诉讼，指控该整形外科医生违反了合伙协议中的竞业禁止条款。商业合作伙伴正确地提出了一份紧急申请，请求法院颁布一项临时禁令（TRO），禁止该整形外科医生经营她的新诊所。在一次仅商业合作伙伴出席的听证会上，法院正确地颁布了该紧急申请的临时禁令，认为如果该整形外科医生违反竞业禁止条款导致商誉损失，商业合作伙伴将立即且不可挽回地受到伤害。该临时禁令在第二天送达给了该整形外科医生。

一周后，商业合作伙伴提出动议，要求将临时禁令转为初步禁令。他请求法院立即批准该动议，而无需通知该整形外科医生。
ask: Will the court grant the business partner's request?
askZh: 法院是否会批准商业合作伙伴的请求？

options.en: No, because notice must be given to an opposing party before a court may issue a preliminary injunction.
options.zh: 否，因为法院在颁布初步禁令前必须通知对方当事人。

options.en: No, because the partner's attorney failed to certify in writing why the plastic surgeon need not be notified.
options.zh: 否，因为商业合作伙伴的律师未能书面证明为何无需通知该整形外科医生。

options.en: Yes, because the ex parte TRO had expired and was no longer in effect.
options.zh: 是，因为该紧急临时禁令已经失效且不再生效。

options.en: Yes, because the partner will suffer immediate and irreparable harm if the request is not granted.
options.zh: 是，因为如果请求不被批准，商业合作伙伴将立即且不可挽回地受到伤害。

explanation.en:
Preliminary relief

(FRCP 65)

Type Required contents Effect

Preliminary injunction

Notice of hearing

• State reasons issued

• Reasonably describe acts restrained or required

• Specify terms

Persons bound upon receiving actual notice of order:

• parties to the case

• parties' officers, agents, employees & attorneys

• anyone in active concert/participation with above persons

Temporary restraining order

Ex parte

(no notice)

Above requirements plus:

• date & hour issued

• why injury is irreparable

• why issued without notice

• promptly filed with clerk & entered into record FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

A temporary restraining order (TRO) is a court order that commands a party to do or stop doing a specified action for 14 days or until a preliminary-injunction hearing can take place—whichever occurs first. A court may issue a TRO without notice to the adverse party (ie, ex parte). But when a party attempts to convert a TRO into a preliminary injunction, the adverse party must receive notice. Therefore, the court will deny the business partner's request because the plastic surgeon did not receive notice of the preliminary-injunction hearing.

(Choice B) The business partner's attorney must certify in writing why the plastic surgeon need not be notified when applying for an ex parte TRO—not a preliminary injunction. That is because, unlike an ex parte TRO, a preliminary injunction may be issued only after the adverse party has received notice of the preliminary-injunction hearing.

(Choice C) An ex parte TRO automatically remains in effect for 14 days unless that time period is (1) shortened by the court or (2) extended by the court for good cause or the adverse party's consent. Here, the TRO was seven days old when the business partner

moved to convert it into a preliminary injunction. Since there is no indication that the TRO was to last fewer than 14 days, it had not expired and was still in effect.

(Choice D) Although the business partner will suffer immediate and irreparable harm if his motion to convert the TRO into a preliminary injunction is denied, the court cannot grant a preliminary injunction on that basis alone. Even if it could, the motion cannot be granted because the plastic surgeon did not receive notice of the hearing.

Educational objective:

A court may issue a temporary restraining order without providing notice to the adverse party (ie, ex parte). However, the adverse party must receive notice before the court can convert a TRO into a preliminary injunction.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(a) (preliminary injunction).

初步救济

(FRCP 65) (法语).

需要的内容类型

初步禁令

临时限制令

单方面

(无通知)

高于所需经费外加:

• 印发日期和时数

• 伤害为何无法弥补

• 为何未经通知印发

• 迅速向书记员备案并记录在案 FRICP=联邦民事诉讼规则。

临时禁止令(TRO)是法院的命令,命令一方在14天之内采取或停止采取特定行动,或直到可以进行初步禁止审讯为止——无论哪种情况先发生。法院可在不通知对方(即单方面)的情况下发布TRO,但当一方当事人试图将TRO转换为初步禁令时,对方必须收到通知。因此,法院将拒绝企业合伙人的请求,因为整形外科医生没有收到初步禁止听证的通知。

(Choice B) 商业伙伴的律师必须书面证明为什么在申请单方TRO时不需要通知整形外科医生,而不是初步禁令。这是因为,与单方面TRO不同,只有在敌对方收到初步禁止听证通知之后才能发出初步禁令。

(选择C) 单方面TRO自动有效14天,除非该期限(1)由法院缩短或(2)由法院因正当理由或对方同意延长。

由于没有任何迹象显示该临时命令将持续不到14天,因此没有过期,仍然有效。

(Choice D)虽然如果拒绝将TRO转换为初步禁令的动议,企业合伙人将立即遭受不可弥补的损害,但法院不能仅以此为由下达初步禁令。即使可以,也不能批准动议,因为整形外科医生没有收到听证通知。

学习要点：

法院可以发布临时限制令,而不向敌对方(即单方面)发出通知,但是,在法院将TRO转换为初步禁令之前,敌对方必须收到通知。

参考资料

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(a)(初步禁令)。

stem: An injured pedestrian filed a diversity action in federal court against a truck driver. The truck driver filed an answer in which he denied liability and asserted an affirmative defense that the pedestrian was contributorily negligent. The truck driver did not assert any counterclaims against the pedestrian in his answer. Thirty days later, the pedestrian seeks to file a pleading to respond to the allegations in the truck driver's answer. The court has not yet issued any orders in the case.
stemZh: 一名受伤的行人在美国联邦法院提起了一项基于不同州籍管辖权的诉讼，起诉一名卡车司机。卡车司机在答状中否认了责任，并提出了一个积极抗辩，即该行人存在共同过失。卡车司机在其答状中并未提出任何针对行人的反诉。30天后，该行人希望提交一份文件以回应卡车司机答状中的指控。法院尚未就本案发布任何命令。
ask: May the pedestrian file a response?
askZh: 该行人是否有权提交回应文件？

options.en: No, because the pedestrian did not file a reply within 14 days after the answer was filed.
options.zh: 否，因为该行人未在答状提交后14天内提交回复文件。

options.en: No, because the truck driver did not assert a counterclaim and the court did not order a reply.
options.zh: 否，因为卡车司机未提出反诉，且法院未下令提交回复文件。

options.en: Yes, because due process allows the pedestrian to file a reply.
options.zh: 是，因为正当程序允许该行人提交回复文件。

options.en: Yes, because the truck driver asserted an affirmative defense.
options.zh: 是，因为卡车司机提出了一个积极抗辩。

explanation.en:
Types of pleadings

(FRCP 7)

Complaint Plaintiff's assertion of cause of action, court's jurisdiction & demand for relief

Answer Response to complaint, counterclaim, crossclaim, or third-party complaint that asserts admissions, denials, affirmative defenses & other claims

Third-party complaint

Party's assertion that nonparty is liable for damages party may owe in original suit based on legal theory (eg, indemnity, contribution)

Reply Response to answer (only required if court ordered)

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 7(a) lists the pleadings allowed in federal court. The most common pleadings are the plaintiff's complaint against the defendant and the defendant's answer in response to that complaint. A plaintiff may also respond to the defendant's answer by filing:

• an answer, but only if the defendant asserted a counterclaim or

• a reply, but only in the rare instance that the court orders it. Here, the truck driver did not assert a counterclaim in his answer, and the court did not order a reply. Therefore, the pedestrian may not respond to the allegations in the truck driver's answer. Instead, the pedestrian's nonresponse is automatically treated as a denial of the affirmative defense alleged in the truck driver's answer.

(Choice A) Had the court ordered a reply, the pedestrian would have needed to serve it within 21 days after being served with the court order—not within 14 days after the answer was filed.

(Choice C) Due process does not allow the pedestrian to file a reply. The pedestrian may only do so pursuant to a court order (not seen here).

(Choice D) The truck driver asserted an affirmative defense (not a counterclaim) alleging that the pedestrian was contributorily negligent. As a result, the pedestrian may not file an answer to respond to the affirmative defense.

Educational objective:

A plaintiff may respond to a defendant's answer by filing (1) an answer if the defendant asserted a counterclaim or (2) a reply if the court orders it.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 7(a) (pleadings).

• 61A Am. Jur. 2d Pleading § 365 (2019) (explaining the permissibility of a reply in federal court).

(FRCP7)

对声称承认、否认、肯定辩护和其他索赔的起诉状、反诉、交叉起诉状或第三方起诉状的答复

第三方起诉状

缔约方关于非当事方对损害负赔偿责任的主张可能根据法律理论(例如赔偿、缴款)在原始诉讼中欠下

FRCP = 联邦民事诉讼规则。

联邦民事诉讼规则第7(a)条列举了联邦法院允许的诉状,最常见的诉状是原告对被告的起诉状和被告对该起诉状的答复。原告也可以以下列方式对被告的答复作出答复:

• 答案,但被告必须提出反诉,或

• 答复,但只有法院下令答复的罕见情况。这里,卡车司机没有在答复中提出反诉,法院也没有下令答复。因此,行人可能不会对卡车司机答复中的指控作出答复。相反,行人不回应被自动视为否认卡车司机回答中指称的肯定性辩护.

(Choice A) 如果法院下令答复,行人必须在收到法院命令后21天内送达,而不是在提出答复后14天内。

(C选择)正当程序不允许行人提交答辩状,行人只能根据法院命令(此处不见)提交.

(Choice D) 卡车司机坚持肯定的抗辩(而不是反诉),声称行人有贡献的过失,因此行人可能不会回答肯定的抗辩.

学习要点：

原告可以对被告的答复作出答复,提出(1)被告主张反诉的,提出答复;或者(2)法院下令答复的,提出答复。

参考资料

• 61A Am. Jur. 2d 书状第365条(2019年)(解释联邦法院对答复的允许性)。

stem: A company located in State A filed a lawsuit against its distributor located in State B in a federal district court. The company's complaint asserted a breach of contract claim for $60,000 and a negligence claim for $30,000. These claims arose from different facts.
stemZh: 一家位于 A 州的公司在美国联邦地区法院对其位于 B 州的分销商提起诉讼。公司的起诉书提出了一个金额为 60,000 美元的合同违约索赔和一个金额为 30,000 美元的过失索赔。这些索赔源于不同的事实。
ask: May the federal court hear these claims in a single suit?
askZh: 联邦法院是否可以在同一诉讼中审理这些索赔？

options.en: No, because neither claim satisfies subject-matter jurisdiction on its own.
options.zh: 否，因为这两个索赔都不单独满足事项管辖权。

options.en: No, because the claims arose out of different facts.
options.zh: 否，因为这些索赔源于不同的事实。

options.en: Yes, because the claims were properly joined, and the federal court has diversity jurisdiction.
options.zh: 是的，因为这些索赔被正确合并，且联邦法院拥有不同州籍管辖权。

options.en: Yes, because the claims were properly joined, and the federal court has supplemental jurisdiction.
options.zh: 是的，因为这些索赔被正确合并，且联邦法院拥有补充管辖权。

explanation.en:
Amount in controversy

(aggregation of claims)

Procedural posture

Claims asserted Outcome

One π v. one Δ • Negligence – $40K

• Battery – $60K

• Aggregation allowed

• Amount in controversy = $100K One π v. multiple Δs

• Negligence against Δ1 – $40K

• Battery against Δ2 – $60K

• Aggregation not allowed unless Δs jointly liable

• Amounts in controversy = $40K & $60K Multiple πs v. one Δ

• π1 asserts negligence – $40K

• π2 asserts battery – $60K

• Aggregation not allowed unless πs enforcing common or undivided interest

• Amounts in controversy = $40K & $60K

• π1 asserts negligence – $40K

• π1 asserts breach of contract – $40K

• π2 asserts battery – $60K

• Aggregation allowed for π1's claims

• Aggregation not allowed for π2's claim

• Amounts in controversy = $80K & $60K π = plaintiff; Δ = defendant.

Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 18 allows a party to join (ie, add) as many claims as it has against an opposing party in a single lawsuit—even if the claims arise from different facts or occurrences* (as seen here) (Choice B). But like all disputes in federal court, a suit involving multiple claims must satisfy subject-matter jurisdiction. This can be established through either:

• federal-question jurisdiction – when a claim arises under the U.S. Constitution, a treaty, or a federal law (not seen here) or

• diversity jurisdiction – when the opposing parties are citizens of different states and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.

The amount in controversy refers to the amount demanded in the plaintiff's complaint (excluding costs and interest). To meet the required amount, a single plaintiff may aggregate (ie, combine) joined claims asserted against a single defendant.

Here, the company and the distributor are citizens of different states (States A and B, respectively). The company properly joined a breach of contract claim for $60,000 and a negligence claim for $30,000, even though they arise from different facts. And though neither claim individually satisfies the amount-in-controversy requirement, they can be aggregated to $90,000 to meet that requirement since both claims are asserted against the distributor. Therefore, the federal district court has diversity jurisdiction and can hear both claims in a single suit (Choice A).

*FRCP 42 allows a federal court to order separate trials of claims for convenience, to avoid prejudice, or to expedite and economize.

(Choice D) A federal court may exercise supplemental jurisdiction to hear certain claims that do not independently satisfy federal-question or diversity jurisdiction. But there is no need for supplemental jurisdiction here since the court has diversity jurisdiction over the aggregated claims.

Educational objective:

A party may join as many claims as it has against an opposing party in federal court—even if the claims arise out of different facts or occurrences—provided subject-matter jurisdiction is satisfied.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 18 (joinder of claims).

• 28 U.S.C. § 1332 (diversity jurisdiction).

《联邦民事诉讼规则》第18条允许一当事方加入(e, 添加)在单一诉讼中对对立方提出的同样多的索赔,即使索赔来自不同事实或事件* (如此处所示)(Choice B)。但是,与联邦法院的所有争端一样,涉及多项索赔的诉讼必须满足事项管辖权的要求。

• 联邦问题管辖权——当根据美国宪法、条约或联邦法律(此处不见)提出要求时;

• 异籍管辖权——当对立方是不同国家的公民,争议金额超过75 000美元。

争议金额是指原告起诉状中要求的金额(不包括成本和利息),为满足要求金额,单一原告可以合并(即合并)对单一被告提出的诉讼。

在这里,公司和经销商是不同国家(分别为A州和B州)的公民。 公司正确地加入了一项违反合同索赔,索赔金额为60,000美元,过失索赔金额为30,000美元,尽管它们来自不同的事实。虽然没有一项单独索赔符合争议中的数额要求,但由于这两项索赔都是对经销商提出的,因此可以合计为90,000美元以满足这一要求。因此,联邦地区法院具有异籍管辖权,可在单一诉讼(Choice A)中审理两项索赔。

*FRCP 42允许联邦法院为了方便而下令对索赔进行单独审判,以避免偏见,或加速和节约.

联邦法院可以行使补充管辖权,审理某些不能独立满足联邦问题或异籍管辖权的要求。但是,在这方面没有必要补充管辖权,因为法院对合并索赔有不同的管辖权。

学习要点：

一方当事人可以在联邦法院对对方当事人提出同样多的索赔要求,即使索赔要求是由不同事实或事件引起的,只要属事管辖权得到满足。

参考资料

• Fed. R. Civ. P.18(合并索赔)。

• 《美国法典》第28编第1332条(异籍管辖权)。

sourceSetLabel: 民事诉讼法 · 第 6 组
stem:
A miner sued a coal company in a federal district court to recover damages for severe injuries he sustained during a mining explosion. Sixty days prior to trial, the company's attorney interviewed a forklift operator who witnessed the incident. The operator stated that he saw the miner violate several safety protocols leading up to the explosion.

At trial, the company sought to have the forklift operator testify to support its contributory negligence defense. The miner's attorney objected and moved for sanctions on the ground that the company had failed to disclose the operator's identity prior to trial. The company's attorney stated that she did not disclose the operator's identity because the miner's attorney never made a formal request.

The district court then sanctioned the company by (1) prohibiting the operator from testifying, (2) informing the jury of the company's nondisclosure, and (3) ordering the company to pay the miner's reasonable expenses. After the jury returned a verdict for the miner, the company appealed the sanctions.
stemZh:
一名矿工在联邦地区法院起诉一家煤炭公司，要求赔偿其在矿井爆炸中遭受的严重伤害。庭审前 60 天，公司律师采访了一名目击事故的叉车操作员。该操作员称，他看到矿工在爆炸前违反了数项安全规程。

庭审中，公司拟让叉车操作员作证，以支持其与有过失抗辩。矿工的律师提出异议并申请制裁，理由是公司在庭审前未披露该操作员的身份。公司律师表示，之所以没有披露，是因为矿工的律师从未正式提出披露请求。

地区法院随后对公司采取制裁措施：(1) 禁止操作员作证；(2) 告知陪审团公司未予披露；(3) 命令公司支付矿工的合理费用。陪审团裁定矿工胜诉后，公司就这些制裁措施提起上诉。
ask: How should the appellate court rule?
askZh: 上诉法院应如何裁决？

options.en: Affirm all the sanctions.
options.zh: 维持所有制裁。

options.en: Affirm the sanction ordering the company to pay the miner's reasonable expenses but reverse the other sanctions.
options.zh: 维持要求公司赔偿矿工合理费用的制裁，但推翻其他制裁。

options.en: Affirm the sanction prohibiting the operator from testifying at trial but reverse the other sanctions.
options.zh: 维持禁止操作员在审判中作证的制裁，但推翻其他制裁。

options.en: Reverse all the sanctions.
options.zh: 推翻所有制裁。

explanation.en:
Parties are required to make initial disclosures, disclosures of expert testimony, and pretrial disclosures without waiting for a discovery request. Such required disclosures are designed to prevent surprises at trial. As part of their pretrial disclosures, parties must disclose the identity of witnesses who may testify at trial. Since the company intended to call the forklift operator as a witness, it was required to disclose his identity as part of its pretrial disclosures. However, the company failed to do so.

To underscore the importance of such disclosures, a court has wide discretion to impose sanctions on a party who fails to make required disclosures. The most common sanction is to prohibit the use of the undisclosed information unless the nondisclosure was substantially justified or harmless. In addition to or in lieu of this sanction, the court may:

• order the payment of the opposing party's reasonable expenses, including attorney's fees, caused by the nondisclosure

• inform the jury of the party's failure to disclose and

• impose any other appropriate sanction (except for contempt of court). Here, the company provided no justification for its failure to disclose the forklift operator's identity, and this nondisclosure was harmful to the miner since he had no time to prepare for the operator's testimony. As a result, the court did not abuse its discretion in prohibiting the operator from testifying, informing the jury of the nondisclosure, and ordering the company to pay the miner's reasonable expenses. The appellate court should therefore affirm all the sanctions (Choices B, C & D).

Educational objective:

A court may impose the following sanctions on a party who fails to make required disclosures: (1) prohibit the use of the undisclosed evidence, (2) order the payment of the opposing party's reasonable expenses, (3) inform the jury of the nondisclosure, and (4) impose any other appropriate sanction (except for contempt of court).

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a) (mandatory-disclosure requirements).

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(c)(1) (sanctions for failure to make mandatory disclosures).

• 8B Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2289.1 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining when sanctions are appropriate for failure to make required disclosures).

explanation.zh:
要求缔约方在不等待证据开示请求的情况下作出初步披露、披露专家证词和审前披露,这些披露旨在防止审判时出现意外。作为审前披露的一部分,当事人必须披露可能在审判时作证的证人的身份,因为公司打算传唤叉车操作员作为证人,因此,它必须披露身份,作为审前披露的一部分。然而,该公司没有这样做。

为了强调这种披露的重要性,法院有广泛的酌处权对未按规定披露的当事人实施制裁。最常见的制裁是禁止使用未公开的信息,除非不披露是有充分理由或无害的。除了或代替这一制裁,法院可以:

• 命令支付对方当事人的合理费用,包括律师费,因为不予披露

• 将当事方未披露的情况通知陪审团;

· 施加任何其他适当的制裁(藐视法庭除外),在这方面,该公司没有说明为何不披露叉车操作员的身份,这种不披露对矿工有害,因为他没有时间为该船做准备。因此,法院没有滥用自由裁量权,禁止经营者作证,告知陪审团不披露,并命令公司支付矿工的合理费用。因此,上诉法院应确认所有制裁(选择B、C和D)。

学习要点：

法院可对未按规定披露的一方实施下列制裁:(1) 禁止使用未披露的证据,(2) 命令支付对方的合理费用,(3) 通知陪审团不披露,(4) 规定任何其他适当的制裁(藐视法庭除外)。

参考资料

• Fed. R. Civ. P.26(a)(强制性披露要求)。

• Fed.R.Civ.P.37(c)(1)(对未进行强制性披露的制裁)。

• 8B Charles Alan Wright等人,《联邦惯例和程序》第2289.1节(第3d编,2020年)(解释何时对未能按规定披露情况实施制裁)。

sourceSetLabel: 民事诉讼法 · 第 6 组
stem:
A pharmaceutical company sued its competitor for patent infringement in federal court. The competitor's attorney hired a pharmacist to examine the case and testify as an expert at trial. The pharmacist studied the case and submitted an initial draft of her report to the attorney. After reading the draft report, the attorney noticed that certain facts and data were missing. To correct this issue, the attorney emailed the pharmacist and provided additional facts and data to include in the report. The pharmacist then revised her report based on this additional information.

After receiving this revised report from the competitor's attorney, the pharmaceutical company served a request for production on the attorney to produce the email exchanged with the pharmacist.
stemZh:
一家制药公司在美国联邦法院起诉其竞争对手侵犯专利权。竞争对手的律师聘请了一名药剂师来审查此案，并在庭审中作为专家证人作证。药剂师研究了此案，并将她的报告初稿提交给律师。在阅读了初稿报告后，律师注意到某些事实和数据缺失。为了解决这个问题，律师通过电子邮件将额外的事实和数据发送给药剂师，要求将其包含在报告中。药剂师随后根据这些额外信息修订了她的报告。

在收到竞争对手律师提供的修订后的报告后，制药公司向该律师发出了一份证据开示请求，要求其提供与药剂师之间交换的电子邮件。
ask: Must the attorney produce the email?
askZh: 律师必须提供这封电子邮件吗？

options.en: No, because attorney communications with expert witnesses are privileged.
options.zh: 否，因为律师与专家证人的通信享有特权。

options.en: No, because the contents of the email are discoverable through interrogatories served on the pharmacist.
options.zh: 否，因为电子邮件的内容可以通过对药剂师发出的询问令进行发现。

options.en: Yes, because a draft of an expert report is discoverable.
options.zh: 是的，因为专家报告的初稿是可发现的。

options.en: Yes, because the email contained facts and data that the pharmacist relied on to revise her report.
options.zh: 是的，因为这封电子邮件包含药剂师修订报告时所依赖的事实和数据。

explanation.en:
Discovery of expert materials

(FRCP 26(b)(4))

Nontestifying expert

• Facts known or opinions held by expert not discoverable unless: – relate to court-ordered physical/mental examination or – exceptional circumstances make it impracticable to obtain information by other means Testifying expert

• Facts known & opinions held by expert discoverable through deposition

• Drafts of expert reports & disclosures not discoverable

• Communications between attorney & expert not discoverable unless: – relate to expert's compensation or – identify facts, data, or assumptions provided by attorney that expert considered in forming opinions FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

Parties can use various discovery methods, including requests for production, to obtain nonprivileged information that is relevant to any claim or defense and proportional to the needs of the case. Materials held by an expert witness expected to testify at trial are discoverable with two exceptions:

• Drafts of expert reports or disclosures

• Privileged attorney-expert communications All attorney-expert communications are privileged unless they (1) relate to the expert's compensation or (2) identify facts, data, or assumptions provided by the attorney that the expert considered or relied on in forming his/her opinions.

Here, the competitor's attorney hired the pharmacist to examine the case and testify as an expert at trial. After reading the pharmacist's draft report, the attorney emailed the pharmacist and provided her with additional facts and data that were missing in the draft. The pharmacist then relied on those facts and data to revise her report, so the email is not a privileged communication (Choice A). Therefore, the attorney must produce the email.

(Choice B) Interrogatories are a discovery request in which a party serves written questions on another party that inquire about any matter within the scope of discovery. However, interrogatories may not be served on a nonparty such as an expert

expected to testify at trial. Therefore, the contents of the email are not discoverable through interrogatories served on the nonparty pharmacist.

(Choice C) Drafts of expert reports are not discoverable. Therefore, the attorney would not be required to produce the email on this basis.

Educational objective:

All attorney-expert communications are privileged unless they (1) relate to the expert's compensation or (2) identify facts, data, or assumptions provided by the attorney that the expert considered or relied on in forming his/her opinions.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(4) (discovery of expert materials).

explanation.zh:
专家材料的证据开示

(FRCP 26(b)(4))

专家

• 专家所了解的事实或持有的意见无法发现,除非: - 涉及法院下令的身体/精神检查或 - - 特殊情况使得无法通过其他手段获得信息

• 专家通过作证发现的事实和意见

• 专家报告草稿和无法发现的披露

• 律师和专家之间的通信是无法发现的,除非:----涉及专家的赔偿或----确定专家在形成意见时考虑过的事实、数据或假设。

缔约方可利用各种证据开示方法,包括生产请求,获取与任何主张或辩护有关并与案件需要相称的非特权信息。预计将在审判中作证的专家证人持有的材料可以发现,但有两个例外:

• 专家报告或披露的草稿

• 所有律师-专家来文均享有特权,除非(1) 涉及专家的赔偿,或(2) 查明专家在形成这些来文时认为或依赖的律师提供的事实、数据或假设。他/她的意见。

在这里,竞争对手的律师聘请药剂师审查案件,作为审判专家出庭作证,律师在阅读药剂师的报告草稿后,给药剂师发电子邮件,并向她提供了草案中缺失的其他事实和数据.药剂师随后依靠这些事实和数据来修改她的报告,因此,电子邮件不是一种特权通信(Choice A)。 因此,律师必须出示电子邮件。

(Choice B) 讯问是一种证据开示请求,其中一方向另一方提出书面问题,询问证据开示范围内的任何事项。

因此,电子邮件的内容无法通过向非当事方药剂师提供的询问而发现。

专家报告草稿是无法发现的,因此不需要律师据此制作电子邮件。

学习要点：

除非(1) 与专家的赔偿有关,或(2) 查明专家在形成其意见时所考虑或依赖的律师提供的事实、数据或假设,否则所有律师-专家来文均享有特权。

参考资料

• Fed. R. Civ. P.26(b)(4)(证据开示专家材料)。

sourceSetLabel: 民事诉讼法 · 第 6 组
stem:
A musician sued a political candidate in a federal court for federal copyright infringement. The complaint requested damages and a preliminary injunction to stop the candidate from using the musician's songs at his political rallies. Notice of a hearing on the preliminary injunction was provided to both parties. After the hearing was conducted, the judge granted the musician's request for a preliminary injunction and stated the reasons for doing so. In addition, the injunction reads as follows:

"The political candidate and any person working or volunteering to put on a rally for the candidate may not play any of the musician's songs. The political campaign is directed to distribute this injunction to all persons, including workers, independent contractors, and volunteers, who are involved in the candidate's rallies. A fine of $1,000 per violation will be assessed against anyone who fails to adhere to this injunction."

At the candidate's next rally, a volunteer who had received a copy of the preliminary injunction nonetheless played the musician's song.
stemZh:
一名音乐家在联邦法院起诉一位政治候选人，指控其侵犯联邦版权。起诉状要求赔偿损失并获得初步禁令，以阻止候选人使用该音乐家的歌曲在其政治集会上。双方均收到了初步禁令听证会的通知。听证会结束后，法官批准了音乐家的初步禁令请求，并说明了批准的理由。此外，该禁令内容如下：

"该政治候选人及其任何参与组织候选人的集会的工作人员或志愿者不得播放该音乐家的歌曲。该政治竞选活动应将本禁令分发给所有涉及候选人集会的人员，包括工作人员、独立承包商和志愿者。任何违反本禁令的人将被处以每违反一次 1000 美元的罚款。"

在候选人的下一场集会上，一名已收到初步禁令副本的志愿者仍然播放了该音乐家的歌曲。
ask: Is the volunteer subject to the monetary fine for violating the preliminary injunction?
askZh: 该志愿者因违反初步禁令是否需承担金钱罚款？

options.en: No, because the volunteer did not receive notice of the hearing.
options.zh: 否，因为该志愿者未收到听证会通知。

options.en: No, because the volunteer is not a party in the musician's suit against the candidate.
options.zh: 否，因为该志愿者不是音乐家起诉候选人的诉讼中的当事人。

options.en: Yes, because the injunction is in the best interests of the public.
options.zh: 是，因为该禁令符合公众的最佳利益。

options.en: Yes, because the injunction reasonably described the prohibited acts.
options.zh: 是，因为该禁令合理地描述了被禁止的行为。

explanation.en:
Preliminary injunction

Grounds* Movant establishes that:

• movant is likely to succeed on merits

• movant is likely to suffer irreparable harm in absence of relief

• balance of equities favors movant and

• injunction is in public's best interests Contents Order granting injunction must:

• state reasons for issuance

• reasonably describe prohibited or commanded acts and

• state terms specifically Effect Binds the following persons who receive actual notice of order:

• parties

• parties' officers, agents, employees & attorneys and

• anyone in active concert or participation with above-listed persons *Movant also must provide bond to pay costs & damages if nonmovant was wrongfully enjoined.

A preliminary injunction is a temporary court order that is issued before or during trial to prohibit or command a specified action while a case is pending before the court. A preliminary injunction can only be granted after notice of the hearing to the adverse party, and it must contain all of the following:

• The reasons why it was granted

• A reasonable description of the prohibited or commanded acts

• The specific terms (eg, persons bound, penalties for noncompliance) Additionally, actual notice of the preliminary injunction must be provided to any person bound by it, including (1) the parties, (2) their officers, agents, employees, and attorneys, and (3) persons in active concert or participation with the parties or their subordinates. Only persons who receive this notice can be held in contempt of court (eg, charged a monetary fine) for violating the injunction.

Here, the judge issued a preliminary injunction and stated the reasons why it was granted. The injunction bound the candidate and all persons working or volunteering on his behalf (specific terms) to stop playing the musician's songs (prohibited acts). And since the volunteer received a copy of the injunction (actual notice), the volunteer is subject to the monetary fine for violating the preliminary injunction.

(Choice A) The volunteer had to receive actual notice of the injunction to be subject to it, but the volunteer did not need to receive notice of the hearing since the candidate was the adverse party in this suit.

(Choice B) Although the volunteer is not a party in the musician's suit against the candidate, the volunteer worked on the candidate's behalf and received actual notice of the injunction. As a result, the volunteer is bound by the injunction.

(Choice C) The injunction may be in the public's best interests because the enforcement of copyright laws protects intellectual property rights. But that alone is not a basis to enforce the injunction against the volunteer.

Educational objective:

A preliminary injunction must contain (1) the reasons why it was issued, (2) a reasonable description of the prohibited or commanded acts, and (3) its specific terms.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(d) (required contents and scope of preliminary injunction).

explanation.zh:
初步禁令

运动规定:

• 根据案情,积极性有可能取得成功

• 如果没有救济,机动部队很可能遭受无法弥补的伤害

• 股利平衡

• 发布禁止令符合公众最大利益的内容命令必须:

• 说明印发的理由

• 合理描述被禁止或指挥的行为;

• 具体阐述以下收到命令通知的人:

• 当事方

• 政党官员、代理人、雇员和律师

• 与以上所列人员进行积极交流或参与的任何人* 如果非动议方被不当要求,运动还必须提供保证金以支付费用和损害赔偿。

初步禁令是在审判前或审判期间发布的临时法院命令,以禁止或命令在法院待审案件期间采取特定行动。只有在向对方当事人发出听证通知后才能下达初步禁令,而且禁令必须包含下列所有内容:

• 批准的理由

• 合理描述被禁止或指挥的行为;

• 具体条款(例如,受约束者,对不遵守行为的惩罚) 此外,必须向任何受禁令约束的人,包括(1) 当事方、(2) 其官员、代理人、雇员和律师,以及(3) 个人,发出关于初步禁令的实际通知;与各方或其下属进行积极的协调或参与。只有收到通知的人才能被藐视法庭(例如,罚款)因为违反禁令

在此,法官发布了一项初步禁令,并说明了批准的理由,禁令规定候选人和所有代表他工作或志愿工作的人(具体条款)必须停止演奏音乐家的歌曲(被禁止的行为)。由于志愿者收到了禁令的副本(实际通知),志愿者因违反初步禁令而被罚款。

(Choice A) 志愿者必须实际收到禁令通知才能服从,但志愿者不需要收到听证通知,因为候选人是本诉讼的不利方.

(Choice B)虽然该志愿者在音乐家对候选人的诉讼中不是一方,但该志愿者代表候选人工作,并收到了禁令的实际通知,因此,该志愿者受禁令的约束.

禁止令可能符合公众的最大利益,因为执行版权法保护知识产权。 但仅此而已并不是对志愿者执行禁止令的依据。

学习要点：

初步禁令必须包含:(1) 发布禁令的原因,(2) 对被禁止或命令的行为的合理描述,(3) 其具体条款。

参考资料

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(d)(初步禁令的必要内容和范围)。

stem:
A fisherman from State A repeatedly trespassed across a homeowner's property in State B to fish in a publicly owned lake. After one of the fisherman's trips across the homeowner's property, the homeowner discovered that her $80,000 marble statue had been destroyed. The homeowner filed a lawsuit in a federal court in State B to enjoin the fisherman from trespassing and to recover for the damage to her statue.

During discovery, the homeowner interviewed a former friend of the fisherman. The friend said that the fisherman had bragged about trespassing across the homeowner's property and accidently knocking over a marble statue on one occasion. The homeowner expects the fisherman to testify at trial that he did not know he was trespassing and never saw the statue. To impeach the fisherman's anticipated testimony, the homeowner intends to call the friend to testify. The homeowner does not want to disclose the friend's identity to the fisherman.
stemZh:
一名来自 A 州的渔民多次擅闯 B 州一名房主的财产，以在公共拥有的湖泊中捕鱼。在一次渔民穿越房主财产的行程中，房主发现她的价值 80,000 美元的大理石雕像被毁。房主在 B 州的联邦法院提起诉讼，要求阻止渔民擅闯，并赔偿雕像损坏的损失。

在证据开示阶段，房主采访了一位渔民的前朋友。这位朋友表示，渔民曾炫耀过擅闯房主财产，并在一次偶然中撞倒了大理石雕像。房主预计渔民会在庭审中作证称他不知道自己在擅闯，也从未见过雕像。为了反驳渔民的预期证词，房主打算传唤这位朋友作证。房主不想向渔民透露这位朋友的身份。
ask: What is the homeowner's strongest argument to accomplish her goal?
askZh: 房主实现其目标的最强有力论点是什么？

options.en: The fisherman could have discovered this evidence on his own.
options.zh: 渔民本可以自行发现这些证据。

options.en: The fisherman will have a full and fair opportunity to cross-examine the friend.
options.zh: 渔民将有机会充分且公平地对这位朋友进行交叉质询。

options.en: The friend's testimony will be used solely to impeach the fisherman's testimony.
options.zh: 这位朋友的证词将仅用于反驳渔民的证词。

options.en: The homeowner's failure to disclose the friend as a witness is harmless.
options.zh: 房主未披露这位朋友作为证人的行为是无害的。

explanation.en:
Required discovery disclosures

(FRCP 26(a))

Type Required disclosures Time to disclose

Initial disclosures*

• Persons with relevant information

• Items in party's possession that support claim/defense

• Computation of damages & supporting material

• Relevant insurance policies

• ≤ 14 days after initial planning conference

• ≤ 30 days after post-conference service

or joinder

• As court orders or parties stipulate Expert testimony

• Identity of expert witnesses

• Expert's written report

• If no report, subject matter & summary of testimony

• ≥ 90 days before trial

• ≤ 30 days after disclosure to rebut evidence

• As court orders or parties stipulate Pretrial disclosures*

• Testifying witnesses

• Deposition testimony to be used at trial

• Documents/exhibits to be used at trial

• ≥ 30 days before trial

• As court orders

FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

*Does not apply to evidence used solely for impeachment.

Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(a) requires parties to automatically make initial disclosures, disclosures of expert testimony, and pretrial disclosures. Pretrial disclosures must include:

• the name, address, and phone number of each witness—separately identifying witnesses expected to testify and those who may be called if the need arises

• the deposition testimony that will be used at trial and

• all documents and exhibits—separately identifying items expected to be offered as evidence and those that may be offered if the need arises.

The purpose of pretrial disclosures is to avoid surprises at trial regarding substantive evidence—ie, evidence offered to help prove a material fact or issue. As a result, these requirements do not apply to impeachment evidence—ie, evidence used solely to discredit a witness and not to prove a material fact or issue. Therefore, the homeowner's strongest argument to avoid disclosing the friend's identity is that his testimony will be used solely to impeach the fisherman's testimony.

(Choices A & B) The fact that the fisherman could have discovered this evidence on his own and will have a full and fair opportunity to cross-examine the friend does not provide grounds for nondisclosure. Instead, the homeowner can withhold the friend's identity only if his testimony will be used solely for impeachment.

(Choice D) Failure to identify a witness in pretrial disclosures bars the nondisclosing party from using that witness's testimony in a motion, hearing, or trial—unless the failure to disclose was substantially justified or is harmless. But if the witness's testimony will be used only for impeachment purposes, the rules for pretrial disclosures do not apply and there is no need to show that the nondisclosure is harmless.

Educational objective:

A party's pretrial disclosures must include (1) the name, address, and phone number of each witness, (2) deposition testimony that will be used at trial, and (3) all documents and exhibits. But these requirements do not apply to witnesses and evidence that will be used solely for impeachment.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(3) (required pretrial disclosures).

explanation.zh:
必要的证据开示披露

(FRCP 26(a))

披露时间

初步披露*

• 有相关信息的人

• 当事方拥有的、支持索赔/辩护的物品

• 损害的计算和辅助材料

• 相关保险单

• 在初步规划会议后14天

• 会议服务30天后

或合并

• 法院命令或当事方规定专家证词

• 鉴定人的身份

• 专家的书面报告

• 如果没有报告、主题事项和证词摘要

• 审判前90天

• 在披露后30天反驳证据

• 法院命令或当事方规定审前披露*

• 鉴定证人

• 将在审判中使用的证言

• 审判时使用的文件/用品

• 审判前30天

• 作为法院命令

FRCP = 联邦民事诉讼规则。

* 不适用于仅用于弹劾的证据。

《联邦民事诉讼规则》第26(a)条要求当事方自动作出初步披露、披露专家证词和审前披露。

• 每一证人的姓名、地址和电话号码——分别指明预期作证的证人和必要时可能传唤的证人

• 用于审判的证言;

· 所有文件和证物——分别指明预期作为证据提供的物品和必要时可能提供的物品。

审前披露的目的是为了避免在审判时对实质性证据——即为帮助证明实质性事实或问题而提供的证据——感到惊讶。因此,这些要求不适用于弹劾证据——即仅仅用来诋毁证人的证据,而不是用来证明实质性事实或问题的证据。因此,房主为避免透露朋友身份而提出的最强烈的论点是,他的证词将完全用来弹劾渔民的证词.

(Choices A & B) 渔夫本可以自己发现这些证据,并且将有充分和公平的机会盘问这位朋友的事实并不能提供不披露的理由.相反,房主只有在朋友的证词只用于弹劾的情况下才能扣留他的身份.

(Choice D) 在审前披露中未指明证人,使未披露的一方无法在动议、听讯或审判中使用该证人的证词——除非未披露有充分理由或无害。但是,如果证人的证词只用于弹劾目的,审前披露规则不适用,也没有必要证明不披露是无害的.

学习要点：

当事人的审前披露必须包括:(1) 每位证人的姓名、地址和电话号码,(2) 将在审判中使用的证言,以及(3) 所有文件和物证。但这些要求并不适用于仅用于弹劾的证人和证据.

参考资料

• Fed. R. Civ. P.26(a)(3)(需要审前披露)。

sourceSetLabel: 民事诉讼法 · 第 6 组
stem:
An employee brought a diversity suit against his employer in federal district court for intentional infliction of emotional distress. The employee claimed that the employer repeatedly engaged in conduct that caused the employee to suffer severe emotional distress that has resulted in physical manifestations. During discovery, the court issued a valid order compelling the employee to submit to a mental and physical examination by a licensed medical professional chosen by the employer. The employee refused to submit to the examination.

The employer's attorney has moved for sanctions against the employee.
stemZh:
一名员工在美国联邦地区法院提起基于不同州籍管辖权的诉讼，指控其雇主故意造成情感痛苦。员工声称，雇主反复进行导致其遭受严重情感痛苦的行为，这种痛苦已导致身体症状。在证据开示阶段，法院发出有效命令，要求员工接受由雇主选定的执业医疗专业人士进行精神和身体检查。员工拒绝接受检查。

雇主的律师提出了对员工的制裁动议。
ask: Which of the following sanctions, if any, may the court order?
askZh: 法院可以下令以下哪种制裁？

options.en: None, because the employee has the right to choose the person who conducts the examination.
options.zh: 无，因为员工有权选择进行检查的人员。

options.en: None, because a court cannot compel a person to submit to a mental examination.
options.zh: 无，因为法院不能命令一个人接受精神检查。

options.en: Hold the employee in contempt of court.
options.zh: 将员工视为蔑视法庭。

options.en: Stay the proceeding until the order for examination is obeyed.
options.zh: 暂停程序，直到遵守检查命令。

explanation.en:
Sanctions for violating discovery order

(FRCP 37(b))

Court location Sanctions allowed

Where deposition occurred

• Hold in contempt of court

Where suit is pending • Direct that certain facts be construed against violator

• Prohibit violator from offering certain evidence

• Strike pleadings in whole or in part

• Stay further proceedings until order is obeyed

• Hold in contempt of court*

• Dismiss claims in whole or in part

• Issue default judgment against violator

• Order payment of reasonable expenses (eg, attorney's fees) caused by violation FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

*Cannot be imposed for failing to comply with order for physical or mental examination.

During discovery, the court where the lawsuit is pending may order a party to undergo a mental or physical examination by a suitably licensed or certified examiner (Choice B). This court order is valid when:

• that party's mental or physical condition is in controversy

• the motion for the order is based on good cause and

• the order provides notice by specifying the time, place, manner, conditions, and scope of the exam, as well as the person(s) who will perform it.

If the party fails to comply with such a court order, as the employee did here, FRCP 37 allows the court to impose certain sanctions (see table above). Such sanctions include staying the proceeding until the order is obeyed.*

*Instead of or in addition to such sanctions, the court must order the noncompliant party, his/her attorney, or both to pay the other party's reasonable expenses (including attorney's fees) unless the noncompliance was substantially justified or the fees would be unjust.

(Choice A) The party to be examined does not have the right to choose who will perform the mental or physical examination. Instead, the party requesting the examination may choose the examiner unless the examined party has a valid objection. In that case, the court will appoint the examiner.

(Choice C) The court where the lawsuit is pending may generally hold a party in contempt of court for failing to comply with a court order that compels discovery. However, a party cannot be held in contempt for failing to comply with a discovery order that requires the party to undergo a mental or physical examination (as seen here).

Educational objective:

A federal court may impose an FRCP 37 sanction on a party who fails to comply with a court order requiring a mental or physical examination, including staying the proceeding until the order is obeyed. But the court cannot hold the noncompliant party in contempt of court for such a violation.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 35 (physical and mental exams).

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(b) (sanctions for noncompliance with court's discovery order).

• 8B Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2238 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining what sanctions may be issued against a party who fails to undergo a court-ordered mental or physical examination).

explanation.zh:
违反证据开示令的制裁

(FRCP 37(b))

允许的制裁

作证地点

• 藐视法庭

• 指示对违反者的某些事实进行解释

• 禁止违法者提供某些证据

• 全部或部分罢诉书状

• 在服从命令之前继续进一步诉讼

• 藐视法庭*

• 全部或部分驳回要求

• 对违规者作出缺席判决

• 命令支付违反《联邦民事诉讼法》引起的合理费用(例如律师费)。

* 不能因不遵守身体或精神检查的命令而强制实施。

在证据开示期间,诉讼正在审理的法院可以命令当事人接受经适当许可或认证的考官(Choice B)的身心检查。

• 该方的精神或身体状况有争议

• 命令动议基于良好理由;

· 命令通过具体说明考试的时间、地点、方式、条件和范围以及进行考试的人来发出通知。

如果当事方未能遵守法院命令,如雇员在此所做的那样,FRCP 37允许法院施加某些制裁(见上表),包括暂停诉讼直至命令得到遵守。

* 法院必须命令违约方、其律师或双方支付另一方的合理费用(包括律师费用),而不是或除此以外,还须命令另一方支付合理费用(包括律师费用),除非有重大理由不履行或收费。不公正。

(Choice A)被检查的一方无权选择谁将进行精神或身体检查,相反,要求考试的一方可以选择被检查方,除非被检查方有有效的异议.在这种情况下,法院将任命审查员。

(C选择)诉讼未决的法院一般可以因一方未遵守法院命令迫使证据开示而判定其藐视法庭。然而,不能因为一方不遵守要求其接受精神或身体检查的证据开示命令(如本文所示)而被蔑视。

学习要点：

联邦法院可以对不遵守要求进行精神或身体检查的法院命令的一方施加FRCP 37制裁,包括中止诉讼程序直至命令得到遵守。但是,法院不能因这种侵权行为而判定不遵守规定的一方藐视法庭。

参考资料

• Fed. R. Civ. P.35(身体和精神检查)。

• Fed. R. Civ. P.37(b)(对不遵守法院的证据开示令的制裁)。

• 8B Charles Alan Wright等人,《联邦惯例和程序》§2238(3d,2020年)(解释对未接受法院命令的身心检查的一方可施加何种制裁)。

stem:
A dispute arose between a woman and a man over who was entitled to insurance policy proceeds held by a company incorporated and headquartered in the northern district of State A. The woman resides in the southern district of State A, and the man resides in the eastern district of State B.

The company filed a statutory interpleader action against the woman and the man in a federal court in the eastern district of State B. The company posted a bond of $50,000, which represents the amount of the disputed insurance policy proceeds. The woman and the man were served with process at their respective homes. The woman has moved to dismiss the action, claiming that the federal court has no subject-matter jurisdiction over the claim, lacks personal jurisdiction over her, and is not a proper venue.
stemZh:
一名女子和一名男子之间因谁有权获得一家公司持有的保险金收益而发生争议。该公司注册并总部设在A 州 北部地区。该女子居住在A 州 南部地区，该男子居住在B 州 东部地区。

该公司在B 州 东部地区的联邦法院提起了一项法定和解诉讼，针对该女子和该男子。该公司提交了 50,000 美元的保释金，该金额代表了争议的保险金收益。该女子和该男子在其各自住所被送达了诉讼文书。该女子提出了驳回诉讼动议，声称联邦法院对该主张没有事项管辖权，对该女子没有属人管辖权，并且该法院不是适当的审判地。
ask: Is the court likely to grant the woman's motion?
askZh: 法院很可能批准该女子的驳回诉讼动议吗？

options.en: No.
options.zh: 否.

options.en: Yes, because the court lacks personal jurisdiction over her.
options.zh: 是, because the court lacks personal jurisdiction over her.

options.en: Yes, because the parties lack complete diversity of citizenship.
options.zh: 是, because the parties lack complete diversity of citizenship.

options.en: Yes, because venue is improper.
options.zh: 是, because venue is improper.

explanation.en:
Rule interpleader v. Statutory interpleader

Requirements Rule interpleader Statutory interpleader

Subject-matter jurisdiction

• Complete diversity between stakeholder & claimants + amount in controversy >$75,000 or

• Claim arises under U.S. Constitution, treaty, or federal law

• Minimal diversity between claimants + amount in controversy ≥$500

Personal jurisdiction

• Consent

• Service of process

• Specific jurisdiction

• General jurisdiction

• Nationwide service of process

Venue Any district where:

• any claimant resides, if all reside in same state

• property located/events occurred or

• any claimant is subject to personal jurisdiction (if neither of above applies)

Any district where

• any claimant resides, even if claimants reside in different states

Deposit Not required Deposit property with court or post bond

The company has filed a statutory interpleader action in federal court. This action, like rule interpleader, is available when multiple persons claim an interest in the same property (ie, the stake). It allows the possessor of the stake (ie, the stakeholder) to avoid multiple liability by joining the claimants to litigate the ownership of the stake among themselves. However, a statutory interpleader action must satisfy special requirements for:

• subject-matter jurisdiction – requires an amount in controversy of at least $500 and minimal diversity of citizenship between at least two claimants

• personal jurisdiction – exists over any claimant who is served with process anywhere within the U.S. and

• venue – proper in any judicial district where any claimant resides, even if the claimants reside in different states.

Here, the court has subject-matter jurisdiction since the disputed proceeds are $50,000 and the woman and the man are citizens of States A and B, respectively. Personal jurisdiction exists over the woman because she was served with process in State A (Choice B). And venue is proper since the man resides in the eastern district of State B—where the court is located (Choice D). Therefore, the court will likely deny the woman's motion.

(Choice C) Rule interpleader actions based on diversity jurisdiction require complete diversity between the stakeholder and the claimants. However, statutory interpleader actions (as seen here) only require minimal diversity between the claimants.*

*Subject-matter jurisdiction can also be established in a rule interpleader action if the claim presents a federal question.

Educational objective:

For statutory interpleader actions, subject-matter jurisdiction requires an amount in controversy of at least $500 and minimal diversity between two or more claimants. Personal jurisdiction exists over any claimant who was served with process anywhere in the U.S. Venue is proper in any judicial district where any claimant resides.

References

• 28 U.S.C. §§ 1335, 1397, 2361 (statutory interpleader).

规则互诉人诉法定互诉人

法定仲裁员规则

属事管辖权

• 利害关系方和索赔人之间完全多样化+争议金额 > 75 000美元或

• 索赔根据美国宪法、条约或联邦法律提出

• 索赔人之间的最小差异+争议金额

属人管辖权

• 同意

• 流程服务

• 具体管辖权

• 普遍管辖权

• 全国范围的流程服务

任何地区:

• 任何申请人居住,如果所有人居住在同一国家

• 发生或发生的财产/活动

• 任何索赔人都受属人管辖权管辖(如果两者均不适用)

任何地区

• 任何申请人居住,即使申请人居住在不同州

交存法院或邮票的财产

公司已经向联邦法院提起了法定诉讼。 与规则诉讼人一样,当多人对同一财产(即股份)提出权益要求时,可以提起诉讼。它使利害关系人(即利益攸关方)能够通过加入索赔人在他们之间就利害关系的所有权提起诉讼。然而,法定的部际行动必须满足以下方面的特别要求:

• 属事管辖权 -- -- 要求争议金额至少500美元,且至少两个申请人的国籍差异最小

• 属人管辖权 -- -- 对任何在美国境内任何地方通过程序得到服务的求偿人具有属人管辖权;

• 地点 -- -- 任何申请人居住的任何司法区的合适地点,即使申请人居住在不同的州。

在这方面,法院具有属事管辖权,因为有争议的收益分别为50 000美元,妇女和男子分别是A州和B州公民,由于她在A州(Choice B)接受过诉讼,因此对该妇女有属事管辖权。地点是适当的,因为男子居住在法院所在地的B州东部地区(Choice D)。 因此,法院很可能拒绝妇女的动议。

(选择C)基于异籍管辖权的规则交叉诉讼要求利害关系方和索赔人之间完全多样化,但法定的交叉诉讼(如此处所示)只要求索赔人之间最低限度的多样性。

* 如果索赔要求提出联邦问题,也可在诉讼间规则中确定属事管辖权。

学习要点：

对于法定的跨诉讼,事项管辖权要求争议金额至少500美元,两个或两个以上求偿人之间的差别最小,对任何在美国任何地方接受过诉讼的求偿人都存在属人管辖权。在任何申请人居住的司法区,地点是适当的。

参考资料

• 28 U.S.C.§§1335、1397、2361(法定诉讼代理人)。

sourceSetLabel: 民事诉讼法 · 第 6 组
stem:
A distributor brought a diversity action against a manufacturer in federal district court for breach of contract. The district court ordered the parties' attorneys to attend a pretrial conference to obtain admissions and stipulations about the facts in the case. When the conference started, the manufacturer's attorney announced that his client had not authorized him to make admissions or stipulations. The district court canceled the conference as a result. This was the third time the court had to cancel a pretrial conference due to the attorney's failure to obtain authorization to make admissions or stipulations on behalf of his client.

After the conference, the district court issued an order that struck one of the manufacturer's affirmative defenses and required the manufacturer to pay the attorney's fees incurred by the distributor for attending the pretrial conference. At the conclusion of trial, the manufacturer appealed the order.
stemZh:
一名分销商在联邦地区法院对一家制造商提起了一项基于不同州籍管辖权的诉讼，指控其违反合同。地区法院命令双方律师参加一次庭前会议，以获取关于案件事实的承认和协议。当会议开始时，制造商的律师宣布他的客户并未授权他进行承认或协议。因此，地区法院取消了这次会议。这是法院第三次因该律师未能获得代表其客户进行承认或协议的授权而取消庭前会议。

会议结束后，地区法院发布了一项命令，删除了制造商的一项抗辩主张，并要求制造商支付分销商因参加庭前会议而产生的律师费用。在审判结束时，制造商上诉了该命令。
ask: Is the appellate court likely to reverse the district court's order?
askZh: 上诉法院很可能推翻地区法院的命令吗？

options.en: No, because the district court has absolute discretion to issue sanctions.
options.zh: 不，因为地区法院有权对制裁行使绝对裁量权。

options.en: No, because the order was reasonable under the circumstances.
options.zh: 不，因为该命令在特定情况下是合理的。

options.en: Yes, because the district court is limited to requiring the manufacturer to pay the distributor's attorney's fees.
options.zh: 是，因为地区法院仅限于要求制造商支付分销商的律师费用。

options.en: Yes, because the manufacturer did not authorize the attorney to make admissions or stipulations.
options.zh: 是，因为制造商未授权律师进行承认或协议。

explanation.en:
A federal district court may order the attorneys and any unrepresented parties to attend one or more pretrial conferences. These conferences are designed to improve the trial's quality, facilitate settlement, and expedite litigation (eg, by obtaining admissions and stipulations). To promote those goals, a district court may impose reasonable sanctions on any party or attorney who:

• failed to attend a pretrial conference

• was substantially unprepared to participate in the conference

• did not participate in good faith in the conference or

• failed to obey a pretrial order. Here, the manufacturer's attorney was substantially unprepared to participate in the pretrial conference because he failed to obtain the manufacturer's authorization to make admissions and stipulations. This led the district court to strike one of the manufacturer's affirmative defenses. This sanction was reasonable since this was the third time the court had to cancel a pretrial conference due to the attorney's failure to obtain such authorization

(Choice C).

Additionally, a court must order a noncompliant party and/or attorney to pay the other party's reasonable expenses, including attorney's fees, unless (1) the noncompliance was substantially justified or (2) the payment would be unjust. The attorney's unpreparedness was not substantially justified because he should have obtained the manufacturer's authorization before the conference (Choice D). And since there is no indication that awarding attorney's fees would be unjust, the appellate court will likely affirm the order.

(Choice A) Although the district court has discretion to decide which sanctions to impose, this discretion is not absolute. The reason is that an appellate court has the power to reverse a district court's arbitrary or unreasonable sanction as an abuse of discretion (not seen here).

Educational objective:

A federal court may issue reasonable sanctions against any party or attorney who is substantially unprepared to participate in a pretrial conference. Additionally, a court must order the payment of the opposing party's reasonable expenses unless (1) noncompliance was substantially justified or (2) the payment would be unjust.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(f) (pretrial conference sanctions).

• 6A Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 1531 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining when sanctions are appropriate for failure to comply with pretrial conference and/or order).

explanation.zh:
联邦地区法院可以命令律师和任何无人代理的当事方出席一次或多次预审会议。这些会议旨在提高审判质量、便利解决和加快诉讼(例如通过获得承认和规定),为了促进实现这些目标,区法院可对下列任何当事方或律师实施合理的制裁:

• 未出席预审会议

• 基本上没有准备好参加会议

• 没有诚意参加会议或

· 不遵守预审命令:在这方面,制造商的律师基本上没有准备好参加预审会议,因为他没有获得制造商的许可,无法作出承认和规定。这导致地区法院对制造商的其中一项平权辩护予以驳回,这一处罚是合理的,因为这是法院第三次因律师未能获得授权而不得不取消预审会议。

(中文(简体) ).

此外,法院必须命令违约方和/或律师支付另一方的合理费用,包括律师费,除非(1)违约有重大理由,或者(2)付款是不公正的。律师的不准备没有实质性的理由,因为他应该在会议之前获得制造商的授权(Choice D)。由于没有迹象表明裁决律师费是不公正的,上诉法院可能会确认这项命令。

(Choice A) 虽然地区法院有权决定实施何种制裁,但这种酌处权并不是绝对的。原因是,上诉法院有权推翻地区法院的任意或不合理制裁,作为滥用裁量权(此处不见)。

学习要点：

联邦法院可以对基本上没有准备参加预审会议的任何当事方或律师发出合理的制裁。此外,法院必须命令对方支付合理费用,除非(1) 违约有重大理由,或(2) 付款是不公正的。

参考资料

• Fed. R. Civ. P.16(f)(预审会议制裁)。

• 6A Charles Alan Wright等人,《联邦惯例和程序》,第1531节(第3d版,2020年)(解释对不遵守预审会议和(或)命令的适当制裁)。

stem:
A corporation brought a patent infringement action in federal court against a manufacturer. The corporation alleged that the manufacturer infringed on the corporation's patent for a shoe design. During discovery, the corporation sent the manufacturer a request to "produce all electronic documents relating to the production of the shoe." The corporation did not specify the form in which the documents were to be produced.

The manufacturer produced one year's worth of electronic documents relating to the production of the shoe, but it argued that it could not produce any documents beyond this time because they had been deleted from its server. The corporation filed a motion to compel the production of the documents. In response to the motion, the manufacturer established that recovering the electronic documents would be unduly burdensome and costly because they could be recovered only if the manufacturer hired an expensive data-recovery firm.
stemZh:
一家公司在美国联邦法院提起专利侵权诉讼，起诉一家制造商。该公司声称制造商侵犯了其鞋类设计的专利。在证据开示阶段，该公司向制造商发出请求，要求提供所有与鞋类生产相关的电子文件。该公司并未具体说明文件应以何种形式提供。

制造商提供了过去一年与鞋类生产相关的电子文件，但其辩称无法提供更早的文件，因为这些文件已被从其服务器中删除。该公司随后提出动议，要求强制制造商提供文件。针对该动议，制造商证明，恢复电子文件将造成极大的负担和成本，因为只有在制造商雇佣一家昂贵的数据恢复公司的情况下才能恢复这些文件。
ask: How should the court rule on the corporation's motion to compel?
askZh: 法院应该如何裁定公司的强制提供动议？

options.en: It should deny the motion, because the corporation failed to specify the form in which the electronic documents should be produced.
options.zh: 应驳回该动议，因为该公司未具体说明电子文件应以何种形式提供。

options.en: It should deny the motion, if the manufacturer provides a meritorious defense to the claim.
options.zh: 应驳回该动议，如果制造商对索赔提出有根据的抗辩。

options.en: It should grant the motion, if the corporation demonstrates that it will prevail on the merits of the case.
options.zh: 应批准该动议，如果该公司证明其将在案件的实质问题上胜诉。

options.en: It should grant the motion, if the corporation shows good cause for the production.
options.zh: 应批准该动议，如果该公司证明提供文件有正当理由。

explanation.en:
During discovery, parties can use various methods to compel disclosure of information related to the case. A request for production is a discovery method used to compel an opposing party to produce and allow inspection of documents, electronically stored information (ESI), tangible things, and real property.

A party generally must produce ESI in the form specified in the request or, if no form is specified, then in the ESI's ordinarily maintained or usable form. If ESI is not produced, the requesting party may file a motion to compel production. The producing party must then show that the ESI is not reasonably accessible due to undue burden or cost. If this is established, the court will order the production of ESI only if the requesting party shows good cause for the production.

Here, the corporation filed a motion to compel the production of the manufacturer's electronic documents related to the shoe design at issue. The manufacturer established that retrieving the documents that had been deleted from its server would be unduly burdensome and costly because it would have to hire an expensive data-recovery firm. However, if the corporation shows good cause for the production, the court should grant the corporation's motion to compel.

(Choice A) A party requesting the production of ESI may, but is not required to, specify the form in which the ESI is to be produced.

(Choices B & C) In opposing a motion to compel discovery, the producing party (the manufacturer) need not provide a meritorious defense. Additionally, the requesting party (the corporation) does not need to show that it will prevail on the merits. Instead, the focus is on whether the discovery at issue should be produced.

Educational objective:

In response to a motion to compel the production of electronically stored information (ESI), the producing party must show that the ESI is not reasonably accessible due to undue burden or cost. If shown, the court will order the production of the ESI only if the requesting party demonstrates good cause for the production.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(2)(B) (limitations on electronic discovery).

• 8 Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2008.2 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining the procedure for inaccessible ESI).

explanation.zh:
在证据开示期间,当事人可以使用各种方法强制披露与案件有关的信息.生产请求是一种证据开示方法,用于迫使对方出示并允许检查文件,电子存储信息(ESI),有形的东西,和不动产.

当事人一般必须按请求中规定的形式生产ESI,如未指明形式,则按ESI通常保持或使用的形式生产ESI,如果不生产ESI,请求方可以提出强制生产的动议。生产方必须表明,由于负担过重或费用太高,ESI无法合理获取,如果确定这一点,法院将命令生产ESI,只有请求方证明生产有正当理由。

在此,该公司提出一项动议,要求生产制造商与所涉鞋类设计有关的电子文件。制造商确定,从服务器上取回删除的文件将造成不适当的负担和费用,因为它必须雇用一家昂贵的数据回收公司。但是,如果公司证明有正当理由进行生产,法院应批准公司强制生产的动议。

(Choice A)请求生产ESI的一方可以但无需指定ESI的生产形式.

(Choices B & C) 在反对强迫证据开示的动议时,生产方(制造商)不必提供有价值辩护,此外,请求方(公司)也不必表明它将以案情为准。相反,重点是是否应产生有争议的证据开示。

学习要点：

针对强制生产电子存储信息(ESI)的动议,生产方必须表明,由于负担或费用过重,ESI无法合理获取。如果出示,法院将只有在请求方证明有正当理由才下令制作ESI。

参考资料

• Fed. R. Civ. P.26(b)(2)(B)(对电子证据开示的限制)。

• 8 Charles Alan Wright等人,《联邦惯例和程序》§2008.2(3d编,2020年)(解释无障碍ESI的程序)。

stem:
A woman bought a piece of farmland in the state where she resides. Three years after this purchase, a man informed her that he held a mortgage against the farmland and that she must pay him.

The woman then filed a quiet title action in an appropriate federal court in the state where the farmland is located. The man was properly served with the complaint and summons.

The day after receiving the complaint and summons, the man called the woman and informed her that he co-owns the mortgage on the farmland with his brother. Both the man and his brother live in another state.
stemZh:
一名女子在她居住的州购买了一块农田。在购买该农田三年后，一名男子告诉她，他持有该农田的抵押权，并要求她支付。

随后，该女子在该农田所在州的适当联邦法院提起了一项不动产权属诉讼。该男子收到了诉状和传票。

在收到诉状和传票的第二天，该男子打电话给该女子，告诉她他与他的兄弟共同拥有该农田的抵押权。该男子和他的兄弟都居住在另一个州。
ask: What is the easiest action the woman can take to join the man's brother in the suit?
askZh: 该女子要将该男子的兄弟加入诉讼，最简单的做法是什么？

options.en: File a motion for compulsory joinder.
options.zh: 提出强制加入的动议。

options.en: Immediately file and serve an amended complaint listing both siblings as defendants.
options.zh: 立即提交并送达一份修订后的诉状，将两名兄弟列为被告。

options.en: Move the court for permission to join the other sibling.
options.zh: 请求法院允许加入另一名兄弟。

options.en: Voluntarily dismiss the case and refile a complaint naming both siblings as defendants.
options.zh: 自愿驳回案件，并重新提交一份将两名兄弟列为被告的诉状。

explanation.en:
Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure (FRCP) 19, a person must be joined as a party to a lawsuit in certain situations. Here, for example, the brother is likely a required party in the woman's quiet title action since his absence could prejudice his mortgage interest. And though the woman failed to name him in her complaint, FRCP 15 allows a party to amend a pleading once as a matter of course—ie, without the court's permission or the opposing party's written consent. But this must be done within 21 days after:

• serving that pleading if a responsive pleading is not required or

• being served with a responsive pleading or FRCP 12 motion (whichever occurs first) if a responsive pleading is required. A defendant is required to file and serve an answer in response to the plaintiff's complaint. And since the man has not yet filed an answer (or FRCP 12 motion), the woman can amend her complaint without the court's permission or the man's written consent

(Choice C). Therefore, the easiest way the woman can join the brother in the suit is to immediately file and serve an amended complaint listing both siblings as defendants.

(Choice A) Compulsory (ie, required) joinder makes it mandatory to include all necessary parties in a lawsuit—eg, co-owners of property in a quiet title action. Therefore, a defendant would file a motion for compulsory joinder to add any necessary parties, while a plaintiff would simply amend the complaint (as seen here).

(Choice D) A plaintiff may voluntarily dismiss a suit if the plaintiff wants to file it in a different court or has reached a settlement with the defendant. But the plaintiff need not dismiss a complaint to add another party.

Educational objective:

A party can amend a pleading once as a matter of course within 21 days (1) after serving that pleading or (2) if a responsive pleading is required, after being served with a responsive pleading or motion under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 12.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a) (amending complaint before trial).

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 19 (required joinder of parties).

explanation.zh:
根据《联邦民事诉讼规则》第19条,在某些情况下,个人必须作为诉讼的一方参与诉讼,例如,在这方面,该兄弟很可能是该妇女静悄悄的产权诉讼的一方,因为他的缺席会损害他的抵押权利益。虽然该妇女没有在起诉状中点名,但FRCP 15允许一方在未经法院许可或对方书面同意的情况下,当然修改一次诉状。

• 如果不需要答辩,为答辩人服务;

• 如果需要答辩,则向被告送达应诉书或FRCP 12动议(无论先发生何种情况),被告必须提交并送达对原告起诉状的答复。由于男子尚未提出答复(或FRCP 12动议),妇女可以不经法院许可或男子书面同意修改其起诉状。

因此,妇女加入诉讼兄弟的最简单方式是立即提出并提交修正后的起诉状,将两个兄弟姐妹列为被告。

(选择A) 强制(即要求)合并使所有必要的当事方必须参加诉讼——例如,财产的共同所有人在静悄悄的所有权诉讼中。因此,被告将提出强制合并诉讼动议,以便增加任何必要的当事方,而原告则只是修改起诉状(如本文所示)。

(Choice D)如果原告想向另一法庭提起诉讼或与被告达成和解,原告可以自愿驳回诉讼,但原告不必驳回起诉状而增加另一当事方。

学习要点：

一方当事人在送达答辩书后21天(1)内,或者(2)如果需要答辩书,在根据《联邦民事诉讼规则》第12条送达答辩书或动议后,可以当然修改答辩书一次。

参考资料

• Fed.R. Civ.P.15(a)(在审判前提出控诉)。

• Fed. R. Civ. P.19(需要加入各方)。

stem:
On July 1, 2015, a man was seriously injured when the helicopter he was piloting crashed. The man's attorney diligently investigated and determined that a valve malfunction caused the crash. The attorney contacted the helicopter distributor and requested the name of the company that manufactured the valve in the man's helicopter. The helicopter distributor mistakenly gave the attorney the name of the wrong valve manufacturer.

On June 1, 2017, the man sued the helicopter distributor and the valve manufacturer in federal court to recover $5 million in damages. On January 3, 2018, the name of the valve manufacturer that actually manufactured the valve in the man's helicopter was revealed during discovery. The same day, the man moved to amend his complaint to substitute the correct valve manufacturer as the defendant. The correct valve company did not receive notice of the man's suit until this time.

The applicable statute of limitations provides: "Any personal injury action shall be brought within two years from the date the alleged injuries occurred. A complaint may be amended to properly name a defendant not identified until after the complaint has been filed if the complaint was filed within the designated limitations period."
stemZh:
2015年7月1日，一名男子在驾驶直升机时因直升机坠毁而严重受伤。该男子的律师认真调查并确定，事故是由于一个阀门故障引起的。律师联系了直升机经销商，要求提供该男子直升机中阀门的制造商名称。直升机经销商错误地向律师提供了错误的阀门制造商名称。

2017年6月1日，该男子在联邦法院起诉直升机经销商和阀门制造商，要求赔偿500万美元的损失。2018年1月3日，在证据开示过程中，揭示了实际制造该男子直升机中阀门的阀门制造商名称。同一天，该男子提出动议，要求修改起诉书，将正确的阀门制造商作为被告。正确的阀门公司直到此时才收到该男子起诉的通知。

适用的诉讼时效规定为："任何人身伤害诉讼应在事故发生之日起两年内提起。如果起诉书是在诉讼时效期限内提出的，且未被识别的被告在起诉后被正确识别，起诉书可以被修改以正确命名该被告。"
ask: May the man amend his complaint?
askZh: 该男子能否修改起诉书？

options.en: No, because the correct valve manufacturer did not receive timely notice of the suit.
options.zh: 不能，因为正确的阀门制造商未及时收到诉讼通知。

options.en: No, because the statute of limitations has expired.
options.zh: 不能，因为诉讼时效已经届满。

options.en: Yes, because the amendment concerns the same transaction asserted in the original pleading.
options.zh: 可以，因为该修改涉及原起诉书中主张的同一交易。

options.en: Yes, because the amendment is permitted under the relation-back doctrine.
options.zh: 可以，因为该修改符合诉讼时效回溯原则。

explanation.en:
A pleading (eg, complaint) cannot be amended after the statute of limitations has expired unless the relation-back doctrine applies. Under this doctrine, an amendment is treated as if it were filed on the same date as the original pleading so that the amendment "relates back" to the date of the original pleading. An amendment that changes a party relates back if the applicable statute of limitations allows.

Here, the statute of limitations on the man's personal-injury claim expired on July 1, 2017— two years after his alleged injury. He moved to amend his complaint on January 1, 2018— six months after the statute of limitations had expired. But the applicable law allows relation back when the plaintiff made a mistake as to the proper defendant's identity. Therefore, the amendment "relates back" to the date the man's original complaint was filed on June 1, 2017—before the statute of limitations expired—and the man may amend his complaint (Choice B).

Had the applicable statute of limitations been silent about relation back, the amendment would still relate back if:

• the amendment concerned the same transaction or occurrence as the original pleading (Choice C)

• the new party received notice of the suit within 90 days after the original pleading was filed (Choice A) and

• the new party knew or should have known that the suit would have been brought against it but for a mistake concerning the proper party's identity (as seen here).

But this analysis is unnecessary since the applicable law does allow relation back under these circumstances.

Educational objective:

An amended pleading that changes a party to a lawsuit after the statute of limitations has expired will "relate back" to the date of the original pleading if the statute of limitations allows.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(c) (relation back of amended pleadings).

explanation.zh:
诉讼时效期满后,不得修改抗辩(例如起诉状),除非适用关系后继原则。根据这一学说,修正案被视作在与原答辩日相同的日期提出,这样修正案就"追溯到"原答辩日.如果适用的诉讼时效允许,变更一方当事人的修正案即具有追溯效力。

在此,该男子的人身伤害索赔的诉讼时效于2017年7月1日——他声称受伤两年后——到期,他于2018年1月1日——诉讼时效期满六个月后提出修改起诉状.但是,当原告对适当的被告身份犯下错误时,适用法律允许恢复关系。因此,该修正案"追溯到"2017年6月1日——诉讼时效到期前——该男子可以修改其起诉状(Choice B)之日.

如果适用的时效法对关系保持沉默,修正仍将关联返回,如果:

• 修正案涉及与原诉状相同的交易或事件(选择C)

• 新当事方在提出原诉状(选择A)后90天内收到诉讼通知;

· 新当事方知道或应该知道,如果不是在适当当事方的身份上出现错误(如这里所见),就会对其提起诉讼。

但这种分析没有必要,因为适用的法律确实允许在这种情况下恢复关系。

学习要点：

修正后的申辩,诉讼时效期满后变更诉讼当事人的,如果诉讼时效允许,将"追溯到"原申辩日.

参考资料

• Fed. R. Civ. P.15(c)(与经修正的书状的关系)。

stem:
A man brought a diversity action against a retail store in federal district court for injuries he sustained from a fall in the store. The man alleged that the store allowed its entryway to become slippery from a pipe that leaked water.

Sixty days before trial, the store sent the man its pretrial disclosures, which included a spreadsheet containing the names, addresses, and telephone numbers of the witnesses whom the store expected to testify at trial. Due to a formatting problem, one of the testifying witnesses was omitted from the spreadsheet. The store discovered the omission the following day. Twenty-one days before trial, the store sent the man's attorney an amended spreadsheet containing the testifying witness's information. This was the first time the man's attorney had heard of the testifying witness.

The man's attorney argues that the witness should be excluded from testifying at trial.
stemZh:
一名男子在联邦地区法院对一家零售商店提起基于不同州籍管辖权的诉讼，指控他在商店内因摔倒而受伤。该男子声称，商店允许其入口因漏水的管道而变得湿滑。

在庭审前60天，商店向该男子发送了其预审披露文件，其中包括商店预计在庭审中作证的证人的姓名、地址和电话号码的电子表格。由于格式问题，其中一个作证的证人未被包含在电子表格中。商店在第二天发现了这一遗漏。在庭审前21天，商店向该男子的律师发送了一份修正后的电子表格，包含该作证证人的信息。这是该男子律师第一次得知该证人。

该男子的律师认为，该证人不应在庭审中作证。
ask: Which of the following arguments is most likely to achieve the man's goal of preventing the witness from testifying at trial?
askZh: 以下哪项论点最有可能实现该男子防止证人作证的目标？

options.en: The parties did not stipulate that pretrial disclosures could be amended before trial.
options.zh: 双方并未约定预审披露文件可以在庭审前进行修改。

options.en: The store failed to timely correct its pretrial disclosures.
options.zh: 商店未能及时纠正其预审披露文件。

options.en: The store never obtained the court's leave before correcting its pretrial disclosures.
options.zh: 商店在纠正其预审披露文件之前从未获得法院的许可。

options.en: The store's initial pretrial disclosures were untimely filed.
options.zh: 商店的初始预审披露文件提交时间不及时。

explanation.en:
Required discovery disclosures

(FRCP 26(a))

Initial disclosures* • Persons with relevant information

• Items in party's possession that support claim/defense

• Computation of damages & supporting material

• Relevant insurance policies Expert testimony • Identity of expert witnesses

• Expert's written report

• If no report, subject matter & summary of testimony Pretrial disclosures* • Testifying witnesses

• Deposition testimony to be used at trial

• Documents/exhibits to be used at trial FRCP = Federal Rule of Civil Procedure.

*Does not apply to evidence used solely for impeachment.

During discovery, certain information must be automatically disclosed through required disclosures. This includes pretrial disclosures, the purpose of which is to avoid surprise at trial regarding substantive evidence. Therefore, pretrial disclosures must, at a minimum, identify the witnesses expected to testify and the evidence expected to be offered at trial.

If a party learns that its disclosures were materially incomplete or incorrect, it must supplement or correct them in a timely manner unless the other parties were made aware of that information during discovery or in writing.* Timeliness is generally evaluated based on how soon the supplemental/corrected information was disclosed after it became available to the disclosing party. Failure to timely supplement generally results in exclusion of the omitted witness or evidence at trial.

Here, the store learned that its pretrial disclosures were materially incomplete because they omitted a testifying witness. The store was required to and did correct those disclosures because the man's attorney had no knowledge of the omission. But waiting nearly 40 days after discovering the mistake before doing so was likely untimely. Therefore, arguing that the correction was untimely will most likely prevent the witness from testifying.

*A party also must supplement or correct any incomplete or incorrect initial disclosures, disclosures of expert testimony, and responses to interrogatories, requests for production, and requests for admission.

(Choices A & C) Neither the court's leave (ie, permission) nor the parties' stipulation is required for a party to supplement or correct its pretrial disclosures.

(Choice D) Pretrial disclosures must be made at least 30 days before trial. Therefore, the store's disclosures were timely submitted 60 days before trial.

Educational objective:

A party must timely supplement or correct pretrial disclosures when (1) the party learns that its disclosures were materially incomplete or incorrect and (2) the other parties have not been made aware of the supplemental or corrected information during discovery or in writing.

References

• Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(e) (supplementing disclosures and responses).

• 8A Charles Alan Wright et al., Federal Practice and Procedure § 2049.1 (3d ed. 2020) (explaining a party's duty to supplement or correct initial disclosures, expert testimony, pretrial disclosures, and certain discovery responses).

explanation.zh:
必要的证据开示披露

(FRCP 26(a))

· 拥有相关信息的人

• 当事方拥有的、支持索赔/辩护的物品

• 损害的计算和辅助材料

• 相关保险单

• 专家的书面报告

• 如果没有报告、事由和证词摘要,审前披露*

• 将在审判中使用的证言

• 审判时使用的文件/出处

* 不适用于仅用于弹劾的证据。

在证据开示期间,某些信息必须通过所要求的披露自动披露,包括审前披露,其目的是避免在审判中证据开示实质性证据。因此,审前披露必须至少确定预期作证的证人和预期在审判时提供的证据。

如果一方当事人获悉其披露内容严重不完整或不正确,必须及时加以补充或纠正,除非其他当事人在证据开示过程中或以书面形式了解到这一信息。补充/更正信息在披露方获得后多久才披露,如不及时补充,一般将遗漏的证人或审判证据排除在外。

在这方面,该商店得知,其审前披露在很大程度上不完整,因为他们忽略了一名作证的证人,该商店被要求并确实纠正这些披露,因为此人的律师不知道该遗漏。但是,在发现错误后近40天的等待很可能是不及时的。 因此,如果认为错误的纠正是不及时的,那很可能阻止证人作证。

* 当事方还必须补充或纠正任何不完整或不正确的初始披露、专家证词的披露以及对询问的答复、生产请求和承认请求。

(Choices A & C) 既不需要法院的许可(即许可),也不需要当事人的规定来补充或纠正其审前披露。

(Choice D) 预审披露必须至少在审判前30天作出,因此,商店的披露在审判前60天及时提交。

学习要点：

(1) 当当事人得知其披露严重不完整或不正确时,当事一方必须及时补充或纠正审前披露;(2) 在证据开示或披露时,其他当事人没有意识到补充或更正的信息。写作。

参考资料

• Fed. R. Civ. P.26(e)(补充披露和答复)。

• 8A Charles Alan Wright等人,《联邦惯例和程序》§2049.1(3d ed.2020)(解释一方补充或纠正初始披露、专家证词、审前披露和某些证据开示答复的义务)。
