stem:
A federal statute provides that the cities in which certain specified airports are located may regulate the rates and services of all limousines that serve those airports, without regard to the origin or destination of the passengers who use the limousines.

A city in State A is located adjacent to a city in State B. The airport serving both of them is located in the State A city and is one of those airports specified in the federal statute. The State A city council has adopted a rule that requires any limousines serving the airport to charge only the rates authorized by the State A city council.

An airline limousine service has a lucrative business transporting passengers between the State B city and the airport in the State A city, at much lower rates than those required by the State A city council. It transports passengers in interstate traffic only; it does not provide local service within the State A city. The new rule adopted by the State A city council will require the limousine service to charge the same rates as limousines operating only in the State A city.
stemZh:
一项联邦法律规定，位于某些指定机场所在城市的市镇可以监管所有服务于这些机场的豪华轿车的费用和服务，无论使用这些豪华轿车的乘客的出发地或目的地如何。

A 州 的一个城市毗邻 B 州 的一个城市。服务于这两个城市的机场位于 A 州 的城市，并且是联邦法律中所指的机场之一。A 州 市议会通过了一项规则，要求任何服务于该机场的豪华轿车只能收取 A 州 市议会授权的费用。

一家航空公司豪华轿车服务在 B 州 城市和 A 州 城市的机场之间运送乘客，其费用远低于 A 州 市议会要求的费用。该服务仅从事州际交通，不提供 A 州 城市内的本地服务。A 州 市议会的新规则将要求该豪华轿车服务收取与仅在 A 州 城市运营的豪华轿车相同的费用。
ask: Must the airline limousine service comply with the new rule of the State A city council?
askZh: 航空公司豪华轿车服务必须遵守 A 州 市议会的新规则吗？

options.en: No, because the airline limousine service is engaged in interstate commerce and this rule is an undue burden on that commerce.
options.zh: 否，因为该航空公司豪华轿车服务从事州际商业，该规则对该商业构成不合理的负担。

options.en: No, because the rule would arbitrarily destroy a lucrative existing business and, therefore, would amount to a taking without just compensation.
options.zh: 否，因为该规则将任意地摧毁一项有利可图的现有业务，因此构成未经合理补偿的征收。

options.en: Yes, because Congress has authorized this form of regulation by the State A city and, therefore, removed any constitutional impediments to it that may have otherwise existed.
options.zh: 是，因为国会已授权 A 州 市进行此类监管，因此消除了该监管可能存在的任何宪法障碍。

options.en: Yes, because the airport is located in the State A city and, therefore, its city council has exclusive regulatory authority over all transportation to and from the airport.
options.zh: 是，因为机场位于 A 州 城市，因此该城市的市议会对所有前往和离开机场的交通拥有专属监管权。

explanation.en:
The commerce clause empowers Congress to regulate interstate commerce—ie, nearly all activities involving two or more states. This clause also carries a negative implication (ie, the dormant commerce clause) that prohibits states and municipalities from discriminating against or otherwise unduly burdening interstate commerce. But Congress can exercise its broad commerce power to explicitly authorize conduct that would otherwise violate the dormant commerce clause.

Here, the State A city council rule requires all airport limousine services to charge only the rates authorized by the city council. It can be presumed that this rule unduly burdens interstate commerce because it regulates economic activities between State A and State B. But since Congress explicitly authorized this type of regulation by the State A city (via the federal statute), any constitutional impediments that may have existed were removed

(Choice A). As a result, the interstate limousine service must comply with the State A city rule.

(Choice B) A regulation that destroys all economic value of a business will be deemed a taking. Here, there is no evidence that the interstate limousine service's business will be destroyed by the higher rates, so the State A city council rule is not a taking. And even if it was, this would only allow the limousine service to seek just compensation (ie, fair market value at the time of the taking)—not to ignore the rule.

(Choice D) The city council's regulatory authority over transportation to and from the airport located in the city is not exclusive. Instead, this authority is shared with State A and the federal government.

Educational objective:

Congress can explicitly authorize states and municipalities to act in ways that would otherwise violate the dormant commerce clause.

References

• U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 3 (commerce clause).

• Ne. Bancorp v. Bd. of Governors of Fed. Reserve Sys., 472 U.S. 159, 174 (1985) (setting forth that states can discriminate against interstate commerce when Congress authorizes such action).

• 15A Am. Jur. 2d Commerce § 27 (2019) (explaining that Congress can authorize state action that would ordinarily violate the dormant commerce clause).

explanation.zh:
商业条款授权国会管理州际商业,即几乎所有涉及两个或两个以上州的活动。该条款还带有负面含义(即休眠商业条款),禁止各州市歧视州际商业或以其他方式不适当地加重其负担。但国会可以行使其广泛的商业权力,明确授权违反休眠商业条款的行为。

在这里,A州市议会规则要求所有机场豪华轿车服务只收取市议会授权的收费标准.可以推定,这一规则对A州和B州之间的经济活动加以管制,因而给州际商务造成了不适当的负担。但是,由于国会明确授权A州市(通过联邦法规)实施这类条例,因此可能存在的任何宪法障碍都得以消除。

(Choice A),因此州际豪华轿车服务必须遵守A州城市规则.

(Choice B) 破坏企业所有经济价值的法规将被视为收购。 这里,没有证据表明州际豪华轿车服务公司的业务会被更高的收费所摧毁,因此A州市议会的统治不是收购.即便如此,这也只能让豪华轿车服务寻求公正的补偿(即取车时的公平市场价值)——而不是无视规则。

(Choice D) 市议会对进出该市机场的交通的监管权并不专属,而是与A州和联邦政府分享这一权限.

学习要点：

国会可以明确授权各州市采取行动,否则将违反休眠商业条款。

参考资料

• 《美国法典》第1条第8款第3项(商业条款)。

• Ne. Bancorp诉联邦储备银行行长Bd.,472 U.S. 159,174(1985年)(规定国家可在国会授权采取这种行动时歧视州际商业)。

• 15A Am. Jur. 2d Commerce §27(2019)(解释国会可以授权通常违反休眠商业条款的国家行动)。

stem:
The United States Department of the Interior granted a man the food and drink concession in a federal park located in a state. The man operated his concession out of federally owned facilities in the park. The federal statute authorizing the Interior Department to grant such concessions provided that the grantees would pay only a nominal rental for use of these federal facilities because of the great benefit their concessions would provide to the people of the United States.

The state legislature enacted a statute imposing an occupancy tax on the occupants of real estate within that state that is not subject to state real estate taxes. The statute was intended to equalize the state tax burden on such occupants with that on people occupying real estate that is subject to state real estate taxes.

Pursuant to that statute, the state's Department of Revenue attempted to collect the state occupancy tax from the man because the federal facilities occupied by the man were not subject to state real estate taxes.

The man sued to invalidate the state occupancy tax as applied to him.
stemZh:
美国内政部在位于一个州的联邦公园里给予一名男子食物和饮料特许经营权,此人在公园里用联邦拥有的设施经营他的特许经营权.授权内政部授予这种特许权的联邦法规规定,受赠方只支付名义租金,用于使用这些联邦设施,因为他们的特许权将给联合国人民带来巨大利益。国家。

州立法机关颁布了一项法规,规定该州内的房地产占有者征收不须缴纳州房地产税的占用税.该法规旨在将这种居住者的国税负担与占用国家房地产税的人的国税负担相等。

根据该法规,该州税务局试图向该男子征收州占用税,因为该男子占用的联邦设施不受州房地产税的制约。

该男子起诉要求取消适用于他的国家占用税。
ask: What is the strongest constitutional ground upon which the man could challenge the occupancy tax?
askZh: 男人对占用税提出质疑的最有力的宪法依据是什么?

options.en: The tax violates the commerce clause by unduly burdening the interstate tourist trade.
options.zh: 该税违反了商业条款,给州际旅游贸易造成了不适当的负担。

options.en: The tax violates the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment because the tax treats him less favorably than federal concessionaires in other states who do not have to pay such occupancy taxes.
options.zh: 该税违反了第十四修正案的平等保护条款,因为该税比其他州不必缴纳这种占用税的联邦特许人对他待遇更不利.

options.en: The tax violates the privileges or immunities clause of the Fourteenth Amendment by interfering with the fundamental right to do business on federal property.
options.zh: 该税因干涉在联邦财产上做生意的基本权利,违反了第十四修正案的特权或豁免条款.

options.en: The tax violates the supremacy clause of Article VI and the federal statute authorizing such concessions.
options.zh: 该税违反了第六条至上条款和授权这种特许权的联邦法规。

explanation.en:
Federal immunity from state & local taxes/regulations

Tax/regulation Definition Permissibility

Direct Applies to federal government— including its agencies & instrumentalities

Immune unless:

• Congress consents to tax/regulation Indirect Applies to affiliates—including persons/entities employed by or doing business with federal government

Not immune unless:

• Congress grants immunity or

• tax/regulation discriminates against or substantially interferes with federal duties The supremacy clause immunizes the federal government, including its agencies and instrumentalities, from state and municipal taxation unless Congress consents. But the federal government's affiliates—ie, persons or entities employed by or doing business with the federal government—are only immune if:

• Congress grants the affiliate immunity

• the tax discriminates against the federal government or its affiliates or

• the tax substantially interferes with the affiliate's federal purpose or duties. Here, the state attempted to collect an occupancy tax from the man—an affiliate of the federal government who was granted the food and drink concession in a federal park. The federal statute authorizing this grant provided that the man would only pay nominal rent due to the great public benefit provided by concessions. And since the state tax may substantially interfere with the man's federal purpose or duties by raising his costs, his strongest argument is that the tax violates the supremacy clause and the federal statute as applied to him.

(Choice A) Under the dormant commerce clause, state taxes are invalid if they unduly burden interstate commerce. But the state tax here does not unduly burden the interstate tourist trade because it (1) applies to activities with a substantial nexus to the state, (2) is fairly apportioned, (3) does not discriminate against interstate commerce, and (4) is fairly related to the services and benefits provided by the state.

(Choice B) The Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause is triggered when a state treats similarly situated persons differently. But state laws that do not substantially impact a fundamental right or intentionally discriminate against a protected class (as seen here) are almost always upheld under mere rational basis scrutiny.

(Choice C) The Fourteenth Amendment privileges or immunities clause bars states from interfering with the very limited rights of national citizenship—which do not include a right to do business on federal property.

Educational objective:

The federal government's affiliates are subject to state and municipal taxation unless (1) Congress grants them immunity, (2) the tax is discriminatory, or (3) the tax substantially interferes with their federal purpose or duties.

References

• U.S. Const. art. VI, cl. 2 (supremacy clause).

• McCulloch v. Maryland, 17 U.S. 316, 436 (1819) (establishing federal immunity from state taxation and regulation).

• United States v. New Mexico, 455 U.S. 720, 735 n.11 (1982) (explaining that state taxes on affiliates of the federal government must be nondiscriminatory and cannot substantially interfere with its activities).

explanation.zh:
联邦豁免州和地方税/条例

税收/条例定义

直接适用于联邦政府,包括其机构和部门

免疫,除非:

• 国会同意税收/条例,间接适用于附属公司,包括联邦政府雇用或与联邦政府做生意的人员/实体

不得豁免,除非:

• 国会给予豁免权或

• 税收/条例歧视或严重干扰联邦义务。 至高无上条款使联邦政府,包括其各机构和部门,免受州和市征税,除非国会同意。但联邦政府的附属机构——联邦政府雇用或与其做生意的个人或实体——只有在下述情况下才享有豁免:

• 国会给予附属豁免

• 税收歧视联邦政府或其下属机构;

· 税收大大干涉了附属公司的联邦目的或职责,在这方面,该州试图向在联邦公园获得食品和饮料特许权的联邦政府下属的男子征收占用税。授权提供这种补助金的联邦法规规定,男子只支付名义租金,因为特许权提供了巨大的公共收益。而由于州税可能通过抬高成本而严重干扰男子的联邦目的或职责,因此他最强烈的理由是,该税违反了适用于他的至高无上条款和联邦法规.

(Choice A) 根据休眠商业条款,国家税如果给州际商务造成不适当的负担则无效.但这里的州税并没有给州际旅游贸易造成不适当的负担,因为它(1) 适用于与国家有重大关系的活动,(2) 公平分摊,(3) 不歧视州际商务,(4) 与州际商务有相当的关系。国家提供的服务和福利。

(Choice B) 当一个国家对处境相似的人区别对待时,第十四修正案的平等保护条款就会被触发.但是,对基本权利没有重大影响或故意歧视受保护阶层的州法律(如这里所见)几乎总是在仅仅理性的根据审查下得到维护。

(C) 第十四修正案的特权或豁免条款禁止国家公民权利的干涉——其中不包括在联邦财产上做生意的权利。

学习要点：

联邦政府下属机构须缴纳州和市税,除非:(1) 国会给予豁免,(2) 税项具有歧视性,或(3) 税项严重妨碍其联邦目的或职责。

参考资料

• 美国康斯特第6条第2款(最高条款)。

• McCulloch诉马里兰州案,17 U.S. 316, 436 (1819年)(确立联邦对州税和条例的豁免)。

• 美国诉新墨西哥,455 U.S. 720,735 n.11(1982年)(解释州对联邦政府附属机构的税收必须是非歧视性的,不能实质性干涉其活动)。

stem:
A state spends several million dollars a year on an oyster conservation program. As part of that program, the state limits, by statute, oyster fishing in its coastal waters to persons who have state oyster permits. In order to promote conservation, it issues only a limited number of oyster permits each year. The permits are effective for only one year from the date of their issuance and are awarded on the basis of a lottery, in which there is no differentiation between resident and nonresident applicants. However, each nonresident who obtains a permit is charged an annual permit fee that is $5 more than the fee charged residents.

A large fishing company operates from a port in another state and is incorporated in that other state. Each of the company's boats has a federal shipping license that permits it "to engage in all aspects of the coastal trade, to fish and to carry cargo from place to place along the coast, and to engage in other lawful activities along the coast of the United States." These shipping licenses are authorized by federal statute. Assume no other federal statutes or administrative rules apply.

Although it had previously held a state oyster permit, the company did not obtain a permit in that state's lottery this year.
stemZh:
一个州每年花费数百万美元用于牡蛎保护计划。作为该计划的一部分，该州通过法律规定，限制在其沿海水域进行牡蛎捕捞的人员只能是拥有州牡蛎许可证的人。为了促进保护，该州每年只发放有限数量的牡蛎许可证。许可证的有效期从签发之日起仅一年，并且是通过抽奖方式发放的，抽奖中没有区分居民和非居民申请人。然而，每个获得许可证的非居民需缴纳的年费比居民多5美元。

一家大型捕鱼公司在另一个州的港口运营，并在该州注册成立。该公司每艘渔船都拥有联邦航运许可证，允许其"从事沿海贸易的所有方面、捕鱼以及在沿海各地运送货物，并在美利坚合众国沿海进行其他合法活动。" 这些航运许可证是由联邦法律授权的。假设没有其他联邦法律或行政规章适用。

尽管该公司之前持有该州的牡蛎许可证，但该公司今年未在该州的抽奖中获得许可证。
ask: Which of the following is the strongest argument that can be made in support of a continued right of the company to fish for oysters this year in the state's coastal waters?
askZh: 下列哪一项是支持该公司今年继续在该州沿海水域捕捞牡蛎的权利的最有力论据？

options.en: The company has a right to fish for oysters in the state's waters despite the state law because it holds a federal shipping license.
options.zh: 尽管有该州法律，该公司仍有权在该州水域捕鱼，因为它持有联邦航运许可证。

options.en: The refusal to grant the company a permit this year is a taking of its property without due process of law because the company previously held a state oyster permit and the state knows that the company is engaged in a continuing business operation.
options.zh: 拒绝向该公司发放许可证的行为是对该公司财产的征收，且未给予正当法律程序，因为该公司之前持有该州的牡蛎许可证，且该州知道该公司正在进行持续的商业运营。

options.en: The state law denies the company the privileges and immunities of state citizenship because it provides higher permit charges for nonresidents.
options.zh: 该州法律剥夺了该公司作为州公民所享有的特权和豁免权，因为它对非居民提供更高的许可证费用。

options.en: The state law is an undue burden on interstate commerce because it provides higher permit charges for nonresidents.
options.zh: 该州法律对州际商业构成了不合理的负担，因为它对非居民提供更高的许可证费用。

explanation.en:
Under the supremacy clause, the provisions of the U.S. Constitution, federal laws, and treaties are the supreme law of the land. As a result, these provisions preempt conflicting provisions in state constitutions, state laws, and local laws—rendering such provisions void and without effect.

Here, the fishing company possesses a shipping license authorized by a federal statute that permits it to fish in the state's waters. But the state statute prohibits the company from fishing since it lacks a state-issued permit. Since these statutes conflict, the company's strongest argument is that its federal shipping license gives it a right to fish in the state's waters despite the state law.

(Choice B) The Fourteenth Amendment due process clause requires a state to provide notice and a meaningful opportunity to be heard to those it deprives of life, liberty, or property. But the company has no property interest in its expired state permit, so the state did not violate this clause.

(Choice C) The Article IV privileges and immunities clause prohibits states from discriminating against citizens of other states by denying them a right of state citizenship. But noncitizens and corporations (like the fishing company) are not considered citizens under this clause. Therefore, this clause does not apply.

(Choice D) The dormant commerce clause generally bars states from discriminating against or otherwise unduly burdening interstate commerce. But discrimination is permitted when the state participates in the market—ie, buys or sells goods or services. And since the state is selling permits to fish in its coastal waters, it can charge nonresidents more for a permit.

Educational objective:

Under the supremacy clause, the U.S. Constitution, federal laws, and treaties preempt conflicting state constitutions, state laws, and local laws.

References

• U.S. Const. art. VI, cl. 2 (supremacy clause).

• Douglas v. Seacoast Prods., Inc., 431 U.S. 265, 283 (1977) (holding that a state fishing law that prohibits federally licensed ships from fishing in the state's waters violates the supremacy clause).

explanation.zh:
根据至高无上条款,美国宪法,联邦法律和条约的规定是国家的最高法律.因此,这些规定预先防止州宪法、州法律和地方法律中相互冲突的规定——使这些规定无效和无效。

在此,捕鱼公司拥有联邦法规授权的航运许可证,允许其在州水域捕鱼。 但州法规禁止该公司捕鱼,因为它没有州颁发的许可证。由于这些法规冲突,该公司最强烈的论点是,尽管有州法律,其联邦航运执照仍赋予其在州水域捕鱼的权利.

(Choice B) 第十四修正案的正当程序条款要求国家向剥夺生命、自由或财产的人发出通知和有意义的陈述机会。但公司在其过期的州许可证中没有财产权益,因此州没有违反这一条款.

(C选择)第四条的特权和豁免条款禁止国家歧视其他国家的公民,剥夺他们国家公民权.但根据这一条款,非公民和公司(如渔业公司)不被视为公民,因此这一条款不适用。

休眠商业条款一般禁止歧视州际商业或以其他方式给州际商业造成不适当的负担。 但当国家参与市场(即买卖商品或服务)时,歧视是允许的。由于国家正在出售在沿海水域捕鱼的许可证,它可以向非居民收取更多的许可证费。

学习要点：

根据至高无上条款,美国宪法,联邦法律和条约先于冲突的国家宪法,州法律,以及地方法律.

参考资料

• 美国康斯特第6条第2款(最高条款)。

• Douglas诉Seacoast Prods, Inc., 431 U.S. 265, 283 (1977)(认为禁止获得联邦执照的船只在州水域捕鱼的州捕鱼法违反了至高无上条款)。

stem: A federally owned and operated office building located in a state is heated with a new, pollution-free heating system. However, in the coldest season of the year, this new system is sometimes insufficient to supply adequate heat to the building. The federal appropriation statute providing the money for construction of the new heating system permitted use of the old, pollution-generating system when necessary to supply additional heat. When the old heating system operates (only about two days in any year), the smokestack of the building emits smoke that exceeds the state's pollution-control standards.
stemZh: 一座由联邦政府拥有并运营的办公楼位于一州，该楼采用了一种新的无污染供暖系统进行供暖。然而，在一年中最寒冷的季节，这种新系统有时无法为大楼提供足够的热量。为新供暖系统建设提供资金的联邦拨款法案允许在需要额外热量时使用旧的、产生污染的供暖系统。当旧供暖系统运行时（每年仅约两天），该建筑的烟囱排放的烟雾超过了该州的污染控制标准。
ask: May the operators of the federal office building be prosecuted successfully by state authorities for violating that state's pollution-control standards?
askZh: 州当局能否成功起诉联邦办公楼的运营者，因其违反该州的污染控制标准？

options.en: No, because the operations of the federal government are immune from state regulation in the absence of federal consent.
options.zh: 不能，因为联邦政府的运作在缺乏联邦同意的情况下不受州监管的豁免。

options.en: No, because the violations of the state pollution-control standards involved here are so insignificant that they are beyond the legitimate reach of state law.
options.zh: 不能，因为此处涉及的违反州污染控制标准的行为如此轻微，以至于超出了州法律的合理范围。

options.en: Yes, because the regulation of pollution is a joint concern of the federal government and the state and, therefore, both of them may regulate conduct causing pollution.
options.zh: 可以，因为污染的监管是联邦政府和州的共同关注事项，因此两者均可对造成污染的行为进行监管。

options.en: Yes, because the regulation of pollution is a legitimate state police power concern.
options.zh: 可以，因为污染的监管是州警察权的正当事项。

explanation.en:
Under the Article VI supremacy clause, the U.S. Constitution, federal laws, and treaties are the supreme law of the land. As a result, the operations of the federal government— including those of its agencies and instrumentalities—are completely immune from state regulation in the absence of congressional consent. And since Congress did not consent to the state's pollution-control standards in this instance, the operators of the federal office building cannot be successfully prosecuted for violating them.

(Choice B) All federal government violations of state regulations—insignificant or otherwise—are beyond the reach of state law unless Congress consented to the regulation.

(Choice C) Both the federal and state governments may regulate pollution. But the supremacy clause prevents states from enforcing their regulations against the federal government without congressional consent.

(Choice D) The Tenth Amendment reserves to states the broad police power to enact and enforce laws that are reasonably related to protecting public health, safety, and welfare—eg, regulating pollution. But when exercising this power, states cannot violate other constitutional provisions like the supremacy clause (as seen here).

Educational objective:

The operations of the federal government—including those of its agencies and instrumentalities—are completely immune from state regulation unless Congress consents.

References

• Arizona v. California, 283 U.S. 423, 451 (1931) (explaining that "[t]he United States may perform its functions without conforming to the police regulations of a State").

explanation.zh:
根据第六条至上条款,美国宪法,联邦法律和条约是国家的最高法律.因此,联邦政府的运作——包括其各机构和机构的运作——在没有国会同意的情况下完全不受国家管制。而由于国会在此情况下不同意该州的污染控制标准,联邦办公大楼的运营商无法因违反这些标准而被成功起诉.

(选择B)所有联邦政府违反州条例的行为——重大或其他行为——都超出州法律的范围,除非国会同意这一条例。

(C选择)联邦和州政府都可以监管污染。 但至高无上条款阻止各州在未经国会同意的情况下对联邦政府实施条例。

(Choice D)第十修正案保留了广泛的警察权力,以颁布和执行与保护公共卫生、安全和福利(例如管理污染)有关的法律。但在行使这一权力时,国家不能违反其他宪法规定,如至高无上条款(如这里所见).

学习要点：

除非国会同意,联邦政府的运作——包括其各机构和部门的运作——完全不受国家管制。

stem:
Congress enacted a statute that annually awards federal funds to states that must be used to improve the quality of public education. Every state agreed to participate in this federal program. On average, the funds awarded by the federal program comprise 15% of a state's overall annual budget.

Several years later, Congress enacted another statute that expanded this federal program to reduce the academic achievement gap between high-performing and low-performing public schools. A provision of this federal statute requires states to administer a statewide academic test to students that is then used to assess the academic performance of public schools. States that choose not to comply with this testing requirement will no longer receive any federal funding from the program and may suffer budgetary shortfalls as a result.

A state that has chosen not to comply with the testing requirement has sued the federal government, arguing that the statute's provision is unconstitutional.
stemZh:
国会通过了一项法律，每年向各州提供联邦资金，这些资金必须用于提高公立教育的质量。每个州都同意参与该联邦计划。该联邦计划提供的资金平均占各州年度总预算的15%。

几年后，国会又通过了一项法律，将该联邦计划扩大到减少高绩效和低绩效公立学校之间的学术成就差距。该联邦法律的一项条款要求各州为学生实施一项州级学术考试，该考试随后用于评估公立学校的学术表现。选择不遵守该考试要求的州将不再从该计划中获得任何联邦资金，并可能因此导致预算赤字。

一个选择不遵守考试要求的州起诉了联邦政府，认为该法律条款是违宪的。
ask: Which of the following is the state's best argument?
askZh: 以下哪一项是该州的最佳论点？

options.en: Incentivizing states to adopt federal policies exceeds the scope of Congress's spending power.
options.zh: 激励各州采用联邦政策超出了国会拨款权力的范围。

options.en: The condition placed on the receipt of federal funding is unduly coercive.
options.zh: 联邦资金的接收条件是过度强制的。

options.en: The funding of public education has traditionally been performed by the states.
options.zh: 公立教育的资金历来由各州负责。

options.en: The Tenth Amendment grants states immunity from direct federal regulation.
options.zh: 第十条修正案赋予各州对联邦直接监管的豁免权。

explanation.en:
Conditional federal funding

(Article I, section 8 spending clause)

Conditions must meet all the following criteria:

• clearly stated & unambiguous

• reasonably related to federal interest in funded program

• do not require states to engage in unconstitutional activity

• do not unduly coerce states into accepting The taxing and spending clause gives Congress broad discretion to spend for the general welfare, such as improving the quality of public education. Congress can use this spending power to incentivize states to adopt federal policies by placing appropriate conditions on the receipt of federal funds (Choice A). A condition is appropriate when it:

• is clear and unambiguous (eg, requiring states to comply with the testing requirement or lose federal funding)

• is reasonably related to the purpose for which the funds will be expended (eg, requiring academic testing to reduce the academic achievement gap)

• does not require recipients to engage in unconstitutional activity (eg, developing and administering a statewide academic test is not unconstitutional) and

• is not unduly coercive.

A condition is unduly coercive if it amounts to a "gun to the head" of a state. Although SCOTUS has not provided concrete guidance on how to make this determination, it has invalidated a condition that would have withheld 10% of a state's overall budget.*

Here, the condition on the receipt of federal funding would withhold 15% of an average state's annual budget. This amounts to a "gun to the head" and is unduly coercive since states that do not comply with this condition may suffer significant budgetary shortfalls. Therefore, this is the state's best argument that the provision is unconstitutional.

*In contrast, SCOTUS has upheld a condition that withheld less than 1% of a state's overall budget.

(Choice C) Although the funding of public education has traditionally been performed by the states, the spending clause gives Congress the power to spend for the general welfare— including public education.

(Choice D) The Tenth Amendment grants states immunity from federal regulations that compel or unduly coerce them to enact state laws or enforce federal laws. However, states must comply with other types of direct federal regulation (eg, EPA pollution standards).

Educational objective:

Congress may use its spending power to regulate states by placing conditions on the receipt of federal funds that (1) are clear and unambiguous, (2) are reasonably related to the purpose for which the funds will be expended, (3) do not require recipients to engage in unconstitutional activity, and (4) are not unduly coercive.

SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States; EPA = Environmental Protection Agency.

References

• U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 1 (taxing and spending clause).

• South Dakota v. Dole, 483 U.S. 203, 212 (1987) (holding that Congress can place a condition on the receipt of federal highway funding that amounts to less than 1% of a state's overall budget).

• Nat'l Fed'n of Indep. Bus. v. Sebelius, 567 U.S. 519, 581–82 (2012) (explaining that Congress cannot place a condition on the receipt of Medicaid funds that amounts to 10% of a state's overall spending).

explanation.zh:
有条件的联邦供资

(第一条第8节支出条款)

条件必须符合下列所有标准:

• 明确声明和毫不含糊

• 合理涉及联邦对资助方案的兴趣

• 不要求各国从事违宪活动

• 不得不适当地强迫国家接受税收和开支条款,使国会有广泛的酌处权,可以用于一般福利,例如提高公共教育的质量。国会可以利用这种支出权力,通过对接受联邦资金规定适当条件(选择A)来激励各州通过联邦政策。

• 明确无误(例如,要求各州遵守测试要求或失去联邦资金)

• 与资金的用途有合理关系(例如,需要进行学术测试以缩小学术成绩差距)

· 不要求受援者从事违宪活动(例如,制定和管理全州范围的学术考试不违反宪法);

• 不过分胁迫。

如果一个条件相当于一个国家的“枪指头”,那么它就具有过度的强制性。 尽管SCOTUS没有就如何作出这种决定提供具体指导,但它已经使一个条件失效,而这一条件本来会扣留一个国家总预算的10%。

在这里,接受联邦资金的条件会扣留平均州年度预算的15%,这相当于"枪指着头",而且过于强制,因为不遵守这一条件的州可能会面临严重的预算短缺.因此,这是该州认为该规定违宪的最好论点.

* 与此相对照,SCOTUS坚持了一个扣留州总预算不到1%的条件。

(选择C)虽然公共教育的经费传统上由各州承担,但支出条款赋予国会为一般福利——包括公共教育——开支的权力.

(Choice D)第十修正案规定,联邦条例可以强制或不适当地强迫它们颁布州法律或执行联邦法律,但各州必须遵守其他类型的直接联邦条例(如环保局污染标准)。

学习要点：

国会可利用其支出权对各州进行管理,规定接受联邦资金的条件(1) 明确和毫不含糊,(2) 与资金的用途有合理关系,(3) 不要求接受者参与。违宪活动,(4)不是不适当的胁迫。

SCOTUS = 美国最高法院;EPA = 环境保护局。

参考资料

• 《美国法典》第1条第8款第1项(征税和支出条款)。

• 南达科他州诉Dole案,483 U.S. 203, 212(1987年)(认为国会可以把获得联邦高速公路资金作为条件,其数额不到州总预算的1%)。

· Nat'l Fed'n of Indep. Bus. v. Sebelius, 567 U.S.519, 581–82(2012)(解释国会不能把接受相当于州总支出10%的医药援助基金作为条件)。

stem:
Widgets are manufactured wholly from raw materials mined and processed in a state. The only two manufacturers of widgets in the United States are also located in that state. However, their widgets are purchased by retailers located in every state.

The state legislature is considering the adoption of a statute that would impose a tax solely on the manufacture of widgets. The tax is to be calculated at 3% of their wholesale value.
stemZh:
Widgets 是完全由在某一州开采和加工的原材料制造的。美国唯一两家 Widgets 制造商也位于该州。然而，他们的 Widgets 被位于美国每个州的零售商购买。

该州立法机关正在考虑通过一项法律，该法律将仅对 Widgets 的制造征收税款。该税款将按其批发价值的 3% 计算。
ask: Which of the following arguments would be LEAST helpful to the state in defending the constitutionality of this proposed state tax on widgets?
askZh: 下列哪一项论据最无助于该州为拟议中的小商品税的合宪性辩护？

options.en: A tax on the manufacture of widgets may be imposed only by the state in which the manufacturing occurs and, therefore, it is not likely to create the danger of a multiple tax burden on interstate commerce.
options.zh: 仅对 Widgets 的制造征税，只能由制造发生地的州进行，因此，这种税款不太可能对州际商业造成多重税款负担。

options.en: At the time widgets are manufactured and taxed they have not yet entered the channels of interstate commerce.
options.zh: 在 Widgets 被制造并征税时，它们尚未进入州际商业的渠道。

options.en: Because of the powers reserved to them by the Tenth Amendment, states have plenary authority to construct their tax system in any manner they choose.
options.zh: 由于第十修正案所保留给各州的权力，各州有权以任何方式构建其税收体系。

options.en: The economic impact of this tax will be passed on to both in-state and out-of-state purchasers of widgets and, therefore, the tax is wholly nondiscriminatory in its effect.
options.zh: 该税款的经济影响将转嫁给 Widgets 的在州内和州外购买者，因此，该税款在效果上是完全非歧视性的。

explanation.en:
State taxation of interstate commerce

(Complete Auto test)

State tax on interstate commerce valid if tax:

• applied to person or activity with substantial nexus to state

• fairly apportioned to avoid taxing interstate activities performed in other states

• does not discriminate against interstate commerce AND

• fairly related to services & benefits provided by state Under the Tenth Amendment, any power that the Constitution does not expressly grant to the federal government—including the power to construct a state tax system—is reserved to the states. But here, this is the least helpful argument for the state because this power is not plenary (ie, absolute). Instead, states must comply with other constitutional provisions. For example, a state tax on interstate commerce (as seen here) must comply with the dormant commerce clause and is only valid if it:

• is applied to persons or activities with a substantial nexus to the state—eg, widgets manufactured from raw materials mined and processed in the state

• is fairly apportioned to avoid taxing interstate activities performed in other states and thereby imposing multiple tax burdens—eg, tax imposed only in state where manufacturing occurs (Choice A), tax applied before widgets enter channels of interstate commerce (Choice B)

• does not discriminate by favoring in-state over out-of-state entities—eg, economic impact passed on to both in-state and out-of-state purchasers (Choice D) and

• is fairly related (ie, reasonable compared) to services and benefits provided by the state—eg, police protection, public roads.

Educational objective:

Under the dormant commerce clause, states cannot tax interstate commerce unless the tax is (1) levied on persons or activities that have a substantial nexus with the state, (2) fairly apportioned, (3) nondiscriminatory, and (4) fairly related to state-provided services or benefits.

References

• Complete Auto Transit, Inc. v. Brady, 430 U.S. 274, 279 (1977) (setting forth the four-factor test used to determine if a state tax violates the commerce clause).

• 71 Am. Jur. 2d State and Local Taxation § 157 (2019) (explaining how state taxation cannot unduly burden interstate commerce).

对州际商业的国家征税

(完成自动测试)

州际商务税有效,如果:

• 适用于与国家有重大关系的个人或活动

• 公平分摊,以避免对在其他国家进行的国家间活动征税

• 不歧视州际商业和

• 与国家根据第十修正案提供的服务和福利有相当关系的任何权力《宪法》没有明确赋予联邦政府包括建设权力州税制度——保留给各州。但在此,这是国家最没有帮助的论点,因为这一权力不是全会(即绝对 ) 。 相反,国家必须遵守其他宪法规定。例如,州际商务税(如此处所示)必须遵守休眠商务条款,并且只有在下述情况下才有效:

• 适用于与国家有重大关系的人或活动,例如用国家开采和加工的原材料制造的部件

• 公平分摊,以避免对在其他国家从事的州际活动征税,从而造成多重税务负担——例如,仅在制造业(选择A州)征税,在部件进入州际商业渠道之前征税(选择B)

• 不因州内实体优于州外实体而有所歧视,例如,给州内和州外购买者带来的经济影响(选择D)和

· 与国家提供的服务和福利(例如警察保护、公共道路)相当相关(即比较合理)。

学习要点：

根据休眠商业条款,国家不得对州际商业征税,除非(1) 对与国家有重大关系的个人或活动征税,(2) 合理分摊,(3) 不歧视,(4) 与国家提供的服务有公平关系。或福利。

• 71 Am. Jur. 2d 国家和地方税务第157条(2019年)(解释国家税务如何不能给州际商务造成不适当的负担)。

stem:
Congressional hearings determined that the use of mechanical power hammers is very dangerous to the persons using them and to persons in the vicinity of the persons using them. As a result, Congress enacted a statute prohibiting the use of mechanical power hammers on all construction projects in the United States.

Subsequently, a study conducted by a private research firm concluded that nails driven by mechanical power hammers have longer-lasting joining power than hand-driven nails. After learning about this study, a city council enacted an amendment to its building safety code requiring the use of mechanical power hammers in the construction of all buildings intended for human habitation.
stemZh:
国会听证会确定，使用机械动力锤对使用它们的人以及在使用这些人的附近的人非常危险。因此，国会通过了一项禁止在美国所有建筑项目中使用机械动力锤的法律。

随后，一家私人研究机构进行的一项研究得出结论，由机械动力锤驱动的钉子比手工驱动的钉子具有更持久的连接力。在了解到这项研究后，一个市议会通过了一项对其建筑安全法规的修正案，要求在所有用于人类居住的建筑物的建设中使用机械动力锤。
ask: Is this amendment to the city's building safety code constitutional?
askZh: 该市建筑安全法规的修正案是否符合宪法？

options.en: No, because it conflicts with the provisions of the federal statute.
options.zh: 否，因为它与联邦法律的规定相冲突。

options.en: No, because it was enacted subsequent to the federal statute.
options.zh: 否，因为它是在联邦法律之后颁布的。

options.en: Yes, because the federal statute does not expressly indicate that it supersedes inconsistent state or local laws.
options.zh: 是，因为联邦法律并未明确表示它要取代不一致的州或地方法律。

options.en: Yes, because the long-term safety of human habitations justifies some additional risk to the people engaged in their construction.
options.zh: 是，因为人类居住建筑的长期安全合理地证明了一些对参与其建设的人的额外风险。

explanation.en:
It is common for the federal government to regulate the same subject matter as states and/or municipalities because these governments share many of the same powers. But under the supremacy clause, federal law is the supreme law of the land. Therefore, a federal law can preempt (ie, supersede) conflicting state or municipal laws and render them void. One example is implied conflict preemption, which occurs when there is:

• direct conflict – a state/municipal law conflicts with a federal law to such a degree that it is impossible (or nearly impossible) for a person or entity to comply with both laws or

• indirect conflict – a state/municipal law frustrates the accomplishment of the federal law's purpose.

Here, the federal statute prohibits the use of mechanized hammers on all construction projects. But the city council amendment requires the use of such hammers on all construction projects for human habitation. These laws directly conflict since it is impossible for a company constructing human habitations in the city to comply with both laws. Therefore, the federal statute impliedly preempts the city council amendment and renders it unconstitutional.

(Choice B) In determining preemption, the timing of the laws is irrelevant. Therefore, it makes no difference whether the city council enacted the amendment before or after the federal statute.

(Choice C) Although the federal statute does not expressly state that it supersedes inconsistent state or local laws, it impliedly preempts them.

(Choice D) Federal laws always preempt inconsistent state and local laws—regardless of their justification.

Educational objective:

Implied conflict preemption exists when (1) it is impossible to comply with a federal law and a conflicting state/municipal law (ie, direct conflict) or (2) a state/municipal law frustrates the accomplishment of a federal law's purpose (ie, indirect conflict).

References

• English v. Gen. Elec. Co., 496 U.S. 72, 79 (1990) (stating that federal law preempts state law when "it is impossible for a private party to comply with both state and federal requirements").

• 16A Am. Jur. 2d Constitutional Law § 235 (2019) (explaining when federal and state laws conflict).

explanation.zh:
联邦政府通常对州和/或市的同一主题事项进行管理,因为这些政府拥有许多相同的权力。 但根据至高无上的条款,联邦法律是国家的最高法律。因此,联邦法可以预先(即取代)冲突州法或市政法,使其无效。 一个例子是隐含冲突先决,这发生在:

• 直接冲突 -- -- 州/市法与联邦法发生冲突,以致个人或实体不可能(或几乎不可能)遵守这两项法律,或

• 间接冲突——州/市法律阻碍联邦法律宗旨的实现。

在这里,联邦法规禁止在所有建筑项目中使用机械化锤子,但市议会修正案要求在所有人类居住建筑项目中使用这种锤子.这些法律直接冲突,因为一家在城市建造人类住宅的公司不可能遵守这两项法律,因此,联邦法规隐含地先于市议会修正案,使其违宪。

(Choice B)在确定先发制人时,法律的时机无关紧要,因此,无论是市议会在联邦法规之前还是之后颁布修正案都无关紧要.

(C选择)虽然联邦法规没有明确规定它取代不一致的州法律或地方法律,但暗示它先发制人.

(Choice D) 联邦法律总是预先防止州和地方法律不一致——不管其理由为何。

学习要点：

当(1) 无法遵守联邦法和相互冲突的州/市法(即直接冲突)或(2) 州/市法阻碍实现联邦法的目的(即间接冲突)时,便存在预设的冲突。

参考资料

• English v. Gen. Elec. Co., 496 U.S.72,79(1990年)(规定联邦法在"私人一方不可能遵守州和联邦的要求"时先于州法).

• 16A Am. Jur. 2d 宪法第235条(2019年)(解释联邦和州法律冲突时的情况)。

stem: A federal statute requires all owners of mineral springs to pay a sales tax on the mineral water they sell. A state that sells mineral water from the springs that it owns has refused to pay the tax. The United States has sued the state in federal court, seeking payment of the tax. The state has moved to dismiss the action.
stemZh: 联邦法规要求所有矿泉水所有者对其出售的矿泉水缴纳销售税,一个从它拥有的矿泉水销售矿泉水的州拒绝缴纳该税.美国在联邦法院起诉该州,要求支付税款,该州已采取行动驳回诉讼.
ask: Is the court likely to dismiss the action?
askZh: 法院是否可能驳回诉讼?

options.en: No, because Congress has unlimited power to tax and spend for the general welfare.
options.zh: 不,因为国会拥有无限的征税和为一般福利花钱的权力.

options.en: No, because the nondiscriminatory tax does not interfere with the essential functions of state government.
options.zh: 不,因为不歧视税并不妨碍国家政府的基本职能。

options.en: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits states from being sued in federal court without the state's consent.
options.zh: 是的,因为第十一修正案禁止州未经州同意在联邦法院起诉.

options.en: Yes, because the Tenth Amendment grants states immunity from all direct federal taxation.
options.zh: 是的,因为第十个修正案 授予了所有联邦直接税的豁免。

explanation.en:
Federalism

(power distribution between federal & state governments)

Constitutional provision

Effect

Article VI supremacy clause

• Prioritizes U.S. Constitution, treaties & federal laws over state constitutions & laws

• Prohibits states from regulating/taxing federal government or its agencies/instrumentalities Tenth Amendment • Reserves all powers not assigned to federal government by U.S. Constitution to states/people

• Prohibits federal government from requiring states to enact laws or enforce federal laws

• Immunizes states from federal taxes that discriminate against states or unduly interfere with essential state functions Article I grants Congress the broad power to tax and spend for the general welfare. But this power is not unlimited (Choice A). Under the Tenth Amendment, Congress is prohibited from imposing federal taxes on states that:

• discriminate against states because the taxes apply to states and their agencies but not private individuals or entities or

• would unduly interfere with the states' essential functions, including property used for or income received from the state's performance of traditional government actions (eg, public schools, state parks).

However, the Tenth Amendment does not immunize states from nondiscriminatory federal taxes that apply to the public and private sectors and do not interfere with essential state functions (Choice D).

Here, the federal sales tax is nondiscriminatory since it applies to all private and public owners of mineral springs who sell mineral water. The tax also does not unduly interfere with essential state functions because selling mineral water (or any other product) is a business action—not a traditional government action. As a result, the Tenth Amendment does not immunize the state from the tax, so the court is not likely to dismiss the action.

(Choice C) The Eleventh Amendment generally prohibits private parties and foreign governments from suing a state in federal court without the state's consent. However, this amendment does not bar actions brought by the United States (as seen here).

Educational objective:

The Tenth Amendment immunizes states from federal taxes that discriminate against states or unduly interfere with essential state functions.

References

• New York v. United States, 326 U.S. 572, 582 (1946) (holding that a state is not immune from a nondiscriminatory federal tax that does not interfere with essential state functions).

explanation.zh:
联邦制

(联邦和州政府之间的权力分配)

宪法规定

效果

第六条 至上条款

• 将美国宪法、条约和联邦法律置于州宪法和法律之上

• 禁止各州管理/向联邦政府或其机构/机构征税• 保留美国未赋予联邦政府的所有权力。州/人民宪法

• 禁止联邦政府要求各州颁布法律或执行联邦法律

• 对各州实行联邦税的豁免,这些联邦税歧视各州或不适当地干预基本的国家职能 第一条赋予国会征税和为一般福利开支的广泛权力。 但这种权力并非无限的(选择A)。根据第十修正案,禁止对下列各州征收联邦税:

• 歧视国家,因为税收适用于国家及其机构,但不适用于私人个人或实体;

• 将不适当地干预州的基本职能,包括用于州执行传统政府行动(如公立学校、州立公园)的财产或收入。

然而,第十修正案并没有使各州免受适用于公共和私营部门且不干涉基本国家职能的非歧视性联邦税(Choice D).

在这方面,联邦销售税是非歧视性的,因为它适用于所有出售矿泉水的私人和公共所有者。税收也没有不适当地干预国家的基本职能,因为出售矿泉水(或任何其他产品)是一种商业行动,而不是传统的政府行动。因此,第十修正案没有将该州从税收中免疫,因此法院不可能驳回诉讼.

(C选择)第十一修正案一般禁止私人政党和外国政府未经该州同意而向联邦法院起诉某州,然而,该修正案并不禁止美国提起的诉讼(如本文所示).

学习要点：

第十修正案对各州实行联邦税的免疫,这些税项歧视各州或不适当地干预基本的国家职能.

参考资料

• 纽约诉美国案,326 U.S. 572, 582(1946)(认为国家不能免于不歧视的联邦税,这种税不干预国家的基本职能)。

stem:
The legislatures of several states entered into an agreement in which each state pledged to curb its pollution emissions. The agreement authorized a commission that contained a representative of each state to investigate how the states could reach their pollution emission goals and propose solutions for the states to adopt. The commission determined that each state needed to commit a fixed percentage of its energy consumption to clean energy sources, and each state enacted legislation that implemented the commission's suggestion. As a result, the states' demand for electricity produced by a company that uses coal-burning plants has significantly declined.

The company has filed suit against the commission in a federal district court, seeking a declaratory judgment that the states' agreement is unconstitutional.

Assume that no federal statute applies.
stemZh:
多个州的立法机构达成了一项协议，其中每个州承诺减少其污染排放。该协议授权一个委员会，该委员会由每个州的代表组成，调查各州如何实现其污染排放目标，并提出解决方案供各州采用。委员会确定，每个州需要将其能源消耗的固定百分比用于清洁能源来源，各州随后通过立法实施了委员会的建议。因此，各州对使用燃煤发电的公司生产的电力的需求显著下降。

该公司在联邦地区法院提起诉讼，要求宣告各州的协议违宪。

假设没有适用的联邦法律。
ask: What action should the federal court take?
askZh: 联邦法院应采取什么行动？

options.en: Dismiss the suit without reaching the merits, because the Eleventh Amendment bars suits of this kind in federal court.
options.zh: 在不涉及实质问题的情况下驳回诉讼，因为第十一修正案禁止联邦法院受理此类诉讼。

options.en: Dismiss the suit without reaching the merits, because the suit presents a nonjusticiable political question.
options.zh: 在不涉及实质问题的情况下驳回诉讼，因为该诉讼提出了一个不可裁判的政治问题。

options.en: Invalidate the states' agreement, because the states failed to obtain congressional consent.
options.zh: 推翻各州的协议，因为各州未能获得国会的同意。

options.en: Uphold the states' agreement, because the states validly entered into an interstate compact.
options.zh: 维持各州的协议，因为各州合法地缔结了一个州际协议。

explanation.en:
Congressional consent for interstate compacts

Required States' political power increased at federal government's expense—eg, states:

• cede territory to each other

• exercise powers they cannot exercise on own Not required

States do not encroach on federal government supremacy—eg, states:

• enact reciprocal legislation for benefit of each state's residents (eg, state college tuition reciprocity)

• form administrative body to study joint problems and make recommendations

• create entity to operate transportation facility (eg, port authority) States generally may enter into agreements with each other (ie, interstates compacts) without permission from the federal government.* However, the compact clause requires that states obtain Congress's consent for interstate compacts that increase the compacting states' political power at the expense of the federal government. This situation arises when the compact grants states or an administrative body powers that they could not exercise on their own.

Here, several states entered into an interstate compact to curb pollution emissions and created a commission that suggested that each state commit a fixed percentage of its energy consumption to clean energy sources. Each state did so. Since each state could have adopted energy guidelines without the commission's suggestion, the compact does not grant power to the states at the expense of the federal government. As a result, congressional consent was not required, and the federal court is likely to uphold the states' agreement (Choice C).

*The compact clause also permits states to enter into agreements with foreign governments if Congress consents.

(Choice A) The Eleventh Amendment generally bars suits in federal court against state governments. However, it does not prohibit suits against commissions created by interstate compacts (as seen here).

(Choice B) The political-question doctrine prevents federal courts from hearing the merits of suits that present issues that (1) are reserved to the executive or legislative branch or (2) lack judicially manageable standards for resolution—neither of which are seen here.

Educational objective:

The compact clause requires states to obtain Congress's consent for agreements between the states (ie, interstate compacts) that increase the political power of the compacting states at the expense of the federal government.

References

• U.S. Const. art. I, § 10, cl. 3 (compact clause).

• U.S. Steel Corp. v. Multistate Tax Comm'n, 434 U.S. 452, 473–76 (1978) (holding that congressional consent was not required when an interstate compact granted powers that compacting states could exercise on their own).

• 72 Am. Jur. 2d States, Territories, and Dependencies § 10 (2020) (explaining when congressional consent is required for an interstate compact).

explanation.zh:
国会同意州际契约

要求的州的政治权力由联邦政府出资增加,例如:

• 相互割让领土

• 行使他们不能自行行使的权力

各州并不侵犯联邦政府的至高无上地位,

• 为各州居民制定互惠立法(如州立大学学费互惠)

• 组建行政机构,研究共同问题并提出建议

• 设立实体来经营运输设施(例如港务局) 国家一般可以进入未经联邦许可,相互订立协定(即州际契约)* 然而,契约条款要求国家获得:国会同意州际契约,增加州际契约的政治权力,而牺牲联邦政府的利益。 当契约授予州或行政机构权力时,就出现了这种情况,而州或行政机构不能单独行使权力。

在此,几个州订立了限制污染排放的州际契约,并成立了一个委员会,建议各州将能源消耗的固定百分比用于清洁能源。由于每个州都可以在没有委员会建议的情况下通过能源准则,因此契约不以联邦政府为代价授予各州权力.因此,不需要国会同意,联邦法院很可能支持各州的协议(Choice C).

* 契约条款还允许各国与外国政府达成协议,如果国会同意。

(Choice A)第十一修正案一般禁止联邦法院对州政府提起诉讼,但并不禁止对州际契约设立的委员会提起诉讼(参见本文).

(Choice B) 政治问题理论使联邦法院无法审理提出(1) 保留给行政部门或立法部门或(2) 缺乏司法上可管理解决标准的问题的诉讼的案情。在这里。

学习要点：

契约条款要求各州在各州之间的协议(即州际契约)中以联邦政府为代价增加契约州的政治权力时,获得国会的同意.

参考资料

• 《美国法典》第1条第10款,第3项(契约条款)。

· 美国钢铁公司诉多国税务委员会案,434 U.S. 452、473-76(1978年)(认为当国家间契约授予契约国可以自行行使的权力时,不需要国会同意)。

• 72 Am. Jur. 2d州、领土和属地§10(2020年)(解释州际契约何时需要国会同意)。

stem:
A federal statute with inseverable provisions established a new five-member National Prosperity Board with broad regulatory powers over the operation of the securities, banking, and commodities industries, including the power to issue rules with the force of law. The statute provides for three of the board members to be appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate. They serve seven-year terms and are removable only for good cause. The other two members of the board were designated in the statute to be the respective general counsel of the Senate and House of Representatives Committees on Government Operations. The statute stipulated that they were to serve on the board for as long as they continued in those positions.

Following all required administrative procedures, the board issued an elaborate set of rules regulating the operations of all banks, securities dealers, and commodities brokers. A securities company, which was subject to the board's rules, sought a declaratory judgment that the rules were invalid because the statute establishing the board was unconstitutional.
stemZh:
一项包含不可分割条款的联邦法律设立了一个新的五人国家繁荣委员会，该委员会对证券、银行和商品行业的运营拥有广泛的监管权力，包括颁布具有法律效力规则的权力。该法律规定，该委员会的三名成员由总统在参议院的建议和同意下任命。他们任期为七年，只有在有充分理由时才可被解除职务。该委员会的另外两名成员在法律中被指定为参议院和众议院政府运作委员会的总法律顾问。法律规定，他们将在担任这些职务期间继续担任委员会成员。

在完成所有必要的行政程序后，该委员会颁布了一套详细的规则，规范所有银行、证券商和商品经纪人的运营。一家受该委员会规则约束的证券公司寻求宣告判决，认为这些规则无效，因为设立该委员会的法律是违宪的。
ask: In this case, should the court rule that the statute establishing the National Prosperity Board is constitutional?
askZh: 在这个案件中，法院应裁定设立国家繁荣委员会的法律是否合宪？

options.en: No, because all members of federal boards exercising executive powers must be appointed by the President or in a manner otherwise consistent with the appointments clause of Article II.
options.zh: 否，因为所有行使行政权力的联邦委员会成员必须由总统任命或以其他方式符合《第二条》的任命条款。

options.en: No, because all members of federal boards having broad powers that are quasi-legislative in nature, such as rulemaking, must be appointed by Congress.
options.zh: 否，因为所有拥有广泛权力的联邦委员会成员，尤其是具有准立法性质的权力（如规则制定），必须由国会任命。

options.en: Yes, because the necessary and proper clause authorizes Congress to determine the means by which members are appointed to boards created by Congress under its power to regulate commerce among the states.
options.zh: 是，因为《必要和适当条款》授权国会确定由国会根据其对州间商业的监管权力所设立的委员会成员的任命方式。

options.en: Yes, because there is a substantial nexus between the power of Congress to legislate for the general welfare and the means specified by Congress in this statute for the appointment of board members.
options.zh: 是，因为国会拥有对一般福利进行立法的权力，且该法律中规定的委员会成员任命方式与该权力存在实质性联系。

explanation.en:
Appointment of federal officers

(Art. II, § 2 appointments clause)

Type Examples Appointment

Principal • Ambassador

• Supreme Court justice

• Cabinet official

Appointed by President (with Senate approval)

Inferior • Independent counsel

• Judicial clerk

• Administrative law judge

Appointed by President (with Senate approval) unless Congress delegates appointment to:

• President alone

• federal courts or

• heads of executive departments Federal officers are persons who:

• hold a continuing public office (eg, for a term of years) and

• have significant discretionary authority to administer and/or enforce laws (ie, executive powers). All federal officers must be appointed by the President or in a manner otherwise consistent with the Article II appointments clause. Under this clause, Congress cannot appoint federal officers.

Here, the National Prosperity Board comprises three members who serve seven-year terms and two who serve indefinitely—all of whom hold a continuing public office. And they all exercise executive powers since they have significant discretionary authority to issue rules with the force of law. As a result, they are federal officers who must be appointed by the President or in a manner otherwise consistent with the appointments clause. And since the applicable statute allows Congress to appoint two members, it is unconstitutional.

(Choice B) Congress may appoint persons to exercise quasi-legislative powers that are investigative or informative in nature. But in Buckley v. Valeo, the Supreme Court held that rulemaking is an administrative power that can only be exercised by federal officers (who can never be appointed by Congress).

(Choice C) The necessary and proper clause authorizes Congress to enact laws that are reasonably appropriate to carry out its express powers—including the power to regulate commerce among the states. But Congress cannot violate other constitutional provisions when doing so.

(Choice D) Article I, section 8 grants Congress the power to tax and spend for the general welfare. But Congress is not taxing or spending here, so this power does not apply.

Educational objective:

Federal officers are persons who hold a continuing public office AND have significant discretionary authority to administer and/or enforce laws (ie, executive powers). They can only be appointed by the President or in a manner otherwise consistent with the Article II appointments clause—never by Congress.

References

• Buckley v. Valeo, 424 U.S. 1, 132–33 (1976) (holding that federal officers must be appointed by the President or in a manner consistent with the appointments clause, which does not allow congressional appointments).

• Lucia v. SEC, 138 S. Ct. 2044, 2053 (2018) (describing the requirements for a federal officer).

任命联邦官员

(第二条第2款任命条款)

类型示例

• 校长

由总统任命(经参议院批准)

由总统任命(经参议院批准),除非国会代表任命:

• 行政部门负责人是下列人员:

• 继续担任公职(例如,任期数年);

• 拥有管理和(或)执行法律的重大自由裁量权(即行政权力),所有联邦官员必须由总统任命或以与第二条任命条款一致的方式任命。根据该条款,国会不能任命联邦官员.

在这方面,国家繁荣委员会由3名成员组成,任期7年,2人无限期任职,他们都继续担任公职。他们都行使行政权力,因为他们拥有颁布具有法律效力的规则的重大酌处权。因此,他们是联邦官员,必须由总统任命,或以与任命条款一致的方式任命,而且由于适用的法规允许国会任命两名议员,这不符合宪法。

(Choice B) 国会可以任命人员行使具有调查或信息性质的准立法权力。Valeo),最高法院认为制定规则是一种行政权力,只能由联邦官员行使(他们永远不能由国会任命).

(C) 必要和适当的条款授权国会颁布合理适合行使其明确权力的法律,包括管理各州间商业的权力。但国会在这样做时不能违反其他宪法规定.

(Choice D) 第一条第八节赋予国会征税和为一般福利支出的权力。 但国会在此不征税或支出,因此这一权力不适用。

学习要点：

联邦官员是继续担任公职的人,拥有管理和(或)执行法律的重大酌处权(即行政权力)。他们只能由总统任命,或以与第二条任命条款不符的方式任命,而不是由国会任命。

参考资料

· Buckley诉Valeo案,424 U.S. 1, 132–33 (1976)(认为联邦官员必须由总统任命,或以符合不允许国会任命的任命条款的方式任命)。

• Lucia诉SEC,138 S. Ct. 2044, 2053 (2018)(说明对联邦官员的要求)。

stem: A drawbridge owned, operated, and maintained by a county government malfunctioned. A portion of the drawbridge fell and collided with a boat owned by a man who resides in another state. The man filed a lawsuit against the county in a federal district court to recover for the damage caused to his boat. The county has moved to dismiss the suit.
stemZh: 一座由县政府拥有、运营和维护的吊桥发生故障。吊桥的一部分掉落并撞到了一艘由另一州居民拥有的船只。该男子在联邦地区法院对县提起诉讼，要求赔偿其船只的损失。县提出了驳回诉讼动议。
ask: Is the court likely to grant the county's motion?
askZh: 法院很可能批准县的动议吗？

options.en: No.
options.zh: 否。

options.en: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits suits against county governments in federal court.
options.zh: 是，因为第十一修正案禁止在联邦法院对县政府提起诉讼。

options.en: Yes, because the Tenth Amendment gives state courts exclusive jurisdiction over suits against state, county, and municipal governments.
options.zh: 是，因为第十修正案赋予州法院对针对州、县和市镇政府的诉讼的专属管辖权。

options.en: Yes, because the U.S. Supreme Court has original and exclusive jurisdiction over suits against governments.
options.zh: 是，因为美国最高法院对针对政府的诉讼拥有原始且专属的管辖权。

explanation.en:
Eleventh Amendment

(state immunity from suit in federal court)

Immunity • Suit brought by private party or foreign government

• Suit against state official violating state law

• Exceptions: – State consents to suit – Immunity removed by 13th, 14th, or 15th Amendment – State official sued for injunctive or declaratory relief – Damages to be paid by state officer personally (not state treasury) – State official sued for prospective (not retroactive) damages to be paid by state treasury No immunity

• Suit brought by United States or other state

• Suit against local government (eg, counties, municipalities)

• Bankruptcy proceedings The Eleventh Amendment prohibits foreign governments and private parties from suing a state in federal court without the state's consent. However, this immunity does not extend to actions brought against local governments (eg, municipalities, counties). Therefore, the Eleventh Amendment does not apply to the man's suit against the county, and the federal court will likely deny the county's motion to dismiss (Choice B).

(Choice C) The Tenth Amendment reserves to the states all powers that the Constitution does not expressly grant to the federal government. However, it does not give state courts exclusive jurisdiction over suits against state, county, and municipal governments. Instead, state and federal courts have concurrent jurisdiction over such suits.

(Choice D) The U.S. Supreme Court has original jurisdiction over cases that affect ambassadors, public ministers, or consuls OR that involve a state as a party (neither seen here). Additionally, the Supreme Court has exclusive jurisdiction over suits between states (also not seen here).

Educational objective:

The Eleventh Amendment bars suits against state governments in federal court. However, this immunity does not extend to suits against local governments (eg, counties, municipalities).

References

• N. Ins. Co. v. Chatham County, 547 U.S. 189, 193–95 (2006) (holding that the Eleventh Amendment does not prohibit suits against local governments).

• 32A Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 918 (2020) (explaining that the Eleventh Amendment does not bar suits against local governments in federal court).

explanation.zh:
第十一次修正

(国家豁免联邦法院的诉讼)

• 私人或外国政府提出的诉讼

• 对违反州法律的国家官员提起诉讼

• 例外:- 国家同意诉 - 第13、14或15修正案取消豁免 - 国家官员被起诉要求强制或宣告性救济 - 国家官员个人(不是国库)应支付的损害 - 国家官员被起诉预期(不是)国家财政应支付的赔偿

• 美国或其他国家提出的诉讼

• 起诉地方政府(例如县、市)

• 破产程序 第十一修正案禁止外国政府和私人当事方未经州同意向联邦法院起诉州。然而,这种豁免并不适用于对地方政府(如市、县)提起的诉讼。因此,第十一修正案不适用于该男子对县的诉讼,联邦法院很可能驳回该县的驳回动议(Choice B).

(Choice)第十修正案将宪法未明确授予联邦政府的所有权力保留给各州,然而,它并没有赋予各州法院针对州、县和市政府的诉讼的专属管辖权。相反,州法院和联邦法院对此类诉讼拥有共同管辖权。

(Choice D) 美国最高法院对影响大使,公使,或领事或涉及国家为一方的案件拥有原审管辖权(这里都看不到).此外,最高法院对州与州之间的诉讼拥有专属管辖权(这里也不见)。

学习要点：

第十一修正案禁止在联邦法院对州政府提起诉讼,但这种豁免不适用于对地方政府(如县,市)提起的诉讼.

参考资料

• N. Ins. Co. v. Chatham County, 547 U.S.189, 193–95(2006年)(认为第十一修正案不禁止对地方政府提起诉讼)。

• 32A Am. Jur. 2d联邦法院§918(2020年)(解释第十一修正案并不禁止在联邦法院对地方政府提起诉讼)。

stem: A state law that restricted access to contraception was challenged in state court as a violation of the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution and as a violation of a similar due process provision of the state constitution. The case made its way to the state's highest court, which ruled that the law violated the due process provisions of both the U.S. and the state constitutions.
stemZh: 一项限制获取避孕药具的州法律在州法院被挑战，指控其违反了美国宪法第十四修正案的正当程序条款以及州宪法中类似的正当程序条款。该案最终上诉至该州最高法院，该法院裁定该法律违反了美国宪法和州宪法的正当程序条款。
ask: If petitioned to do so, may the U.S. Supreme Court exercise jurisdiction to review the state court decision?
askZh: 如果请求这样做，美国最高法院是否有权审理该州法院的裁决？

options.en: No, because the state court's decision in this case rests on adequate and independent state law grounds.
options.zh: 否，因为本案中州法院的裁决是基于充分且独立的州法律依据。

options.en: No, because the U.S. Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction only over state court decisions that determine the constitutionality of federal laws.
options.zh: 否，因为美国最高法院仅对确定联邦法律合宪性的州法院裁决拥有上诉管辖权。

options.en: Yes, because the U.S. Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction over any ruling of a state's highest court based on an interpretation of federal law.
options.zh: 是，因为美国最高法院对任何基于解释联邦法律的州最高法院裁决拥有上诉管辖权。

options.en: Yes, because the U.S. Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction over decisions that find state laws in violation of the federal Constitution.
options.zh: 是，因为美国最高法院对裁定州法律违反联邦宪法的裁决拥有上诉管辖权。

explanation.en:
Appellate jurisdiction of SCOTUS

Type of review Applicability

Certiorari

(discretionary review)

• Appeal from lower federal court or highest state court by filing petition for writ of certiorari

• SCOTUS will review if ≥ 4 Justices vote to accept appeal

• Very common – how most cases come before SCOTUS Direct appeal

(mandatory review)

• Appeal from decision on injunction by special three-judge federal district court panel

• Extremely rare – limited to cases brought under specific statutes (eg, Voting Rights Act) SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States

The U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has discretionary jurisdiction to review final state court decisions that involve federal law. But SCOTUS cannot exercise jurisdiction to review those decisions if they rest on adequate and independent state grounds—ie, when:

• state law completely resolves the matter such that the application of federal law would not affect the outcome of the case (adequate) and

• the state court did not rely on federal law to decide the state law issue (independent).

This limit on SCOTUS's jurisdiction promotes judicial economy by barring SCOTUS from deciding a federal question when it would not change the outcome of the case.

Here, the highest state court's ruling rests on an adequate state ground because the court found the law invalid under the state constitution. So even if SCOTUS reversed the state court's ruling on the U.S. Constitution, the law would still violate the state constitution and the outcome of the case would remain the same. The ruling also rests on an independent state ground because the state court did not rely on federal law in ruling on the similar state constitutional issue.* As a result, SCOTUS may not exercise jurisdiction to review the state court decision.

*A state court ruling is not independent if the state court relied on an "identical" federal provision to rule on the state provision. Here, the federal and state due process provisions are similar but not the same, so the ruling rests on an independent state ground.

(Choice B) SCOTUS has appellate jurisdiction over state court decisions determining the constitutionality of federal laws AND the validity of state laws under the U.S. Constitution.

(Choices C & D) SCOTUS has appellate jurisdiction over state court decisions based on federal law—including decisions that find state laws in violation of the federal constitution—unless that decision rests on adequate and independent state grounds.

Educational objective:

The U.S. Supreme Court has no jurisdiction to review state court decisions based on adequate and independent state grounds—ie, when state grounds completely resolve the matter and the court does not rely on federal law to reach that decision.

References

• Michigan v. Long, 463 U.S. 1032, 1041 (1983) (explaining when a state supreme court judgment rests on adequate and independent state grounds).

explanation.zh:
SCOTUS的上诉管辖权

审查类型

塞尔蒂奥拉里

(酌审).

• 联邦下级法院或州级最高法院提出上诉,提出诉讼令状

• 如果有4名法官投票接受上诉,SCOTUS将进行审查。

• 非常常见——大多数案件是如何提交SCOTUS直接上诉的

(强制性审查)

• 联邦地区法院特别法官小组就禁令的裁决提出上诉

• 极为罕见——仅限于根据具体法规(如投票权法)提起的案件 SCOTUS = 美国最高法院

美国最高法院(SCOTUS)拥有审查涉及联邦法律的州法院最终裁决的裁量权。 但SCOTUS不能行使审查这些裁决的管辖权,如果这些裁决基于充分和独立的国家理由——即:

• 州法律完全解决了问题,联邦法律的适用不会影响案件的结果(充分)和

• 州法院没有依靠联邦法律来裁定州法律问题(独立)。

对SCOTUS管辖权的这一限制促进了司法经济,阻止SCOTUS在不会改变案件结果时决定联邦问题。

因此,即使SCOTUS推翻了州法院对美国的裁决。 州最高法院的裁决基于充足的州理由,因为法院根据州宪法认定法律无效。宪法,法律仍会违反州宪法和结果案件将保持不变。裁决还基于一个独立的州理由,因为州法院在就类似的州宪法问题作出裁决时不依赖联邦法律。 * 因此,SCOTUS不得行使对州法院裁决进行审查的管辖权。

* 如果州法院依据一项“相同”的联邦条款对州条款作出裁决,州法院的裁决并不独立。 这里,联邦和州正当程序条款相似,但并不相同,因此裁决基于一个独立的州理由。

(Choice B) SCOTUS对州法院决定联邦法律合宪性以及州法律根据美国宪法的有效性具有上诉管辖权.

(Choices C & D) SCOTUS对基于联邦法律的州法院裁决有上诉管辖权,包括裁定州法律违反联邦宪法的裁决,除非该裁决基于充分和独立的国家理由。

学习要点：

美国最高法院没有管辖权审查州法院基于充分和独立的国家理由作出的裁决,即当州的理由完全解决了这一问题,而法院并不依赖联邦法律来作出这一决定时。

参考资料

• 密歇根州诉Long案,463 U.S. 1032, 1041(1983年)(解释州最高法院何时根据适当和独立的国家理由作出判决)。

stem:
A state legislature recently enacted a statute forbidding public utilities regulated by the State Public Service Commission from increasing their rates more than once every two years.

A public utility company regulated by that commission has just obtained approval from the commission for a general rate increase. The company has routinely filed for a rate increase every 10 to 14 months during the last 20 years. Because of uncertainties about future fuel prices, the company cannot ascertain with any certainty the date when it will need a further rate increase, but it thinks that it may need such an increase sometime within the next 18 months.

The company files an action in the federal district court in the state requesting a declaratory judgment that this new state statute forbidding public utility rate increases more than once every two years is unconstitutional. Assume no federal statute is relevant.
stemZh:
某州立法机关最近颁布一项法律，规定受该州公共事业委员会监管的公用事业公司每两年最多只能上调一次费率。

一家受该委员会监管的公用事业公司刚获准普遍上调费率。过去 20 年，该公司通常每隔 10 至 14 个月就申请一次涨价。由于未来燃料价格不确定，公司无法确切知道何时需要再次涨价，但认为可能在未来 18 个月内提出申请。

公司在该州联邦地区法院起诉，请求法院宣告这项限制公用事业费率上调频次的新州法律违宪。假设没有相关联邦法律。
ask: How should the court rule in this case?
askZh: 法院应该如何裁决此案？

options.en: Dismiss the complaint, because controversies over state-regulated utility rates are outside of the jurisdiction conferred on federal courts by Article III of the Constitution.
options.zh: 驳回起诉，因为关于州监管的公用事业费率的争议超出了宪法第三条授予联邦法院的管辖权。

options.en: Dismiss the complaint, because this action is not ripe for decision.
options.zh: 驳回起诉，因为该诉讼尚不成熟。

options.en: Hold the statute constitutional, because the judgment of a legislature on a matter involving economic regulation is entitled to great deference.
options.zh: 认定该法律合宪，因为立法机关对涉及经济监管事项的判断应受到高度尊重。

options.en: Hold the statute unconstitutional, because such a moratorium on rate increases deprives utilities of their property without due process of law.
options.zh: 认定该法律违宪，因为这种对费率上涨的暂停剥夺了公用事业的财产权，没有正当法律程序。

explanation.en:
Article III, Section 2 of the Constitution allows federal courts to hear cases and controversies that are ripe for adjudication (ie, capable of judicial resolution). This requirement is met when the plaintiff has suffered an actual harm or an immediate threat thereof. But a suit cannot be heard by a federal court if the plaintiff faces the mere possibility of harm (unripe) or the plaintiff's harm is no longer capable of judicial resolution (moot).

Here, the company filed a complaint in federal court requesting a declaratory judgment regarding the new statute limiting rate increases for public utilities to once every two years. But since the company had just obtained approval for a rate increase and merely thinks that it may need another rate increase in the next 18 months, it has suffered no actual harm or immediate threat of harm. Therefore, this action is unripe and should be dismissed.

(Choice A) Article III grants federal courts subject-matter jurisdiction over claims arising under the Constitution, federal laws, or treaties. Therefore, the company's complaint regarding the constitutionality of the new statute falls within the court's conferred jurisdiction and will not be dismissed on this basis.

(Choices C & D) A determination as to whether (1) the court should defer to the legislature's economic judgment or (2) the moratorium is a deprivation of property without due process of law involves the merits of the suit. But since the action is not ripe for adjudication, the court cannot consider the merits and must dismiss the suit.

Educational objective:

Federal courts can only hear cases and controversies that are ripe for adjudication—ie, claims that concern an actual or immediate threat of harm suffered by the plaintiff. Therefore, courts must dismiss claims that allege the mere possibility of harm (unripe) or harm that is no longer capable of judicial resolution (moot).

References

• Texas v. United States, 523 U.S. 296, 300 (1998) (explaining when a claim is unripe for adjudication).

explanation.zh:
《宪法》第3条第2款允许联邦法院审理时机成熟的案件和争议(即能够通过司法途径解决的案件和争议),如果原告遭受了实际伤害或直接受到伤害的威胁,则满足了这一要求。但是,如果原告仅面临伤害(unripe)的可能性,或者原告的伤害不再能够司法解决(moot),则联邦法院不能审理诉讼.

在此,该公司向联邦法院提出申诉,要求就新的法规作出宣告性判决,将公用事业费率的提高限制在每两年一次。但是,由于该公司刚刚获得提高利率的批准,并且仅仅认为在未来18个月里可能需要再提高利率,因此它没有遭受实际伤害或直接的伤害威胁。 因此,这一行动是无效的,应当予以驳回。

(选择A) 第三条赋予联邦法院对宪法、联邦法律或条约引起的索赔的属事管辖权。因此,公司关于新法规合宪性的申诉属于法院赋予的管辖权,不会因此被驳回。

(选择C & D) 决定(1) 法院应服从立法机关的经济判决,还是(2) 暂停是未经正当法律程序剥夺财产,涉及诉讼的案情。但由于诉讼时机尚不成熟,法院不能考虑案情,必须驳回诉讼.

学习要点：

联邦法院只能审理时机已成熟可供裁决的案件和争议,即涉及原告遭受实际或直接损害威胁的索赔。因此,法院必须驳回仅仅声称可能造成损害(unripe)或不再能够司法解决(moot)的损害的申诉。

参考资料

• Texas诉美国案,523 U.S. 296, 300 (1998)(解释一项要求何时不能裁定)。

stem:
A national coalition of activists announced that it would be holding a rally at the Capitol to protest federal laws that criminalize the possession or use of cannabis. The rally has been advertised as a "smoke-in," where the activists would smoke cannabis during the protest.

The President, who has recently announced her support for the decriminalization of recreational cannabis under federal law, does not want any of the activists to face criminal charges for participating in the rally. The President has proposed to grant a group pardon to the activists before the rally begins.
stemZh:
一个全国性的活动人士联盟宣布，它将在国会大厦举行一次集会，抗议联邦法律将大麻的持有或使用定为犯罪。这次集会被宣传为一次"吸烟集会"，活动人士将在抗议期间吸食大麻。

总统最近宣布支持在联邦法律下对娱乐用大麻的非刑事化，她不希望任何活动人士因参加集会而面临刑事指控。总统提议在集会开始前向活动人士授予一组赦免。
ask: May the President constitutionally grant this pardon?
askZh: 总统是否有宪法依据授予这种赦免？

options.en: No, because the President may not grant a pardon before a federal offense has been committed.
options.zh: 否，因为总统在联邦犯罪发生前不能授予赦免。

options.en: No, because the President may not grant a pardon to a group of people.
options.zh: 否，因为总统不能向一组人授予赦免。

options.en: Yes, because the President may grant a pardon for federal offenses.
options.zh: 是，因为总统可以对联邦犯罪授予赦免。

options.en: Yes, because the President's power to pardon is plenary.
options.zh: 是，因为总统的赦免权是完整的。

explanation.en:
Exclusive executive powers

• Nominate principal officers

• Veto bills

• Prosecute & pardon federal offenses

• Communicate & negotiate with foreign governments

• Recognize foreign governments

• Enter executive agreements Article II of the Constitution vests the President with plenary (ie, absolute) power to grant reprieves and pardons to persons or groups of people that have committed federal offenses—except in cases of impeachment (Choices C & D). But the President may grant a pardon only after the federal offense has been committed—not before. Since the President here seeks to grant a group pardon to the activists before they commit a federal offense by smoking cannabis at the rally, she may not constitutionally grant this pardon.

(Choice B) A President may grant a pardon to a group of people who have committed a federal offense. For example, President Carter granted a group pardon to every person who avoided the military draft during the Vietnam War.

Educational objective:

Article II of the Constitution vests the President with plenary power to generally grant pardons to individuals or groups that have committed federal offenses. But a pardon cannot be granted before the federal offense has been committed.

References

• U.S. Const. art. II, § 2, cl. 1 (vesting the President with the power to grant reprieves and pardons).

• Ex Parte Garland, 71 U.S. (4 Wall) 333, 380 (1866) (explaining that a pardon can be granted only after a federal offense has been committed).

explanation.zh:
专属行政权力

• 提名主要官员

• 维托法案

• 起诉和赦免联邦罪行

• 与外国政府交流和谈判

• 承认外国政府

• 加入行政协议 《宪法》第二条赋予总统全体会议(即绝对)权力,对犯下联邦罪行的个人或群体给予缓刑和赦免,但弹劾案件除外(Choices C & D)。但是,总统只有在联邦罪行发生之后才能赦免,而不是在此前。 由于总统试图在活动分子在集会上吸食大麻犯下联邦罪行之前给予他们集体赦免,因此她不能在宪法上这样做。请原谅

(Choice B)总统可以赦免犯下联邦罪的一群人,例如卡特总统对在越南战争期间逃避军事草案的每一个人给予集体赦免.

学习要点：

《宪法》第2条赋予总统以普遍赦免犯下联邦罪行的个人或团体的全权,但在犯下联邦罪行之前不能给予赦免。

参考资料

• Garland,71 U.S.(4墙),333,380(1866)(解释只有在联邦罪行发生后才能赦免)。

stem:
Under the authority of a federal voting rights statute, some states drew congressional districts in a manner calculated to increase the likelihood that members of historically disadvantaged minority racial groups would be elected. The U.S. Supreme Court declared these districts to be unconstitutional, as improper racial gerrymanders.

In response to this ruling, Congress passed a new statute that explicitly denies the Supreme Court appellate jurisdiction over all future cases challenging the constitutionality of action taken under the authority of the federal voting rights statute.
stemZh:
根据一项联邦选举权法的授权，一些州以一种旨在增加历史上处于不利地位的少数族裔群体成员被选举的可能性的方式划分了国会选区。美国最高法院宣布这些选区是违宪的，因为它们构成了不正当的种族画界。

作为对此裁决的回应，国会通过了一项新法案，明确否认最高法院对所有未来挑战根据联邦选举权法授权采取的行动的合宪性的上诉管辖权。
ask: Which of the following is the most persuasive argument for the constitutionality of the new statute restricting the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction?
askZh: 以下哪一项是新法案限制最高法院上诉管辖权合宪性的最有说服力的论点？

options.en: Article III of the Constitution explicitly states that the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction is subject to such exceptions and regulations as Congress shall make.
options.zh: 宪法第三条明确指出，最高法院的上诉管辖权应受国会制定的例外和规章的约束。

options.en: The constitutional principle of separation of powers authorizes Congress to pass statutes calculated to reduce the effects of Supreme Court decisions that interfere with the exercise of powers that have been delegated to the legislative branch.
options.zh: 宪法上的权力分立原则授权国会通过旨在减轻最高法院判决影响的法律，而这些判决妨碍了立法部门行使获授予的权力。

options.en: The establishment and apportionment of congressional districts directly affect interstate commerce, and the Constitution authorizes Congress to use its plenary authority over such commerce for any purpose it believes will promote the general welfare.
options.zh: 国会选区的设立和分配直接影响州际贸易，宪法授权国会使用其对这类贸易的完全权力，以实现其认为有利于公共福利的任何目的。

options.en: The Fifteenth Amendment authorizes Congress to enforce the amendment's voting rights provisions by appropriate legislation, and Congress could reasonably determine that this restriction on the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction is an appropriate means to that end.
options.zh: 第十五修正案授权国会通过适当立法执行该修正案的选举权条款，国会可以合理地认为，对最高法院上诉管辖权的这种限制是实现该目的的适当手段。

explanation.en:
Article III exceptions clause

Congress can modify SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction unless modification would violate:

• separation-of-powers doctrine (eg, by usurping judicial power) or

• other constitutional provisions (eg, violating equal protection clause by only allowing men to appeal) SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States

Appellate jurisdiction is a court's authority to overturn, modify, or affirm another court's decision. The U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has appellate jurisdiction over decisions by (1) lower federal courts and (2) the highest state courts when the decision turns on federal law. But Article III explicitly provides that this jurisdiction is subject to such exceptions and regulations as Congress shall make. Therefore, that is the most persuasive argument supporting the constitutionality of the statute restricting SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction.

(Choice B) The constitutional principle of separation of powers bars each federal government branch from usurping another branch's powers. And since a congressional statute calculated to reduce the effects of SCOTUS decisions may usurp judicial power, this argument does not support the statute's constitutionality.

(Choice C) The Article I commerce clause grants Congress plenary (ie, absolute) authority to regulate activities that, singly or in the aggregate, have a substantial impact on interstate commerce. But since establishing and apportioning congressional districts only has a mild impact on interstate commerce, this argument would fail.

(Choice D) The Fifteenth Amendment authorizes Congress to enact legislation to ensure that the federal and state governments do not deny or abridge the right to vote based on race, color, or previous servitude. But Article III specifically allows Congress to alter SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction, so it provides the more persuasive argument.

Educational objective:

Congress has the power to regulate and make exceptions to the U.S. Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction under Article III of the Constitution.

References

• Ex parte McCardle, 74 U.S. 506, 514 (1869) (establishing that Congress has almost unlimited power to regulate and make exceptions to the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction).

explanation.zh:
第三条例外条款

国会可以修改SCOTUS的上诉管辖权,除非修改会违反:

• 分权原则(例如通过篡夺司法权力)或

• 其他宪法规定(例如,只允许男子上诉,违反了平等保护条款)SCOTUS = 美国最高法院

上诉管辖权是法院推翻、修改或确认另一法院裁决的权力。最高法院(SCOTUS)对(1)联邦下级法院和(2)联邦法裁决时的最高州法院的裁决具有上诉管辖权.但是,第三条明确规定,这种管辖权须遵守国会应制定的例外和条例,因此,这是支持限制SCOTUS上诉管辖权的法规合宪性的最有说服力的论点。

(Choice B)宪法中的三权分立原则阻止了每个联邦政府分支篡夺另一个分支的权力.而由于一项旨在减少SCOTUS决定的影响的国会法规可能会篡夺司法权,这一论点并不支持该法规的合宪性.

(C选择) 第一条商业条款赋予国会全体会议(即绝对)权力来管制那些单独或从总体上对州际商务有重大影响的活动.但是由于建立和划分国会区只对州际商务产生轻微影响,这一论点将失败.

(Choice D) 第十五修正案授权国会颁布立法,以确保联邦和州政府不因种族,肤色,或以前的劳役而否定或取消选举权.但第三条特别允许国会改变SCOTUS的上诉管辖权,因此它提供了更有说服力的论点.

学习要点：

国会有权根据宪法第三条对美国最高法院的上诉管辖权进行管理和例外处理.

参考资料

^ Ex parte McCardle,74 U.S. 506,514 (1869)(规定国会几乎拥有无限的权力,可以对最高法院的上诉管辖权进行管理和例外处理).

stem: A county district attorney opened a criminal investigation into the President's business transactions conducted before the President assumed office. The district attorney brought the case before a grand jury, which validly issued a subpoena duces tecum requiring the President to produce various financial records related to the business transactions at issue. The President has refused to produce the financial records, citing absolute immunity and executive privilege.
stemZh: 一名县检察官对总统任职前进行的商业交易展开了刑事调查。检察官将案件提交给大陪审团，该陪审团合法地发出了一份 subpoena duces tecum（传唤证人提供证据），要求总统提供与相关商业交易有关的财务记录。总统拒绝提供这些财务记录，声称享有绝对豁免权和行政特权。
ask: Under what circumstances, if any, may the grand jury compel production of the financial records over the President's assertions of absolute immunity and executive privilege?
askZh: 在何种情况下，如果有的话，大陪审团可以不顾总统主张的绝对豁免权和行政特权，强制要求提供财务记录？

options.en: It may compel production only if the subpoena seeks critical evidence that cannot be obtained by any other means.
options.zh: 只有当传票所寻求的关键证据无法通过其他方式获得时，才可以强制提供。

options.en: It may compel production without providing any additional justification.
options.zh: 无需提供任何额外理由即可强制提供。

options.en: It may not compel production under any circumstances because the disclosure of financial records is protected by executive privilege.
options.zh: 在任何情况下都不能强制提供，因为财务记录的披露受到行政特权的保护。

options.en: It may not compel production under any circumstances because the President has absolute immunity from complying with a subpoena.
options.zh: 在任何情况下都不能强制提供，因为总统享有对遵守传票的绝对豁免权。

explanation.en:
Presidential immunity & privilege

Immunity Absolute immunity from civil suits seeking damages for official executive actions

• No immunity for actions that occurred before taking office

• No immunity for actions unrelated to executive functions

• No immunity from criminal subpoena Privilege Power to withhold official documents & communications:

• National security secrets – afforded greatest deference

• Civil case – afforded greater deference than in criminal trial

• Criminal case – afforded least deference (disclosure required if prosecution shows need) As the head of the executive branch, the President possesses all Article II powers, including the power to execute federal laws and serve as the commander in chief of the armed forces. To safeguard the President's ability to perform these important duties, the President has the following protections in judicial proceedings:

• Executive privilege – prevents the disclosure of confidential documents and communications made in performance of official duties and responsibilities

• Absolute immunity – prevents civil suits for damages against the President for any act performed as part of the President's official duties and responsibilities* However, these protections are not infinite. For example, executive privilege does not extend to documents and communications that were made in performing private functions (ie, private papers). Since the financial records at issue here relate to the President's private affairs before taking office—not official conduct while in office—the records are not protected by executive privilege (Choice C).

Additionally, the President is not absolutely immune from complying with a validly issued subpoena that seeks the President's private papers in a criminal proceeding (Choice D). Instead, the President must comply with the subpoena just like any other citizen. Since the grand jury validly issued the subpoena duces tecum in this case, the President must produce the requested financial records. As a result, the grand jury need not provide any additional justification to compel production of those records.

*The U.S. Supreme Court has never ruled whether a President can be indicted for a crime while in office. However, Congress can use the impeachment process to remove the President from office for a high crime or misdemeanor.

(Choice A) The grand jury does not need to meet a heightened standard of need by showing that the subpoena seeks critical evidence that cannot be obtained by any other means. The reason is that, in the absence of a need to protect the President, the public interest in fair and effective law enforcement favors access to such evidence.

Educational objective:

Executive privilege and absolute immunity safeguard a President from liability when performing official duties and responsibilities. However, these protections are not absolute and will not shield the President from complying with a criminal subpoena that seeks the President's private papers.

References

• Trump v. Vance, 140 S. Ct. 2412, 2430 (2020) (holding that the President is not absolutely immune from state criminal subpoenas seeking his private papers and is not entitled to a heightened standard of need).
