explanation.zh:
总统豁免和特权

因官方行政诉讼寻求损害赔偿的民事诉讼绝对豁免

• 对就职前发生的行为没有豁免

• 与行政职能无关的行动没有豁免权

• 没有刑事传票豁免扣留正式文件的权力( I)来文:

• 国家安全机密 -- -- 最受尊重

• 民事案件 -- -- 比刑事审判更受尊重

• 刑事案件 -- -- 最不尊重(如果起诉显示有必要,必须披露) -- -- 作为行政部门负责人,总统拥有第二条规定的所有权力,包括执行联邦法律和担任武装部队总司令的权力。为了保障总统履行这些重要职责的能力,总统在司法程序中享有以下保护:

• 行政特权 -- -- 防止披露履行公务和职责时的机密文件和通信

• 绝对豁免 -- -- 防止就任何行为向总统提起损害赔偿民事诉讼* 然而,这些保护不是《公约》规定的。无限的例如,行政特权不适用于为履行私人职能(即私人文件)而制作的文件和通信。由于此处所涉及的财务记录涉及总统就职前的私人事务,而不是任职期间的官方行为,这些记录不受行政特权的保护(Choice C)。

此外,总统在刑事诉讼(Choice D)中也不能完全免于遵守有效发出的传票。 相反,总统必须像任何其他公民一样遵守传票。由于大陪审团在本案中有效签发了传票,总统必须出示所要求的财务记录,因此大陪审团不必提供任何其他理由强制出示这些记录。

*美国最高法院从未裁定总统在任期间是否可以因犯罪被起诉,但国会可以使用弹劾程序,以高犯罪率或轻罪免去总统职务.

(Choice A)大陪审团无需通过显示传票寻求无法通过任何其他手段获取的关键证据来达到更高的需求标准.原因是,在不需要保护总统的情况下,公众对于公平和有效执法的利益有利于获取此类证据。

学习要点：

行政特权和绝对豁免保障总统在履行公务和责任时不承担责任。然而,这些保护并不是绝对的,不会阻止总统遵守一份寻求总统私人文件的刑事传票。

参考资料

• Trump v. Vance, 140 S. Ct. 2412, 2430 (2020年) (认为总统不能绝对豁免国家刑事传票寻求私人证件,无权享受更高的需要标准).

stem:
A woman contracted for expensive cable television service for a period of six months solely to view the televised trial of a man who was on trial for murder in a state court. In the midst of the trial, the judge prohibited any further televising of the man's trial because the judge concluded that the presence of television cameras was disruptive.

The woman brought an action in a federal district court against the judge in the man's case and sought an injunction that would require the judge to resume the televising of the man's trial. The woman alleged that the judge's order to stop televising the trial deprived her of property—her investment in cable television service—without due process of law.

Before the woman's case came to trial, the man's criminal trial concluded in a conviction and sentencing. There do not appear to be any obvious errors in the proceeding that led to the result in the man's case. After the man's conviction and sentencing, the judge moved to dismiss the woman's suit.
stemZh:
一名女子签订了一份为期六个月的昂贵有线电视服务合同，仅为了观看一名正在州法院受审的男子的电视审判。在审判过程中，法官禁止进一步转播该男子的审判，因为法官认为电视摄像机的存在是干扰性的。

该女子在该男子案件的联邦地区法院对法官提起诉讼，并寻求一项禁令，要求法官恢复该男子审判的转播。该女子声称，法官停止转播审判的命令剥夺了她的财产权——她对有线电视服务的投资——且没有给予正当法律程序。

在该女子的案件开庭前，该男子的刑事案件已得出有罪判决并进行判决。似乎没有导致该男子案件结果的明显错误。在该男子被判有罪并被判决后，法官提出了驳回该女子诉讼的动议。
ask: What is the most proper disposition of this motion by the federal court?
askZh: 联邦法院对该动议的最适当处理方式是什么？

options.en: Defer action on the motion until after any appellate proceedings in the man's case have concluded, because the man might appeal, his conviction might be set aside, he might be tried again, and television cameras might be barred from the new trial.
options.zh: 将动议的处理推迟到该男子案件的上诉程序结束后，因为该男子可能上诉，其有罪判决可能被推翻，他可能再次受审，且电视摄像机可能被禁止进入新的审判。

options.en: Defer action on the motion until after the state's supreme court expresses a view on its proper disposition, because the state law of mootness governs suits in federal court when the federal case is inexorably intertwined with a state proceeding.
options.zh: 将动议的处理推迟到州最高法院对该问题表达观点后，因为州的诉讼终止规则在联邦法院处理联邦案件与州程序不可分割地交织时适用。

options.en: Deny the motion, because the woman has raised an important constitutional question—whether her investment in cable service solely to view the man's trial is protected by the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause.
options.zh: 拒绝动议，因为该女子提出了一个重要的宪法问题——她仅为了观看该男子审判而投资有线电视服务是否受到第十四修正案正当法律程序条款的保护。

options.en: Grant the motion, because the subject matter of the controversy between the woman and the judge has ceased to exist and there is no strong likelihood that it will be revived.
options.zh: 批准动议，因为该女子与法官之间的争议事项已不再存在，且不太可能被重新提起。

explanation.en:
Federal courts have the power to decide actual cases and controversies—ie, disputes that are capable of judicial resolution. But once the plaintiff's harm is resolved, his/her claim becomes moot and should be dismissed unless:

• the harm is capable of repetition yet evading review due to a reasonable chance that the same harm will (1) affect the plaintiff again and (2) not last long enough to be fully litigated (eg, pregnancy) or

• the defendant voluntarily stops the challenged action but can resume it at any time. Here, the woman sued in federal court to force the judge to resume televising the man's murder trial. But before the court could consider her claim, this controversy ceased to exist because the man was convicted and sentenced. And the controversy is not likely to be revived since there were no obvious errors in the man's trial warranting a new trial. Therefore, this controversy is moot, and the federal court should grant the judge's motion to dismiss.

(Choice A) It is highly unlikely that the man will succeed on appeal. But even if he does and obtains a new trial, it is pure speculation whether television cameras will again be barred from the courtroom. Therefore, the woman's suit is moot and should be dismissed—not deferred.

(Choice B) Federal courts always apply federal law to decide procedural issues like mootness—even when the federal case is inexorably intertwined with a state proceeding.

(Choice C) The woman's claim would require the court to determine whether her investment in the cable service is a property interest protected by the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause. But the fact that a claim raises an important constitutional question does not make it an actual case or controversy subject to judicial review.

Educational objective:

When the plaintiff's harm is resolved, his/her claim becomes moot and must be dismissed unless (1) the harm is capable of repetition yet evading review or (2) the defendant voluntarily stops the challenged action but can resume it at any time.

References

• U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case or controversy requirement).

• Turner v. Rogers, 564 U.S. 431, 439–40 (2011) (explaining the mootness doctrine and its exceptions).

• 32 Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 575 (2019) (defining mootness and its exceptions).

explanation.zh:
联邦法院有权裁决实际案件和争议,即能够通过司法途径解决的争议。 但一旦原告的伤害得到解决,其索赔就无实际意义,除非:

• 由于同一损害的合理机会,损害有可能重复,但却逃避审查将(1)再次影响原告,(2)持续时间不足以充分诉讼(例如,怀孕)或

· 被告自愿停止受到质疑的诉讼,但可以随时恢复诉讼,在这方面,该妇女在联邦法院起诉,强迫法官恢复对男子谋杀案的审判。但是在法庭可以审理她的申诉之前,由于该男子被定罪和判刑,这一争议就不复存在了,而且由于该男子的审判没有明显错误,因此该争议不太可能重新出现,从而可以进行新的审判。因此,这一争议是没有实际意义的,联邦法院应当批准法官的驳回动议.

(Choice A) 此人极不可能在上诉时成功.但是,即使他这样做 并获得新的审判, 这是纯粹的猜测 电视摄像机会再次被禁止进入法庭。因此,该妇女的诉讼没有实际意义,应当驳回,而不是推迟。

联邦法院总是适用联邦法律来裁定诸如无实际意义之类的程序性问题,即使联邦案件与州程序不可避免地交织在一起。

妇女的要求要求法院确定她在电缆服务方面的投资是否属于《第十四修正案》正当程序条款所保护的财产权益。但是,一个诉求引起一个重要的宪法问题这一事实并没有使它成为实际案件或争议,需要司法审查.

学习要点：

在解决原告的伤害时,他/她的要求已无实际意义,必须予以驳回,除非(1) 损害能够重复而逃避复审,或者(2) 被告自愿停止被质疑的诉讼,但可随时恢复诉讼。

参考资料

• 美国康斯特公司第3条第2款(案件或争议要求)。

• Turner诉Rogers案,564 U.S.431,439–40 (2011)(解释无实际意义理论及其例外)。

• 32 Am. Jur. 2d 联邦法院第575条(2019年)(定义无实际意义及其例外)。

stem:
The House of Representatives created an investigatory committee to look into the judicial administrative processes of federal judges. In particular, the committee was tasked with investigating the issuance of court orders, the management of trial schedules, and the drafting of basic court documents by judicial assistants. The goal of the committee was to ensure that the administrative processes were carried out efficiently, accurately, and pursuant to federal legislation regarding the judicial administrative process.

After much investigation, the committee concluded that a federal district court judge was negligently mismanaging his trial schedule, causing undue delays in his case log. Based upon its findings, the committee made a recommendation to the House of Representatives to remove the federal judge.
stemZh:
众议院成立了一个调查委员会，调查联邦法官的司法行政程序。具体而言，该委员会的任务是调查司法助手发布法院命令、管理庭审日程以及起草基本法院文件的程序。该委员会的目标是确保司法行政程序高效、准确地进行，并符合有关司法行政程序的联邦立法。

经过大量调查后，该委员会得出结论，一名联邦地区法院法官在管理其庭审日程时存在疏忽，导致其案件日志出现不必要的延误。基于其调查结果，该委员会向众议院提出了将该联邦法官免职的建议。
ask: Can the House of Representatives remove the federal judge based on the committee's recommendation?
askZh: 众议院能否根据委员会的建议将联邦法官免职？

options.en: No, because the House of Representatives cannot investigate a federal judge's administrative processes.
options.zh: 不能，因为众议院不能调查联邦法官的行政程序。

options.en: No, because the federal judge can be removed only by impeachment.
options.zh: 不能，因为联邦法官只能通过弹劾被免职。

options.en: Yes, because the House of Representatives can remove federal judges with or without cause.
options.zh: 可以，因为众议院可以无理由或有理由地免职联邦法官。

options.en: Yes, because the federal judge mismanaged his trial schedule.
options.zh: 可以，因为该联邦法官管理了其庭审日程。

explanation.en:
Federal judges

Type Attributes Examples

Article I • Implement Congress's enumerated powers

• Not entitled to life tenure & undiminished pay

• Tax court

• Bankruptcy court

• Veterans' claims court

Article III

• Decide actual cases or controversies

• Entitled to life tenure & undiminished pay

• District court

• Circuit appellate court

• SCOTUS SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States.

There are two types of federal judges:

• Article I judges – who serve on specialized courts created by Congress under Article I to perform functions deemed helpful in carrying out Congress's enumerated powers (e.g., veterans' claims courts)

• Article III judges – who serve on courts created under Article III to decide the merits of actual cases or controversies (e.g., federal district courts)

Article III judges are independent of Congress, the President, and the political process. To help guarantee their judicial independence, Article III judges are entitled to life tenure during good behavior and undiminished pay during their service. This has been interpreted to mean that Article III judges can be removed from office only through impeachment. This process requires the House of Representatives to adopt articles of impeachment by a majority vote and the Senate to convict by a two-thirds vote.

Here, the House of Representatives created a committee to investigate the work of federal judges. After concluding that a federal district court judge negligently mismanaged his trial schedule, the committee recommended that the House of Representatives remove him

(Choice D). But since the federal district court judge can be removed only by impeachment—which also requires Senate action—the House of Representatives cannot unilaterally remove him based on the committee's recommendation.

(Choice A) Both the House of Representatives and the Senate have the power to investigate a federal judge's administrative processes. But a federal district court judge can be removed only through impeachment.

(Choice C) A federal district court judge can be removed through impeachment— regardless of whether adequate cause exists for removal.

Educational objective:

Article III judges are entitled to life tenure during good behavior and undiminished pay during their service—and therefore can be removed from office only through impeachment. This process requires the House of Representatives to adopt articles of impeachment by a majority vote and the Senate to convict by a two-thirds vote.

References

• Glidden Co. v. Zdanok, 370 U.S. 530, 534 (1962) (stating that only Article III judges are entitled to life tenure during good behavior and undiminished salaries while in service).

explanation.zh:
联邦法官

类型属性示例

第一条 执行议会列举的权力

• 无权享有终身保有权和薪酬不受减损

• 税务法院

• 破产法院

• 退伍军人索赔法庭

第三条

• 决定实际案件或争议

• 终身保有权和薪酬不受减损

• 地区法院

• 巡回上诉法院

• SCOTUS SCOTUS = 美国最高法院。

联邦法官有两种类型:

• 第一条法官——在国会根据第一条设立的专门法院任职,履行被认为有助于行使国会所列举权力的职能(例如退伍军人索赔法院)

• 第三条 法官 -- -- 在根据第三条设立的法院任职,以裁定实际案件或争议的案情(例如联邦地区法院)

第三条 法官独立于国会,院长和政治进程,为保障司法独立,第三条法官在行为良好期间有权终身任职,任职期间薪酬不受减损.这被解释为,第三条规定的法官只能通过弹劾被免职,这一过程要求众议院以多数票通过弹劾条款,参议院以三分之二的票数定罪.

在此,众议院设立了一个委员会来调查联邦法官的工作。 在得出结论,联邦地区法院法官疏忽地管理了他的审判时间表之后,委员会建议众议院将他除名。

但是,由于联邦地区法院法官只能通过弹劾来罢免,这也需要参议院采取行动,众议院不能根据委员会的建议单方面罢免他。

(Choice A)众议院和参议院都有权调查联邦法官的行政程序,但联邦地区法院法官只能通过弹劾被撤职.

(C) 联邦地区法院法官可通过弹劾方式罢免,而不论是否有适当的理由罢免。

学习要点：

第三条 法官在行为良好期间有权终身任职,在任职期间薪酬不受减损,因此只能通过弹劾予以免职。这一过程要求众议院以多数表决通过弹劾条款,参议院以三分之二表决通过定罪.

参考资料

• Glidden Co.诉Zdanok案,370 U.S.530, 534(1962年)(规定只有第三条规定的法官在良好行为期间有权终身任职,在职期间的薪金不受减损)。

stem: A statute passed by both houses of Congress and signed by the President created a federal agency to regulate consumer financial products such as credit cards, student loans, and mortgages. The federal statute authorizes the agency to issue regulatory rules, conduct administrative proceedings, and initiate suits in federal court on behalf of consumers. A statutory provision establishes that the agency is led by a single director who must be appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate. The provision also states that the director serves a five-year term and can only be removed from office by the President for good cause.
stemZh: 国会两院通过并由总统签署的一项法律创建了一个联邦机构，用于监管信用卡、学生贷款和抵押贷款等消费者金融产品。该联邦法律授权该机构制定监管规则、进行行政程序，并代表消费者在联邦法院提起诉讼。一项法律规定，该机构由一名单一负责人领导，该负责人必须由总统提名并经参议院同意后任命。该条款还规定，负责人任期为五年，仅能因正当理由由总统解除职务。
ask: Is the provision allowing the director to be removed by the President for good cause constitutional?
askZh: 该条款允许总统因正当理由解除负责人职务是否符合宪法？

options.en: No, because the President may remove a federal executive officer only with the advice and consent of the Senate.
options.zh: 否，因为总统只有在获得参议院的建议和同意后才能解除联邦行政官员的职务。

options.en: No, because the provision amounts to an unconstitutional legislative interference with an executive function.
options.zh: 否，因为该条款构成对行政职能的违宪立法干涉。

options.en: Yes, because Congress may require the President to show good cause to remove a federal executive officer.
options.zh: 是，因为国会可以要求总统在解除联邦行政官员职务时必须出示正当理由。

options.en: Yes, because the provision is part of a statute that was passed by both houses of Congress and signed by the President.
options.zh: 是，因为该条款是国会两院通过并由总统签署的法律的一部分。

explanation.en:
The Constitution divides the federal government into three coequal branches that possess distinct powers (ie, separation of powers). Article II vests the executive power in the President, including the power to faithfully execute federal laws. Since it is impossible for one person to carry out this power, federal executive officers may be appointed pursuant to the appointments clause to assist the President.

The Constitution is silent about the removal of federal executive officers, but the U.S. Supreme Court has repeatedly held that the President has absolute authority to remove such officers absent two exceptions. This means that Congress cannot impose any removal restrictions, including good-cause requirements, except for officers who either:

• belong to a multimember body that is balanced along partisan lines and exercises no executive power (eg, committees that conduct investigations on behalf of Congress) or

• lack policymaking or administrative authority (eg, independent counsel who investigates and prosecutes alleged crimes by government officials). Here, Congress created a federal agency headed by a single director. The director exercises significant executive power and administrative authority by issuing regulatory rules, conducting administrative proceedings, and initiating suits in federal court. As a result, the President has the absolute authority to remove the director. The provision requiring good cause for removal therefore amounts to an unconstitutional legislative interference with an executive function (Choice C).

(Choice A) The President must appoint certain federal executive officers (eg, cabinet secretaries) with the advice and consent of the Senate. However, the Senate's advice and consent is not required for the President to remove such officers.

(Choice D) The removal provision is part of a statute that satisfied the federal legislative process because it was passed by both houses of Congress and signed by the President. But the provision is still an unconstitutional legislative interference with an executive power.

Educational objective:

The President has absolute authority to remove federal executive officers. Congress may impose restrictions on this power only for officers who (1) belong to a multimember body that is balanced along partisan lines and exercises no executive power or (2) lack policymaking or administrative authority.

References

• Seila Law Ltd. Liab. Corp. v. Consumer Fin. Prot. Bureau, 140 S. Ct. 2183, 2197–2200 (2020) (explaining that the President has the absolute power to remove federal executive officers subject to very narrow exceptions).

explanation.zh:
《宪法》将联邦政府分为三个平等分支,它们拥有不同的权力(即三权分立),第二条赋予总统行政权力,包括忠实执行联邦法律的权力。由于一个人不可能行使这一权力,因此可根据任命条款任命联邦执行官员协助总统。

宪法对撤换联邦执行官一事保持沉默,但美国最高法院一再认定,总统在没有两个例外的情况下有绝对权力撤换这些官员.这意味着,国会不得施加任何撤职限制,包括有正当理由的要求,但下列官员除外:

● 属于一个按党派路线平衡的多成员机构,不行使行政权力(例如代表国会进行调查的委员会)或

• 缺乏决策或行政权力(例如独立律师,负责调查和起诉政府官员被指控的罪行),在这方面,国会设立了一个联邦机构,由一名主任领导。局长通过发布监管规则、进行行政诉讼和向联邦法院提起诉讼行使重要的行政权力和行政权力,因此,总统拥有解除局长职务的绝对权力。因此,要求有充分理由驱逐的规定相当于违宪的立法干预行政职能(Choice C)。

(Choice A) 总统必须在参议院的建议和同意下任命某些联邦执行官员(如内阁秘书),然而,参议院的建议和同意并不需要总统解除这些官员的职务.

(Choice D) 罢免条款是符合联邦立法程序的一项法规的一部分,因为它由国会两院通过,并由总统签署.但这项规定仍然是对行政权力的违宪立法干涉.

学习要点：

总统绝对有权罢免联邦行政官员,国会只能对(1) 属于多党制机构、且不行使行政权力或(2) 缺乏行政权力的官员施加限制。决策或行政权力。

参考资料

· Seila Law Ltd. Liab. Corp. v. Consumn Fin. Prot. Bureau, 140 S. Ct. 2183, 2197–2200 (2020) (解释总统有绝对权力解除联邦执行官员的职务,但有极小的例外)。

stem:
A nightclub owner applied for a required zoning permit to open a nude-dancing nightclub in the theater district of a city. An organization of influential city residents began an intensive lobbying effort to persuade the city council to deny the owner a permit to operate any type of nude-dancing facility at any time or in any place in the city.

The owner has sued the city in an appropriate federal court, seeking an injunction that would prohibit the city council from considering the organization's views, on the ground that if the organization is successful in its lobbying efforts, the owner's First and Fourteenth Amendment rights would be violated. The city has moved to dismiss the action.
stemZh:
一家夜总会老板申请了必需的规划许可，以便在该市剧院区开设一家裸体舞蹈夜总会。一个由有影响力市民组成的组织开始进行积极的游说，说服市议会拒绝该老板在城市任何时间或任何地点经营任何类型的裸体舞蹈设施的许可。

老板在适当的联邦法院起诉该市，要求颁布禁令，禁止市议会考虑该组织的观点，理由是如果该组织在游说努力中成功，老板的言论自由和第十四修正案权利将受到侵犯。该市提出了驳回诉讼的动议。
ask: Should the court dismiss the owner's action?
askZh: 法院应驳回老板的诉讼吗？

options.en: No, because nude dancing is symbolic speech and is therefore protected by the First and Fourteenth Amendments.
options.zh: 不应驳回，因为裸体舞蹈属于象征性言论，受到第一修正案和第十四修正案的保护。

options.en: No, because the organization does not seek a reasonable time, place, and manner regulation of nude dancing, but instead seeks a total ban on the owner's opening any type of nude-dancing facility at any time or in any place in the city.
options.zh: 不应驳回，因为该组织并不寻求对裸体舞蹈进行合理的时间、地点和方式的管制，而是寻求在城市任何时间或任何地点禁止老板开设任何类型的裸体舞蹈设施。

options.en: Yes, because the action is not ripe.
options.zh: 应驳回，因为该诉讼尚未成熟。

options.en: Yes, because the First and Fourteenth Amendments do not protect obscenity, and nude dancing is obscene.
options.zh: 应驳回，因为第一修正案和第十四修正案并不保护淫秽内容，而裸体舞蹈属于淫秽内容。

explanation.en:
Article III of the Constitution limits the jurisdiction of federal courts to actual cases or controversies. An actual case or controversy exists when a dispute between adverse parties is capable of judicial resolution—ie, ripe for adjudication. A suit is ripe when the plaintiff has suffered actual harm or an immediate threat thereof. But a suit based on potential future harm is unripe and should be dismissed.

Here, the nightclub owner applied for a permit to open a nude-dancing facility. An organization then lobbied the city council to deny the permit. In response, the owner sued in federal court to enjoin the city council from considering the organization's views. But the city council has not yet denied his permit request (no actual harm), nor is there any indication that it will do so soon (no immediate threat). And since the owner's action is not ripe, the court should grant the city's motion and dismiss the suit.

(Choices A & B) Nude dancing is symbolic speech that is protected by the First and Fourteenth Amendments. As a result, a total ban on nude dancing (ie, a content-based restriction) would be presumptively unconstitutional. In contrast, a reasonable time, place, and manner (ie, content-neutral) regulation would likely be valid. But the court will not consider the constitutionality of the potential regulation since the suit is unripe.

(Choice D) The First and Fourteenth Amendments do not protect certain forms of speech, including obscenity. But mere nudity (including nude dancing) is not obscene.

Educational objective:

For a suit to be ripe for adjudication, the plaintiff must have suffered actual harm or an immediate threat thereof. Therefore, a claim based on potential future harm is unripe and will be dismissed.

References

• U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case or controversy requirement).

• Texas v. United States, 523 U.S. 296, 300 (1998) (explaining when a claim is unripe for adjudication).

explanation.zh:
《宪法》第三条将联邦法院的管辖权限于实际案件或争议。 当敌对方之间的纠纷能够通过司法手段解决时,实际案件或争议就存在 — — 时机已经成熟,可以裁决。当原告遭受了实际伤害或直接的伤害威胁时,诉讼已经成熟,但基于未来潜在伤害的诉讼是无效的,应当驳回。

在这里,夜总会老板申请了开放裸舞设施的许可。 然后,一个组织游说市议会拒绝许可。 对此,业主在联邦法院起诉,要求市议会不要考虑该组织的观点。但是市议会还没有拒绝他的许可请求(没有实际伤害),也没有迹象表明会很快这样做(没有立即威胁),而且由于业主的行为还不成熟,法院应该批准市政府的动议并驳回诉讼.

(Choices A & B) Nude 跳舞是受第一修正案和第十四修正案保护的象征性言论,因此,完全禁止裸体跳舞(即基于内容的限制)将被认为是违宪的。相比之下,合理的时间、地点和方式(即内容中性)监管可能有效。 但法院不会考虑潜在监管的合宪性,因为诉讼不合理。

(Choice D)第一和第十四修正案并不保护某些形式的言论,包括淫秽。 但仅仅裸体(包括裸体舞)并不淫秽。

学习要点：

原告必须遭受了实际伤害或直接的伤害威胁,因此,根据未来潜在伤害提出的索赔是无效的,将被驳回。

参考资料

• Texas诉美国案,523 U.S. 296, 300 (1998)(解释一项要求何时不能裁定)。

stem: The federal parole commission denied a federal prisoner's request for parole based on the commission's parole guidelines. The prisoner subsequently filed a class action against the commission in federal court, challenging the facial validity of the commission's parole guidelines on the basis that the guidelines violate federal law. After the court certified the class action, the prisoner was released from prison. The commission has moved to dismiss the case.
stemZh: 联邦假释委员会根据其假释指南拒绝了联邦囚犯的假释请求。该囚犯随后在联邦法院提起了一项集体诉讼，挑战该委员会假释指南的表面有效性，理由是这些指南违反联邦法律。在法院确认了集体诉讼后，该囚犯被释放出监狱。委员会已提出驳回诉讼动议。
ask: Should the court grant the motion?
askZh: 法院应否批准该动议？

options.en: No, because an actual case or controversy exists for the court to decide.
options.zh: 不应，因为存在一个实际的案件或争议供法院裁决。

options.en: No, because the prisoner's suit is not ripe for decision.
options.zh: 不应，因为该囚犯的诉讼尚不成熟。

options.en: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits this type of action in federal court.
options.zh: 应，因为第十一修正案禁止在联邦法院提起此类诉讼。

options.en: Yes, because the prisoner's claim has become moot.
options.zh: 应，因为该囚犯的主张已变得无争议。

explanation.en:
Ripeness v. Mootness

Ripe

(too soon)

Action will not be heard until plaintiff has experienced actual injury or imminent threat thereof

Moot

(too late)

Action will be dismissed if further proceedings would have no effect unless:

• plaintiff's harm is capable of repetition yet evading review (eg, pregnancy)

• defendant voluntarily stops action but can resume it anytime

• plaintiff is named plaintiff in class action & claims of unnamed plaintiffs are still viable Article III of the Constitution grants federal courts the power to decide actual cases and controversies—ie, disputes that are capable of judicial resolution. If further legal proceedings would no longer have an effect—often because the plaintiff's harm has been resolved—then an actual case or controversy typically ceases to exist. When this occurs, the plaintiff's claim is typically rendered moot and the case must then be dismissed.

However, one exception to this rule applies when the plaintiff whose claim has become moot is the named plaintiff in a certified class action (as seen here). If the claims of the unnamed plaintiffs in the class are still viable, then the class action will not be dismissed as moot. That is because, while the named plaintiff's personal claim has become moot, an actual case or controversy still exists for the unnamed plaintiffs' claims.

Here, the prisoner filed a class action in federal court, thereby serving as the named plaintiff. The prisoner's personal claim—that the commission's parole guidelines violate federal law—became moot when he was released from prison. However, an actual case or controversy still exists for the unnamed plaintiffs who have not been released (Choice D). Therefore, the court should deny the commission's motion to dismiss.

(Choice B) For a suit to be ripe for decision, the plaintiff must have experienced a real injury or an immediate threat thereof. Here, the prisoner suffered actual harm when the commission denied the prisoner's request for parole, so this suit is ripe for decision.

(Choice C) The Eleventh Amendment prohibits foreign governments and private parties from suing a state in federal court. It does not prohibit private parties from suing the federal government in federal court (as seen here).

Educational objective:

A federal court typically must dismiss a case when the plaintiff's claim becomes moot. However, one exception applies when (1) a plaintiff whose claim is moot is the named plaintiff in a certified class action and (2) the claims of the unnamed plaintiffs in that class action are still viable.

References

• U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case-or-controversy requirement).

• U.S. Parole Comm'n v. Geraghty, 445 U.S. 388, 404 (1980) (holding that federal courts must not dismiss a class action when the named plaintiff's claim becomes moot so long as the claims of the unnamed plaintiffs are viable).

• 32 Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 575 (2020) (defining mootness and its exceptions).

explanation.zh:
里佩内斯诉模拟法庭

撕开

(太快了) (笑声)

在原告遭受实际伤害或迫在眉睫的伤害威胁之前,不受理诉讼

模拟

(太迟)

如果进一步的诉讼没有效果,除非:

• 原告的伤害可以重复但逃避审查(如怀孕)

• 被告自愿停止诉讼,但可随时恢复诉讼

· 在集体诉讼中,原告是原告,对无名原告的要求仍然是可行的《宪法》第三条规定,联邦法院有权裁定实际案件和争议,即能够通过司法途径解决的争议。如果进一步的法律诉讼不再产生效果——往往是因为原告的伤害已经解决——那么一个实际案件或争议一般就不复存在。发生这种情况时,原告的主张一般会失去实际意义,因此案件必须驳回。

然而,如果原告的权利主张已失去实际意义,则该规则的一个例外适用于在经认证的集体诉讼中被点名的原告(见这里)。如果该类中无名原告的诉求仍然可行,那么集体诉讼将不会被作为无实际意义驳回.这是因为,虽然被点名的原告的个人要求已无实际意义,但对无点名的原告的要求,实际案件或争议依然存在.

在此,该囚犯向联邦法院提起集体诉讼,从而担任了被点名的原告。 囚犯的个人诉求 — — 委员会的假释准则违反了联邦法律 — — 在他出狱时已无实际意义。然而,对于尚未获释的无名原告,实际案件或争议依然存在(Choice D)。 因此,法院应当驳回委员会提出的驳回动议。

(Choice B)诉讼要成熟决定,原告必须已经遭受了真正的伤害或直接的威胁,在这里,当委员会拒绝囚犯的假释请求时,囚犯遭受了实际伤害,所以这一诉讼已经成熟决定.

(Choice)第十一修正案禁止外国政府和私人政党在联邦法院起诉某州,并不禁止私人政党在联邦法院起诉联邦政府(如本文所示).

学习要点：

通常,当原告的诉讼请求失去实际意义时,联邦法院必须驳回案件。但是,如果(1) 原告的诉讼请求不成立,在经认证的集体诉讼中被指名原告,以及(2) 原告的诉讼请求无效,则适用一个例外。原告的求偿权行动仍然是可行的。

参考资料

• 美国康斯特公司第3条第2款(案件或争议要求)。

• 美国假释委员会诉Geraghty案,445 U.S. 388, 404(1980年)(认为,只要无名原告的诉求可行,在被点名原告的诉求失去实际意义时,联邦法院不得驳回集体诉讼)。

• 32 Am. Jur. 2d 联邦法院§575(2020年)(定义无实际意义及其例外)。

stem:
A federal statute provides that the United States Supreme Court has authority to review any case filed in a United States court of appeals, even if that case has not yet been decided by the court of appeals.

The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), an agency in the executive branch of the federal government, issued an important environmental rule. Although the rule had not yet been enforced against them, companies that would be adversely affected by the rule filed a petition for review of the rule in a court of appeals, seeking a declaration that the rule was invalid solely because it was beyond the statutory authority of the EPA. The companies made no constitutional claim. A statute specifically provides for direct review of EPA rules by a court of appeals without any initial action in a district court.

The companies have filed a petition for a writ of certiorari in the Supreme Court requesting immediate review of this case by the Supreme Court before the court of appeals has actually decided the case. The EPA acknowledges that the case is important enough to warrant Supreme Court review and that it should be decided promptly, but it asks the Supreme Court to dismiss the petition on jurisdictional grounds.
stemZh:
一项联邦法律规定，美国最高法院有权审查任何在联邦上诉法院提起的案件，即使该案件尚未由上诉法院作出裁决。

美国环境保护署（EPA）是联邦政府行政部门的一个机构，颁布了一项重要的环境规则。尽管该规则尚未被实施，但一些可能受到该规则不利影响的公司向上诉法院提起审查该规则的申请，请求宣告该规则无效，理由是该规则超出了EPA的法定授权范围。这些公司并未提出任何宪法主张。一项具体法律规定了上诉法院可以直接审查EPA规则，而无需在地区法院进行初步行动。

这些公司已向最高法院提起一份颁发提审令的申请，请求最高法院在上诉法院尚未作出裁决之前立即审查此案。EPA承认此案的重要性足以引起最高法院的审查，并且应当尽快作出裁决，但它请求最高法院以管辖权为由驳回该申请。
ask: What is the best constitutional argument in support of the EPA's request?
askZh: 支持EPA请求的最佳宪法论点是什么？

options.en: Article III precludes federal courts from reviewing the validity of any federal agency rule in any proceeding other than an action to enforce the rule.
options.zh: 《宪法》第三条禁止联邦法院在非执行规则的诉讼程序中审查任何联邦机构规则的有效性。

options.en: Article III provides that all federal cases, except those within the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, must be initiated by an action in a federal district court.
options.zh: 《宪法》第三条规定，所有联邦案件，除最高法院原始管辖权范围内的案件外，必须首先在联邦地区法院提起诉讼。

options.en: The case is appellate in nature, but it is beyond the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, because Article III states that its jurisdiction extends only to cases arising under the Constitution.
options.zh: 此案属于上诉性质，但因其超出最高法院的上诉管辖权范围，因为《宪法》第三条规定其管辖权仅限于涉及宪法的案件。

options.en: The case is not within the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court as defined by Article III, and it is not a proper subject of that court's appellate jurisdiction because it has not yet been decided by any lower court.
options.zh: 此案不属于最高法院根据《宪法》第三条定义的原始管辖权范围，也不属于该法院上诉管辖权的适当主题，因为尚未由任何下级法院作出裁决。

explanation.en:
Article III of the Constitution states that the U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has both:

• original jurisdiction – the authority to directly review (1) cases involving an ambassador, public minister, or consul and (2) cases in which a state is a party and

• appellate jurisdiction – the authority to overturn, modify, or affirm a decision made by a lower federal court or a state's highest court in all other cases falling within federal judicial power.

Here, the companies filed a petition for a writ of certiorari requesting that SCOTUS immediately review their case against the EPA. But the case is not within SCOTUS's original jurisdiction as narrowly defined by Article III. And since the case has not yet been decided by a lower court—ie, there is no decision being appealed from—it is not a proper subject of SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction. Accordingly, that is the best constitutional argument in support of the EPA's request.

(Choice A) Article III allows federal courts to review the validity of a federal rule in a proceeding other than an action to enforce the rule. For example, federal courts may issue a declaratory judgment that a rule is invalid before it has been enforced if the plaintiff faces imminent harm.

(Choice B) Under Article III, Congress has broad power to regulate the original and appellate jurisdiction of lower federal courts. As a result, a federal case can be initiated by an action in a U.S. court of appeals rather than a U.S. district court if authorized by Congress.

(Choice C) SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction extends to all cases arising under the Constitution, a treaty, or federal law (as seen here). But this case is not appellate in nature since there is no lower court decision to review.

Educational objective:

The U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has original jurisdiction in (1) cases involving an ambassador, public minister, or consul and (2) cases in which a state is a party. But in all other cases, SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction requires a lower court decision.

References

• Balt. & Ohio R.R. Co. v. Interstate Com. Comm'n, 215 U.S. 216, 224–25 (1909) (explaining that SCOTUS has original jurisdiction in limited circumstances and that appellate jurisdiction requires a lower court decision).

• 32 Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 453 (2019) (defining original and appellate jurisdiction).

explanation.zh:
《宪法》第三条规定,美国最高法院:

• 原始管辖权 -- -- 直接审查(1)涉及大使、公使或领事的案件;(2) 国家是当事方的案件;

• 上诉管辖权——推翻、修改或确认下级联邦法院或州最高法院在属于联邦司法权力的所有其他案件中所作决定的权力。

在此,这些公司提出诉讼请求,要求SCOTUS立即审查它们针对环保局的案件。 但该案不属于第三条狭义界定的SCOTUS的原管辖范围。由于此案尚未由下级法院裁决,因此没有就裁决提出上诉,这不是SCOTUS上诉管辖权的适当主体。 因此,这是支持环保局请求的最佳宪法论据。

(Choice A) 第三条允许联邦法院在强制执行该规则的诉讼以外的诉讼中审查联邦规则的有效性.例如,如果原告面临迫在眉睫的损害,联邦法院可以作出宣告性判决,宣布一项规则在执行之前无效。

(Choice B)根据第三条,国会拥有广泛的权力来规范下级联邦法院的原始和上诉管辖权,因此,一个联邦案件可以通过美国上诉法院而不是美国的诉讼提起.由国会授权的地区法院。

最高法院的上诉管辖权适用于《宪法》、条约或联邦法律(如本文所示)规定的所有案件。 但本案不属于上诉性质,因为没有下级法院的复审决定。

学习要点：

美国最高法院(SCOTUS)对(1)涉及大使、公使或领事的案件和(2)涉及国家为当事方的案件拥有原始管辖权。 但在所有其他案件中,SCOTUS的上诉管辖权要求下级法院做出裁决。

参考资料

• Balt. & Ohio R.R. Co.诉Interstate Comm. Comm'n, 215 U.S.216, 224–25 (1909)(解释SCOTUS在有限情况下拥有原始管辖权,上诉管辖权要求下级法院裁决)。

• 32 Am. Jur. 2d联邦法院第453条(2019年)(界定原管辖权和上诉管辖权)。

stem: Assume that Congress passed and the President signed the following statute: "The appellate jurisdiction of the United States Supreme Court shall not extend to any case involving the constitutionality of any state statute limiting the circumstances in which a person may obtain contraception, or involving the constitutionality of this statute."
stemZh: 假设国会通过并总统签署了以下法律："美国最高法院的上诉管辖权不得适用于任何涉及州法律限制个人获得避孕药具的情况的合宪性案件，或涉及本法律合宪性的案件。"
ask: What is the strongest argument against the constitutionality of this statute?
askZh: 该法律合宪性的最强反对论点是什么？

options.en: Congress may not exercise its authority over the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in a way that seriously interferes with the establishment of a supreme and uniform body of federal constitutional law.
options.zh: 国会不得以严重干扰建立统一的联邦宪法法律体系的方式行使对其上诉管辖权的权力。

options.en: Congress may only regulate the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court over cases initially arising in federal courts.
options.zh: 国会只能对最初在联邦法院提起的案件的最高法院上诉管辖权进行监管。

options.en: The appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court may only be altered by constitutional amendment.
options.zh: 最高法院的上诉管辖权只能通过宪法修正案进行修改。

options.en: The statute violates the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
options.zh: 该法律违反了第十四修正案的平等保护条款。

explanation.en:
Most cases come before the U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) through its appellate jurisdiction. This allows SCOTUS to review certain cases that have been decided by a lower federal court or a state's highest court. Article III grants Congress the power to regulate and make exceptions to SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction. But when exercising this almost unlimited power, Congress cannot violate:

• the separation-of-powers doctrine—eg, usurping judicial power to decide cases— or

• other constitutional provisions—eg, giving only men the right to appeal, in violation of the equal protection component of the Fifth Amendment.

Here, the federal statute denies SCOTUS appellate jurisdiction over any case involving the constitutionality of a state statute limiting access to contraception. As a result, the federal statute may violate the separation-of-powers doctrine since it could usurp SCOTUS's power to establish a supreme and uniform body of federal constitutional law on this issue. Therefore, this is the strongest argument against the constitutionality of the federal statute.

(Choices B & C) Since Article III of the Constitution gives Congress the power to limit SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction over cases initially arising in federal or state court, no constitutional amendment is required.

(Choice D) The Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause applies when states treat similarly situated persons differently. But since the challenged statute was enacted by the federal government, this clause does not apply.

Educational objective:

Article III grants Congress the power to regulate and limit SCOTUS's appellate jurisdiction. But when exercising this power, Congress cannot violate the separation-of-powers doctrine or other constitutional provisions.

References

• United States v. Klein, 80 U.S. 128, 147–48 (1871) (establishing that Congress cannot alter the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction if it would violate the separation-of-powers doctrine).

explanation.zh:
美国最高法院(SCOTUS)通过其上诉管辖权受理大多数案件,这使得SCOTUS可以复审由下级联邦法院或州最高法院裁决的某些案件.第三条赋予国会对SCOTUS的上诉管辖权进行管理和例外的权力。 但当行使这一几乎无限的权力时,国会不能违反:

· 分权原则——例如,篡夺司法权力以裁决案件——或

• 其他宪法规定——例如,只给予男子上诉的权利,违反了第五修正案的平等保护部分。

在此,联邦法规剥夺了SCOTUS对涉及限制获得避孕药具的州法规合宪性的任何案件的上诉管辖权。因此,联邦法规可能违反权力分离原则,因为它可能篡夺SCOTUS在这个问题上建立最高和统一的联邦宪法法律机构的权力。因此,这是反对联邦法规合宪性的最有力论据.

由于《宪法》第三条授权国会限制SCOTUS对最初发生在联邦或州法院的案件的上诉管辖权,因此不需要修改宪法。

(Choice D) 第十四修正案的平等保护条款适用于各州对处境相似的人的区别对待。 但是,由于受到质疑的法规是由联邦政府颁布的,这一条款并不适用。

学习要点：

第三条赋予国会管理和限制SCOTUS上诉管辖权的权力,但国会在行使这一权力时不得违反权力分离原则或其他宪法规定.

参考资料

· 美国诉Klein案,80 U.S.128,147–48(1871)(规定如果违反分权原则,国会不能改变最高法院的上诉管辖权)。

stem:
Congress enacted a statute over the President's veto establishing a program to protect areas in the United States that are rich in biological diversity. The program is consistent with the terms of an environmental treaty that the President objected to and did not sign.

The statute creates an executive agency and authorizes it to designate parts of federal lands for inclusion in the program in accordance with criteria taken from the treaty. In an inseverable provision, the statute further provides that the agency must report each designation to a committee of Congress and that the committee may overturn the agency's designation by a majority vote.
stemZh:
国会不顾总统否决意见通过了一项法律，设立了一个保护美国境内生物多样性丰富的地区的计划。该计划与总统反对并拒绝签署的一项环境条约的条款一致。

该法律设立了一个行政机关，并授权其根据条约中的标准，将联邦土地的部分区域纳入该计划。在一项不可分割的条款中，该法律进一步规定，该行政机关必须将每个指定区域向国会委员会报告，并且该委员会可以通过多数投票推翻该行政机关的指定。
ask: Why is the statute unconstitutional?
askZh: 为什么该法律是违宪的？

options.en: It authorizes a committee of Congress to overturn an executive decision.
options.zh: 它授权国会委员会推翻行政机关的决定。

options.en: It constitutes an invalid delegation of legislative authority to an executive agency.
options.zh: 它构成将立法权非法委托给行政机关的无效行为。

options.en: It interferes with the exercise of the President's paramount authority in foreign affairs.
options.zh: 它干涉总统在对外事务中的最高权力。

options.en: It requires an executive agency to report its decisions to Congress.
options.zh: 它要求行政机关向国会报告其决定。

explanation.en:
The nondelegation doctrine prohibits Congress from delegating purely legislative powers (eg, making or repealing laws). But it allows Congress to delegate its incidental powers (eg, regulating federal lands) to executive agencies if it provides an intelligible principle— ie, a clear statement defining:

• the policy Congress seeks to advance (eg, protect areas in the United States that are rich in biodiversity)

• the agency to carry out that policy (eg, the agency created by statute here) and

• the scope of that agency's authority (eg, designate parts of federal lands for inclusion in the environmental protection program) (Choice B).

But once Congress has delegated authority to an executive agency, Congress cannot authorize a committee to veto (ie, overturn) that agency's executive decisions. Such decisions can only be overturned through new legislation, which requires:

• bicameralism—which entails a majority vote in both the House of Representatives and the Senate (not merely a congressional committee)—and

• presentment to the President for approval or disapproval (which did not occur here).

Therefore, the statute is unconstitutional because it authorizes a committee of Congress to overturn an executive decision.

(Choice C) Article II gives the President paramount authority in foreign affairs, so Congress could not have forced the President to sign the environmental treaty. But since Congress has the power to enact domestic laws, it can implement this program protecting areas in the United States despite the President's objection to the treaty.

(Choice D) Congress can require executive agencies to report their decisions to Congress if this is necessary and proper for (ie, reasonably related to) implementing federal law. But Congress cannot veto executive agency decisions without adhering to bicameralism and presentment.

Educational objective:

Congress can only overturn an executive agency's actions by enacting new legislation. This requires both (1) passage by majority vote in the House of Representatives and the Senate (ie, bicameralism) and (2) presentation to the President for approval or disapproval (ie, presentment).

References

• Gundy v. United States, 139 S. Ct. 2116, 2123 (2019) (explaining that the nondelegation doctrine allows Congress to delegate power as long as it provides an intelligible principle to guide the delegate's use of discretion).

• INS v. Chadha, 462 U.S. 919, 946–59 (1982) (striking down the congressional-veto provision of an immigration statute since it bypasses bicameralism and presentment).

explanation.zh:
不授权原则禁止国会授予纯粹的立法权(例如制定或废除法律)。但它允许国会将其附带权力(例如,管理联邦土地)下放给执行机构,如果它提供了一项可理解的原则——即明确规定:

• 政策大会力求推动(例如保护美国生物多样性丰富的地区)

• 执行这项政策的机构(例如,根据法令设立的机构)和

• 该机构的权力范围(例如,指定部分联邦土地列入环境保护方案)(选择B)。

但一旦国会将权力授予执行机构,国会就不能授权一个委员会否决(即推翻)该机构的行政决定。 此类决定只能通过新的立法推翻,它要求:

• 两院制——在众议院和参议院(不仅仅是国会委员会)均需获得多数票——和

• 向总统提交供批准或不批准(此处没有出现这种情况)。

因此,该章程违宪,因为它授权国会的一个委员会推翻一项行政决定.

(C选择)第二条赋予总统在外交事务上的最高权力,因此国会不可能强迫总统签署环境条约.但由于国会有权颁布国内法,因此尽管总统反对条约,国会仍可以在美国实施这个保护地区的方案.

(Choice D)国会可以要求执行机构向国会报告其决定,如果这是执行联邦法律(即与联邦法律有合理关系)所必要和适当的.但国会不能不坚持两院制和呈礼制而否决行政机构的决定.

国会只能通过颁布新的立法来推翻行政机构的行动,这需要:(1) 众议院和参议院以多数票通过(即两院制)和(2) 提交总统批准或不批准(即:页:1

stem: State A suffers from a high unemployment rate. To combat this problem, the State A legislature passed a statute requiring every business that sells over $5 million worth of goods each year in State A to annually buy goods produced in State A in an amount equal to half of its State A sales. Several persons and entities seek to challenge the constitutionality of this state statute in federal court.
stemZh: A州面临高失业率问题。为解决这一问题，A州议会通过了一项法律规定，要求每个在A州每年销售超过500万美元商品的商业实体，每年必须购买在A州生产的价值等于其A州销售额一半的商品。几名个人和实体试图在联邦法院挑战该州法律的合宪性。
ask: Which of the following persons or entities most clearly has standing to do so?
askZh: 以下哪位个人或实体最明显具有提起诉讼的资格？

options.en: A company that sells $3 million worth of goods in State A annually but currently purchases only $1 million in State A goods.
options.zh: 一家公司每年在A州销售300万美元的商品，但目前仅在A州购买100万美元的商品。

options.en: A distributor that currently does not sell or purchase goods in State A but expects to sell $15 million worth of goods in State A next fiscal year.
options.zh: 一家分销商目前不销售或购买A州的商品，但预计下财年将在A州销售1500万美元的商品。

options.en: A State B manufacturer that supplies 75 percent of the goods bought by a corporation with annual sales in State A of $10 million.
options.zh: B州的一家制造商，为一家在A州年销售额为1000万美元的公司购买了75%的商品。

options.en: The governor of State B on behalf of her state's businesses.
options.zh: B州州长代表其州的商业实体。

explanation.en:
A federal court will not hear a case unless the plaintiff has standing—ie, a personal stake in the outcome of the case. This requires the plaintiff to allege three elements:

• Injury-in-fact – actual or imminent harm that is concrete and particularized

• Causation – the injury is fairly traceable to the defendant's challenged conduct

• Redressability – a favorable judicial decision will likely remedy or prevent the injury Here, the State A statute requires businesses selling over $5 million worth of goods each year in State A to buy State A produced goods in an amount equal to half of their State A sales. As a result, a corporation annually selling $10 million worth of goods in State A but purchasing 75% of its goods from a State B manufacturer must now buy more State A goods. This will cause the State B manufacturer imminent financial harm that can be prevented if the statute is found unconstitutional. Therefore, the State B manufacturer likely has standing to contest the statute.

(Choice A) The statute does not apply to the company that annually sells $3 million (not over $5 million) worth of goods in State A. Therefore, this company does not have standing to contest the statute.

(Choice B) The distributor that currently does not sell or purchase goods in State A but expects to sell $15 million worth of goods in State A next year will need to purchase $7.5 million worth of State A goods if its prediction is accurate. But it lacks standing to contest the statute because this harm is speculative—not concrete.

(Choice D) The third-party standing doctrine allows an injured party to assert a third party's rights in limited circumstances. But the State B governor does not have standing to sue on behalf of her state's businesses because there is no evidence that the statute injured the governor.

Educational objective:

A plaintiff has standing to sue in federal court if he/she allegedly (1) suffered an injury-in-fact that (2) was caused by the defendant's challenged conduct and (3) is redressable by a

favorable judicial decision.

References

• Lujan v. Defs. of Wildlife, 504 U.S. 555, 560–61 (1992) (holding that standing requires proof of an injury-in-fact, causation, and redressability).

• 32 Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 577 (2019) (explaining the injury-in-fact element of standing).

explanation.zh:
联邦法院将不审理案件,除非原告具有诉讼资格——a案件结果涉及个人利益。这要求原告提出三个要素:

• 实际伤害 -- -- 具体和具体的实际或即将发生的伤害

• 因果关系——损害可以相当地追溯到被告受到质疑的行为

• 可补救性 -- -- 有利的司法裁决可能补救或防止损害。每年在A州销售价值超过500万美元的商品的企业购买A州生产的货物,其数额相当于A州因此,一家公司每年在A州出售价值1 000万美元的货物,但现在必须向B州制造商购买75%的货物。如果法规被裁定违宪,这将给B州制造商造成迫在眉睫的经济损失。 因此,B州制造商可能有权对法规提出质疑。

(Choice A) 章程不适用于在A州每年销售价值300万美元(不超过500万美元)的货物的公司。 因此,该公司没有资格对章程提出质疑。

(Choice B)目前并不在A州销售或购买商品但预计明年在A州销售价值1500万美元的商品的经销商,如果其预测准确,则需要购买价值750万美元的A州商品.但是,它没有资格对规约提出质疑,因为这种伤害是推测性的,而不是具体的。

(Choice D)第三方常设原则允许受害方在有限的情况下主张第三方的权利。但B州州长没有代表她州企业起诉的资格,因为没有证据表明法规伤害州长.

学习要点：

如果原告声称(1) 遭受了(2) 由被告受到质疑的行为造成的伤害,(3) 可由法院予以补救,则原告有权向联邦法院起诉。

有利的司法裁决。

• 32 Am. Jur. 2d 联邦法院第577条(2019年)(解释站立的事实伤害因素)。

stem: A federal statute imposes an excise tax of $100 on each new computer sold in the United States. It also appropriates the entire proceeds of that tax to a special fund, which is required to be used to purchase licenses for computer software that will be made available for use, free of charge, to any resident of the United States.
stemZh: 一项联邦法律对在美国销售的每一台新电脑征收 100 美元的附加税。该法律还规定将该税款的全部收入拨入一个特别基金，该基金必须用于购买计算机软件许可证，这些许可证将免费提供给任何美国居民使用。
ask: Is this statute constitutional?
askZh: 该法律是否合宪？

options.en: No, because the federal government may not impose any direct taxes on citizens of the United States.
options.zh: 否，因为联邦政府不得对美国公民征收任何直接税。

options.en: No, because the statute takes, without just compensation, the property of persons who hold patents or copyrights on computer software.
options.zh: 否，因为该法律未经正当补偿就剥夺了持有计算机软件专利或版权的人的财产。

options.en: Yes, because it is a reasonable exercise of Congress's powers to tax and spend for the general welfare.
options.zh: 是，因为这是国会行使征税和为公共福利支出权力的合理体现。

options.en: Yes, because the patent power authorizes Congress to impose reasonable charges on the sale of technology and to spend the proceeds of those charges to advance the use of technology in the United States.
options.zh: 是，因为专利权授权国会可以对技术销售征收合理费用，并将这些费用用于促进技术在美国的使用。

explanation.en:
Congressional taxing power

Type of tax

Definition Constitutional requirements

Direct • Taxes on persons or their property

• Payment cannot be avoided

Allowed if:

• apportioned proportionately among states

• reasonably related to revenue production Indirect • Taxes on goods/transactions

• Payment can be avoided or shifted to another (eg, consumer)

Allowed if:

• identical taxation in every state

• reasonably related to revenue production Export • Taxes on goods/services leaving the country

Not allowed

The taxing and spending clause gives Congress broad power to tax and spend for the general welfare (ie, any public purpose). Congress can use its taxing power:

• directly (ie, on persons or real property) – so long as the tax is apportioned proportionately among the states and reasonably related to revenue production

(Choice A) or

• indirectly (ie, on goods or transactions) – so long as the tax is identical in every state and reasonably related to revenue production.

Here, a federal statute imposes an indirect excise tax on new computers sold in the U.S. This tax is identical in every state since it applies to every sale of a new computer. Excise taxes are a common and reasonable way to raise revenue, and the proceeds of this tax are used for the general welfare—to provide free computer-software licenses to U.S. residents. Therefore, the statute is constitutional.

(Choice B) The takings clause prohibits the government from taking private property for public use without just compensation. But here, the federal government is purchasing licenses to use the computer software—not taking property from the holders of patents or copyrights on that software.

(Choice D) Under the copyright and patent clause, Congress can enact laws encouraging the production of creative works (copyright laws) and inventions (patent laws). But this clause does not authorize Congress to impose reasonable charges on, or spend proceeds from, the sale of these works or inventions.

Educational objective:

Congress has broad power to impose (1) direct taxes that are apportioned proportionately among the states and reasonably related to revenue production or (2) indirect taxes that are identical in every state and reasonably related to revenue production.

References

• Thomas v. United States, 192 U.S. 363, 371 (1904) (holding that a tax on the sale of stock is an indirect tax).

• Fernandez v. Wiener, 326 U.S. 340, 360–63 (1945) (upholding an indirect tax that is identical in every state).

国会征税权

税种

宪法要求

• 个人或财产税

• 无法避免付款

允许:

• 各国按比例分摊

• 与收入生产有合理关系的间接货物/交易税

• 付款可以避免或转嫁给他人(例如消费者)

允许:

• 各州征税相同

• 与收入生产有合理关系离开该国

不允许

税收和支出条款赋予国会征税和为一般福利(即任何公共目的)支出的广泛权力。

• 直接(即个人或不动产) -- -- 只要该税由各州按比例分摊并与收入生产有合理关系

(选择A)或

• 间接(即货物或交易)——只要各州的税收相同,并且与收入生产有合理关系。

在这里,一项联邦法规对在美国销售的新计算机征收间接消费税,这种税在每个州都是相同的,因为它适用于新计算机的每一次销售.货物税是增加收入的一种常见和合理的方式,这种税收的收益被用于一般福利 — — 向美国居民提供免费的计算机软件许可证。 因此,法规是宪法性的。

(Choice B) 取用条款禁止政府不经公正补偿而将私人财产用于公共用途.但是,联邦政府正在购买使用计算机软件的许可证,而不是从该软件的专利或版权持有人手中夺取财产。

(Choice D)根据版权和专利条款,国会可以颁布法律鼓励创作作品(版权法)和发明(专利法)的制作.但这一条款并未授权国会对这些作品或发明的销售收取合理费用或花费收益.

学习要点：

国会拥有广泛权力,可以征收(1)由各州按比例分摊的与收入生产有合理关系的直接税,或者(2)每个州相同且与收入生产有合理关系的间接税.

参考资料

• Thomas诉美国案,192 U.S.363,371 (1904)(认为出售股票税是间接税)。

· Fernandez诉Wiener案,326 U.S. 340, 360–63(1945年)(持有每个州相同的间接税)。

stem:
Congress passed a statute that expressly authorizes suits for damages in federal courts against state governments that violate federal copyright laws.

A photographer sued a state in a federal district court for damages pursuant to the federal statute. The photographer claimed that the state published her copyrighted photographs and videos on its website without her permission. The state has moved to dismiss the photographer's suit.
stemZh:
国会通过了一项法律，明确授权在联邦法院对违反联邦版权法的州政府提起损害赔偿诉讼。

一名摄影师根据联邦法律在联邦地区法院起诉了一个州，声称该州在其网站上未经其同意发布了她的受版权保护的照片和视频。该州提出了驳回诉讼动议。
ask: Should the court grant the state's motion?
askZh: 法院应否批准该州的驳回动议？

options.en: No, because Article I grants Congress the power to enact laws that protect copyrighted materials.
options.zh: 不应批准，因为第一修正案授予国会制定保护版权材料法律的权力。

options.en: No, because Articles I and III grant Congress the power to regulate the jurisdiction and procedures of the federal courts.
options.zh: 不应批准，因为第一修正案和第三修正案授予国会制定联邦法院管辖权和程序的权力。

options.en: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits the action for damages against the state in federal court.
options.zh: 应批准，因为第十一修正案禁止在联邦法院对州提起损害赔偿诉讼。

options.en: Yes, because the Tenth Amendment prohibits the federal government from compelling states to act.
options.zh: 应批准，因为第十修正案禁止联邦政府强制州采取行动。

explanation.en:
Eleventh Amendment

(state immunity from suit in federal court)

Immunity • Suit brought by private party or foreign government

• Suit against state official violating state law

• Exceptions: – State consents to suit – Immunity removed by 13th, 14th, or 15th Amendment – State official sued for injunctive or declaratory relief – Damages to be paid by state officer personally (not state treasury) – State official sued for prospective (not retroactive) damages to be paid by state treasury No immunity

• Suit brought by United States or other state

• Suit against local government (eg, counties, municipalities)

• Bankruptcy proceedings The Eleventh Amendment generally prohibits private parties and foreign governments from suing a state for money damages or equitable relief in federal court. Congress can abrogate (ie, repeal) this immunity if it is clearly acting to enforce a Civil War Amendment—ie, the Thirteenth, Fourteenth, or Fifteenth Amendment (not seen here). Congress may then enact appropriate remedial legislation expressly subjecting the states to private suits for damages in federal court.

However, Congress cannot abrogate a state's Eleventh Amendment immunity through its other powers.* This includes its Article I power to enact laws protecting copyrighted materials (Choice A). This also includes its power under Articles I and III to regulate the jurisdiction of the federal courts (Choice B). Therefore, the court will likely grant the state's motion to dismiss the photographer's suit pursuant to the Eleventh Amendment.

*The lone exception to this rule is that Congress may subject nonconsenting states to bankruptcy proceedings through the Article I bankruptcy clause. The Supreme Court has justified this exception based on the bankruptcy clause's unique history and exceptionalism.

(Choice D) The Tenth Amendment prohibits the federal government from compelling states to enact state laws or enforce federal laws. However, states can be subjected to suits for damages in federal court if Congress validly abrogates state immunity.

Educational objective:

The Eleventh Amendment generally grants states immunity from suits for damages. Congress can abrogate this immunity when it clearly acts to enforce a Civil War Amendment but cannot do so through its other powers—eg, its powers to protect copyrights and regulate federal court jurisdiction.

References

• Allen v. Cooper, 140 S. Ct. 994, 1007 (2020) (holding that Congress cannot abrogate the states' Eleventh Amendment immunity through the Article I copyright clause).

第十一次修正

(国家豁免联邦法院的诉讼)

• 私人或外国政府提出的诉讼

• 对违反州法律的国家官员提起诉讼

• 例外:- 国家同意诉 - 第13、14或15修正案取消豁免 - 国家官员被起诉要求强制或宣告性救济 - 国家官员个人(不是国库)应支付的损害 - 国家官员被起诉预期(不是)国家财政应支付的赔偿

• 美国或其他国家提出的诉讼

• 起诉地方政府(例如县、市)

• 破产程序 第十一修正案一般禁止私人当事方和外国政府向联邦法院起诉某州要求金钱损失或公平救济。如果国会显然采取行动执行内战修正案,即第十三、第十四或第十五修正案(此处不见),可以废除(即废除)这一豁免。然后,国会可以颁布适当的补救立法,明确要求各州在联邦法院接受私人损害赔偿诉讼。

然而,国会不能通过其他权力来废除州第十一修正案的豁免权。 * 这包括其第一条赋予的颁布保护版权材料的法律的权力(Choice A)。这也包括它根据第一条和第三条拥有的规范联邦法院管辖权的权力(Choice B),因此,法院可能批准该州根据第十一项修正案提出的驳回摄影师诉讼的动议.

* 这项规则的唯一例外是,国会可以通过第一条破产条款对不同意的国家进行破产程序。 最高法院根据破产条款的独特历史和例外主义为这一例外提供了理由。

(Choice D)第十修正案禁止联邦政府强迫各州颁布州法律或执行联邦法律,不过,如果国会有效废除州豁免权,各州可以向联邦法院提起损害赔偿诉讼.

学习要点：

《第十一修正案》一般都赋予国家不受损害诉讼的豁免权。 国会在明确采取行动执行《内战修正案》时,可以废除这一豁免权,但不能通过其其他权力,例如保护版权和管理联邦权力。法院管辖权。

参考资料

• Allen诉Cooper案,140 S. Ct. 994, 1007 (2020年)(认为国会不能通过第一条版权条款废除各州的第十一次修正案豁免)。

stem:
Congress recently enacted a statute imposing severe criminal penalties on anyone engaged in trading in the stock market who, in the course of that trading, takes "unfair advantage" of other investors who are also trading in the stock market. The statute does not define the term "unfair advantage." There have been no prosecutions under this new statute.

The members of an association of law school professors that is dedicated to increasing the clarity of the language used in criminal statutes believe that this statute is unconstitutionally vague. Neither the association nor any of its members is currently engaged in, or intends in the future to engage in, trading in the stock market.

The association and its members bring suit against the Attorney General of the United States in a federal district court, seeking an injunction against the enforcement of this statute on the ground that it is unconstitutional.
stemZh:
国会最近通过了一项法律，对任何在股票市场进行交易的人施加严重的刑事处罚，如果在进行该交易时，利用"不公平优势"对也在股票市场进行交易的其他投资者造成损害。该法律并未对"不公平优势"一词进行定义。截至目前，尚未有人根据这项新法律被起诉。

一个致力于提高刑事法律条文中语言清晰度的法学院教授协会的成员认为，这项法律是违宪的模糊条款。该协会及其任何成员目前并未参与，也无意未来参与股票市场的交易。

该协会及其成员在联邦地区法院对美国司法部长提起诉讼，要求禁止执行该法律，理由是该法律违宪。
ask: May the federal court determine the merits of this suit?
askZh: 联邦法院能否确定此案的实质问题？

options.en: No, because a suit for an injunction against enforcement of a criminal statute may not be brought in federal court at any time prior to a bona fide effort to enforce that statute.
options.zh: 不能，因为对执行刑事法律的禁令诉讼不能在任何时间在联邦法院提起，直到对该法律进行真正的执行努力。

options.en: No, because the plaintiffs do not have an interest in invalidating this statute that is adequate to ensure that the suit presents an Article III controversy.
options.zh: 不能，因为原告没有足够的利益去使该诉讼构成《联邦民事诉讼规则》第三条的争议。

options.en: Yes, because the plaintiffs seek real relief of a conclusive nature—an injunction against enforcement of this statute.
options.zh: 可以，因为原告寻求的是具有决定性质的实质性救济——禁止执行该法律的禁令。

options.en: Yes, because the suit involves a dispute over the constitutionality of a federal statute.
options.zh: 可以，因为此案涉及对联邦法律合宪性的争议。

explanation.en:
Article III only allows federal courts to determine the merits of actual cases or controversies. The doctrine of standing ensures that this requirement is met by requiring the plaintiff to show that he/she has a personal stake in the outcome of the case. This exists when the plaintiff has suffered an injury-in-fact—ie, concrete and particularized harm that is actual or imminent—that was caused by the challenged conduct and is redressable by a favorable decision.

Here, the association and its members sued in federal court to challenge the constitutionality of the stock market statute. But the statute has not caused these plaintiffs an injury-in-fact because neither is currently engaged in, or intends to engage in, stock market trading (no actual or imminent harm). This means that the plaintiffs do not have an interest in invalidating the statute that would satisfy Article III's case-or-controversy requirement. As a result, the court cannot determine the merits of their suit.

(Choice A) Even if a criminal statute has not been enforced, a suit for an injunction to prevent such enforcement may be brought in federal court if the plaintiff shows that the statute poses an immediate threat of harm (not seen here).

(Choice C) The injunction would provide real and conclusive relief. But the federal court does not have the power to issue an injunction in a suit that does not meet the case-or-controversy requirement (as seen here).

(Choice D) Federal courts have subject-matter jurisdiction over suits involving the constitutionality of federal statutes. But the court cannot hear the merits of such a suit when, as here, the plaintiffs lack standing to assert their constitutional challenge.

Educational objective:

Under the doctrine of standing, an injury-in-fact exists when the plaintiff has suffered concrete and particularized harm that is actual or imminent.

References

• Lujan v. Defs. of Wildlife, 504 U.S. 555, 560–61 (1992) (holding that standing requires proof of an injury-in-fact, causation, and redressability).

explanation.zh:
第三条只允许联邦法院确定实际案件或争议的案情,诉讼资格原则通过要求原告证明自己在案件结果中有个人利益,确保满足这一要求。当原告遭受实际或即将发生的实际、具体和具体损害时,即为存在这种情况,这种损害是由受到质疑的行为造成的,可通过有利的裁决予以补救。

在此,协会及其成员在联邦法院起诉,质疑股票市场法规的合宪性.但该法规并没有给这些原告造成实际伤害,因为目前没有或打算进行股票市场交易(没有实际或即将发生的伤害)。这意味着原告没有兴趣使符合第三条案件或争议要求的法规无效,因此,法院无法确定其诉讼案情。

(Choice A)即使没有执行刑事法规,如果原告表明法规构成直接的伤害威胁(此处不见),也可以向联邦法院提起禁止执行令的诉讼.

(C) 强制令将提供真实和决定性的补救。 但联邦法院无权在不符合案件或争议要求的诉讼中发布强制令(如本文所示 ) 。

(Choice D ) 联邦法院对涉及联邦法规合宪性的诉讼拥有属事管辖权。 但法院无法审理这种诉讼的案情,因为原告在这里没有资格提出宪法质疑。

学习要点：

根据诉讼资格原则,当原告遭受实际或即将发生的具体和具体损害时,即存在事实损害。

参考资料

· Lujan诉Devs of Wildish, 504 U.S. 555, 560-61(1992年)(认为这种地位需要证明事实伤害、因果关系和可补救性)。

stem:
Congress enacted a statute providing grants of federal funds for the restoration and preservation of courthouses that were built before 1900 and are still in use. The statute contains an inseverable condition requiring that any courthouse restored with the aid of such a grant must be equipped with ramps and other facilities necessary to accommodate physically handicapped people.

A state law requires public buildings in the state to have ramps and other facilities for handicapped people. It exempts from those requirements any building that is more than 70 years old if the State Board of Architects finds that the installation of such facilities would destroy the architectural integrity of the building.

A county courthouse in the state was built in 1895 and is still in use. It does not contain ramps or other special facilities for handicapped people. The State Board of Architects has determined that the installation of those facilities would destroy the architectural integrity of the building. Nevertheless, the county applies for a federal grant to restore and preserve that county's courthouse.
stemZh:
国会通过了一项法律，提供联邦资金补助用于修复和保存建于1900年之前且仍在使用的法院建筑。该法律包含一个不可分割的条件，要求任何借助此类补助进行修复的法院建筑必须配备坡道和其他设施，以方便身体残疾人士使用。

该州法律要求该州的公共建筑必须配备坡道和其他设施，以方便残疾人士使用。但该法律豁免任何超过70年的建筑，如果州建筑师委员会认定安装这些设施会破坏建筑的建筑完整性，则不适用这些要求。

该州的一个县法院建筑建于1895年，仍在使用，但该建筑没有坡道或其他特殊设施方便残疾人士使用。州建筑师委员会已认定安装这些设施会破坏该建筑的建筑完整性。尽管如此，该县仍申请联邦补助，以修复和保存该县的法院建筑。
ask: If the county restores the courthouse with the aid of a federal restoration and preservation grant, is the county bound to install ramps and other facilities for handicapped people in that building?
askZh: 如果该县借助联邦修复和保存补助修复该法院建筑，该县是否必须在该建筑中安装坡道和其他方便残疾人士使用的设施？

options.en: No, because any acceptance of this condition by the county would, as a matter of law, be considered to be under duress.
options.zh: 否，因为该县接受该条件的行为，从法律上讲，将被视为受到胁迫。

options.en: No, because the Constitution does not authorize the federal government to direct the actions of the states or any of their political subdivisions with respect to matters affecting their own governmental buildings.
options.zh: 否，因为宪法并未授权联邦政府指导各州或其政治附属机构在涉及其自身政府建筑事项上的行为。

options.en: Yes, because Congress may impose reasonable conditions related to the public welfare on grants of federal funds to public bodies when the public bodies are free to accept or reject the grants.
options.zh: 是，因为国会可以在公共机构接受或拒绝补助时，对联邦资金补助施加与公共福利相关的合理条件。

options.en: Yes, because the rights of handicapped and disabled people are fundamental rights that take precedence, as a constitutional matter, over considerations of architectural integrity.
options.zh: 是，因为残疾人士的权利是基本权利，在宪法问题上，这些权利优先于建筑完整性的考虑。

explanation.en:
Conditional federal funding

(Article I, section 8 spending clause)

Conditions must meet all the following criteria:

• clearly stated & unambiguous

• reasonably related to federal interest in funded program

• do not require states to engage in unconstitutional activity

• do not unduly coerce states into accepting The taxing and spending clause gives Congress broad discretion to tax and spend for the general welfare (ie, for any public purpose). Congress may use its spending power to incentivize state or local governments to act in certain ways by placing conditions on their receipt of federal funds. But these conditions are only valid if they:

• are clearly stated and unambiguous so that potential recipients may make an informed decision

• are reasonably related to the purpose for which the funds will be expended

• do not require recipients to engage in unconstitutional activity and

• are not unduly coercive—ie, are not so extreme that they amount to a "gun to the head." Here, Congress imposed a condition on the receipt of federal grants for the restoration and preservation of historic courthouses (public welfare). That condition is valid—and the county will be bound to that condition if it restores its courthouse with the aid of such a grant—because:

• it unambiguously requires any courthouse restored with the aid of such a grant to be equipped with facilities for handicapped people

• installing handicap facilities in courthouses is reasonably related to restoring and preserving those buildings

• recipients are not required to do anything unconstitutional and

• being required to install handicap facilities is a relatively minor condition for receiving funds to restore and preserve an entire courthouse (ie, no undue coercion)

(Choice A).

(Choice B) Under the Tenth Amendment, the federal government cannot direct states or their political subdivisions (eg, counties) to enact legislation or enforce federal law. But Congress may incentivize them to act through conditional federal funding (as seen here).

(Choice D) Handicapped and disabled people enjoy the same fundamental rights as everyone else—but no such rights are implicated here.

Educational objective:

Conditional federal funding is valid if the conditions (1) are clear and unambiguous, (2) are reasonably related to the purpose for which the funds are expended, (3) do not require recipients to engage in unconstitutional activity, and (4) are not unduly coercive.

References

• South Dakota v. Dole, 483 U.S. 203, 207–12 (1987) (holding that conditions on states' receipt of federal funds must be unambiguous, related to the purpose of the funding, and noncoercive).

explanation.zh:
有条件的联邦供资

(第一条第8节支出条款)

条件必须符合下列所有标准:

• 明确声明和毫不含糊

• 合理涉及联邦对资助方案的兴趣

• 不要求各国从事违宪活动

• 不得不适当地强迫国家接受税收和开支条款,使国会有广泛的征税和开支的自由裁量权(即为任何公共目的)。国会可以利用其开支权力激励州或地方政府以某些方式采取行动,在接受联邦资金时附加条件。 但是,这些条件只有在以下情况下才有效:

• 明确和毫不含糊,以便潜在接受者作出知情的决定

• 与资金用途有合理关系

• 不要求接受者从事违宪活动;

——不是不适当的胁迫性——不是那么极端,以至于相当于"枪指着头". )在这里,国会规定了一个条件,要求接受联邦拨款,以恢复和保护历史的法院(公共福利).这一条件是有效的——如果该县在这笔赠款的帮助下恢复其法院,则将受到这一条件的约束——因为:

• 毫不含糊地要求在这种赠款的帮助下恢复的任何法院都配备残疾人设施

• 在法院安装残疾人设施与修复和维护这些建筑有合理关系

• 不要求受援者从事任何违宪行为;

• 要求安装残疾人设施是获得资金以恢复和维护整个法院的一个相对次要的条件(即没有不当的胁迫)

(Choice A) (英语).

(Choice B)根据第十修正案,联邦政府不能指示各州或其政治分支(如县)颁布立法或执行联邦法律。 但国会可以鼓励他们通过有条件的联邦资助(如本文所示)采取行动。

残疾人和残疾人与其他人一样享有同样的基本权利,但这里没有涉及这些权利。

学习要点：

如果条件(1)明确和毫不含糊,(2)与资金用途合理相关,(3)不要求接受者从事违宪活动,(4)不过分强制,则有条件的联邦供资是有效的。

参考资料

• 南达科他州诉Dole案,483 U.S.203, 207–12(1987年)(认为各州接受联邦资金的条件必须明确,与资金目的有关,且不强制)。

stem: A newly enacted federal statute appropriates $100 million in federal funds to support basic research by universities located in the United States. The statute provides that "the 10 best universities in the United States" will each receive $10 million. It also provides that "the 10 best universities" shall be "determined by a poll of the presidents of all the universities in the nation, to be conducted by the United States Department of Education." In responding to that poll, each university president is required to apply the well-recognized and generally accepted standards of academic quality that are specified in the statute. The provisions of the statute are inseverable.
stemZh: 一项新颁布的联邦法律拨款 1 亿美元联邦资金，用于支持位于美国的大学进行基础研究。该法律规定，"美国最好的 10 所大学"将各获得 1000 万美元。它还规定，"美国最好的 10 所大学"将由美国教育部进行的全国大学校长调查来确定。在回应该调查时，每位大学校长必须应用法律中规定的、被广泛认可且普遍接受的学术质量标准。该法律的条款是不可分割的。
ask: Which of the following statements about this statute is correct?
askZh: 以下关于该法律的陈述哪一项是正确的？

options.en: The statute is constitutional, because Congress has plenary authority to determine the objects of its spending and the methods used to achieve them, so long as they may reasonably be deemed to serve the general welfare and do not violate any prohibitory language in the Constitution.
options.zh: 该法律是合宪的，因为国会拥有充分的权力来确定其资金的使用对象和实现目标的方法，只要这些方法可以合理地被认为服务于公共福利，并且不违反宪法中的任何禁止性条款。

options.en: The statute is unconstitutional, because the limitation on recipients to the 10 best universities is arbitrary and capricious and denies other high-quality universities the equal protection of the laws.
options.zh: 该法律是违宪的，因为将受资助者限制为"美国最好的 10 所大学"是任意和专断的，并且剥夺了其他高质量大学获得法律平等保护的权利。

options.en: The statute is unconstitutional, because the reliance by Congress on a poll of individuals who are not federal officials to determine the recipients of its appropriated funds is an unconstitutional delegation of legislative power.
options.zh: 该法律是违宪的，因为国会依赖于对非联邦官员的个人进行调查来确定其拨款的受资助者，这是对立法权的违宪委任。

options.en: The validity of the statute is nonjusticiable, because the use by Congress of its spending power necessarily involves political considerations that must be resolved finally by those branches of the government that are closest to the political process.
options.zh: 该法律的有效性不可诉，因为国会使用其支出权力的手段必然涉及政治考量，这些考量必须由最接近政治过程的政府分支最终解决。

explanation.en:
Congress's taxing & spending powers

(U.S. Const. art. I, sec. 8, cl. 1)

Taxing • Direct taxes – must be: – apportioned evenly among states and – reasonably related to revenue raising

• Indirect taxes – must be: – uniformly applied in every state and – reasonably related to revenue raising

• Export taxes – always unconstitutional Spending • Funds must be spent for general welfare

• Conditions on receipt of funds must: – be clearly stated & unambiguous – be reasonably related to federal interest in funded program – not require states to engage in unconstitutional activity and – not unduly coerce states into accepting The taxing and spending clause gives Congress the power to spend federal revenue for the general welfare—ie, for any public purpose. Aside from this narrow constraint, Congress has plenary (ie, absolute) authority to determine the objects of its spending and the methods used to achieve them. But when doing so, Congress cannot violate any prohibitory language in the Constitution (eg, equal protection clause).

Here, the federal statute appropriates $100 million in federal funds to support basic research by universities located in the United States. Such research may reasonably be deemed to serve the general welfare, and the statute does not violate any prohibitory language in the Constitution. And since Congress has plenary authority to determine its spending goals and the methods for achieving them, the statute is constitutional.

(Choice B) Equal protection principles extend to all persons and organizations. And though the statute limits funding to the 10 best universities, all universities are eligible to receive votes and have their presidents' votes counted. Therefore, the statute does not deny other high-quality universities the equal protection of the laws.

(Choice C) Congress can delegate legislative power if it provides intelligible guidelines for the delegates to follow. This standard is met here since Congress has clearly directed the Department of Education to conduct a poll of university presidents and specified the standards that must be applied in responding to that poll.

(Choice D) Federal courts are prohibited from adjudicating political questions—ie, issues that (1) are reserved to the executive or legislative branch or (2) lack judicially manageable standards for resolution. But since courts regularly determine the constitutionality of federal statutes, this prohibition does not apply.

Educational objective:

The taxing and spending clause gives Congress broad power to spend federal revenue, as long as the spending (1) is for the general welfare and (2) does not violate any prohibitory language in the Constitution.

References

• South Dakota v. Dole, 483 U.S. 203, 207–08 (1987) (explaining that Congress's spending power must serve a public purpose and cannot violate any prohibitory language of the Constitution).

explanation.zh:
国会的税收和开支权力

(《美国法典》第1条第8款,第1项)

• 直接税必须:国家间平均分摊,而且与税收有合理关系

• 间接税必须:在每一个州统一适用,而且与税收有合理联系

• 出口税——总是违宪的开支——资金必须用于一般福利

• 接受资金的条件必须:明确和毫不含糊,与联邦对资助方案的兴趣有合理联系,不要求各州从事违宪活动,不过分强迫各州接受征税和支出。条款赋予国会将联邦收入用于一般福利——即任何公共福利——的权力。除了这一狭隘的制约因素之外,国会还有全体会议(即绝对)的权力。确定支出对象和用于实现这些目标的方法。但在这样做时,国会不能违反宪法中的任何禁止性语言(如平等保护条款).

在这里,联邦法规拨出1亿美元的联邦资金支持位于美国的大学进行基础研究.此类研究可被合理地视为服务于一般福利,法规并不违反《宪法》中的任何禁止性语言。由于国会拥有全权来决定其开支目标以及实现这些目的的方法,因此章程是宪法性的.

平等保护原则适用于所有个人和组织。 尽管法规将资金限制在10所最好的大学,但所有大学都有资格获得选票,并拥有总统选票。因此,该法规并不否认其他高素质大学受到法律的平等保护。

(选择C)国会如果为代表们提供可理解的指导,可以授予立法权.由于国会明确指示教育部对大学校长进行民意调查,并具体规定了在对民意调查作出反应时必须采用的标准,因此,这一标准在此得到满足。

(选择D) 联邦法院不得裁定政治问题,即(1) 保留给行政部门或立法部门的问题,或(2) 缺乏司法上可管理的解决标准的问题。但是,由于法院经常确定联邦法规是否符合宪法,因此这一禁令不适用.

学习要点：

税收和支出条款赋予国会使用联邦收入的广泛权力,只要支出(1)用于一般福利和(2)不违反宪法中任何禁止性语言.

参考资料

· 南达科他州诉多尔案,483 U.S.203,207-08(1987)(解释国会的消费权必须服务于公共目的,不能违反《宪法》的任何禁止性语言)。

stem:
The U.S. House of Representatives authorized a House committee to investigate current election laws and develop new legislation to close any loopholes that permit foreign governments to interfere in the U.S. election process. The House authorized this investigation because of widespread reports of foreign interference in the most recent presidential election. As part of its investigation, the House committee issued subpoenas to various financial institutions that sought the President's financial records for the years preceding her election to the presidency. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) possesses nearly the same information as the financial records sought by the House committee.

The President filed suit against the financial institutions in federal court to enjoin them from complying with the congressional subpoenas.
stemZh:
美国众议院授权一个众议院委员会调查现行选举法律，并制定新立法以填补任何允许外国政府干涉美国选举过程的漏洞。众议院授权此次调查是因为最近总统选举中广泛报告了外国干涉的情况。作为调查的一部分，众议院委员会向多家金融机构发出传票，要求提供总统就职前几年的财务记录。美国国税局（IRS）拥有几乎与该委员会所寻求的财务记录相同的信息。

总统在联邦法院提起诉讼，要求阻止金融机构遵守国会的传票。
ask: Which of the following is the best argument in favor of the President's effort to obtain the injunction?
askZh: 以下哪一项是支持总统获得禁令的最佳论点？

options.en: A congressional subpoena that seeks the President's personal information violates the separation of powers.
options.zh: 寻求总统个人信息的国会传票违反了权力分立原则。

options.en: A subpoena is unnecessary when the information that Congress seeks can be reasonably obtained from a source other than the President.
options.zh: 当国会寻求的信息可以从总统以外的来源合理获得时，传票是不必要的。

options.en: The power to conduct investigations or issue subpoenas is not among the powers of Congress enumerated in Article I.
options.zh: 调查或发出传票的权力并不属于《宪法》第一条规定列举的国会权力之一。

options.en: The President's private information from before taking office is protected by executive privilege.
options.zh: 总统就职前的私人信息受到行政特权的保护。

explanation.en:
The necessary and proper clause allows Congress to take actions that are reasonably necessary to carry out its enumerated Article I powers. Although conducting investigations and issuing subpoenas are not enumerated powers, investigations are reasonably necessary to obtain information that will help Congress carry out its enumerated powers (Choice C). As part of an investigation, a congressional committee may issue subpoenas to compel testimony and/or the production of documents and tangible things related to the investigation.

However, a congressional subpoena that seeks the President's personal information raises significant separation of powers issues between these two branches of government. Without proper limitations, Congress could usurp presidential authority. But prohibiting all subpoenas seeking the President's personal information would undercut Congress's investigatory power (Choice A). As a result, a congressional committee seeking the President's personal information must provide detailed evidence that the subpoena:

• is necessary to obtain the information sought because that information cannot be reasonably obtained from another source

• is limited in scope to a valid legislative purpose (not vague or overbroad) and

• does not impose an undue burden on the President's time and attention.

Here, the IRS possesses nearly the same information as the financial records sought by the House committee. Therefore, the President's best argument to enjoin the financial institutions from complying with the congressional subpoenas is that they are unnecessary since the information that Congress seeks can be reasonably obtained from a source other than the President—the IRS.

(Choice D) The President may assert executive privilege to prevent the disclosure of confidential documents and communications made in performance of official duties and responsibilities—not private functions (eg, the President's personal financial records sought here).

Educational objective:

A congressional committee seeking the President's personal information must provide detailed evidence that a subpoena (1) is necessary to obtain the information, (2) is limited in scope to a valid legislative purpose, and (3) does not unduly burden the President's time and attention.

References

• Trump v. Mazars, USA, Ltd. Liab. P'ship, 140 S. Ct. 2019, 2035–36 (2020) (setting forth the requirements for a congressional subpoena of the President's personal documents).

explanation.zh:
必要和适当的条款允许国会采取合理必要的行动,以行使第一条规定的权力。虽然进行调查和发出传票的权力没有列举,但调查是获得有助于国会行使其列举权力的资料的合理必要的(Choice C)。作为调查的一部分,国会委员会可以发出传票,强迫作证和(或)出示与调查有关的文件和有形物品。

然而,寻求总统个人信息的国会传票引起了政府这两个分支之间的重大分权问题。 没有适当的限制,国会可能篡夺总统权力。但禁止所有寻求总统个人信息的传票会削弱国会的调查权(Choice A),因此,寻求总统个人信息的国会委员会必须提供详细证据证明传票:

• 获取所要求的信息是必要的,因为无法合理地从其他来源获取这一信息

• 范围限于有效的立法目的(不含糊或过于宽泛)和

• 不给主席的时间和注意力造成不应有的负担。

在这方面,国税局掌握的资料与众议院委员会所要求的财务记录几乎相同。因此,总统要求金融机构遵守国会传票的最佳论点是,这些传票是不必要的,因为国会所寻求的信息可以合理地从总统以外的来源获得——即:国税局.

(Choice D) 总统可行使行政特权,防止披露履行公务和责任时发表的机密文件和来文,而不是私人职能(例如在此要求的总统个人财务记录)。

学习要点：

寻求总统个人信息的国会委员会必须提供详细证据,证明传票(1)是获取信息所必需的,(2)范围限于有效的立法目的,(3)不会给总统的时间造成不适当的负担.注意了 注意点
