stem:
A federal statute provides states with funds to establish a disability benefits program. The statute requires a participating state to disburse the benefits to eligible applicants within one month after an application is approved. A commissioner of a State A agency that established a disability benefits program pursuant to the federal statute issued a regulation that delayed the disbursement of benefits until six months after an application is approved.

Hundreds of residents of State A whose disability benefits were delayed because of the regulation have filed a class action against the commissioner in federal district court, arguing that the regulation violates the federal statute. The residents seek retroactive damages for the payment of the withheld benefits to be paid by the state treasury and an injunction to compel payment of future benefits. The commissioner has moved to dismiss the action and alleges that the requested relief is a violation of the Eleventh Amendment.
stemZh:
一项联邦法律为各州提供资金，以建立残疾补助金计划。该法律要求参与该计划的州在申请被批准后一个月内向符合条件的申请人发放补助金。A州的一个机构负责人根据联邦法律建立了残疾补助金计划，颁布了一项规定，将补助金的发放时间推迟到申请被批准后六个月。

由于该规定导致A州数百名残疾补助金被延迟发放的居民在联邦地区法院对负责人提起集体诉讼，认为该规定违反了联邦法律。居民要求追索性赔偿，即由州财政支付被扣留的补助金，并要求颁布禁令，强制未来补助金的支付。负责人提出了驳回诉讼的动议，并声称所要求的救济措施违反了第十一修正案。
ask: Should the federal court hear the merits of the residents' suit?
askZh: 联邦法院是否应审理居民的诉讼请求？

options.en: No, because the commissioner is immune from suit under the Eleventh Amendment.
options.zh: 否，因为负责人根据第十一修正案享有诉讼豁免权。

options.en: Yes, but only on the request for retroactive damages for the withheld benefits.
options.zh: 是，但仅限于追索性赔偿请求，即被扣留补助金的赔偿。

options.en: Yes, but only on the request for the injunction to compel payment of future benefits.
options.zh: 是，但仅限于颁布禁令，强制未来补助金支付的请求。

options.en: Yes, on both because the suit is not subject to the Eleventh Amendment.

explanation.en:
Eleventh Amendment

(state immunity from suit in federal court)

Immunity • Suit brought by private party or foreign government

• Suit against state official violating state law

• Exceptions: – State consents to suit – Immunity removed by 13th, 14th, or 15th Amendment – State official sued for injunctive or declaratory relief – Damages to be paid by state officer personally (not state treasury) – State official sued for prospective (not retroactive) damages to be paid by state treasury No immunity

• Suit brought by United States or other state

• Suit against local government (eg, counties, municipalities)

• Bankruptcy proceedings The Eleventh Amendment generally bars private parties from suing a state in federal court without the state's consent. This immunity extends to suits against a state official for violating federal law when the state treasury, rather than the official, will be forced to pay damages that allegedly occurred before the action commenced (ie, retroactive damages). However, the Eleventh Amendment does not prohibit suits against a state official when:

• the official will pay the damages from his/her own pocket, which occurs when the official is sued for actions taken as an individual rather than as a government official or

• the suit seeks a declaratory judgment or injunction, even if such relief would force the state treasury to pay money in the future to comply with the court order (ie, prospective damages).

Here, the residents filed a class action in federal court against the state commissioner, arguing that the regulation delaying their disability benefits violates the federal statute. The court may hear their request for an injunction to compel payment of future benefits because such payments would constitute prospective damages (Choice A). However, the court may not hear the merits of their request for payment of the withheld benefits since such payments would constitute retroactive damages that would be paid by the state treasury (Choices B & D).

Educational objective:

The Eleventh Amendment bars suits against state officials for violating federal law when the state would pay retroactive damages. But it allows such suits when (1) the official will pay the damages or (2) the suit seeks declaratory or injunctive relief, even if the state would have to pay prospective damages under the court order.

References

• Ex parte Young, 209 U.S. 123, 159–60 (1908) (describing when the Eleventh Amendment does not bar suits in federal court against state officials for violations of federal law).

• Edelman v. Jordan, 415 U.S. 651, 675–77 (1974) (holding that actions for injunctive relief against state officials in federal court are limited to those that result in the future payment of monetary damages from the state treasury).

• 32A Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 916 (2020) (explaining that the Eleventh Amendment bars citizens from suing state officials in federal court unless certain exceptions apply).

explanation.zh:
第十一次修正

(国家豁免联邦法院的诉讼)

• 私人或外国政府提出的诉讼

• 对违反州法律的国家官员提起诉讼

• 例外:- 国家同意诉 - 第13、14或15修正案取消豁免 - 国家官员被起诉要求强制或宣告性救济 - 国家官员个人(不是国库)应支付的损害 - 国家官员被起诉预期(不是)国家财政应支付的赔偿

• 美国或其他国家提出的诉讼

• 起诉地方政府(例如县、市)

• 破产程序 第十一修正案一般禁止私人当事方未经州同意向联邦法院起诉州。这一豁免适用于针对州官员违反联邦法律的诉讼,因为州国库而不是官员将被迫支付据称在诉讼开始前发生的损害(即追溯性损害)。然而,第十一修正案并不禁止在下列情况下对国家官员提起诉讼:

• 官员将自费支付赔偿金,这发生在官员因作为个人而不是作为政府官员采取行动而受到起诉时;

• 诉讼寻求宣告性判决或强制令,即使这种减免会迫使国库今后支付款项以遵守法院命令(即预期损害)。

在此,居民在联邦法院对州专员提起集体诉讼,认为推迟其残疾津贴的条例违反了联邦法规。法院可以审理他们关于强制支付未来福利的强制令的请求,因为这种支付将构成预期损害(选择A)。然而,法院可能不审理他们要求支付被扣福利的案情,因为这种支付将构成国家财政(Choices B & D)将支付的追溯性损害赔偿。

学习要点：

《第十一修正案》禁止在州政府支付追溯赔偿金时对违反联邦法律的州官员提起诉讼。但是,当(1) 官员将支付损害赔偿金或(2) 诉讼寻求宣告性或强制性补救时,即使国家根据法院命令必须支付预期损害赔偿金,也允许提出此类诉讼。

参考资料

· Ex Parte Young,209 U.S.123,159–60 (1908)(说明当第十一修正案没有禁止在联邦法院起诉违反联邦法律的州官员时)。

· Edelman诉约旦案,415 U.S. 651, 675–77(1974)(认为联邦法院对州官员采取的强制救济行动仅限于导致今后从国库支付金钱损失的行动)。

• 32A Am. Jur. 2d联邦法院§916(2020年)(解释第十一修正案禁止公民在联邦法院起诉州官员,除非适用某些例外)。

stem:
In response to the need for additional toxic waste landfills in a state, the state's legislature enacted a law authorizing a state agency to establish five new state-owned and state-operated toxic waste landfills. The law provided that the agency would decide the locations

and sizes of the landfills after an investigation of all potential sites and a determination that the particular sites chosen would not endanger public health and would be consistent with the public welfare.

A community in the state was scheduled for inspection by the agency as a potential toxic waste landfill site. Because the community's residents obtained most of their drinking water from an aquifer that ran under the entire community, a citizens' group, made up of residents of that community, sued the appropriate officials of the agency in federal court. The group sought a declaratory judgment that selecting their community as the site of a toxic waste landfill would be unconstitutional and an injunction preventing the agency from doing so. The agency officials moved to dismiss.
stemZh:
为了应对该州对更多有毒废物垃圾填埋场的需求，该州立法机关通过了一项法律，授权一个州机构建立五个新的州拥有和运营的有毒废物垃圾填埋场。该法律规定，该机构在对所有潜在选址进行调查，并确定所选选址不会危及公众健康且符合公共福利后，将决定垃圾填埋场的选址和规模。

该州的一个社区被安排接受该机构的检查，作为潜在的有毒废物垃圾填埋场选址。由于该社区的居民大部分饮用水来自贯穿整个社区的地下水层，由该社区居民组成的公民团体，向该机构的相关官员在联邦法院提起诉讼。该团体要求宣告将该社区选为有毒废物垃圾填埋场选址是违宪的，并请求法院颁布禁令，阻止该机构这样做。该机构官员提出了驳回诉讼动议。
ask: Which of the following is the most appropriate basis for the court to dismiss this suit?
askZh: 以下哪一项是法院驳回此案的最适当理由？

options.en: The case is not ripe for a decision on the merits.
options.zh: 此案在实质问题上尚未成熟。

options.en: The case presents a nonjusticiable political question.
options.zh: 此案涉及一个不可裁决的政治问题。

options.en: The Eleventh Amendment bars suits of this kind in the federal courts.
options.zh: 第十一修正案禁止此类诉讼在联邦法院进行。

options.en: The interest of the state in obtaining suitable sites for toxic waste landfills is sufficiently compelling to justify the selection of the community as a location for such a facility.
options.zh: 该州在获取适合的有毒废物垃圾填埋场选址方面的利益足够有力，足以证明选择该社区作为此类设施的选址是合理的。

explanation.en:
Justiciability

(suitability for judicial resolution)

Case or controversy Prohibits advisory opinions under three doctrines:

• Standing – plaintiff must allege injury-in-fact caused by challenged action & redressable by remedy sought

• Ripeness – claim must present actual controversy involving past injury or present threat of injury

• Mootness – claim must be unresolved Adequate & independent state grounds

SCOTUS cannot review final state court judgment that rests on adequate & independent state grounds

Political question Court cannot hear case if issue presented:

• is reserved for executive/legislative branches or

• lacks judicially manageable standards for resolution SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States.

A suit may only be heard by a federal court if it is justiciable. A suit is justiciable if it presents an actual case or controversy that is ripe for (and capable of) judicial resolution—ie, when the plaintiff has suffered actual harm or an imminent threat of harm. Therefore, a suit based on potential harm (unripe) or harm that is no longer capable of judicial resolution (moot) should be dismissed.

Here, the group sued to prevent agency officials from selecting its community as a toxic waste landfill site. But the suit is based on potential—not actual or imminent—harm since the agency is still investigating where to place these landfills. Therefore, the most appropriate basis to dismiss this suit is that it is not ripe for a decision on the merits. But the group's claim may become justiciable and can be re-filed in federal court if its community is later selected as a landfill site.

(Choice B) The political-question doctrine prohibits federal courts from hearing cases that present issues that (1) are reserved for the executive or legislative branch or (2) lack judicially manageable standards for resolution. But since federal courts often determine the constitutionality of state laws, this doctrine is not a basis for dismissal.

(Choice C) The Eleventh Amendment generally bars private parties and foreign governments from suing a state in federal court for monetary relief. But it does not bar suits against state officials for declaratory or injunctive relief (as seen here).

(Choice D) Federal courts can only determine the merits of a suit—eg, whether a government action is necessary to serve a compelling government interest (strict scrutiny)—if that suit is justiciable. And since this suit is not ripe for judicial resolution, the court cannot determine the merits of the group's claim.

Educational objective:

To be justiciable, a suit must present an actual case or controversy. This occurs when the plaintiff has suffered actual harm or an imminent threat thereof—not a mere possibility of harm.

References

• U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case or controversy requirement).

• Abbot Labs. v. Gardner, 387 U.S. 136, 148 (1967) (stating that federal courts cannot adjudicate unripe suits).

explanation.zh:
可审理性

(适合司法解决)

案例或争议禁止根据以下三种理论发表咨询意见:

• 身份 - 原告必须声称受到质疑的诉讼造成事实伤害,而且可以通过寻求的补救予以补救

• Ripeness - 索赔必须涉及过去伤害或目前伤害威胁的实际争议

• 模拟 - 索赔必须得到解决

SCOTUS不能审查基于充分和独立的国家理由的州法院最后判决

政治问题法院不能审理下列案件:

• 专供行政/立法部门使用;

• 缺乏SCOTUS = 美国最高法院的司法管理标准。

一项诉讼只有在可由法院审理的情况下才能由联邦法院审理,如果诉讼提出实际案件或争议,而这种案件或争议已经成熟,而且能够通过司法手段解决,即原告遭受了实际伤害或迫在眉睫的伤害威胁,则可以受理。因此,基于潜在伤害(unripe)或不再能够司法解决(moot)的损害的诉讼应予驳回。

在此,该团体提起诉讼是为了防止机构官员选择其社区作为有毒废物填埋场。 但诉讼是基于潜在而非实际或即将发生的伤害,因为机构仍在调查这些填埋场的位置。因此,驳回这一诉讼的最恰当依据是,就案情作出决定的时机还不成熟。 但是,如果其社区后来被选为垃圾填埋场,则该团体的诉求可能会成为可审理案件,并可在联邦法院重新提出。

(Choice B)政治问题学说禁止联邦法院审理提出:(1) 保留给行政或立法部门或(2) 缺乏司法上可管理解决标准的问题。但由于联邦法院往往决定州法律是否符合宪法,因此这个学说并不是开除的依据.

(C选择 ) 第十一修正案一般禁止私人政党和外国政府向联邦法院起诉某州以获得金钱救济。 但并不禁止针对州官员的宣告性或强制性救济诉讼(如这里所示 ) 。

(Choice D) 联邦法院只能确定一项诉讼的案情——例如,政府是否有必要采取行动,以服务于一项令人信服的政府利益(严格审查)——如果这项诉讼可由法院审理的话。并且由于这一诉讼还没有到司法解决的时机,法院无法确定该团体的诉求的案情.

学习要点：

为了可由法院审理,诉讼必须提出实际案件或争议,这发生在原告遭受了实际损害或迫在眉睫的伤害威胁,而不仅仅是可能造成损害的情况下。

参考资料

• 美国康斯特公司第3条第2款(案件或争议要求)。

• Abbot Labs诉Gardner案,387 U.S.136,148(1967年)(规定联邦法院不能裁定不审理的诉讼)。

explanation.en:
Eleventh Amendment

(state immunity from suit in federal court)

Immunity • Suit brought by private party or foreign government

• Suit against state official violating state law

• Exceptions: – State consents to suit – Immunity removed by 13th, 14th, or 15th Amendment – State official sued for injunctive or declaratory relief – Damages to be paid by state officer personally (not state treasury) – State official sued for prospective (not retroactive) damages to be paid by state treasury No immunity

• Suit brought by United States or other state

• Suit against local government (eg, counties, municipalities)

• Bankruptcy proceedings The Eleventh Amendment prohibits private parties and foreign governments from suing a state in federal court without the state's consent.* However, this amendment does not bar actions brought by the United States or another state. And since the United States sued the state here for injunctive relief, the Eleventh Amendment does not apply. As a result, the federal court likely will not dismiss this action (Choice C).

*Additionally, the doctrine of sovereign immunity bars private federal-law actions against a state sued in the courts of that state or any other state without the state's consent.

(Choice A) Congress may place certain conditions on the receipt of federal funds. Such conditions are valid if they (1) are unambiguous, (2) relate to the funded program's purpose, and (3) are not unduly coercive. Therefore, the federal court will likely retain this suit and determine if this funding condition satisfies these requirements.

(Choice D) Under the Tenth Amendment, all powers not expressly granted to the federal government by the Constitution are reserved to the states—eg, the power over child welfare. But the federal government can use its taxing and spending power to encourage states to adopt certain policies by placing conditions on the receipt of federal funds—eg, requiring state-recipients to comply with federal standards (as seen here).

Educational objective:

The Eleventh Amendment bars private parties and foreign governments from suing a state in federal court without the state's consent. But it does not bar suits brought by the United States or another state.

References

• Principality of Monaco v. Mississippi, 292 U.S. 313, 329 (1934) (stating that the Eleventh Amendment does not bar a suit by the United States against a state in federal court).

• 32A Am. Jur. 2d Federal Courts § 911 (2019) (explaining that the United States may sue a state in federal court without the state's consent).

第十一次修正

(国家豁免联邦法院的诉讼)

• 私人或外国政府提出的诉讼

• 对违反州法律的国家官员提起诉讼

• 例外:- 国家同意诉 - 第13、14或15修正案取消豁免 - 国家官员被起诉要求强制或宣告性救济 - 国家官员个人(不是国库)应支付的损害 - 国家官员被起诉预期(不是)国家财政应支付的赔偿

• 美国或其他国家提出的诉讼

• 起诉地方政府(例如县、市)

• 破产程序 第十一修正案禁止私人当事方和外国政府* 但是,这一修正案没有规定,在未经州同意的情况下,不得向联邦法院起诉州。美国或其他国家提起的诉讼。而由于美国在此起诉该州要求强制补救,第十一修正案并不适用。 因此,联邦法院很可能不会驳回这一诉讼(Choice C).

* 此外,主权豁免原则禁止未经国家同意而在该州或任何其他州法院起诉国家的联邦私法行动。

(Choice A)国会可以对接受联邦资金规定某些条件,如果这些条件 (1) 明确, (2) 与资助方案的目的有关, (3) 并不过分强制,那么这些条件是有效的.因此,联邦法院可能保留这一诉讼,并确定这一供资条件是否符合这些要求。

根据第十修正案,《宪法》未明确授予联邦政府的所有权力都留给各州——例如,对儿童福利的权力。但是,联邦政府可以利用其征税和支出权力来鼓励各州通过某些政策,对接受联邦资金设置条件——例如,要求州接收者遵守联邦标准(见这里)。

学习要点：

第十一修正案禁止私人政党和外国政府在未经州同意的情况下向联邦法院起诉州。 但并不禁止美国或另一州提起的诉讼。

参考资料

• 摩纳哥公国诉密西西比州案,292 U.S.331, 329 (1934年)(声明第十一修正案并不妨碍美国在联邦法院对一个国家提起诉讼)。

• 32A Am. Jur. 2d 联邦法院第911条(2019年)(解释美国可以在未经该州同意的情况下向联邦法院起诉该州)。

stem: Congress enacted a statute directing U.S. ambassadors to send formal letters to the governments of their host countries, protesting any violations by those governments of international treaties on weapons sales. The President prefers to handle violations by certain countries in a less formal manner and has directed ambassadors not to comply with the statute.
stemZh: 国会通过了一项法律，要求美国大使向其驻在国政府发送正式信函，抗议这些政府违反武器销售国际条约的行为。总统更倾向于以不太正式的方式处理某些国家的违规行为，并指示大使不要遵守该法律。
ask: Is the President's action constitutional?
askZh: 总统的行为是否合宪？

options.en: No, because Congress has the power to implement treaties, and therefore the statute is binding on the President.
options.zh: 否，因为国会拥有实施条约的权力，因此该法律对总统具有约束力。

options.en: No, because Congress has the power to regulate commerce with foreign nations, and therefore the statute is binding on the President.
options.zh: 否，因为国会拥有监管与外国国家贸易的权力，因此该法律对总统具有约束力。

options.en: Yes, because Congress has no jurisdiction over matters outside the U.S. borders.
options.zh: 是，因为国会对美国国界以外的事务没有管辖权。

options.en: Yes, because the President and his subordinates are the exclusive official representatives of the United States in foreign affairs.
options.zh: 是，因为总统及其下属是美国在外交事务中的唯一官方代表。

explanation.en:
Article II vests the President with authority over a wide array of domestic and foreign policy areas. When the President shares authority with Congress over a particular area (eg, federal agencies), the validity of the President's actions is determined by the Youngstown framework. But when the President does not share authority with Congress, the President can exercise that exclusive Article II power without adhering to congressional directives.

One exclusive Article II power is the authority to communicate and negotiate with foreign governments as the official U.S. representative in foreign affairs. The President can exercise this power directly or through his/her subordinates—including ambassadors and other executive-branch officials. Therefore, it was constitutional for the President to direct the ambassadors not to comply with the federal statute regarding formal letters to foreign governments.

(Choice A) Congress has the power to implement treaties through appropriate legislation under the necessary and proper clause. But such legislation cannot restrict the President's ability to exercise an exclusive Article II power (as seen here).

(Choices B & C) Congress has some jurisdiction over matters outside U.S. borders—eg, the power to declare war and to regulate commerce with foreign nations. But this does not give Congress the power to bind the President (or his/her subordinates) on matters within the President's exclusive authority.

Educational objective:

When the President does not share power with Congress over a particular area—eg, communicating with foreign governments—the President can exercise that exclusive Article II power without congressional interference.

References

• United States v. Curtiss-Wright Exp. Corp., 299 U.S. 304, 319 (1936) (stating that "the President alone has the power to speak or listen as a representative of the nation").

explanation.zh:
第二条赋予总统对广泛的国内和外交政策领域的权力,当总统与国会分享对某一特定领域(如联邦机构)的权力时,总统行动的有效性由青年城决定。但是,当总统不与国会分享权力时,总统可以行使第二条规定的专属权力,而不必遵守国会的指示。

第二条的一项专属权力是有权作为美国外交事务官方代表与外国政府沟通和谈判.总统可以直接或通过下属——包括大使和其他行政部门官员——行使这一权力。因此,总统指示大使不遵守关于向外国政府发出正式信函的联邦法规是符合宪法的。

(Choice A)国会有权根据必要和适当的条款通过适当的立法执行条约,但这种立法不能限制总统行使第二条专有权力的能力(如这里所见)。

(Choices B & C)国会对美国境外事务有一定管辖权——例如,有权宣战和管制与外国的商业。但这并不赋予国会在总统专有权力范围内对总统(或其下属)事务有约束力的权力.

学习要点：

当总统不与国会分享特定领域的权力(例如与外国政府沟通)时,总统可以在没有国会干涉的情况下行使第二条规定的专属权力。

参考资料

• 美国诉Curtis-Wright Exp. Corp.,299 U.S.304,319 (1936)(规定"总统一人有权作为国家的代表发言或聆听").

stem:
The constitution of State A grants the state legislature the power to redraw the boundaries of the state's federal congressional districts every 10 years. In the last redistricting cycle, the legislature's majority political party redrew the equally populated districts with the express intent to increase the party's representation in Congress. During the most recent election, the legislature's majority political party won 10 of the 13 available congressional seats despite receiving less than 50 percent of the overall statewide vote.

A resident of State A who voted for a congressional candidate representing another political party filed suit in a State A federal court against the state legislators who drafted the redistricting map. The resident argued that the court should enjoin the use of the map in future elections because the legislators violated the U.S. Constitution by engaging in partisan gerrymandering.
stemZh:
A州宪法赋予州立法机关每十年重新绘制该州联邦国会选区边界的权力。在最近一次选区重划周期中，立法机关的多数政党重新绘制了人口相等的选区，其明确意图是增加该政党在国会的代表人数。在最近一次选举中，该政党尽管获得的全州总选票不足50%，却赢得了13个可选国会席位中的10个。

一名A州居民投票支持代表另一政党的国会候选人，对该州制定选区地图的立法者提起诉讼，诉讼地点是A州联邦法院。该居民认为，法院应下令禁止在未来的选举中使用该地图，因为立法者违反了美国宪法，通过党派性选区划分行为。
ask: Should the federal court hear the merits of the resident's suit?
askZh: 联邦法院是否应审理该居民的诉讼请求？

options.en: No, because the case presents a nonjusticiable issue.
options.zh: 否，因为此案涉及不可裁判的问题。

options.en: No, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits suits against state officials in federal court.
options.zh: 否，因为第十一修正案禁止在联邦法院对州官员提起诉讼。

options.en: Yes, because the court must guarantee that the state has a republican form of government.
options.zh: 是，因为法院必须确保州拥有共和政体。

options.en: Yes, because the map violates the "one person, one vote" principle.
options.zh: 是，因为该地图违反了"一人一票"原则。

explanation.en:
Nonjusticiable political questions

(issues incapable of judicial resolution)

• Recognition of foreign governments

• Reception of ambassadors

• Nature of wars/hostilities

• Partisan gerrymandering

• Guarantee of republican form of government

• Recognition of Native American tribes

• House/Senate rules for impeachment

• Ratification process for constitutional amendments Article III of the U.S. Constitution grants federal courts the power to decide justiciable cases and controversies. However, the political-question doctrine bars a federal court from hearing the merits of nonjusticiable political questions. A case presents a political question when:

• the Constitution reserves the issue to the legislative or executive branch and/or

• there is a lack of judicially discoverable and manageable standards to resolve the issue. Here, the resident filed suit in federal court to enjoin the use of the state's redistricting map in future elections due to partisan gerrymandering—ie, drawing electoral districts to favor or weaken a political party. However, SCOTUS held in Rucho v. Common Cause that partisan gerrymandering suits present nonjusticiable political questions because there are no judicial standards to resolve them. Therefore, the court should not hear the merits of the resident's suit.

(Choice B) The Eleventh Amendment generally bars private parties and foreign governments from suing a state in federal court for monetary relief. But it does not bar suits against state officials for injunctive relief (as seen here).

(Choice C) Under Article IV of the Constitution, the federal government must guarantee a republican form of government to every state. However, the issue of what constitutes a republican form of government is a nonjusticiable political question reserved to Congress.

(Choice D) The "one person, one vote" principle holds that one person's vote must be essentially equal to any other person's vote. When a state establishes congressional districts, this principle requires nearly precise mathematical equality between the districts. Since State A's 13 congressional districts are equally populated, the map does not violate the "one person, one vote" principle.

Educational objective:

Under the political-question doctrine, federal courts cannot hear the merits of a suit that presents a nonjusticiable political question—ie, an issue that (1) the Constitution reserves to another branch of government and/or (2) lacks judicially discoverable and manageable standards for the issue to be resolved by a court.

SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States.

References

• Rucho v. Common Cause, 139 S. Ct. 2484, 2506–07 (2019) (holding that partisan gerrymandering claims are nonjusticiable because there is no judicially discoverable and manageable standard to review them).

• Baker v. Carr, 369 U.S. 186, 210–17 (1962) (explaining the political-question doctrine).

• 32 Am. Jur. 2d Fed. Courts § 574 (2020) (listing common examples of political questions).

explanation.zh:
不可审理的政治问题

(无法司法解决的问题)

• 承认外国政府

• 接待大使

• 战争/敌对行动的性质

• Partisan采石场

• 保障共和政体

• 承认美洲原住民部落

• 众议院/参议院弹劾规则

• 批准宪法修正案的程序 《美国宪法》第三条赋予联邦法院裁决可审理的案件和争议的权力。然而,政治问题学说阻止联邦法院听取最高法院的意见。不可审理的政治问题的优点。案件提出了政治问题,因为:

• 《宪法》将这一问题保留给立法或行政部门和(或)

· 缺乏司法上可发现的、可管理的标准来解决这一问题,这里,居民向联邦法院提起诉讼,要求由于党派的游击手,在选举过程中使用州重新分区地图。然而,SCOTUS在Rucho诉Common 案 中认为,由于没有司法标准可以解决这些问题,党派迫害诉讼提出了不可审理的政治问题。因此,法院不应审理居民诉讼的案情。

(Choice B)第十一修正案一般禁止私人政党和外国政府向联邦法院起诉某州要求货币救济。 但并不禁止针对州官员要求强制救济的诉讼(如本文所示 ) 。

(C选择)根据宪法第四条,联邦政府必须保证每个州都有一个共和制政府形式,然而,什么是共和制政府形式的问题是一个留给国会处理的不可审理的政治问题.

(Choice D)"一人一票"的原则认为,一个人的投票必须基本上等于任何其他人的投票,当一个国家建立国会选区时,这一原则要求各区之间几乎精确的数学平等.由于A州13个国会区人口相同,故该地图并不违反"一人一票"的原则.

学习要点：

根据政治问题学说,联邦法院不能审理提出不可审理的政治问题的诉讼的案情,即(1) 《宪法》保留给政府另一分支和/或(2) 缺乏司法发现和(或)缺乏司法证据的问题。由法院解决这一问题的可管理标准。

SCOTUS = 美国最高法院.

参考资料

· Rucho诉Common Cause,139 S. Ct. 2484,2506-07 (2019年)(认为党派的gerrymander索赔是不可审理的,因为没有司法上可以发现和可以管理的标准来审查这些索赔)。

· Baker诉Carr案,369 U.S.186, 210–17 (1962)(解释政治问题理论)。

• 32 Am. Jur. 2d Fed. Courts §574(2020)(列举政治问题的共同例子)。

stem:
The vaccination of children against childhood contagious diseases (such as measles, diphtheria, and whooping cough) has traditionally been a function of private doctors and local and state health departments. Because vaccination rates have declined in recent years, especially in urban areas, the President proposes to appoint a Presidential Advisory Commission on Vaccination which would be charged with conducting a national publicity campaign to encourage vaccination as a public health measure.

No federal statute authorizes or prohibits this action by the President.

The activities of the Presidential Advisory Commission on Vaccination would be financed entirely from funds appropriated by Congress to the Office of the President for "such other purposes as the President may think appropriate."
stemZh:
儿童接种疫苗以预防儿童传染病（如麻疹、白喉和百日咳）历来是私人医生和地方及州卫生部门的职责。由于近年来疫苗接种率有所下降，尤其是在城市地区，总统提议设立一个总统疫苗咨询委员会，该委员会负责开展一项全国性的宣传活动，以鼓励接种疫苗作为公共卫生措施。

没有联邦法律授权或禁止总统采取这一行动。

总统疫苗咨询委员会的活动将完全由国会拨款给总统办公室用于“总统认为适当的其他用途”的资金来资助。
ask: May the President constitutionally create such a commission for this purpose?
askZh: 总统是否有宪法权力创建这样一个委员会用于此目的？

options.en: No, because Congress has not specifically authorized the creation and support of such a new federal agency.
options.zh: 否，因为国会并未明确授权创建和资助这样一个新的联邦机构。

options.en: No, because the protection of children against common diseases by vaccination is a traditional state function and, therefore, is reserved to the states by the Tenth Amendment.
options.zh: 否，因为通过接种疫苗保护儿童免受常见疾病侵害是传统州职能，因此根据第十修正案保留给各州。

options.en: Yes, because the President has plenary authority to provide for the health, safety, and welfare of the people of the United States.
options.zh: 是，因为总统有权为美国人民的健康、安全和福利提供保障。

options.en: Yes, because this action is within the scope of executive authority vested in the President by the Constitution, and no federal statute prohibits it.
options.zh: 是，因为这一行动属于宪法赋予总统的行政权力范围，且没有联邦法律禁止该行为。

explanation.en:
Article II gives the President the power to manage the executive branch. Pursuant to this power, the President can use congressional funds to create advisory commissions that will recommend and promote policies. Congress can limit the President's powers when they share authority over an area (eg, use of federal funds). The Youngstown framework is then used to determine the extent of the President's authority. And when Congress is silent, the President's action is valid so long as it:

• falls within the President's Article II powers and

• does not interfere with another branch's powers. Here, the President proposes an advisory commission that would encourage vaccination and be financed entirely from funds already appropriated for Presidential use. Congress is silent on the President's proposal since no federal statute authorizes or prohibits it. And since the President is acting within the scope of his Article II executive authority and is not interfering with another branch's powers, he may constitutionally create the commission.

(Choice A) Specific congressional authorization is not needed since the President is establishing an advisory commission—not a new federal agency with rule-making powers (eg, Securities and Exchange Commission).

(Choice B) All powers that the Constitution does not expressly give to the federal government—including the police power to protect children against common diseases—are reserved to the states by the Tenth Amendment. But the President has the power to establish advisory commissions on traditional state functions like protecting child welfare.

(Choice C) The President does not have plenary (ie, absolute) authority to provide for the health, safety, and welfare of the people of the United States. Instead, the President must comply with the Constitution and relevant federal statutes.

Educational objective:

When Congress has remained silent about the President's actions in an area over which they share authority, those actions are valid so long as they (1) fall within the President's Article II powers and (2) do not interfere with another branch's powers.

References

• Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer, 343 U.S. 579, 635–38 (1952) (Jackson, J., concurring) (setting forth the tripartite framework for analyzing the constitutionality of presidential actions).

第二条赋予总统管理行政部门的权力,根据这一权力,总统可以利用国会资金设立咨询委员会,负责建议和促进政策。国会可以限制总统对一个领域(如联邦资金的使用)的权力分享. 永斯敦框架随后被用来决定总统的权力范围.而国会沉默时,只要总统的行动是有效的:

• 属于主席第二条的权力范围;

• 不干涉另一分支的权力。在此,总统建议成立一个咨询委员会,鼓励接种疫苗并获得资金。全部来自已经拨给总统使用的资金。国会对总统的提议保持沉默,因为没有任何联邦法规授权或禁止总统的提议,而且由于总统是在第二条行政权力范围内行事的,并且没有干涉另一分支的权力,因此他可以根据宪法行事。创建佣金。

(选择A) 不需要国会的具体授权,因为总统正在设立一个咨询委员会,而不是一个新的联邦机构,拥有制定规则的权力(例如证券和交易委员会)。

宪法没有明确赋予联邦政府的所有权力——包括警察保护儿童免受常见疾病之害的权力——由第十修正案保留给各州。但是,总统有权设立诸如保护儿童福利等传统国家职能的咨询委员会。

(C选择 ) 总统没有全体会议(即绝对)的权力来保障美国人民的健康,安全和福利。 相反,总统必须遵守宪法和相关联邦法规。

学习要点：

当国会对总统在他们共同拥有权力的领域的行动保持沉默时,只要:(1) 属于总统第二条的权力范围,(2) 不干涉另一部门的权力,这些行动就是合法的。

stem:
A federal statute prohibits the construction of nuclear energy plants in this country without a license from the Federal Nuclear Plant Siting Commission. The statute provides that the Commission may issue a license authorizing the construction of a proposed nuclear energy plant 30 days after the Commission makes a finding that the plant will comply with specified standards of safety, technological and commercial feasibility, and public convenience. In a severable provision, the Commission's enabling statute also provides that Congress, by simple majorities in each house, may veto the issuance of a particular license by the Commission if such a veto occurs within 30 days following the required Commission finding.

Early last year, the Commission found that an energy corporation met all statutory requirements and, therefore, voted to issue the corporation a license authorizing it to construct a nuclear energy plant. Because they believed that the issuance of a license to the corporation was not in accord with the applicable statutory criteria, a majority of each of the two houses of Congress voted, within the specified 30-day period, to veto the license. On the basis of that veto, the Commission refused to issue the license.

Subsequently, the corporation sued the Commission in an appropriate federal district court, challenging the constitutionality of the Commission's refusal to issue the license.
stemZh:
一项联邦法律规定，未经联邦核电站选址委员会许可，不得在美国建造核电站。该法律规定：委员会认定拟建核电站符合特定的安全、技术和商业可行性以及公共便利标准 30 天后，可以颁发许可，授权建造该核电站。委员会的授权法另有一项可分割的规定：如果国会两院分别在委员会作出上述认定后的 30 天内以简单多数通过否决，国会可以否决委员会颁发某项特定许可。

去年年初，委员会认定一家能源公司满足全部法定要求，因此表决决定颁发许可，授权该公司建造核电站。但国会两院各有过半数议员认为向该公司颁发许可不符合适用的法定标准，于是在规定的 30 天期限内分别投票否决该许可。委员会据此拒绝颁发许可。

此后，该公司在有管辖权的联邦地区法院起诉委员会，质疑委员会拒绝颁发许可的行为是否合宪。
ask: In this suit, how should the court rule regarding the congressional veto of the energy corporation's license?
askZh: 在本案中，法院应该如何裁定国会否决能源公司许可证的行为？

options.en: The veto is invalid, because any determination by Congress that particular agency action does not satisfy statutory criteria violates Article III, Section 1 of the Constitution because it constitutes the performance of a judicial function by the legislative branch.
options.zh: 该否决无效，因为国会认定特定行政行为不符合法定标准的行为违反了宪法第三条第一款，因为它构成立法部门行使司法职能。

options.en: The veto is invalid, because Article I, Section 7 of the Constitution has been interpreted to mean that any action of Congress purporting to alter the legal rights of persons outside of the legislative branch must be presented to the President for his signature or veto.
options.zh: 该否决无效，因为宪法第一条第七款已被解释为，任何旨在改变立法部门以外个人法律权利的国会行为，必须提交总统签署或否决。

options.en: The veto is valid, because Congress has authority under the commerce clause to regulate the construction of nuclear energy plants.
options.zh: 该否决有效，因为国会根据商业条款有权监管核电站的建设。

options.en: The veto is valid, because there is a compelling national interest in the close congressional supervision of nuclear-plant siting in light of the grave dangers to the public health and safety that are associated with the operation of such plants.
options.zh: 该否决有效，因为考虑到核电站运营对公众健康和安全的严重危险，国会对核电站选址进行密切监督存在强烈的国家利益。

explanation.en:
Article I grants all federal legislative power to Congress, which consists of the House of Representatives and the Senate. Article I also prescribes the method Congress must use to take legislative action—ie, any action that alters the legal rights of persons outside of the legislative branch. Under this method, all legislative action must be:

• approved by both houses of Congress (ie, bicameralism) and

• presented to the President for approval or disapproval (ie, presentment). As a result, congressional vetoes are always invalid since they attempt to overturn agency actions without adhering to the proper method of bicameralism and presentment.

Here, the federal statute authorizes an agency to issue licenses for the construction of nuclear energy plants. Pursuant to this statute, the agency voted to issue a license to an energy corporation. But the statute also includes a provision allowing Congress, by majority vote of both houses, to veto the agency's issuance of a license. And though a majority of each house of Congress voted to veto the corporation's license (bicameralism), the veto was not presented to the President (no presentment). Therefore, this legislative action is invalid.

(Choice A) Article III, section 1 gives federal courts the power to resolve cases and controversies. This precludes Congress from issuing a judgment in individual cases. But Congress can still make a nonbinding determination (eg, through a resolution) that particular agency action does not satisfy statutory criteria.

(Choice C) Congress can regulate the construction of nuclear energy plants under the commerce clause since the production of energy substantially impacts interstate commerce. But Congress must do so through bicameralism and presentment.

(Choice D) Congressional vetoes are always invalid—even when they are supported by a compelling national interest (eg, public health and safety).

Educational objective:

Congressional vetoes are always invalid since they attempt to overturn agency actions without adhering to the proper method for legislative action—ie, bicameralism and presentment.

References

• INS v. Chadha, 462 U.S. 919, 959 (1983) (striking down a congressional-veto provision in a federal immigration statute).

explanation.zh:
第一条赋予由众议院和参议院组成的国会所有联邦立法权.第一条还规定了国会采取立法行动时必须采用的方法,即任何改变立法部门以外人员合法权利的行动。

• 议会两院批准(即两院制)和

· 提交总统批准或不批准(即提交),因此,国会否决总是无效的,因为它们试图推翻机构行动,而不遵循两院制和提交的适当方法。

在此,联邦法规授权一个机构颁发建造核能工厂的许可证,根据该法规,该机构投票决定向一家能源公司颁发许可证。但章程中还包括一项条款,允许国会通过两院的多数票否决该机构颁发的许可证.尽管国会每院多数议员投票否决了该公司的牌照(两院制 ) , 但否决并没有提交总统(没有呈递 ) 。 因此,这一立法行动无效。

(Choice A) 第三条第一节赋予联邦法院解决案件和争议的权力,这禁止国会对个别案件作出判决.但国会仍然可以作出不具约束力的决定(例如通过一项决议),即特定机构的行动不符合法定标准.

(Choice C)国会可以根据商业条款来监管核能工厂的建设,因为能源生产对州际商务有重大影响。 但国会必须通过两院制和展示来做到这一点。

(选择D)国会否决总是无效的——即使它们得到迫切的国家利益(例如公共卫生和安全)的支持。

学习要点：

国会的否决总是无效的,因为它们试图推翻机构的行动,而不遵循适当的立法行动方法——即两院制和表现。

参考资料

• INS诉Chadha案,462 U.S.919,959(1983年)(在联邦移民法规中删除国会核查条款)。

stem:
The House of Representatives passed a bill imposing a tax on all insurance premiums for policies covering shipments of goods to foreign countries. The legislative record states that the purpose of this export tax is to subsidize the marine insurance industry. The tax applies to all goods manufactured or grown in every state. The bill passed the Senate and was signed into law by the President.

Pursuant to the statute, a company paid the tax on insurance premiums for policies that cover goods exported to its foreign subsidiaries. The company filed a claim for a tax refund and was denied. The company filed suit alleging that the tax is unconstitutional.
stemZh:
众议院通过了一项法案，对所有覆盖向外国国家运送货物的保险费征收税款。立法记录中说明，这项出口税的目的是补贴海事保险行业。该税款适用于每个州制造或种植的所有货物。该法案通过了参议院，并由总统签署成为法律。

根据该法律，一家公司为其出口至其外国子公司的货物保险费支付了税款。该公司提出了退税申请，但被拒绝。该公司提起诉讼，声称该税款违宪。
ask: Is this federal tax likely constitutional?
askZh: 这项联邦税款是否很可能合宪？

options.en: No, because Congress does not have the power to tax exported goods or closely related services.
options.zh: 否，因为国会无权对出口货物或密切相关服务征税。

options.en: No, because the tax does not reasonably relate to raising revenue.
options.zh: 否，因为该税款与提高收入无合理关联。

options.en: Yes, because Congress's taxing power is unlimited.
options.zh: 是，因为国会的征税权是无限的。

options.en: Yes, because the tax is necessary to serve a compelling government interest.
options.zh: 是，因为该税款是为实现政府的迫切利益所必需的。

explanation.en:
The taxing and spending clause gives Congress broad power to tax and spend for the general welfare (ie, any public purpose). However, this power is not unlimited and must comply with other constitutional provisions—including the export clause (Choice C). The export clause prohibits federal taxation of:

• exported goods, which are goods leaving the U.S. and shipped to foreign countries and

• services and activities closely related to the export process—eg, insurance premiums paid to cover the shipment of exported goods (as seen here).

Therefore, the federal tax on insurance premiums for policies covering shipments of goods to foreign countries is not within Congress's power to tax and is unconstitutional.

(Choice B) The tax in this case is reasonably related to raising revenue because its purpose is to raise funds that will be used to subsidize the marine insurance industry. But this issue is irrelevant because the tax is an unconstitutional export tax.

(Choice D) Federal export taxes are never valid, even if the government shows that they are necessary to serve a compelling interest (ie, satisfy strict scrutiny).

Educational objective:

Congress has broad power to tax and spend for the general welfare. However, Congress can never impose taxes on exported goods or on services and activities closely related to the export process.

References

• U.S. Const. art. I, § 9 (export clause).

• United States v. Int'l Bus. Machs. Corp., 517 U.S. 843, 846–47 (1996) (explaining that the export clause prohibits federal taxation of exported goods and services and activities closely related to the export process).

explanation.zh:
税收和支出条款赋予国会为一般福利(即任何公共目的)征税和支出的广泛权力,但这种权力并非无限的,必须遵守其他宪法规定——包括出口条款(Choice C)。出口条款禁止联邦对下列货物征税:

• 出口货物,即离开美国运往外国的货物;

与出口过程密切相关的服务和活动——例如,为出口货物的运输支付的保险费(见这里)。

因此,联邦对向外国运送货物的保单的保险费征税不属于国会的征税权限,是违宪的.

(Choice B)本案中的税收与增加收入有合理关系,因为其目的是为了筹集资金,用于补贴海洋保险业。 但这一问题无关紧要,因为税收是违宪的出口税。

(Choice D) 联邦出口税永远无效,即使政府表明它们对于服务于令人信服的利益是必需的(即满足严格的审查).

学习要点：

国会拥有为普遍福利征税和开支的广泛权力,但是,国会绝对不能对出口货物或与出口过程密切相关的服务和活动征税。

参考资料

• 美国康斯特第1条第9款(出口条款)。

• 美国诉Int'l Bus.Machs. Corp.,517 U.S.843、846-47(1996年)(解释出口条款禁止联邦对出口货物和服务以及与出口过程密切相关的活动征税)。

stem:
A valid treaty between the United States and a foreign country provides for the elimination of all tariff barriers between the two countries. It authorizes the president of either country to issue a proclamation nullifying any state or local laws in that country that have the effect of impeding imports from the other country.

The foreign country uses the metric system of measurement, and thus all goods produced there and exported to the United States are packaged in metric sizes, such as liters and kilograms. A law of a state in the United States requires all goods sold in that state to be packaged in traditional American sizes, such as quarts or pounds. Because the state law substantially impedes imports from the foreign country, the President of the United States has issued a proclamation nullifying the state law pursuant to the treaty.
stemZh:
一项有效的美利坚合众国与外国之间的条约规定，消除两国之间的所有关税壁垒。该条约授权美利坚合众国或外国的总统可以发布一项宣言，使该国的任何州或地方法律无效，如果这些法律实质上阻碍从另一国进口商品。

该外国使用公制计量系统，因此该国生产并出口到美利坚合众国的所有商品均以公制单位包装，如升和千克。美利坚合众国一州的法律要求该州销售的所有商品必须以传统的美式单位包装，如夸脱或磅。由于该州法律实质上阻碍从该外国进口商品，美利坚合众国总统根据条约发布了该州法律的宣言。
ask: Is the President's proclamation valid?
askZh: 总统的宣言是否有效？

options.en: No, because the Constitution vests in Congress the exclusive authority to specify binding legal standards for weights and measures, and the President therefore lacks constitutional authority for the proclamation.
options.zh: 否，因为宪法将制定具有约束力的法定重量和度量标准的专属权力授予国会，因此总统缺乏宪法授权来发布该宣言。

options.en: No, because the principles of federalism embedded in the Constitution prohibit the President from taking action to invalidate a state law.
options.zh: 否，因为宪法中联邦主义的原则禁止总统采取行动来使州法律无效。

options.en: Yes, because it is authorized by a valid treaty of the United States and is not prohibited by any provision of the Constitution and, therefore, is the supreme law of the land.
options.zh: 是，因为该宣言由一项有效的美利坚合众国条约授权，且不被宪法的任何条款禁止，因此是至高无上的法律。

options.en: Yes, because the President has inherent authority to nullify any state law that substantially impedes commerce between the United States and another country.
options.zh: 是，因为总统有权撤销任何实质上阻碍美利坚合众国与其他国家之间商业的州法律。

explanation.en:
Article II gives the President extensive power over foreign policy and international relations—including the power to negotiate and enter into treaties with foreign nations. But a treaty cannot be ratified (ie, signed into law) until it has been approved by a two-thirds Senate vote (no action by the House of Representatives required). It then becomes valid and binding on the federal and state governments:

• immediately, if the treaty is self-executing—ie, contains explicit enforcement provisions (as seen here)—or

• after implementing legislation or judicial action, if the treaty is non-self-executing—ie, lacks explicit enforcement provisions.

And under the supremacy clause, an executed treaty supersedes any conflicting state law so long as the treaty is consistent with other constitutional provisions.

Here, the President issued a proclamation nullifying a state law that substantially impeded imports from a foreign country. This proclamation was authorized by an explicit enforcement provision in a self-executing treaty between the U.S. and the foreign nation. And since the proclamation is not prohibited by any constitutional provision, it is the supreme law of the land and nullifies the state law.

(Choice A) Article I, section 8 gives Congress the exclusive authority to specify standards for weights and measures. The President's proclamation does not interfere with that authority because it was merely used to eliminate a state-imposed packaging requirement—not to adjust national measurement standards.

(Choice B) The principles of federalism allocate power between the federal and state governments. But federalism does not prohibit the President from invalidating state laws pursuant to a federal statute or treaty (as seen here).

(Choice D) The President has no inherent authority to nullify a state law that substantially impedes commerce between the U.S. and another country. But the President can do so if authorized by Congress (eg, under its commerce power) or a valid treaty (as seen here).

Educational objective:

A treaty must be approved by a two-thirds vote in the Senate (not the House of Representatives) before it can be ratified. Once this occurs, the treaty takes precedence over any conflicting state law pursuant to the supremacy clause.

References

• Medellin v. Texas, 552 U.S. 491, 526–30 (2008) (explaining the President's powers to implement self-executing and non-self-executing treaties).

• Ware v. Hylton, 3 U.S. 199, 236–37 (1796) (declaring that treaties take precedence over conflicting state laws).

explanation.zh:
第二条赋予总统对外交政策和国际关系的广泛权力,包括同外国谈判和缔结条约的权力。但是,一项条约(即签署为法律)在获得参议院三分之二的表决(众议院不需采取行动)批准之前是不能批准的。

• 如果条约是自动执行的,立即载有明确的执行规定(如此处所示)——或

• 在执行立法或司法行动之后,如果条约不能自动执行,则缺乏明确的执行规定。

并且根据至高无上条款,只要条约与其他宪法规定一致,被执行的条约就取代任何相互冲突的州法律.

在此,总统发布了一项公告,宣布一项严重妨碍从外国进口的州法律无效。 这一公告是美国与外国之间一项自动执行条约中的一项明确执行条款授权的。而由于公告并未受到任何宪法条款的禁止,因此它是国家的最高法律,并废除了州法律.

(Choice A) 第一条第八节赋予国会规定权重和措施标准的专属权力.总统的公告并不妨碍这一权力,因为它只是用来取消国家规定的包装要求,而不是用来调整国家计量标准。

(Choice B)联邦制原则在联邦和州政府之间分配权力,但联邦制并不禁止总统根据联邦法规或条约废除州法律(见这里).

(Choice D)总统没有内在的权力来废除一项严重妨碍美国和另一国之间的商业的州法律,但是如果国会授权(例如在其商业权力下)或有效的条约(如这里所见),总统可以这样做.

学习要点：

条约必须在参议院(而不是众议院)以三分之二的表决通过后才能批准,一旦批准,根据至高无上条款,条约优先于任何相互冲突的州法律。

参考资料

stem: A statute passed by both houses of Congress and signed by the President authorizes a federal agency to select a site for and to construct a monument honoring members of the capitol police force killed in the line of duty. The statute appropriates the necessary funds but provides that the funds may not be expended until both houses of Congress have adopted a concurrent resolution, not subject to presentment to the President, approving the agency's plans for the monument's location and design.
stemZh: 由国会两院通过并由总统签署的一项法律授权一个联邦机构选择并建造一座纪念在执行公务中牺牲的国会警察成员的纪念碑的地点，并进行建造。该法律拨付了必要的资金，但规定资金在国会两院通过一项联合决议批准该机构对纪念碑选址和设计的计划之前不得使用，该决议不需提交总统签署。
ask: Is the provision requiring further congressional approval before expenditure of the funds constitutional?
askZh: 要求在动用资金之前获得国会进一步批准的条款是否符合宪法？

options.en: No, because decisions regarding the placement and design of government-owned structures are an exclusively executive function with which Congress may not interfere by any means.
options.zh: 否，因为关于政府拥有的建筑物选址和设计的决定是专属的行政职能，国会不得以任何方式干涉。

options.en: No, because the provision amounts to an unconstitutional legislative interference with an executive function.
options.zh: 否，因为该条款构成对行政职能的违宪立法干涉。

options.en: Yes, because Congress may attach reasonable conditions to its appropriation of funds to executive departments, and its special interest in the members of its own police force makes the provision a reasonable condition.
options.zh: 是，因为国会可以将其资金拨付给行政部门附加合理的条件，且其对自身警察成员的特殊利益使该条款构成合理的条件。

options.en: Yes, because the provision is part of a statute that was passed by both houses of Congress and signed by the President.
options.zh: 是，因为该条款是国会两院通过并由总统签署的一项法律的一部分。

explanation.en:
Article I entrusts Congress (ie, the House of Representatives and the Senate) with the power to take legislative action. Action is legislative when its purpose or effect is to alter the legal rights or duties of persons outside of Congress. And legislative action, absent narrow exceptions, must be:

• approved by both houses of Congress (ie, bicameralism) and

• presented to the President for approval or disapproval (ie, presentment). Through this process, Congress can delegate some of its powers (eg, rulemaking) to federal executive agencies. But once Congress does so, it cannot interfere with the agencies' functions unless it again complies with the legislative-action process. Any attempt to bypass this process amounts to an unconstitutional legislative veto.

Here, Congress delegated power to the federal agency to select a site for and construct a monument. But a statutory provision prevents the agency from expending the appropriated funds until Congress adopts a concurrent resolution approving the agency's plans. And since the resolution will not be presented to the President, the provision amounts to an unconstitutional legislative interference with an executive function (ie, legislative veto).

(Choice A) Decisions regarding the placement and design of government structures are not an exclusively executive function because Congress also has the authority to make these determinations.

(Choice C) Congress may attach reasonable conditions to its appropriations of funds—eg, directing how executive departments can spend funds. But such conditions must comply with the Constitution (not seen here).

(Choice D) The provision is part of a statute that passed both houses of Congress and was signed by the President. However, the provision amounts to an unconstitutional legislative veto since it grants Congress the future power to approve or disapprove the agency's plans without presentment to the President.

Educational objective:

Once Congress delegates power to an executive agency, it cannot interfere with the agency's functions without satisfying the legislative-action process—ie, bicameralism and presentment. Any attempt to bypass this process is an unconstitutional legislative veto.

References

• U.S. Const. art. I, § 7, cl. 2 (bicameralism and presentment requirements).

• INS v. Chadha, 462 U.S. 919, 951–52 (1983) (explaining that almost all legislative acts must satisfy the constitutional requirements of bicameralism and presentment to have effect).

explanation.zh:
第一条赋予国会(即众议院和参议院)采取立法行动的权力,当行动的目的或效果是改变国会以外的人的合法权利或义务时,即为立法。立法行动必须:

• 议会两院批准(即两院制)和

• 提交总统批准或不批准(即呈递),通过这一过程,国会可以将其一些权力(例如制定规则)下放给联邦行政机构。但一旦国会这样做,它就无法干预各机构的职能,除非它再次遵守立法行动程序。 任何绕过这一进程的企图都等于违宪的立法否决。

在此,国会授权联邦机构选择和建造纪念碑。 但一项法律规定阻止该机构在国会同时通过决议批准该机构的计划之前动用所拨款项。而由于该决议不会提交总统,该条款相当于对行政职能(即立法否决权)的违宪立法干预.

(Choice A) 关于政府机构的设置和设计的决定不完全是行政职能,因为国会也有权作出这些决定。

国会可以给其拨款附加合理的条件,比如指导行政部门如何使用资金。 但这种条件必须符合宪法(此处不见).

(Choice D) 该条款是国会两院通过的法规的一部分,由总统签署.然而,这一规定相当于违宪的立法否决,因为它赋予国会今后在不向总统介绍的情况下批准或不批准该机构计划的权力。

学习要点：

一旦国会将权力下放给一个行政机构,它就不能不满足立法行动程序 — — 即两院制和呈礼 — — 干预该机构的职能。 任何绕过这一进程的企图都是违宪的立法否决。

参考资料

• 《美国法典》第1条第7款,第2项(两院制和出示要求)。

· INS诉Chadha, 462 U.S.919, 951–52(1983)(解释几乎所有立法法案都必须符合两院制和呈文的宪法要求才能生效)。

stem:
A trade association in State A was formed for the purpose of protecting the state's lucrative cattle industry. The association's members, who are cattle breeders and dealers, use a grading system to grade the quality of cattle bred in the state. The grades assigned by the association are nationally recognized and prominently displayed on cattle to promote the state's cattle industry.

The commissioner of the agency that regulates cattle in State B has adopted a regulation that requires cattle sold in the state to display a grade approved by the federal government or no grade at all. The sales in State B of several members of the trade association have declined as a result of complying with this regulation. As a result, the association has filed suit against the commissioner in a federal district court, seeking an injunction against the enforcement of the regulation on the ground that it is unconstitutional.
stemZh:
A 位于 A 州的贸易协会成立是为了保护该州有利可图的畜牧业。该协会的成员是养牛者和经销商，他们使用一种分级系统来评估该州养殖的牛的质量。该协会所赋予的等级在全国范围内被认可，并在牛身上显著显示，以促进该州的畜牧业。

B 州监管畜牧业的机构负责人通过了一项规定，要求在该州出售的牛必须显示经联邦政府批准的等级，或者不显示任何等级。由于遵守这一规定，该贸易协会的几位成员在 B 州的销售有所下降。因此，该协会在联邦地区法院对负责人提起诉讼，要求禁止执行该规定，理由是该规定违宪。
ask: May the court determine the merits of this suit?
askZh: 法院可以确定此案的实质问题吗？

options.en: No, because the association itself has suffered no injury.
options.zh: 不能，因为该协会本身并未遭受损害。

options.en: No, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits suits against state officials in federal court.
options.zh: 不能，因为第十一修正案禁止在联邦法院对州官员提起诉讼。

options.en: Yes, because federal courts have exclusive jurisdiction over federal-law claims.
options.zh: 可以，因为联邦法院对联邦法律主张拥有专属管辖权。

options.en: Yes, because the association has standing to sue on behalf of its members.
options.zh: 可以，因为该协会有权代表其成员提起诉讼。

explanation.en:
Article III standing

(suing on another's behalf)

Organization members

Organization has standing if:

• members have standing to sue on their own behalf

• their injuries relate to organization's purpose AND

• lawsuit does not require member participation (if damages sought) Third party Injured plaintiff has standing when:

• parties share inextricably close relationship (eg, doctor/patient) AND

• obstacle prevents third party from suing (eg, privacy/retaliation concern) Child Parent has standing unless parental rights have been limited by court OR lawsuit may adversely affect child

Assignor Assignee has standing if assigned legal claim for ordinary & good faith business purpose

A federal court cannot hear a case unless the plaintiff has standing—ie, a concrete interest in the outcome of the case—to bring it. When the plaintiff is an organization (eg, trade association), the organization has standing to sue when it has suffered an injury. It also has standing to bring an action on behalf of its members when:

• the members themselves would have standing to sue (ie, members suffered an injury-in-fact that was caused by the defendant and is redressable by the remedy sought)

• the interests at stake (eg, members' injuries) relate to the organization's purpose and

• if damages are sought, the lawsuit does not require member participation (eg, to prove monetary damages).

Here, the association's members would have standing because the decline in sales (injury-in-fact) caused by the commissioner's regulation (causation) will be remedied if the court

grants an injunction (redressability). The decline in sales relates to the association's purpose of protecting State A's cattle industry. And since the association seeks an injunction (not damages), member participation is not needed. Therefore, the association

has standing to sue on behalf of its members, and the court may determine the merits of this suit.

(Choice A) An organization must suffer an injury-in-fact to have standing to sue on its own behalf. But an organization may have standing to sue on its members' behalf even if it has not suffered an injury.

(Choice B) The Eleventh Amendment generally bars private parties and foreign governments from suing a state in federal court for monetary relief. But it does not bar suits against state officials for injunctive relief (as seen here).

(Choice C) Federal and state courts have concurrent jurisdiction over federal-law claims unless the Constitution or Congress expressly provides federal courts with exclusive jurisdiction (not seen here).

Educational objective:

An organization has standing to sue on its members' behalf when (1) the members themselves would have standing to sue, (2) the interests at stake relate to the organization's purpose, and (3) if damages are sought, the lawsuit does not require member participation.

References

• U.S. Const. art. III, § 2 (case-or-controversy requirement).

• Hunt v. Wash. State Apple Adver. Comm'n, 432 U.S. 333, 343–45 (1977) (holding that organizations may bring actions on behalf of their members when the requirements for organizational standing are met.)

explanation.zh:
第三条

(代表他人发言)

组织成员

如果:

• 成员有权代表自己提起诉讼

• 他们的受伤与组织的宗旨有关;

• 诉讼不要求成员参与(如果要求损害赔偿)处于下列状态:

• 各方有着不可分割的密切关系(如医生/病人),

• 阻碍第三方起诉(例如隐私/报复问题),除非父母的权利受到法院或诉讼的限制,否则儿童父母有地位

为普通和诚信商业目的转让的法律债权的,受让人具有资格

联邦法院不能审理一个案件,除非原告有权提起诉讼,即对案件结果有具体利益。 当原告是一个组织(例如贸易协会)时,该组织在受到损害时有权提起诉讼。它还有权代表其成员在下列情况下采取行动:

• 成员本身应具有起诉资格(即成员遭受被告造成的实际伤害,可通过所寻求的补救办法予以补救)

• 利害关系(如成员受伤)与该组织的宗旨有关;

• 如果要求损害赔偿,诉讼并不要求成员参与(例如证明金钱损失)。

在此,该协会的成员将具有地位,因为如果法院裁决,由于专员条例(原因)造成的销售量下降(伤害)将得到补救。

销售量的下降与该协会保护A州牛业的目的有关,而且由于该协会寻求一项禁令(而不是损害赔偿),因此不需要会员参与。

有权代表其成员提出诉讼,法院可以裁定该诉讼的案情。

(Choice A) 一个组织必须受到事实伤害才能有代表自己起诉的资格,但一个组织即使没有受到伤害也可能有代表其成员起诉的资格。

(Choice B)第十一修正案一般禁止私人政党和外国政府向联邦法院起诉某州要求货币救济。 但并不禁止针对州官员要求强制救济的诉讼(如本文所示 ) 。

(C选择)联邦和州法院对联邦法律权利要求拥有共同管辖权,除非宪法或国会明确规定联邦法院拥有专属管辖权(此处不见).

学习要点：

一个组织有权代表其成员提起诉讼:(1) 成员本身有权提起诉讼,(2) 所涉利益与该组织的宗旨有关,(3) 如果要求损害赔偿,诉讼并不要求成员参与。

参考资料

• 美国康斯特公司第3条第2款(案件或争议要求)。

• Hunt诉Wash. State Apple Adver. Communication, 432 U.S.333, 343–45(1977年)(认为各组织在达到组织地位要求时可以代表其成员采取行动。 )

stem:
A senator made a speech on the floor of the U.S. Senate in which she asserted that a federal civil servant with minor responsibilities was twice convicted of fraud by a state. In making this assertion, the senator relied wholly on research done by her chief legislative assistant.

In fact, it was a different man with the same name, and not the civil servant, who was convicted of these crimes in the state court proceedings. This mistake was the result of carelessness on the legislative assistant's part.

No legislation affecting the appointment or discipline of civil servants or the program of the federal agency for which the civil servant works was under consideration at the time the senator made her speech about him on the floor of the Senate.

The civil servant sues the senator and her legislative assistant for defamation. Both defendants move to dismiss the complaint.
stemZh:
一名参议员在美国参议院议场发表演讲，其中她声称一名联邦文职雇员因欺诈罪被州法院两次定罪。在作出这一声明时，该参议员完全依赖其首席立法助理的研究。

事实上，被定罪的人是一个与该文职雇员同名但不同的人，且不是该文职雇员。这个错误是由于立法助理的疏忽造成的。

当时该参议员在参议院议场发表演讲时，并未涉及任何有关联邦文职雇员任命或纪律的立法，也未涉及该文职雇员所在联邦机构的项目。

该文职雇员起诉该参议员及其立法助理诽谤。两名被告均提出驳回诉讼的动议。
ask: As a matter of constitutional law, how should the court proceed on the defendants' motion?
askZh: 从宪法法的角度来看，法院应如何处理被告的动议？

options.en: Deny it as to both defendants, because any immunity of the senator under the speech or debate clause does not attach to a speech that is not germane to pending legislative business, and her legislative assistant is entitled to no greater immunity than the legislator he was assisting.
options.zh: 驳回针对两名被告的动议，因为参议员根据言论自由条款的豁免权不适用于与待审议立法事务无关的言论，且她的立法助理没有比他协助的立法者享有更大的豁免权。

options.en: Deny it as to the legislative assistant, because he is not a legislator protected by the speech or debate clause; but grant it as to the senator, because she is immune from suit for her speech by virtue of that clause.
options.zh: 驳回针对立法助理的动议，因为他是不受言论自由条款保护的立法者；但同意针对参议员的动议，因为根据该条款，她因言论而免于诉讼。

options.en: Grant it as to both defendants, because the senator is immune to suit for any speech she makes in the Senate under the speech or debate clause of Article I, section 6, and her legislative assistant may assert the senator's immunity for his assistance to her in preparing the speech.
options.zh: 同意针对两名被告的动议，因为参议员根据《宪法》第一修正案第六条的言论自由条款，对于她在参议院发表的任何言论均享有豁免权，且她的立法助理可以主张该豁免权以作为协助她准备演讲的依据。

options.en: Grant it as to the legislative assistant, because he is protected by the freedom of speech guarantee against defamation actions by government officials based on his mere carelessness; but deny it as to the senator, because, as an officer of the United States, she is a constituent part of the government and, therefore, has no freedom of speech rights in that capacity.
options.zh: 同意针对立法助理的动议，因为根据言论自由保障，基于其疏忽的言论不应受到政府官员的诽谤诉讼；但驳回针对参议员的动议，因为作为美国政府官员，她作为政府的一部分，因此在该身份下没有言论自由权利。

explanation.en:
Federal government immunities

Branch Actor Immunity Applicable suit

Legislative Member of Congress

• Absolute immunity for official legislative acts

Civil & criminal

Aide • Absolute immunity for acts that would be immune if performed by member of Congress Executive President • Absolute immunity for official executive acts

• No immunity for acts before taking office or unrelated to executive function

Civil

Aide/official • Qualified immunity for discretionary acts Judicial Judge/prosecutor • Absolute immunity for official judicial acts unless clearly lacks subject matter jurisdiction

Civil

Officer/employee • Absolute immunity for acts pursuant to court order

• Qualified immunity for discretionary acts The Article I, section 6 speech or debate clause gives members of Congress absolute immunity from criminal and civil liability for official legislative activities. This includes any speech made on the House or Senate floor—regardless of whether the speech relates to pending legislative business (Choice A). And this immunity extends to legislative aides who engage in activities that would be immune if performed by a member of Congress.

Here, the senator relied on the legislative assistant's careless research and falsely asserted that the civil servant had previously been convicted of fraud. The civil servant then sued both for defamation. But since the senator made the assertion during a speech on the Senate floor, she is immune from suit for that speech. And the legislative assistant may assert the senator's immunity for his assistance to her in preparing that speech. Therefore, the court should grant the motion to dismiss as to both defendants (Choice B).

(Choice D) All persons—including legislators—have freedom of speech. But defamatory statements fall outside First Amendment protections. And though prominent government

officials can only prevail in a defamation action if they prove actual malice, minor government officials need only prove negligence (as seen here). Therefore, only the speech or debate clause will immunize the defendants' conduct.

Educational objective:

Under the speech or debate clause, members of Congress are immune from criminal and civil liability for any official legislative activity (eg, a speech given on the floor of Congress). And this immunity extends to legislative aides who engage in conduct that would be immune if performed by a member of Congress.

References

• Gravel v. United States, 408 U.S. 606, 621–22 (1972) (holding that the speech or debate clause grants immunity to members of Congress and legislative aides for certain conduct).

• 77 Am. Jur. 2d United States § 7 (2019) (explaining that the speech or debate clause grants legislative immunity).

explanation.zh:
联邦政府豁免

适用诉讼

国会议员

• 官方立法行为的绝对豁免

民事和刑事

• 绝对豁免如果由议员执行的豁免行为 执行主席 绝对豁免官方行政行为

• 对就职前的行为或与行政职能无关的行为没有豁免

民事

• 司法法官/检察官绝对享有自由裁量行为合格豁免官方司法行为豁免,除非明显缺乏属事管辖权

民事

• 根据法院命令行事的绝对豁免

· 酌情行事的有限豁免 第一条,第6节 言论或辩论条款给予国会议员绝对豁免,使其免于对官方立法活动承担刑事和民事责任。这包括在众议院或参议院发言——无论发言是否涉及待决的立法事务(Choice A)。而这种豁免也适用于从事如果由国会议员执行则可以豁免的活动的立法助理。

在此,参议员依靠立法助理的粗心大意的研究,并谎称该公务员以前曾被判犯有欺诈罪,随后该公务员以诽谤罪起诉了两者。但是,由于参议员在参议院的一次演讲中提出了这一主张,她可以免去该演讲的诉讼。 立法助理可以主张参议员的豁免权,因为他协助她准备演讲。因此,法院应批准驳回两名被告的动议(Choice B)。

(Choice D) 所有人,包括立法者,都有言论自由,但诽谤性言论不属于第一修正案的保护范围。

只有在诽谤行动证明有恶意的情况下,官员才能胜诉,政府小官员只需要证明疏忽(如这里所见 ) 。 因此,只有言论或辩论条款才能对被告的行为免疫。

学习要点：

根据演说或辩论条款,国会成员对任何官方立法活动(如在国会场上发表的演说)免负刑事和民事责任.这种豁免也适用于立法助理人员,他们从事如果由国会议员执行则可以豁免的行为。

参考资料

• Gravel诉美国,408 U.S. 606, 621–22 (1972)(认为演讲或辩论条款给予议员和立法助理某些行为的豁免权)。

• 77 Am. Jur. 2d United States § 7 (2019)(解释言论或辩论条款赋予立法豁免权)。

stem: A state constitution provides that in every criminal trial "the accused shall have the right to confront all witnesses against him face to face." A defendant was convicted in state court of child abuse based on testimony from a six-year-old child. The child testified while she was seated behind one-way glass, which allowed the defendant to see the child but did not allow the child to see the defendant. The defendant appealed his conviction to the state's highest court, claiming that the inability of the child to see the defendant while she testified violated both the United States Constitution and the state constitution. Without addressing the federal constitutional issue, the state's highest court reversed the defendant's conviction and ordered a new trial. The court held that "the constitution of this state is clear, and it requires that while testifying in a criminal trial, a witness must be able to see the defendant." The state petitioned the United States Supreme Court for a writ of certiorari.
stemZh: 一州宪法规定，在每一刑事审判中，"被告有权面对指控他的证人进行对质。" 一名被告因儿童虐待罪在州法院被定罪，该罪名基于一名六岁儿童的证词。该儿童在作证时坐在单向玻璃后面，这使得被告可以看到该儿童，但该儿童看不到被告。被告向该州最高法院提出上诉，声称该儿童在作证时无法看到被告，违反了美国宪法和州宪法。最高法院未涉及联邦宪法问题，推翻了被告的定罪并下令重新审理。法院认为，"本州宪法明确要求，在刑事审判中，证人必须能够看到被告。" 该州向美国最高法院申请颁发调卷令。
ask: On which ground should the United States Supreme Court DENY the state's petition?
askZh: 美国最高法院应以何种理由驳回该州的申请？

options.en: A state may not seek appellate review in the United States Supreme Court of the reversal of a criminal conviction by its highest court.
options.zh: 一州不得向美国最高法院申请上诉审查其最高法院推翻刑事定罪的决定。

options.en: The decision of the state's highest court requires a new trial, and therefore it is not a final judgment.
options.zh: 该州最高法院的决定要求重新审理，因此它不是最终判决。

options.en: The decision of the state's highest court was based on an adequate and independent state ground.
options.zh: 该州最高法院的决定是基于一个充分且独立的州法律依据。

options.en: The Sixth Amendment to the United States Constitution does not require that a witness against a criminal defendant be able to see the defendant while the witness testifies.
options.zh: 美国宪法第六修正案不要求在证人作证时证人能够看到被告。

explanation.en:
The U.S. Supreme Court (SCOTUS) has discretion to review a highest state court judgment that turns on federal law. But SCOTUS must decline to review a state court judgment based on state grounds that are:

• adequate – the state grounds fully resolve the matter such that the application of federal law would not affect the outcome of the case and

• independent – it is clear from the opinion that the state court did not rely on federal law in reaching its conclusion.

Here, the defendant appealed his conviction to the state's highest court, claiming violations of both the U.S. Constitution and the state constitution. Without addressing the federal constitutional issue, the court reversed his conviction on the ground that the state constitution clearly requires that a witness be able to see a criminal defendant while testifying. Since the court's decision was based on an adequate and independent state ground, SCOTUS should deny the state's petition for a writ of certiorari (ie, request for appellate review).

(Choice A) A state may seek appellate review in the Supreme Court of the reversal of a criminal conviction by the state's highest court. But SCOTUS must decline to review the reversal if it rests on adequate and independent state grounds.

(Choice B) Although the decision of the state's highest court requires a new trial, it is a final judgment since it fully resolves the confrontation issue—ie, whether witnesses must be able to see criminal defendants while testifying—and that issue will not arise on retrial.

(Choice D) A criminal defendant's Sixth Amendment right to confront adverse witnesses does not require that a witness be able to see the defendant while testifying. But here, SCOTUS would not reach the merits of the defendant's Sixth Amendment claim since the decision of the state's highest court was based entirely on state law.

Educational objective:

The U.S. Supreme Court cannot review a state court judgment based on state-law grounds that are adequate (ie, the state grounds fully resolve the matter) AND independent (ie, the state court did not rely on federal law).

References

• Michigan v. Long, 463 U.S. 1032, 1041 (1983) (holding that a state supreme court judgment rests on adequate and independent state-law grounds if the state court makes a plain statement to that effect).

• 4 Am. Jur. 2d Appellate Review § 44 (2019) (explaining the plain statement rule).

explanation.zh:
美国最高法院(SCOTUS)有自由裁量权来审查最高州法院关于联邦法律的判决。 但SCOTUS必须拒绝审查州法院基于州理由的判决:

• 充分 - 州理由充分解决了联邦法律的适用不会影响案件结果的问题;

· 独立 – 从意见中可以明显看出,州法院在得出结论时并不依赖联邦法律.

在此,被告就他的定罪向州最高法院提出上诉,声称违反了《公约》。美国宪法和州宪法都是如此法院没有解决联邦宪法问题,就推翻了对他的定罪,理由是州宪法明确要求证人在作证时能够见到刑事被告。由于法院的裁决是基于充分和独立的国家理由,SCOTUS应拒绝国家要求获得复审令的请求(即上诉复审请求)。

(Choice A ) 州可以要求最高法院对州最高法院推翻刑事判决进行上诉复审。 但SCOTUS必须拒绝对推翻判决进行复审,如果它基于充分和独立的国家理由。

尽管州最高法院的裁决要求进行新的审判,但这是最后的判决,因为它充分解决了对抗问题——即证人在作证时是否必须能够见到刑事被告——而且这个问题不会出现。重审。

(Choice D) 刑事被告的第六修正案对面不利证人的权利并不要求证人在作证时能够见到被告.但在这里,SCOTUS不会达到被告第六修正案要求的案情,因为州最高法院的裁决完全基于州法律.

学习要点：

美国最高法院不能审查州法院基于州法理由做出的判决,这些依据是适当的(即州理由充分解决了问题)和独立(即州法院不依赖联邦法律).

参考资料

• 密歇根州诉Long案,463 U.S. 1032, 1041 (1983年)(认为州最高法院的判决基于适当和独立的国家法理由,如果州法院就此作出明确声明)。

• 4 Am. Jur. 2d 上诉审查§44(2019)(解释简单陈述规则)。

stem:
The United States found itself involved in a foreign conflict. Congress enacted a statute that established a military court in a foreign country to determine if individuals captured in an active combat zone should be classified as enemy combatants and detained until the cessation of hostilities. The statute provides that the military court may hear evidence presented by the captured individual at its discretion.

A man, a U.S. citizen, was captured in an active combat zone and tried by the military court. After the government presented its evidence, the court determined that the man was an enemy combatant and ordered that he be detained until the end of hostilities. The man was not permitted to provide a defense.

The man seeks to overturn his detention in a habeas corpus proceeding in a federal district court, claiming that the statute is unconstitutional as applied to him.
stemZh:
美国发现自己卷入了一场外国冲突。国会通过了一项法律，设立了一个外国国家的军事法庭，以确定在活跃战区被俘的个人是否应被认定为敌方战斗人员并被拘留，直到敌对行动结束。该法律提供，军事法庭可以自行决定听取被俘个人提供的证据。

一名男子，美国公民，在活跃战区被俘，并由军事法庭审判。在政府提出其证据后，法庭认定该男子为敌方战斗人员，并下令将其拘留至敌对行动结束。该男子未被允许提供辩护。

该男子在联邦地区法院提起人身保护令程序，声称该法律在适用于他时是违宪的。
ask: How is the federal court likely to rule in this action?
askZh: 联邦法院在这种情况下很可能如何裁决？

options.en: It will set aside the military court's ruling, because Congress has no enumerated power to establish military courts.
options.zh: 它将推翻军事法庭的裁决，因为国会没有明确列举的权力来设立军事法庭。

options.en: It will set aside the military court's ruling, because the man was entitled to a fair opportunity to rebut the government's factual assertions before a neutral decision-maker.
options.zh: 它将推翻军事法庭的裁决，因为该男子有权在中立的决策者面前反驳政府的实质性主张。

options.en: It will uphold the military court's ruling, because an individual in a foreign country does not possess constitutional rights.
options.zh: 它将维持军事法庭的裁决，因为外国国家的个人并不享有宪法权利。

options.en: It will uphold the military court's ruling, because federal courts do not have jurisdiction to review decisions issued by military courts.
options.zh: 它将维持军事法庭的裁决，因为联邦法院没有管辖权审查军事法庭的决定。

explanation.en:
The necessary and proper clause allows Congress to take actions that are reasonably necessary to carry out its enumerated Article I powers. Congress may therefore establish military courts and tribunals to carry out its enumerated powers to regulate the military and make rules regarding captures on land and sea (Choice A). Congress may grant military courts jurisdiction over enemy combatants, enemy civilians, and current members of the U.S. military.*

However, Congress must afford procedural due process to U.S. citizens classified and detained as enemy combatants. Procedural due process requires that U.S. citizens be given:

• notice of the factual basis for the citizen's classification as an enemy combatant and

• a fair opportunity to rebut the government's factual assertions before a neutral decision-maker. A U.S. citizen detained as an enemy combatant who does not receive these protections may file a petition for a writ of habeas corpus in a federal court unless Congress has explicitly suspended the writ (not seen here). The federal court has jurisdiction to then set aside an unlawful detention (Choice D).

Here, the man was captured in an active combat zone and classified as an enemy combatant by the military court. The statute gives the military court the discretion whether to allow a captured individual to provide evidence in his/her defense. However, the man is entitled to rebut the government's factual assertions because he is a U.S. citizen. Since the military court did not provide the man that opportunity, the statute is unconstitutional as applied to him. Therefore, the federal court will likely set aside the military court's ruling.

*Military courts and tribunals do not have jurisdiction over U.S. civilians who are not classified as enemy combatants unless hostilities have forced state and federal civilian courts to close.

(Choice C) U.S. citizens, including citizens in foreign countries, always possess constitutional rights.

Educational objective:

Congress may establish military courts and tribunals but must afford U.S. citizens classified as enemy combatants procedural due process. This requires (1) notice of the factual basis for the citizen's classification and (2) a fair opportunity to rebut those facts before a neutral decision-maker.

References

• U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 14 (power to make rules regarding capture).

• Hamdi v. Rumsfeld, 542 U.S. 507, 533 (2004) (O'Connor, J., plurality) (holding that detained U.S. citizens seeking to challenge enemy combatant status are entitled to procedural due process).

explanation.zh:
必要和适当的条款允许国会采取合理必要的行动,以行使第一条规定的权力。因此,国会可设立军事法庭和法庭,以行使其列举的监管军队的权力,并就陆地和海上的俘虏制定规则(Choice A)。国会可授予军事法庭对敌方战斗人员、敌方平民和现任美国军人的管辖权。

然而,国会必须向被归类为敌方战斗人员并被拘留的美国公民提供程序正当程序. 程序正当程序要求给予美国公民:

• 通知将公民列为敌方战斗人员的事实依据;

· 向中立决策者反驳政府事实指控的公平机会。 身为敌方战斗人员被拘留、得不到这些保护的美国公民可向联邦法院提出人身保护令申请,除非国会已经提出过。明确中止命令(此处不见)。联邦法院有权撤销非法拘留(Choice D)。

在此,此人在一个活跃的战区被俘,被军事法庭列为敌方战斗人员,法规赋予军事法庭是否允许被俘个人提供辩护证据的酌处权.但是,此人有权反驳政府的事实断言,因为他是美国公民。 由于军事法庭没有为此人提供这一机会,因此该法规对他适用是违宪的。因此,联邦法院很可能撤销军事法庭的裁决。

* 军事法院和法庭对不属于敌方战斗人员的美国平民没有管辖权,除非敌对行动迫使州和联邦民事法院关闭。

(CC) 美国公民,包括外国公民,始终拥有宪法权利.

学习要点：

国会可以设立军事法庭和法庭,但必须向被列为敌方战斗人员的美国公民提供正当程序。这要求(1) 通知公民分类的事实依据和(2) 向中立决策者反驳这些事实的公平机会。

参考资料

• 美国康斯特第一条,第8节,第14节(制定捕获规则的权力)。

• Hamdi诉Rumsfeld案,542 U.S. 507, 533(2004)(O'Connor, J.,多元性)(认为被拘留的美国公民试图对敌方战斗人员地位提出质疑,他们有权享有程序正当的程序)。

stem:
Congressional committees heard testimony from present and former holders of licenses issued by state vocational licensing boards. According to the testimony, the boards had unfairly manipulated their disciplinary proceedings in order to revoke the licenses of some license holders as a means of protecting favored licensees from competition.

In response, Congress enacted a statute prescribing detailed procedural requirements for the disciplinary proceedings of all state vocational licensing boards. The statute requires the state boards to provide licensees with adequate notice and opportunity for an adjudicatory hearing in all disciplinary proceedings. The statute also prescribes membership criteria for state vocational licensing boards, designed to ensure that the boards are likely to be neutral.
stemZh:
国会特别委员会听取了现任和前任州职业执照委员会所颁发执照持有者的证词。根据证词，这些委员会不公平地操纵了其纪律程序，以撤销某些执照持有者的执照，作为保护受青睐的执照持有人免受竞争的手段。

作为回应，国会通过了一项法律，规定所有州职业执照委员会的纪律程序的详细程序要求。该法律要求州委员会在所有纪律程序中，向执照持有人提供充分的通知和听证会的机会。该法律还规定了州职业执照委员会的成员资格标准，旨在确保这些委员会很可能保持中立。
ask: Which of the following provides the best source of authority for this federal statute?
askZh: 以下哪一项为该联邦法律的最佳权威依据？

options.en: Section 5 of the Fourteenth Amendment.
options.zh: 第十四修正案第五款。

options.en: The general welfare clause of Article I, Section 8.
options.zh: 第一修正案第八款的一般福利条款。

options.en: The privileges and immunities clause of Article IV, Section 2.
options.zh: 第四修正案第二款的特权与豁免条款。

options.en: The takings clause of the Fifth Amendment.
options.zh: 第五修正案的征收条款。

explanation.en:
Fourteenth Amendment protections

Clause Applicability

Equal protection Discriminatory treatment of similarly situated people

Due process Substantive – deprivation of life, liberty, or property without adequate justification

Procedural – deprivation of life, liberty, or property without adequate process

Privileges or immunities*

Interference with rights of national citizenship

*Rarely a correct answer.

Section 5 of the Fourteenth Amendment gives Congress the power to enact appropriate legislation to enforce the rights guaranteed by the amendment (eg, procedural due process). Legislation is appropriate under this section when it:

• seeks to remedy or prevent state action that violates the Fourteenth Amendment and

• is narrowly tailored—ie, its requirements are congruent with and proportional to the violations it addresses. A violation of procedural due process occurs when the state fails to follow certain procedures when it intentionally deprives a person of a life, liberty, or property interest (eg, vocational license). These procedures include giving the person notice and a meaningful opportunity to be heard by a neutral decision-maker.

Here, state vocational licensing boards apparently violated procedural due process by unfairly manipulating their disciplinary proceedings. Congress attempted to remedy this by enacting a statute prescribing detailed procedural requirements for such proceedings in all states. This statute is narrowly tailored since its requirements—ie, adequate notice and a hearing before a neutral board—are the basic standards of procedural fairness. Therefore, section 5 of the Fourteenth Amendment is the best source of authority for this statute.

(Choice B) The Article I, section 8 general welfare clause empowers Congress to spend for the general welfare (ie, for any public purpose). But this clause does not apply because the statute is not a spending measure.

(Choice C) The privileges and immunities clause of Article IV, section 2 prohibits states from improperly discriminating against citizens of other states. Since this statute does not address discrimination against citizens of other states, this clause does not apply.

(Choice D) The Fifth Amendment takings clause prohibits governmental taking of private property for public use without just compensation. But this clause only applies to real or personal property—not vocational licenses.

Educational objective:

Congress can enforce Fourteenth Amendment rights through legislation that (1) seeks to remedy or prevent state violations of the amendment and (2) is narrowly tailored—ie, its requirements are congruent with and proportional to the violations it addresses.

References

• Tennessee v. Lane, 541 U.S. 509, 520 (2004) (explaining that Congress can enact laws to remedy or prevent Fourteenth Amendment violations if there is congruence and proportionality between the injury and the law).

explanation.zh:
第十四修正案的保护

条款的适用

同等保护 对处境相似者的歧视性待遇

实质性 -- -- 剥夺生命、自由或财产,不充分说明理由

程序性----未经适当程序剥夺生命、自由或财产

特权和豁免*

干涉国家公民权利

* 几乎是一个正确的答案。

《第十四修正案》第5节规定,国会有权颁布适当立法。落实修正案所保障的权利(如程序正当程序)。在下列情况下,本节的立法是适当的:

• 寻求补救或防止违反第十四修正案的国家行动;

· 规定范围很窄——即其要求与它所处理的侵权行为相符,并与其相称。如果国家故意剥夺某人的生命、自由或财产利益(如职业许可证),却不遵守某些程序,即为违反程序正当程序。这些程序包括给予当事人通知和由中立决策者听取其意见的有意义的机会。

在这方面,国家职业许可证颁发委员会显然违反程序正当程序,不公平地操纵其纪律程序。国会试图通过颁布一项法规来补救这一点,该法规规定了各州此类程序的详细程序要求。这项法规是狭义的,因为其要求——即充分通知和在中立委员会听证——是程序公正的基本标准,因此,第十四修正案第5节是这一法规的最佳权威来源。

(Choice B) 第一条第八节一般福利条款授权国会为一般福利(即用于任何公共目的)支出。 但该条款不适用,因为法规不是支出措施。

(选择C)第四条第二款的特权和豁免条款禁止国家不适当地歧视其他国家的公民,由于本规约不涉及对其他国家的公民的歧视,本条款不适用.

(Choice D)第五修正案条款禁止政府将私人财产用于公共用途而不给予公正的赔偿,但这一条款只适用于不动产或个人财产,而不是职业许可证。

学习要点：

国会可通过立法强制执行第十四修正案的权利,立法:(1) 寻求补救或防止国家违反修正案的行为;(2) 立法的针对性狭隘,其要求与它所处理的侵权行为一致,并与其相称。

参考资料

• 田纳西州诉Lane案,541 U.S. 509, 520(2004年)(解释如果损害与法律之间有一致和相称性,国会可以颁布法律补救或防止违反第十四修正案的行为)。
