stem:
A jurisdiction has the following decisional law on questions of principal and accomplice liability:

CASE A: The defendant, a hardware store owner, sold several customers a device which detects police radar and enables speeders to avoid detection. When one of the devices broke down and the speeder was arrested, he confessed that he often sped, secure in the knowledge that the device would warn him of police radar in the vicinity. Held: The defendant is guilty as an accomplice to speeding.

CASE B: The defendant told a friend that the defendant had stored some stereo equipment in a self-storage locker. He gave the friend a key and asked her to pick up the equipment and deliver it to the defendant's house. The friend complied and removed the equipment from the locker using the key. In fact, the equipment belonged to the defendant's neighbor, whose locker key the defendant had found in the driveway. Held: The defendant is guilty as a principal to burglary.

CASE C: A city council member accepted a bribe from the defendant in exchange for his vote on the defendant's application for a zoning variance. A statute prohibits the taking of bribes by public officials. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to the city council member's violation of the bribery statute.

CASE D: The defendant, an innkeeper, sometimes let his rooms to prostitutes whom he knew to be using the rooms to ply their trade. He charged the prostitutes the same price as other guests at his inn. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to prostitution.

A plastic surgeon agreed to remove the fingerprints from the hands of a man whom the surgeon knew to be a safecracker. The surgeon charged his usual hourly rate for the operation. Afterward, the man burglarized a bank safe and was convicted of burglary. The surgeon has been charged with burglary.
stemZh:
在主要责任和共犯责任问题上,管辖权具有下列裁决法:

CASE A:被告是一家五金店的业主,他向几个客户出售了一个侦测警察雷达和使快车能避免侦测的装置。当其中一个装置故障,速度器被捕时,他承认他经常跳跃,明知该装置会警告他附近有警察雷达。被告是超速的共犯

CASE B:被告告诉一位朋友,被告将一些立体设备存放在自存柜里,他给了这位朋友一把钥匙,叫她拿起设备,送到被告家中.朋友听从了,用钥匙把设备从柜子里移走。事实上,这些设备属于被告的邻居,被告有他的储物柜钥匙被告犯有盗窃罪

CASE C:一名市议员接受被告的贿赂,以换取他对以下事项的投票:被告申请分区差异。一项法规禁止公职人员收受贿赂。被告人张某某违反受贿法规,作为市委委员的共犯不成立.

案件D:被告是一名旅馆老板,有时让他的房间给妓女,他知道这些妓女利用这些房间来拉皮条,他在旅馆对妓女收取与其他客人相同的费用。

一名整形外科医生同意从一名医生手中摘下指纹,外科医生知道他是一名安全者,外科医生为手术收取了他通常的小时费用,之后,他盗窃了一家银行的保险箱,并被判入室盗窃罪。外科医生被控入室盗窃
ask: Should he be convicted or acquitted of this crime?
askZh: 是否应当判定他有罪或无罪?

options.en: Convicted on the authority of Case A.
options.zh: 根据案件A的授权定罪。

options.en: Convicted on the authority of Case B.
options.zh: 根据B案的授权被定罪。

options.en: Acquitted on the authority of Case C.
options.zh: 根据C号案件的授权无罪释放。

options.en: Acquitted on the authority of Case D.
options.zh: 依据案件D的授权无罪释放.

explanation.en:
Although the surgeon did not commit burglary, he can be convicted under the theory of accomplice liability if he:

intentionally aided or encouraged the principal (the safecracker) before or during the crime with the specific intent that the crime be completed. As Case D shows, mere knowledge that the principal intended to use a person's aid— particularly aid involving the sale of goods or services—to commit a crime does not show that the person intentionally aided the principal. But such intent can be inferred when a seller provides highly specialized goods or services (as seen in Case A), receives unusually large profits from the sale, or has an interest in the crime's success beyond a mere sale.

Here, the surgeon removed fingerprints from a known safecracker at the surgeon's usual hourly rate (Choice D). But since a procedure that allows persons to avoid detection is highly specialized, the surgeon's intent to aid the safecracker in committing the burglary can be inferred—just as in Case A. Therefore, the surgeon should be convicted as an accomplice to the safecracker's burglary on this authority.

(Choice B) Case B shows that a defendant can be convicted as a principal for encouraging an innocent agent to commit a crime. An innocent agent is someone who lacked the requisite mens rea (eg, intent) because he/she was tricked or forced into committing the crime. But since the safecracker intentionally committed burglary, this authority does not apply here.

(Choice C) Case C shows that a person is exempt from accomplice liability when (1) the aided crime requires at least two participants but (2) the criminal statute only imposes liability on one participant. But this exception does not apply here because burglary— unlike bribery or the sale of narcotics—only requires one participant.

Educational objective:

An accomplice's intent to aid the principal can be inferred when the accomplice (1) provides highly specialized goods or services, (2) receives unusually large profits from a sale, or (3) has some greater interest in the crime's success.

explanation.zh:
虽然外科医生没有犯入室盗窃罪 但根据共犯的理论责任:

故意在犯罪之前或犯罪期间帮助或鼓励主犯(安全棍),具体意图是完成犯罪。如案件D所示,仅仅知道主犯意图利用某人的援助——特别是涉及货物或服务销售的援助——实施犯罪,并不表明该人有意帮助主犯。但是,如果卖方提供高度专门化的货物或服务(如案例A所示),从出售中获得异常巨大的利润,或者在单纯的出售之外与犯罪的成功有关,则可以推断出这种意图。

在这里,外科医生按照外科医生通常每小时的费率(Choice D)从一个已知的保险箱中取出指纹.但是,由于允许人们逃避侦查的程序是高度专门化的,因此可以推断出外科医生帮助保险柜员进行盗窃的用意——正如在A号案件中那样。因此,该外科医生应被判定为该当局盗窃保险箱的共犯。

B案(Choice B)表明,被告可以被判定为鼓励无辜代理人犯罪的主犯。 无辜的代理人是缺乏必要意图(例如意图)的人,因为他/她被骗或被迫犯罪。但是,由于保险箱是故意入室盗窃的,此权限在此不适用.

(C组)C案表明,如果(1)被协助的犯罪至少需要两名参与者,则一个人可以免除共犯责任,但(2)《刑法》只规定了一名参与者的责任。但这一例外在此不适用,因为盗窃——与贿赂或销售麻醉品不同——只需要一名参与者。

学习要点：

如果共犯(1)提供高度专业化的货物或服务,(2)从销售中获得异常大的收益,或(3)对犯罪的成功有某种更大的利益,则可以推断出共犯援助主犯的意图。

stem: A man decided to steal a valuable coin collection from a collector's house while the collector was away. Knowing that the house had an alarm system, the man contacted the pool cleaner who worked at the house twice a week. The man offered the pool cleaner part of the proceeds from selling the coin collection if she would disarm the alarm and leave a side door unlocked so that the man could enter the house. The pool cleaner pretended to agree but then contacted the police, who immediately arrested the man.
stemZh: 一个人决定趁收藏家不在时从收藏家家中偷一具珍贵的硬币收藏品,他知道房子有报警系统,便联系了每周在房子工作两次的游泳池清洁工.该男子提供出售硬币收藏所得的游泳池清洁剂部分,如果她解除警报并留下一个侧门未锁,以便男子可以进入房子.泳池清洁工假装同意,但随后联系警方,警方立即逮捕了此人.
ask: In a jurisdiction that follows the common law and has adopted the bilateral requirement for conspiracy, what crime has the man committed?
askZh: 在一个遵循普通法并采纳了共谋双边要求的法域中,此人犯了什么罪行?

options.en: Attempted burglary.
options.zh: 盗窃未遂.

options.en: Attempted larceny.
options.zh: 企图盗窃.

options.en: Conspiracy.
options.zh: 密谋.

options.en: Solicitation.
options.zh: 索隐.

explanation.en:
Inchoate crimes

Attempt Specific intent to commit crime & overt act committed in furtherance of target crime Merges with intended crime if completed Conspiracy Agreement entered with specific intent to commit crime & overt act committed in furtherance of agreement No merger Solicitation Inducing or encouraging another to commit crime with specific intent that crime be committed, but solicited party need not agree Merges with solicited crime if completed At common law (and in most jurisdictions), solicitation is an inchoate offense that requires proof that the defendant:

enticed, encouraged, or commanded another to commit a crime (eg, burglary or larceny) with the specific intent that the person commit that crime. Here, the man enticed the pool cleaner to help him steal the coin collection from the collector's house by offering to share proceeds from selling the collection with her. And the man specifically intended that the pool cleaner help him steal the coins by disarming the alarm and leaving a side door unlocked. Therefore, he committed solicitation.

(Choices A & B) Attempt occurs when a defendant (1) has the specific intent to commit a crime, (2) commits an act in furtherance of that crime, but (3) does not complete it. In this common law jurisdiction, an act must bring the defendant sufficiently close to completing the target offense. Therefore, mere preparation (eg, soliciting help to commit a crime) is not enough.

(Choice C) Conspiracy occurs when two or more persons enter an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime. The common law bilateral theory of conspiracy requires proof of at least two guilty minds—the defendant and one other conspirator. Therefore, a defendant cannot be convicted when the only other conspirator feigns agreement (as seen here).

Educational objective:

Common law solicitation occurs when a defendant (1) entices, encourages, or commands another to commit a crime (2) with the specific intent that the person commit the crime.

explanation.zh:
潜伏犯罪

实施犯罪的具体意图和为推进目标犯罪而实施的公开行为与意图犯罪有关的犯罪,如果完成共谋协议,有实施犯罪的具体意图;为促进协议而实施的公开行为引诱或鼓励他人犯罪,其具体意图是:虽已实施,但被请求方不必同意与被请求的犯罪合并,如果完成(和在大多数法域),教唆是一种不言自明的罪行,即:需要证明被告:

引诱、鼓励或命令他人实施犯罪(如盗窃或盗窃),具体意图是该人实施该犯罪。在这里,这名男子引诱泳池清洁工帮助他从收藏家家偷取钱币收藏品,提议与她分享出售收藏品的收益.这个人特别想让泳池清洁工解除警报器并打开侧门帮助他偷硬币。因此,他承诺要讨价还价。

(Choices A & B) 未遂发生在被告(1)有实施犯罪的具体意图,(2) 实施促进该犯罪的行为,但(3) 不完成。在这种普通法管辖权中,行为必须使被告充分接近完成目标犯罪,因此,仅仅准备(例如,寻求帮助犯罪)是不够的。

(C组)两人或两人以上达成有实施犯罪具体意图的协议时,即为共谋,普通法关于共谋的双边理论要求至少两个有罪的头脑——被告和另一个同谋——的证据。因此,当唯一的其他共谋者假意达成协议时(如本文所示),被告不能被定罪。

学习要点：

当被告(1) 引诱、鼓励或命令他人实施犯罪时,即发生普通法诱惑行为,(2) 其具体意图是该人实施犯罪。

stem: An undercover police detective told a local drug dealer that she wanted to buy cocaine but needed time to raise the necessary funds. The drug dealer said that he needed time to get the cocaine. They agreed to meet again in 10 days. An hour later, without a warrant, other officers forcibly entered the drug dealer's apartment and arrested him for attempted possession of a controlled substance.
stemZh: 一名卧底警察侦探告诉一名当地毒贩,她想购买可卡因,但需要时间来筹集必要的资金,毒贩说他需要时间来得到可卡因,他们同意在10天内再次见面.一小时后,其他警官在没有逮捕证的情况下强行进入毒贩的公寓,以企图持有受管制物质的罪名逮捕了他.
ask: If the drug dealer is prosecuted in a common law jurisdiction for attempted possession of cocaine, should he be convicted?
askZh: 如果毒品贩子因企图持有可卡因而在普通法管辖区受到起诉,他是否应当被定罪?

options.en: No, because he had not taken sufficient steps toward commission of the crime.
options.zh: 不,因为他没有为犯罪采取足够的步骤。

options.en: No, because he was illegally arrested.
options.zh: 不,因为他被非法逮捕。

options.en: Yes, because by objective standards the undercover detective and the drug dealer had made an agreement that the dealer would obtain cocaine.
options.zh: 是的,因为根据客观标准 卧底侦探和毒贩 已经达成了协议 毒贩会得到可卡因。

options.en: Yes, because he unequivocally expressed his intent to obtain the cocaine.
options.zh: 是的,因为他明确表示他想要得到可卡因。

explanation.en:
Attempt

(inchoate crime)

Mens rea

(specific intent)

Actus reus

(overt act)

Common law

Intends to commit target offense

Dangerous proximity test – performs act sufficiently close to completing target offense

Majority & MPC

Substantial step test – engages in conduct that exceeds mere preparation & strongly corroborates criminal intent

MPC = Model Penal Code.

Criminal liability for an attempted crime arises when a defendant:

has the specific intent to commit a crime performs an overt act in furtherance of the target crime but does not complete it. An overt act must go beyond mere preparation for the target crime. At common law, this requires the defendant to perform an act that is sufficiently close—in time and physical proximity—to completing the target crime (ie, dangerous proximity test). In other words, the defendant must commit an act that is indispensable to the crime's success.

Here, the drug dealer was charged with attempted possession of cocaine because he told the undercover detective that he needed time to get cocaine for her to buy. The drug dealer's statement evidences his intent to obtain cocaine. But this interaction did not amount to an overt act because it did not bring the drug dealer dangerously close to completing the crime—especially since he and the detective were not going to meet again for 10 days

(Choice D). Therefore, the drug dealer should not be convicted.

(Choice B) While an illegal (eg, warrantless) arrest may lead to suppression of evidence, it will not stop a criminal prosecution or serve as a defense to the charged crime. Therefore, the dealer could be convicted despite being illegally arrested.

(Choice C) Merely agreeing to commit a crime is not an overt act under either the dangerous proximity test (common law approach) or substantial step test (modern approach).

Educational objective:

Attempt requires proof that the defendant committed an overt act in furtherance of the intended crime. At common law, this requirement is met when the defendant performs an act that is dangerously close (in time and physical proximity) to completing the intended crime.

explanation.zh:
尝试

(潜伏犯罪)

男性犯罪意图a

(具体意图)

动作

(过时行为)

普通法

意图实施目标犯罪

危险近距离试验 -- -- 充分接近完成目标犯罪

多数和多氯乙烯

实质性步骤测试 -- -- 从事的行为超出单纯的准备,并有力地证实了犯罪意图

MPC=示范刑法。

如果被告:

有实施犯罪的具体意图的公开行为是为了推进目标犯罪,但没有完成它;公开行为必须不仅仅是为目标犯罪做准备。在普通法中,这要求被告的行为在时间和实际距离上足够接近,以完成目标犯罪(即危险距离测试)。换句话说,被告必须实施犯罪成功不可或缺的行为。

在这里,毒贩被指控企图持有可卡因,因为他告诉卧底侦探他需要时间为她购买可卡因,毒贩的陈述证明了他获取可卡因的意图.但这种互动并不等于是公开的行为,因为它没有使毒贩危险地接近完成犯罪,特别是因为他和侦探在十天之内不会再次见面。

因此,不应对毒贩定罪。

虽然非法(例如无证)逮捕可能导致对证据的压制,但它不会停止刑事起诉,也不会成为被指控罪行的辩护人,因此,尽管被非法逮捕,经销商仍可能被判罪。

仅仅同意实施犯罪,既不是在危险的近距离试验(普通法方法)下,也不是实质性步骤试验(现代方法)下的公开行为。

学习要点：

企图要求证明被告为推进意图而实施了公开行为。在普通法中,当被告实施危险行为时,即符合这一要求。(时间和实际距离)接近完成预定犯罪。

stem:
A man was planning to propose to his girlfriend, so he took her to a jewelry store to look at engagement rings. After trying on several rings, the girlfriend selected a ring that was well outside of the man's price range. The man asked the girlfriend to wait in the car while he purchased the ring. Once she exited the jewelry store, the man pulled out a gun and robbed the store.

After the robbery, the man calmly returned to the car and sat silently as the girlfriend unwittingly drove them to their house. Shortly after their arrival, a police officer knocked on their front door. Panicked, the man told the girlfriend that he had robbed the jewelry store and begged her not to open the door. Despite his pleas, the girlfriend answered the door. The man quickly hid inside their bedroom closet. When the officer asked the girlfriend where the man was, she said that the man was headed to a neighboring town. The girlfriend provided no further information to the police.
stemZh:
一个男人正打算向女友求婚,于是带她到一家珠宝店看订婚戒指,在试了几个戒指后,女友选择了远远超出男方价格范围的戒指.男方要求女友在购买戒指时在车上等候,当她离开珠宝店后,男方拿出枪抢走了店内.

ask: If the woman is charged as an accessory after the fact to robbery and the above evidence is presented at trial, which verdict should the jury render?

options.en: Guilty, because the girlfriend aided the man by driving the getaway car.
options.zh: 有罪 因为那个女朋友开着逃跑的车 帮了那个男人

options.en: Guilty, because the girlfriend told the police officer that the man was headed to a neighboring town.
options.zh: 罪名成立,因为女友告诉警察,这名男子正前往一个邻镇.

options.zh: 无罪,因为女友在案发后才得知抢劫事件.

explanation.en:
Parties to a crime

Modern view

Common law

Definition Liability

Principal Principal

(first degree)

Performs criminal act with requisite intent or uses innocent agent to commit criminal act

Target & foreseeable crimes

Accomplice Principal

(second degree)

Present at crime & aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime

Accessory

before the fact*

Not present at crime but aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime

Accessory

after the fact

Knows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or conviction

Independent crime

*Common law liability requires conviction of principal.

A person is an accessory after the fact if he/she:

knew that the principal had committed a felony aided or assisted the principal after the felony was committed and did so for the specific purpose of helping the principal avoid apprehension or conviction. As a result, a person who gives false information to the police to prevent the apprehension of a felon is an accessory after the fact. But a person who merely fails to report a crime is generally not.

Here, the girlfriend learned that the man had committed a felony after he told her that he had robbed the jewelry store. And though the girlfriend had no duty to report the robbery upon learning about it, she gave the police false information—that the man was headed to a neighboring town—to help him avoid apprehension (Choice D). Therefore, the jury should find the girlfriend guilty as an accessory after the fact to robbery.

(Choice A) The girlfriend may have aided the man by driving him away from the robbery. But at that time, she did not know that the man had committed the

robbery. Therefore, this fact is insufficient to find the girlfriend guilty as an accessory after the fact.

(Choice C) The girlfriend did not learn of the robbery until after its commission. But upon learning of it, she lied to the police for the specific purpose of helping the man avoid arrest and is therefore an accessory after the fact.

Educational objective:

An accessory after the fact is someone who knows that a person committed a felony and aids that person for the purpose of helping him/her avoid apprehension or conviction. One can be convicted as an accessory after the fact for giving the police false information to prevent apprehension of a felon, but not for merely failing to report a crime.

如果一个人:

因此,这个事实不足以认定女友在事后是同谋。

(Choice C) 女友直到犯罪后才得知抢劫,但在得知后,她为了帮助男子避免被捕的特定目的向警方撒谎,因此是事后的从犯.

stem: A man and a woman agreed that the woman would rob a bank and that the man would steal a car beforehand for the woman to use as a getaway vehicle. The man stole a car and parked it two blocks from the bank. He left the car key under the floor mat with a note saying that he wanted nothing more to do with the scheme. The next day, the woman robbed the bank and ran to the spot where the man had said he would leave the stolen car. She then escaped in the car and disappeared. She never shared any of the money with the man.
stemZh: 一名男女同意,该女子将抢劫银行,男子将事先偷一辆汽车供该女子用作逃跑的车辆,男子偷了一辆汽车,将其停在离银行两条街的地方。他把车钥匙留在地板垫下的纸条上,上面写着他不想再与这个计划有任何关系,第二天,那个女人抢劫了银行,跑到那个男人说他会离开被偷的车的地方,她随后在车里逃脱,然后失踪.她从未与他分享任何钱。
ask: In a jurisdiction that has adopted the bilateral requirement for conspiracy, can the man properly be convicted of conspiring with the woman to rob the bank?
askZh: 在一个采纳了双边共谋要求的法域中,能否适当地判定该男子与该妇女共谋抢劫银行?

options.en: No, because the man received no benefit from the robbery.
options.zh: 不,因为那人没有从抢劫中获得好处

options.en: No, because the man withdrew from the conspiracy.
options.zh: 不 因为那个男人退出了阴谋

options.en: Yes, because the robbery was successful due in part to the man's actions.
options.zh: 是的,因为抢劫是成功的 部分是由于他的行为。

options.en: Yes, because there was an agreement to rob the bank and an overt act in furtherance of the agreement.
options.zh: 是的,因为有一份抢劫银行的协议 和公开的行为推进协议。

explanation.en:
Conspiracy

Agreement Overt act

Majority view (modern & MPC)

Unilateral approach – at least one person specifically intends to enter agreement

At least one conspirator must commit overt act

Minority view (common law)

Bilateral approach – two or more persons specifically intend to enter agreement

Not required

MPC = Model Penal Code.

Conspiracy, at its core, is an agreement between two or more persons to commit a crime. Proof of an agreement depends on whether the prosecuting jurisdiction follows either:

the bilateral approach (minority rule) – requires proof that two or more persons entered the agreement with the specific intent to commit the target crime, so the defendant must be acquitted if other participants feigned agreement or

the unilateral approach (majority rule) – requires proof that the defendant entered the agreement with the specific intent to commit the target crime, so the defendant can be convicted even if other participants feigned agreement.

And most jurisdictions also require proof that at least one of the conspirators committed an overt act in furtherance of the conspiracy.

Here, there is proof of two guilty minds since the man and the woman agreed and specifically intended to rob a bank by having (1) the man steal a getaway vehicle and (2) the woman rob the bank. And they both committed overt acts in furtherance of their agreement when he stole the getaway car and she robbed the bank. As a result, the man can be convicted of conspiracy in this bilateral-approach jurisdiction (and any other jurisdiction).

(Choice A) A conspirator need not benefit from the target crime to be convicted of conspiracy.

(Choice B) A defendant can withdraw from a conspiracy before it is completed. But since the man attempted to withdraw after the conspiracy was completed—ie, after an agreement was formed and, if required, an overt act occurred—withdrawal is no defense.

(Choice C) The bank robbery was successful due in part to the man's overt act—stealing the getaway car. But he could be convicted even if the overt act had been completed by another conspirator or if the robbery had failed.

Educational objective:

The bilateral approach to conspiracy (minority rule) requires proof that two or more persons entered an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime. But the unilateral approach (majority rule) only requires proof that the defendant entered an agreement with such intent.

explanation.zh:
阴谋

公开行为

多数视图( 现代 & MPC)

单方面做法——至少有一人明确打算订立协议

至少一个同谋必须公开行动

少数群体观点(普通法)

双边办法 -- -- 两个或两个以上的人明确打算达成协议

无需

MPC=示范刑法。

共谋的核心是两人或两人以上之间达成犯罪协议。协议的证据取决于起诉管辖权是否遵循:

双边办法(少数群体规则)——要求证明两人或两人以上订立协议时有实施目标犯罪的具体意图,因此,如果其他参与者伪造协议,或

单方面做法(多数规则)——要求证明被告订立协议时有实施目标犯罪的具体意图,因此即使其他参与者假称协议,被告也可以被定罪。

并且大多数法域还要求证明至少有一名共谋者为推动共谋而实施公开行为。

这里有证据表明,由于男女双方同意并特别打算抢劫银行,他们 (1) 男子偷窃一辆逃跑的车辆,(2) 女子抢劫银行,所以有两个有罪的思想。两人都犯下了公开的行为,以推进他们的协议,当时他偷走了逃跑的汽车,她抢劫了银行。 结果,这名男子在双边管辖权(以及任何其他管辖权)中被判定犯有阴谋罪。

(Choice A) 共谋者不必从目标犯罪中获益而被判犯有共谋罪。

被告可以在阴谋完成之前退出阴谋。 但是,既然在阴谋完成之后,也就是在达成协议之后,如果需要,公开行为发生之后,此人试图退出,那么撤回就不是辩护。

银行抢劫之所以成功,部分原因在于此人的公开行为——偷逃车,但即使另一共谋者完成了公开行为,或者抢劫失败,他也可能被定罪。

学习要点：

对共谋采取的双边做法(少数群体规则)要求证明两人或多人达成有实施犯罪具体意图的协议。但单方面办法(多数规则)只要求证明被告有这种意图。

stem:
Four men are being tried for conspiracy to commit a series of bank robberies. Nine successful bank robberies took place during the period of the charged conspiracy. Because the robbers wore masks and gloves and stole the bank surveillance tapes, no witnesses have been able to directly identify the robbers. Some circumstantial evidence ties each of the men to the overall conspiracy.

During cross-examination, a prosecution witness testified that one of the men was in jail on other charges during the last six robberies. That man's lawyer has moved for a judgment of acquittal at the close of the government's case.
stemZh:
四名男子因阴谋进行一系列银行抢劫而受到审判,在被指控的阴谋期间发生了九起成功的银行抢劫。由于强盗们戴着面具和手套,并偷走了银行监视带,所以没有目击者能够直接辨认强盗的身份,一些间接证据将每个人与整个阴谋联系起来.

在盘问期间,一名检方证人作证说,其中一名男子在过去六起抢劫中因其他罪名而入狱,此人的律师在政府案件结束时提出宣布无罪的动议。
ask: Should the motion be granted?
askZh: 是否应该批准该动议?

options.en: No, because a conspirator is not required to agree to all of the objectives of the conspiracy.
options.zh: 不,因为不要求共谋者同意共谋的所有目标。

options.en: No, because a conspirator need not be present at the commission of each crime conspired upon.
options.zh: 不,因为共谋者不必在场 实施每一项犯罪共谋。

options.en: Yes, provided that the man has complied with the rule requiring pretrial notice of alibi.
options.zh: 是的,只要此人遵守了要求审前通知不在犯罪现场的规则。

options.en: Yes, regardless of compliance with the alibi rule, because the government is bound by exculpatory evidence elicited during its case-in-chief.
options.zh: 是的,不管不在场证明规则是否得到遵守,因为政府受到在主案期间获得的无罪证明的约束。

explanation.en:
A motion for a judgment of acquittal (ie, court-ordered acquittal) should be granted if the evidence presented at trial cannot establish guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. For conspiracy, this occurs when no rational trier of fact could find that:

two or more people entered an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime and in most jurisdictions, at least one conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of that agreement. Since the crime of conspiracy is completed once an agreement and (if required) overt act occur, a conspirator need not be present during the commission of the agreed-upon crime(s). Therefore, the man's inability to participate in the last six robberies due to his incarceration is no defense. And since circumstantial evidence ties him to the overall conspiracy to commit a series of bank robberies, his motion for acquittal should be denied.

(Choice A) Conspirators are required to agree on all essential objectives of the conspiracy—ie, the target crime or crimes.

(Choice C) Under the alibi-notice rule, the government may request information about a defendant's alibi defense. The defendant must then state (1) where the defendant claims to have been during the alleged crime and (2) the names, addresses, and telephone numbers of the defendant's alibi witnesses. But since the government's witness provided the man's alibi—ie, that he was in jail—this rule is irrelevant.

(Choice D) The government is not bound by exculpatory evidence elicited during its case-in-chief. But even if it were, the elicited testimony was not exculpatory because it was

immaterial to the man's guilt or innocence.

Educational objective:

A conspiracy is completed once an agreement and, if required, overt act occur. Therefore, a conspirator need not be present during the commission of the target crime(s) to be convicted of conspiracy.

explanation.zh:
如果在审判时提出的证据不能在有合理怀疑的情况下确定有罪,就应批准宣布无罪(即法院下令无罪)的动议。

两人或两人以上达成有实施犯罪具体意图的协议,在大多数法域中,至少有一名同谋为推动该协议而实施公开行为。由于一旦发生协议和(如果需要)公开行为,共谋罪即告结束,因此实施商定犯罪期间不必有共谋者在场。因此,此人由于被监禁而无法参与最后六起抢劫,这绝非辩护。 由于间接证据将他与实施一系列银行抢劫的整体阴谋联系在一起,因此应当驳回他的无罪释放请求。

(选择A) 阴谋者必须商定阴谋的所有基本目标——目标犯罪。

(C选择) 根据不在场证明通知规则,政府可以要求被告提供不在场证明辩护的信息.然后,被告必须说明:(1) 被告声称在被指控的犯罪期间的所在地;(2) 被告不在犯罪现场证人的姓名、地址和电话号码。但既然政府证人提供了此人的不在场证明 他当时在监狱里无关紧要

(Choice D) 政府不受在主案期间所引证的开脱罪责证据的约束,但即使如此,所引证的证言也并非因为是开脱罪责的证据.

对他有罪或无罪无关紧要

学习要点：

一旦达成协议,即完成共谋,如果需要,则公开行为发生,因此,实施目标犯罪期间,不必有共谋者在场,以共谋罪定罪。

stem: A man decided to rob a bank to pay off his crippling loan debt, so he purchased a gun, a mask, and some duffel bags. The man then told his friend that he had decided to rob a local bank and was going to scope it out the next day. As planned, the man went inside the local bank to look around. After surveilling the bank, he decided not to go through with robbing the bank because a bank in the neighboring city had fewer cameras. Unbeknownst to the man, the friend had called the police to inform them of the man's plan. As the man was walking back to his car, he was arrested by the police.
stemZh: 一个人决定抢劫一家银行以还清他沉重的贷款债务,于是购买了一把枪、一个面具和一些垃圾袋。 之后,他告诉朋友,他决定抢劫一家当地银行,并准备在第二天把它放出来。按计划,这名男子进入当地银行四处查看,在监视银行后,他决定不抢劫银行,因为邻近城市的一家银行的摄像头较少.此人不知情,这位朋友曾报警告知他们此人的计谋,当此人正步行回车时,被警方逮捕.
ask: Of what crime, if any, may the man be properly convicted?
askZh: 如果有犯罪的话,该男子可被适当定罪?

options.en: Attempted robbery, because he still intended to rob the neighboring bank.
options.zh: 企图抢劫,因为他仍然打算抢劫邻家银行.

options.en: No crime, because he voluntarily withdrew from the robbery.
options.zh: 没有犯罪,因为他自愿退出抢劫。

options.en: No crime, because his conduct did not exceed mere preparation.
options.zh: 没有犯罪,因为他的行为没有超过仅仅准备。

options.en: Robbery, because he committed an act in furtherance of that crime.
options.zh: 抢劫,因为他犯下了助长这种罪行的行为。

explanation.en:
Act

(requirement for attempt crimes)

Dangerous-proximity test

(common law)

Defendant performs act sufficiently close to completing crime—eg, act indispensable to crime's success, act close in time or physical proximity to crime

Substantial-step test

(majority & MPC)

Defendant's conduct exceeds mere preparation & strongly corroborates defendant's criminal intent—eg, surveilling place where crime is to occur

MPC = Model Penal Code.

Attempt occurs when a defendant (1) has the specific intent to commit a crime, (2) commits an act in furtherance of that crime, but (3) does not complete it. Under the substantial-step test used in the majority of jurisdictions, an act occurs when the defendant's conduct

exceeds mere preparation and strongly corroborates the defendant's criminal intent.

Here, the man did not actually rob a bank, so he cannot be convicted of robbery (Choice D). However, he did intend to do so. And though merely purchasing supplies for a robbery would not constitute a substantial step, his conduct exceeded mere preparation when he surveilled the bank (Choice C). Therefore, absent a defense, the man may be convicted of attempted robbery.

However, most jurisdictions recognize abandonment as a defense to attempt when a person completely and voluntarily turns away from a crime before completing it.* Abandonment is not voluntary if it is motivated by:

a desire to avoid detection a decision to delay the commission until a more favorable time or the selection of another similar objective or victim. Here, the man decided not to rob the local bank because a bank in the neighboring city had fewer cameras. This shows that his abandonment was motivated by his desire to avoid detection and the selection of another similar objective. Therefore, abandonment is not a defense here (Choice B).

*At common law, once the defendant has taken a substantial step toward the commission of the offense, the defendant may not claim abandonment due to a change of heart as a defense.

Educational objective:

Abandonment is not a defense to attempt if it was motivated by (1) a desire to avoid detection, (2) a decision to delay the commission until a more favorable time, or (3) the selection of another similar objective or victim.

explanation.zh:
行为

(犯罪未遂要求)

危险近距离试验

(普通法)

被告的行为足以接近完成犯罪——例如,犯罪成功必不可少的行为、及时行动或接近犯罪

实质性步骤试验

(多数和MPC)

被告的行为超出了单纯的准备,有力地证实了被告的犯罪意图——例如,监视犯罪发生地

MPC=示范刑法。

如果被告(1) 具有实施犯罪的具体意图,(2) 犯下了助长该犯罪的行为,但(3) 未能完成犯罪,则发生未遂。根据大多数法域采用的重大步骤标准,当被告的行为发生时即发生行为。

超越了单纯的准备 并有力地证实了被告的罪犯意图。

在此,此人实际上没有抢劫银行,因此他不能被判抢劫罪(Choice D)。 然而,他确实打算这样做。尽管仅仅为抢劫购买用品不构成实质性的步骤,但他在监视银行(Choice C)时的行为超出了准备范围。 因此,如果没有辩护,此人可能被判犯有抢劫未遂罪。

然而,大多数法域都承认,当一个人在完成犯罪之前完全和自愿地放弃犯罪时,放弃是一种企图辩护。

想要避免发现将佣金延迟到更有利的时间或选择另一个类似的目标或受害者的决定。 在此,此人决定不抢劫当地银行,因为邻近城市的一家银行的摄像头较少。这表明他的抛弃是出于他想要避免被发现和选择另一个相似的目标的动机,因此,放弃在这里不是辩护(Choice B).

* 根据普通法,一旦被告对犯罪采取了实质性步骤,被告不得因改变心意而要求放弃辩护。

stem: A woman wanted to kill a business competitor. She contacted a man who she believed was willing to commit murder for hire and offered him $50,000 to kill the competitor. The man agreed to do so and accepted $25,000 as a down payment. Unbeknownst to the woman, the man was an undercover police officer.
stemZh: 一个女人想杀死一个商业竞争者,她联系了一个她相信愿意杀人的人租借,并提议他5万美元杀死竞争者,这名男人同意了,并接受25000美元作为定金.这名男子是一名卧底警察。
ask: In a jurisdiction that has adopted the unilateral theory of conspiracy, is the woman guilty of conspiracy to murder the business competitor?
askZh: 在采用单方面阴谋论的管辖区,妇女是否犯有阴谋谋杀商业竞争者的罪行?

options.en: No, because it would have been impossible for the woman to kill the competitor by this method.
options.zh: 不 因为女人不可能用这种方法杀死竞争对手

options.en: No, because the man did not intend to kill the competitor.
options.zh: 不,因为他不想杀竞争对手

options.en: Yes, because the woman believed that she had an agreement with the man that would bring about the competitor's death.
options.zh: 是的,因为那个女人相信 她与那个男人有协议 会导致竞争者的死亡。

options.en: Yes, because the woman took a substantial step toward bringing about the competitor's death by paying the man $25,000.
options.zh: 是的,因为那个女人付出了25 000美元 朝着让竞争者的死亡迈出了一大步。

explanation.en:
Conspiracy

Agreement Overt act

Majority view (modern & MPC)

Unilateral approach – at least one person specifically intends to enter agreement

At least one conspirator must commit overt act

Minority view (common law)

Bilateral approach – two or more persons specifically intend to enter agreement

Not required

MPC = Model Penal Code.

Conspiracy occurs when:

two or more persons enter an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime and in most jurisdictions, an overt act is committed in furtherance of that agreement. The common law bilateral theory of conspiracy required proof of at least two guilty minds, so a defendant could not be convicted if the other conspirators had feigned agreement. But most jurisdictions now follow the unilateral theory of conspiracy, where only one guilty mind is required. That means a defendant can be convicted even if the other conspirators feigned agreement to commit the crime.

Here, the woman hired a man to kill her business competitor (agreement and intent) and gave him a $25,000 down payment (overt act). Therefore, the woman is guilty under the unilateral theory of conspiracy even though the man (an undercover police officer) did not intend to commit the crime. But had this jurisdiction followed the bilateral theory of conspiracy, the man's feigned agreement would have absolved the woman of this crime

(Choice B).

(Choice A) It would have been impossible for the woman to kill the competitor by this method since the man was an undercover police officer. But the woman is still guilty since factual impossibility is no defense to conspiracy.

(Choice D) Most jurisdictions require proof of an overt act to convict a defendant of attempt or conspiracy. While attempt requires proof of a substantial step—ie, conduct strongly corroborating criminal intent (more than mere preparation)—conspiracy only requires discernible evidence that the conspiracy is at work (including acts of mere preparation). Here, the woman's $25,000 down payment is an overt act under both standards. But it would only support her conviction if an overt act is an element of conspiracy in this jurisdiction.

Educational objective:

The unilateral theory of conspiracy requires only one guilty mind, so a defendant is guilty even if the other conspirators feigned agreement to commit the crime. But since the bilateral theory requires two guilty minds, a defendant would not be guilty if the other conspirators feigned agreement.

References

16 Am. Jur. 2d Conspiracy § 16 (2019) (unilateral theory of conspiracy).

Model Penal Code § 5.03 (Am. Law Inst. 2019) (criminal conspiracy).

explanation.zh:
阴谋

公开行为

多数视图( 现代 & MPC)

单方面做法——至少有一人明确打算订立协议

至少一个同谋必须公开行动

少数群体观点(普通法)

双边办法 -- -- 两个或两个以上的人明确打算达成协议

无需

MPC=示范刑法。

阴谋发生于:

两人或两人以上订立有实施犯罪具体意图的协议,在大多数法域,实施公开行为是为了促进该协议。普通法关于共谋的双边理论要求至少证明两个有罪的思想,因此,如果其他共谋者假意达成协议,被告就不能被定罪。但是,大多数法域现在都遵循了单方面的阴谋论,即只需要一种有罪的思想。 这意味着即使其他共谋者假意同意犯罪,被告也可以被定罪。

在此,该妇女雇用一名男子杀害其商业竞争者(协议和意图),并给他25 000美元的首付(公开行为)。因此,即使该男子(一名卧底警官)不打算犯罪,根据单方面的阴谋论,该妇女仍有罪。但是如果这个司法管辖权遵循了双边的阴谋论,那男人的假协议本可以免除这个女人的罪行

(中文(简体) ).

由于该男子是卧底警察,该妇女不可能用这种方法杀死竞争者。 但该妇女仍然有罪,因为事实上不可能不是阴谋辩护。

(Choice D)大多数法域都要求证明公开的行为,以判定被告犯有未遂或共谋罪。虽然企图需要证明实质性步骤——即进行有力证实犯罪意图(不仅仅是准备)——但阴谋只需要有明显证据证明阴谋正在起作用(包括仅仅准备的行为)。这里,妇女25 000美元的首付是两种标准下的公开行为,但只有公开行为是本辖区内阴谋的一个因素,才能支持她的定罪。

学习要点：

单方面的阴谋论只需要一个有罪的思想,所以即使另一个阴谋者假装同意犯罪,被告也是有罪的.但是由于双边理论需要两个有罪的头脑,如果其他阴谋者假装同意,被告就不会有罪.

参考资料

16 Am. Jur. 2d Conspiracy § 16 (2019)(单方阴谋论).

《刑法典范本》第5.03条(第2019号法律)(共谋犯罪)。

stem:
A jurisdiction has the following decisional law on questions of principal and accomplice liability:

CASE A: The defendant, a hardware store owner, sold several customers a device which detects police radar and enables speeders to avoid detection. When one of the devices broke down and the speeder was arrested, he confessed that he often sped, secure in the knowledge that the device would warn him of police radar in the vicinity. Held: The defendant is guilty as an accomplice to speeding.

CASE B: The defendant told a friend that the defendant had stored some stereo equipment in a self-storage locker. He gave the friend a key and asked her to pick up the equipment and deliver it to the defendant's house. The friend complied and removed the equipment from the locker using the key. In fact, the equipment belonged to the defendant's neighbor, whose locker key the defendant had found in the driveway. Held: The defendant is guilty as a principal to burglary.

CASE C: A city council member accepted a bribe from the defendant in exchange for his vote on the defendant's application for a zoning variance. A statute prohibits the taking of bribes by public officials. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to the city council member's violation of the bribery statute.

CASE D: The defendant, an innkeeper, sometimes lent his rooms to prostitutes whom he knew to be using the rooms to ply their trade. He charged the prostitutes the same price as other guests at his inn. Held: The defendant is not guilty as an accomplice to prostitution.

In this jurisdiction, conviction for statutory rape requires proof of the defendant's knowledge that the victim is underage. A high school student, who knew that a girl was underage, encouraged his friend, who was unaware of the girl's age, to have sex with the girl. The student has been charged with statutory rape.
stemZh:
在主要责任和共犯责任问题上,管辖权具有下列裁决法:

CASE A:被告是一家五金店的业主,他向几个客户出售了一个侦测警察雷达和使快车能避免侦测的装置。当其中一个装置故障,速度器被捕时,他承认他经常跳跃,明知该装置会警告他附近有警察雷达。被告是超速的共犯

CASE B:被告告诉一位朋友,被告将一些立体设备存放在自存柜里,他给了这位朋友一把钥匙,叫她拿起设备,送到被告家中.朋友听从了,用钥匙把设备从柜子里移走。事实上,这些设备属于被告的邻居,被告有他的储物柜钥匙被告犯有盗窃罪

CASE C:一名市议员接受被告的贿赂,以换取他对以下事项的投票:被告申请分区差异。一项法规禁止公职人员收受贿赂。被告人张某某违反受贿法规,作为市委委员的共犯不成立.

CASE D:被告是一名旅馆老板,他有时把房间借给妓女,他知道这些妓女利用这些房间来拉皮条,他在旅馆对妓女收取与其他客人相同的费用。

在这个管辖区内,对法定强奸的定罪需要证明被告知道受害人是未成年人,一名高中生知道一个女孩是未成年人,他鼓励不知道女孩年龄的朋友与女孩发生性关系。该学生被指控犯有法定强奸罪。
ask: Should the student be convicted or acquitted of this crime?
askZh: 该学生应被判有罪还是无罪?

options.en: Convicted on the authority of Case A.
options.zh: 根据案件A的授权定罪。

options.en: Convicted on the authority of Case B.
options.zh: 根据B案的授权被定罪。

options.en: Acquitted on the authority of Case C.
options.zh: 根据C号案件的授权无罪释放。

options.en: Acquitted on the authority of Case D.
options.zh: 依据案件D的授权无罪释放.

explanation.en:
Parties to a crime

Modern view

Common law

Definition Liability

Principal Principal

(first degree)

Performs criminal act with requisite intent or uses innocent agent to commit criminal act

Target & foreseeable crimes

Accomplice Principal

(second degree)

Present at crime & aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime

Accessory

before the fact*

Not present at crime but aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime

Accessory

after the fact

Knows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or conviction

Independent crime

*Common law liability requires conviction of principal.

In this jurisdiction, statutory rape occurs when a person has sex with a victim (actus reus) with knowledge that the victim is underage (mens rea). And a conviction can stem from either:

principal liability – if the actus reus was committed by the defendant or, as evidenced in Case B, another who acted on the defendant's behalf but lacked the requisite mens rea (ie, an innocent agent) or

accomplice liability – if the defendant intentionally aided or encouraged another who had the requisite mens rea (ie, the principal) before or during a crime with the intent that the crime be completed.

Here, the student had the requisite mens rea since he knew that the girl was underage. But like the defendant in Case B, the student did not commit the actus reus—he encouraged his friend to do so. And since the friend lacked the mens rea necessary to commit statutory rape because he did not know that the girl was underage, he was an innocent agent (like the friend in Case B). Therefore, the student should be convicted of statutory rape as a principal—not an accomplice.

(Choices A, C, & D) Cases A, C, and D concern accomplice liability, which subjects the principal and accomplice to equal liability for a crime. But this theory of liability does not apply here because the friend lacked the necessary mens rea for statutory rape in this jurisdiction—ie, knowledge that the victim was underage. Therefore, the student cannot be liable as an accomplice to the friend's innocent act.

Educational objective:

Principal liability is imposed when (1) the defendant possessed the requisite mens rea and (2) the actus reus was committed by the defendant or the defendant's innocent agent—ie, a person who lacked the mens rea required for the crime.

学生知道这名女孩是未成年人,因此拥有必要的犯罪意图。 但是,与B号案件的被告一样,学生没有犯下犯罪意图——他鼓励他的朋友这样做。而由于这位朋友缺乏实施法定强奸所必需的男性犯罪意图,因为他不知道这名女孩是未成年人,所以他是一个无辜的特工(如案件B中的朋友).因此,学生应作为主犯而不是从犯被判犯有法定强奸罪。

(选择A、C、和D)案件A、C和D涉及共犯责任,使主犯和共犯对犯罪负有同等责任。但这一责任论在此不适用,因为朋友在本辖区缺乏法定强奸的必要意图,即知道受害者是未成年人,因此,学生不能作为朋友的无辜行为的共犯承担责任。

stem:
A landlord decided to destroy his dilapidated building in order to collect the insurance money. He hired a man to burn down the building. The man broke into the building and carefully searched it to make sure no one was inside. The man failed, however, to see a person experiencing homelessness asleep in an office closet. The man started a fire. The building was destroyed, and the person experiencing homelessness died from burns a week later. Two days after the fire, the landlord filed an insurance claim in which he stated that he had no information about the cause of the fire.

The landlord is charged with felony murder of the person experiencing homelessness.
stemZh:
一个房东决定摧毁他破旧的建筑,以收取保险金,他雇了一个人烧毁建筑,那人闯进大楼仔细搜查,以确保里面没有人.然而,这名男子没有看到一个正在经历无家可归的人在办公室的衣柜里睡觉,这名男子引发了火灾,大楼被毁,这名经历无家可归的人一周后因烧伤而死亡.火灾发生两天后,房东提出保险索赔,称自己没有火灾原因的信息.

房东被控重罪谋杀受难者无家可归。
ask: If the landlord is found guilty, it is because the death of the person experiencing homelessness occurred in connection with which felony?
askZh: 如果房东被判有罪,那是因为无家可归的人的死亡与哪一种重罪有关?

options.en: Arson.
options.zh: 纵火

options.en: Burglary.
options.zh: 盗ary.

options.en: Conspiracy.
options.zh: 密谋.

options.en: Fraud.
options.zh: 欺诈。

explanation.en:
Accomplice liability arises when a person intentionally aids, encourages, or solicits another (principal) to commit a crime with the intent that the crime be completed. An accomplice is liable to the same extent as the principal for the encouraged crime and any crimes that occur as a natural and probable (ie, foreseeable) consequence of that crime.

Here, the landlord became an accomplice when he hired the man to burn down his building (ie, solicited arson). The landlord did not encourage the commission of felony murder—the killing of another during the commission, or attempted commission, of an inherently dangerous felony like arson. But he still could be found guilty of felony murder since the person experiencing homelessness died from burns caused by that fire (foreseeable consequence of arson).

(Choice B) Burglary is an inherently dangerous felony that requires proof of a (1) trespassory entering of another's property (2) with the specific intent to commit a crime therein. Although the man intended to commit arson in the landlord's building, he did not trespass because the landlord consented to his entry (no burglary).

(Choice C) Criminal conspiracy occurs when (1) two or more persons enter an agreement with the specific intent to commit a crime and (2) one of the conspirators commits an overt act in furtherance of that agreement. Although the landlord and the man conspired to commit arson, the felony murder conviction must be based on an inherently dangerous felony—not their conspiracy.

(Choice D) Fraud requires proof that the defendant made a false representation with the specific intent to permanently obtain the victim's property. But since fraud is not an inherently dangerous felony, it can never be the basis for felony murder.

Educational objective:

An accomplice is someone who intentionally aids, encourages, or solicits another to commit a crime with the intent that the crime be completed. As a result, an accomplice is liable for the encouraged crime and any crimes that occur as a natural and probable consequence of that crime.

explanation.zh:
如果某人故意协助、鼓励或教唆他人(主要)犯罪,意图完成犯罪,则产生共犯责任。共犯应承担与所鼓励的犯罪和作为该犯罪的自然和可能(即可预见的)后果而发生的犯罪的主犯同等的责任。

在这里,当房东雇人烧毁他的建筑(即煽动纵火)时,他成了同谋.房东不鼓励实施重罪谋杀——在纵火等具有内在危险性的重罪中杀害另一人,或企图这样做。但是,他仍然可以被判犯有重罪谋杀罪,因为遭受无家可归的人死于那场火灾造成的烧伤(可预见纵火的后果)。

(Choice B) 盗窃是一种固有的危险重罪,需要证明(1) 非法进入他人财产(2) 具有在其中犯罪的具体意图。虽然这名男子打算在房东的建筑内纵火,但他没有侵入,因为房东同意他进入(没有入室盗窃).

(C类) 犯罪共谋是指:(1) 两人或两人以上达成有实施犯罪具体意图的协议,(2) 共谋者中一人为推动该协议而实施公开行为。虽然地主和男人密谋纵火,但重罪谋杀判决必须基于固有的危险重罪,而不是他们的阴谋。

(Choice D ) 欺诈需要证明被告做了虚假陈述,其具体意图是永久获得受害人的财产。 但是,由于欺诈不是一个固有的危险重罪,它永远不能成为重罪谋杀的依据。

学习要点：

共犯是指故意协助、鼓励或教唆他人从事下列活动的人:- 犯罪意图是完成犯罪。因此,共犯应对所鼓励的犯罪和作为该犯罪的自然和可能后果发生的任何犯罪承担责任。

stem: A man was angry at a coworker who had received a promotion. The man believed that the coworker had taken credit for the man's work and had bad-mouthed him to their boss. One day, as the man was leaving the company parking lot in his car, he saw the coworker walking through the lot. On a sudden impulse, the man pushed the accelerator pedal hard and veered toward the coworker with the intention of scaring him. The coworker tried to jump out of the way but slipped and fell and was run over. Although the coworker suffered life-threatening injuries, he survived.
stemZh: 一个人对得到晋升的同工感到愤怒,他相信同工的功劳是他的功劳,并对他们的老板说坏话.有一天,当这名男子正坐在车里离开公司停车场时,他看到同事走过停车场,突然的冲动,他把加速器踩踏硬地推向同事,意图吓唬他.同事试图跳出路面,但滑倒后被撞倒,虽然同事遭受了危及生命的伤害,但幸存下来.
ask: In a jurisdiction that follows the common law of homicide, could the man properly be convicted of attempted murder?
askZh: 在一个遵循杀人普通法的法域中,该男子是否可以被判定犯有谋杀未遂罪?

options.en: No, because the coworker's slip and fall broke the chain of proximate causation.
options.zh: 不,因为同事的滑倒 打破了近因的链条。

options.en: No, because the man lacked the requisite intent.
options.zh: 不,因为这个人缺乏必要的意图。

options.en: Yes, because the coworker suffered life-threatening injuries.
options.zh: 是的,因为同事受到危及生命的伤害。

options.en: Yes, because the man acted with reckless disregard for human life.
options.zh: 是的,因为这个人不顾人的生命 鲁莽地行事

explanation.en:
Attempt is an inchoate crime that requires proof that a defendant:

had the specific intent to commit a crime (eg, murder) performed an overt act in furtherance of the intended crime but did not complete it. Therefore, attempted murder requires proof that the defendant specifically intended to kill the victim. This is true even though a completed murder can be established without showing an intent to kill—ie, when there is some other type of malice aforethought.

Here, the man cannot be convicted of attempted murder because he only intended to scare the coworker—not kill him. But had the coworker died, the man could have been convicted of murder since he acted with reckless disregard for human life (ie, malice aforethought) when he accelerated toward the coworker (Choice D).

(Choice A) Causation is relevant to crimes that require the occurrence of a particular result—eg, murder requires that the defendant cause the victim's death. But causation is irrelevant to attempt (and other inchoate crimes) since the intended result need not be completed. Therefore, the man is not guilty of attempted murder regardless of whether the coworker's slip and fall broke the chain of causation.

(Choice C) Although the coworker suffered life-threatening injuries, the man cannot be convicted of attempted murder since he lacked the specific intent to kill.

Educational objective:

Attempt is a specific intent crime. Therefore, attempted murder requires proof that the defendant acted with the intent to kill—no other form of malice aforethought will suffice.

explanation.zh:
未遂是一种无中生有的罪行,需要证明被告:

犯下罪行(例如谋杀)的具体意图是为了促进有意犯罪,但并未完成。因此,谋杀未遂需要证明被告特别意图杀害被害者们即便在有某种其他恶意预谋的情况下,在不表明杀人意图的情况下,可以确定已完成的谋杀也是事实。

这里,他不能被判谋杀未遂 因为他只是想吓唬他同事 不要杀了他但是,如果合作者死亡,他可能被判犯有谋杀罪,因为他在加速向合作者(Choice D)前进时不顾人的生命(即恶意的预谋)。

(Choice A) 因果关系与需要发生某一特定结果的犯罪有关——例如,谋杀要求被告造成受害者的死亡。但因果关系与企图无关(以及其他不言而喻的罪行),因为预期结果不需要完成。 因此,无论同事的失误和倒下是否打破了因果关系链条,此人都没有谋杀未遂罪。

(Choice C)虽然同事遭受了危及生命的伤害,但由于他缺乏杀人的具体意图,因此不能判定他犯有谋杀未遂罪.

学习要点：

因此,谋杀未遂需要证明被告有杀人意图——任何其他形式的恶意预谋都是不够的。

stem:
A bank teller was fired by the president of the bank. The teller decided to take revenge against the president but decided against attempting it personally because he knew the president was protected around the clock by bank security guards. The teller also knew that his cousin had a violent temper and was very jealous. The teller falsely told his cousin that the cousin's wife was having an affair with the president. Enraged, the cousin said, "What am I going to do?" The teller said, "If it were my wife, I'd just march into his office and blow his brains out."

The cousin grabbed a revolver and rushed to the bank. He walked into the bank, carrying the gun in his hand. One of the security guards, believing a holdup was about to occur, shot and killed the cousin.
stemZh:
一名银行出纳员被银行总裁解雇,出纳员决定对总统进行报复,但决定不亲自尝试,因为他知道总统全天候受到银行保安的保护.计票人也知道他的表弟脾气暴躁,非常嫉妒.出纳者谎称其表妹,表妹的妻子与总统有染.怒,表弟曰:"吾何所为?"出纳者曰:"若是吾妻,我只可进其办公室,轰其脑.

该堂兄弟抓住左轮手枪冲向银行,他走进银行,手里拿着枪,其中一名保安认为即将发生抢劫,开枪打死了该堂兄弟.
ask: If the teller is charged with attempted murder of the president, which verdict should be rendered?
askZh: 如果监票人被控谋杀总统未遂,应作出何种判决?

options.en: Guilty, because he intended to kill the president and used the cousin to carry out his plan.
options.zh: 罪过 因为他打算杀死总统 利用表弟来实施他的计划

options.en: Guilty, because he was extremely reckless as to the president.
options.zh: 因为他对总统极其鲁莽

options.en: Not guilty, because the cousin, if successful, would be guilty of no more than manslaughter and an accomplice cannot be guilty of a higher crime than the principal.
options.zh: 无罪,因为堂兄弟如果成功,只能犯过失杀人罪,而共犯的罪行不能高于主犯。

options.en: Not guilty, because the president was never in imminent danger of being killed.
options.zh: 无罪 因为总统从未面临被杀的危险

explanation.en:
Attempt is an inchoate crime that requires proof of three elements:

The defendant had the specific intent to commit a crime. The defendant—or his/her agent—performed an act in furtherance of that crime. The target crime was not completed. Proof of specific intent is always required for attempt—even when proof of a lesser mental state would be sufficient for the target crime. Therefore, a defendant is only guilty of attempted murder if he/she specifically intended to kill the victim. No other type of malice aforethought will suffice (Choice B).

Here, the teller intended to have the bank president killed. And the teller committed an act in furtherance of this crime—and used the cousin to carry out his plan—when the teller lied to the cousin about his wife's affair and urged him to shoot the president. But since the cousin was shot by a security guard, the president's murder was never completed. Therefore, the teller is guilty of attempted murder.

(Choice C) Had the intended murder been successful, it would not have been reduced to voluntary manslaughter since there was no adequate provocation or other mitigating factor. And though an accomplice (person encouraging crime) cannot be guilty of a higher crime than the principal (person committing criminal act), they are equally liable. Therefore, the teller (accomplice) and the cousin (principal) are equally guilty of attempted murder.

(Choice D) The lack of imminent danger would only negate the act requirement in the few jurisdictions that use the dangerous proximity test. Under this test, an act occurs when the defendant is so close to completing the target crime that it is essentially unstoppable. But most jurisdictions use the substantial step test, which only requires that an act exceed mere preparation and strongly corroborate the defendant's criminal intent.

Educational objective:

Attempt always requires (1) the specific intent to commit a crime and (2) an act by the defendant or his/her agent in furtherance of that crime.

explanation.zh:
未遂是一种不言自明的犯罪,需要证明三个要素:

被告有实施犯罪的具体意图,被告——或其代理人——为推进这一犯罪而实施了一种行为,目标犯罪尚未完成。未遂总是需要具体意图的证据——即使精神状态较低的证据足以证明目标罪行,因此,被告只有在具体意图杀害受害者的情况下才犯有谋杀未遂罪。任何其他类型的恶意预谋都不足以解决问题(选择B)。

这时,出纳官打算杀死银行总裁。 而出纳官为了推进这一犯罪而做了一件事情 — — 并用表哥来实施他的计划 — — 当时,出纳官对表哥谎报了他妻子的外遇,敦促他向总统开枪。但是由于表弟被保安开枪射杀,总统的谋杀从未完成,因此计票人犯有谋杀未遂罪.

(C组)如果计划谋杀成功,就不会沦为故意杀人罪,因为没有适当的挑衅或其他减轻罪责的因素。尽管共犯(个人鼓励犯罪)不能比主犯(实施犯罪的人)更重,但他们同样负有责任,因此,计票人(共犯)和堂兄弟(主犯)同样犯有谋杀未遂罪。

(Choice D) 缺乏迫在眉睫的危险只会否定少数使用危险近距离测试的法域的行为要求,在这个测试下,当被告接近完成目标犯罪以致基本无法阻止时,就会发生行为.但大多数法域都采用实质性步骤标准,这只要求一项行为超越单纯的准备,并有力证实被告的犯罪意图。

学习要点：

企图总是需要(1) 实施犯罪的具体意图和(2) 被告或其代理人为推动犯罪而实施的行为。

stem:
A woman who wanted to rob a bank offered to pay her friend one-third of the money she stole if the friend would drive the getaway car to be used in the robbery. The friend agreed but made the woman promise not to hurt anyone during the robbery.

The woman then drove to a sporting goods store, where she explained to the store owner that she needed a small firearm for use in a bank robbery. The store owner responded that he would charge extra because the woman was so unwise as to confide her unlawful plans for using the weapon, and he sold her a handgun at four times the regular price.

During the robbery, the woman used the gun to threaten a bank teller, who handed over money. The gun discharged by accident and killed a bank customer. The friend drove the woman away from the bank.
stemZh:
一个想抢劫银行的妇女提出,如果朋友开着逃跑的车去抢劫,她要向朋友支付所偷钱的三分之一,朋友同意但让女人承诺在抢劫期间不伤害任何人.

这名妇女随后开车到一家体育用品店,在那里她向店主解释说,她需要一支小火器,用于银行抢劫。店主回应称,他会额外收费,因为那女人太不明智,不敢透露她使用武器的非法计划,他以正常价格的四倍将手枪卖给她.

抢劫期间,该女子用枪威胁交出钱款的银行出纳员,枪意外放出并杀死了银行客户,朋友将该女子驱离银行.

options.zh: 无论是朋友还是店主

options.zh: 无论是朋友还是店主

options.en: Only the store owner.
options.zh: 只见店主.

explanation.en:
Parties to a crime

Modern view

Common law

Definition Liability

Principal Principal

(first degree)

Performs criminal act with requisite intent or uses innocent agent to commit criminal act

Target & foreseeable crimes

Accomplice Principal

(second degree)

Present at crime & aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime

Accessory

before the fact*

Not present at crime but aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime

Accessory

after the fact

Knows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or conviction

Independent crime

*Common law liability requires conviction of principal.

Accomplice liability extends to anyone who:

intentionally aids or encourages a principal before or during the commission of a crime with the specific intent that the principal commit the encouraged crime. Common law jurisdictions (as seen here) divide accomplices into two categories—those who were present for the crime (principals in the second degree) and those who were not (accessories before the fact). But accomplices under either category are liable to the same extent as the principal for the encouraged crime and any crimes that occurred as a natural and probable (i.e., foreseeable) consequence of that crime.

Here, the woman (principal in the first degree) can be convicted of murder because she killed a customer in the course of a bank robbery. The friend intentionally aided in that robbery by driving the woman away from the bank after the robbery was completed—as they previously agreed. And since the killing was a foreseeable consequence of the robbery, the friend (who was at the crime) can be convicted of murder as a principal in the second degree (Choices B & D).

The store owner's intent to aid in the woman's robbery cannot be inferred from his decision to sell her a gun after learning of her criminal plan. But it can be inferred from his sale of the gun at four times the regular price since the sale shows that the store owner has an interest in the outcome of the criminal venture. And since it was foreseeable that the gun would be used to kill someone during the robbery, the store owner (who was not at the crime) can be convicted of murder as an accessory before the fact (Choice C).

Educational objective:

Principals in the second degree (accomplices at the crime) and accessories before the fact (accomplices not at the crime) are liable at common law for (1) any crimes that they encouraged a principal in the first degree to commit and (2) any crimes that occurred as a foreseeable consequence of the encouraged crime.

在此,该妇女(一级校长)可被判谋杀罪,因为她在银行抢劫过程中杀害了客户。该朋友故意协助抢劫,在抢劫完成后将这名妇女赶出银行,这是他们以前商定的。而由于杀人是抢劫的可预见后果,因此该朋友(曾参与犯罪)可以作为二级主犯(Choices B & D)被判谋杀罪.

店主协助妇女抢劫的意图不能从他得知她的犯罪计划后决定卖枪来推断。但可以从他以正常价格的四倍出售枪支中推断出,因为出售表明店主对罪恶冒险的结果有利益.而由于在抢劫期间可以预见到枪会被用来杀人,因此店主(未参与犯罪)在事实(Choice C)之前可以被判谋杀为从犯.

学习要点：

二等校长(犯罪同谋)和事实之前的从犯(犯罪同谋)根据普通法应负以下责任:(1)他们鼓励一级校长实施的任何罪行;(2)作为犯罪发生的任何罪行。所鼓励的犯罪的可预见后果。

stem: A man wanted to kill his coworker because the man believed the coworker was having an affair with the man's wife. Early one morning, armed with a pistol, the man crouched behind some bushes on a park hillside overlooking a path upon which the coworker frequently jogged. On this morning, however, the man saw the coworker jogging on another path about a half mile away. Nonetheless, the man fired five shots at the coworker. None of the five shots came anywhere close to the coworker as he was well out of the range of the pistol the man was using.
stemZh: 一个男人想杀死他的同工,因为男人相信同工和他妻子有染.一天清晨,这名男子拿着手枪,坐在一个公园山坡的灌木丛后面,俯瞰着同事经常慢跑的路径。 然而,今天上午,他看到同事在大约半英里外的另一条道路上慢跑。尽管如此,这名男子向同事开了5枪,这5枪都没有靠近同事,因为他不在同事使用的手枪范围内。

explanation.en:
A defendant is guilty of attempt if he/she:

had the specific intent to commit a crime (eg, murder) performed an act in furtherance of the target crime but did not complete it. In most jurisdictions, an act is a substantial step taken toward the completion of the target crime that exceeds mere preparation and strongly corroborates criminal intent. Once this occurs, the defendant can be convicted of attempt even if it was factually impossible to complete the target crime.

Here, the man wanted to kill his coworker (intent to commit murder) and fired five shots at him with a pistol. None of the shots came anywhere close to the coworker because he was well out of the pistol's range (factual impossibility). But since the man was not aware of the pistol's limited range, he acted with the intent to kill the coworker—and took a substantial step toward murder by pulling the trigger (overt act). Therefore, the jury should find him guilty of attempted murder.

(Choice A) There is no reasonable person standard for attempt. Therefore, the man can be guilty of attempt even if a reasonable person would not have been aware of the pistol's limited range.

(Choice C) Assault is (1) an attempted battery or (2) conduct that intentionally puts the victim in reasonable apprehension of imminent bodily harm. Here, the man may have committed assault when he shot at the coworker. But since the man intended to kill his coworker, the jury should find the man guilty of the greater offense of attempted murder.

(Choice D) It was impossible for the man to kill his coworker under the circumstances since the coworker was well out of the pistol's range. But factual impossibility is never a defense to attempt.

Educational objective:

Attempt requires proof that the defendant specifically intended to commit a crime and performed an act (ie, substantial step) in furtherance of that crime. A defendant can be convicted even if it was factually impossible for the target crime to be committed.

explanation.zh:
被告如果:

具有实施犯罪(如谋杀)的具体意图的行为是为了推进目标犯罪,但没有完成。在大多数法域,一项行为是朝着完成目标犯罪迈出的重大一步,它超出了单纯的准备,有力地证实了犯罪意图。一旦发生这种情况,即使事实上不可能完成目标犯罪,被告也可能被判犯有未遂罪。

这名男子想杀死他的同事(意图谋杀),并用手枪向他开了五枪。 由于他完全不在手枪的射程(实际上不可能),这些枪都没有靠近同事。但是,由于这名男子不知道手枪的射程有限,因此他故意杀害这名同事,并通过扣动扳机(公开行为)朝着谋杀迈出了实质性的一步。 因此,陪审团应该判定他犯有谋杀未遂罪。

(Choice A) 尝试没有合理的人标准,因此,即使一个合理的人不知道手枪的有限射程,此人也可能犯有尝试罪.

(选择C)攻击是指(1) 故意将受害人置于有理由担心即将发生的人身伤害。在这里,这个人在向同事开枪时可能犯了攻击罪.但既然此人打算杀害他的同事,陪审团应该认定此人犯有谋杀未遂这一更大的罪行.

(Choice D)这名男子不可能在当时的情况下杀死他的同工,因为同工完全不在手枪的射程之内。 但事实上不可能不是试图辩护的理由。

学习要点：

企图要求证明被告有实施犯罪的具体意图,并为促进犯罪而实施某种行为(即实质性步骤),即使事实上不可能实施目标犯罪,被告也可被定罪。

stem:
A man who owned a failing construction business lacked the money and supplies necessary to complete a major industrial project. In order to acquire supplies for the major project, the man planned to take supplies that another client had purchased and delivered for the construction of an apartment complex. The man shared his plan with a friend, an employee of the construction business, and asked the friend to help him retrieve the supplies from the business's storage facility. The friend knew that the supplies belonged to the other client but nevertheless agreed to help the man. Unbeknownst to the man and the friend, the apartment project had recently been canceled and the supplies had been returned to the client.

The next day, the friend went to the storage facility to get the supplies. The friend searched the facility for only a few minutes when he had a change of heart and left. However, his movement around the facility had triggered a silent alarm that turned on the surveillance cameras and alerted the police.

The friend and the man were later arrested, charged with conspiracy to commit larceny, and tried separately. The man was acquitted based on a lack of evidence, but the friend's trial is still pending.
stemZh:
一个拥有一个失败的建筑企业的人缺乏完成一个重大工业项目所需的资金和用品。为了为主要项目购置用品,该男子计划购买另一客户购买的用品,并交付建造公寓楼。这名男子与一个朋友,建筑行业的一名雇员分享了他的计划,并要求这位朋友帮助他从企业的储藏设施中取回用品.朋友知道这些用品属于另一客户,但仍同意帮助此人,不知此人和朋友最近取消了公寓项目,用品已退还客户。

次日,这位朋友到储藏所取物资.朋友在设施里搜了几分钟,当时他换了心,走了.然而,他在该设施周围的行动引发了无声警报,开启了监视摄像机并报警.

这名朋友和那名男子后来被捕,被控阴谋盗窃罪,并分别审判,那名男子因证据不足被宣告无罪,但该名朋友的审判仍悬而未决.
ask: In a jurisdiction that follows the modern-prevailing approach for conspiracy, is the friend likely guilty?
askZh: 在一个遵循现代阴谋法的法域中,朋友很可能有罪吗?

options.en: No, because the friend's subsequent withdrawal from the conspiracy prevented its success.
options.zh: 不,因为朋友后来退出阴谋 阻止了它的成功。

options.en: No, because the man was acquitted due to insufficient evidence.
options.zh: 不,因为他因为证据不足而无罪释放。

options.en: Yes, because impossibility is not a defense to conspiracy.
options.zh: 是的,因为不可能不是阴谋的辩护

options.en: Yes, because the friend agreed to take the supplies and committed an overt act.
options.zh: 是的,因为那个朋友同意拿走这些物资 并做了一个公开的行为。

explanation.en:
Conspiracy

Agreement Overt act

Majority view (modern & MPC)

Unilateral approach – at least one person specifically intends to enter agreement

At least one conspirator must commit overt act

Minority view (common law)

Bilateral approach – two or more persons specifically intend to enter agreement

Not required

MPC = Model Penal Code.

In most jurisdictions (including this one) and under the MPC, conspiracy requires proof of the following:

two or more persons entered an agreement with the specific intent to accomplish an unlawful purpose (e.g., larceny) and

at least one conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement.

And since these jurisdictions follow the unilateral approach, a conspiracy may be formed when only one party actually agrees and, for example, the other party merely feigns agreement.

Here, the friend entered an agreement to commit larceny when he agreed to help the man take another client's supplies and use them for a different project. The friend then committed an overt act in furtherance of this agreement when he went to the storage facility to retrieve the supplies. As a result, the friend is likely guilty of conspiracy to commit larceny.

(Choice A) Under the MPC and the minority view, subsequent withdrawal is a defense to conspiracy if the defendant voluntary acts to "thwart the success" of the conspiracy. But in most jurisdictions, withdrawal is a defense only if it occurs before an overt act has been committed. Here, the friend committed an overt act when he went to the storage facility, so his subsequent change of heart is no defense.

(Choice B) The fact that the man was acquitted of conspiracy in a previous trial does not affect the friend's guilt because unilateral-approach jurisdictions require proof of only one guilty mind. Therefore, a jury is not precluded from finding the friend guilty of conspiracy to commit larceny in his separate trial.

(Choices C) Impossibility is a defense to conspiracy if the object of the agreement is not a crime. But it is not a defense when, as here, an unknown condition (e.g., return of the supplies) prevents the completion of the intended crime.

Educational objective:

Under the modern-prevailing view, conspiracy requires proof that (1) one party actually entered an agreement with the specific intent to accomplish an unlawful purpose and (2) at least one conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement.

explanation.zh:
阴谋

公开行为

多数视图( 现代 & MPC)

单方面做法——至少有一人明确打算订立协议

至少一个同谋必须公开行动

少数群体观点(普通法)

双边办法 -- -- 两个或两个以上的人明确打算达成协议

无需

MPC=示范刑法。

在大多数法域(包括这一法域),根据《刑法》,共谋需要证明:

两人或两人以上订立协议,其具体意图是达到非法目的(如盗窃)和

至少有一名共谋者为推动协议采取了公开行动。

由于这些法域采取单方面做法,当只有一方实际同意,例如,另一方只是假装同意时,就可能形成阴谋。

在这里,这位朋友达成了一项实施盗窃的协议,当时他同意帮助这名男子拿走另一个客户的用品,并将其用于另一个项目.这名朋友随后在前往储藏设施取回物资时,采取了公开行动,以推进这一协议,因此,他很可能犯有阴谋盗窃罪。

(Choice A)在MPC和少数派观点下,如果被告自愿采取行动"动摇阴谋的成败",随后的退出就是对阴谋的辩护.但在大多数司法管辖区中,退出只有在公开行为发生之前才是一种辩护。 在这里,这位朋友在前往存储设施时做出了公开的行为,因此他后来的改变心意不是辩护。

(Choice B)此人在前一次审判中因共谋被宣告无罪的事实并不影响朋友的罪责,因为单方司法管辖只需要证明一个有罪的思想.因此,不排除陪审团在单独审判中裁定该朋友犯有共谋盗窃罪。

(Choices C)如果协议的对象不是犯罪,则不可能是共谋的辩护,但是,在这里,一个未知的条件(如补给的返还)阻止了预定的犯罪的完成,这也不是辩护.

学习要点：

根据现代流行的观点,阴谋需要证明:(1) 一方当事人实际上订立了一项协议,其具体意图是达到非法目的;(2) 至少有一名共谋者为促进协议而实施公开行为。

stem: A woman wanted to make some money, so she decided to sell cocaine. She asked her neighbor, who was reputed to have access to illegal drugs, to supply her with cocaine so she could resell it. The neighbor agreed and sold the woman a bag of white powder. The woman then repackaged the white powder into smaller containers and sold one to an undercover police officer who promptly arrested the woman. The woman immediately confessed and said that her neighbor was her supplier. Upon examination, the white powder was found not to be cocaine or any type of illegal substance.
stemZh: 一个女人想赚点钱,于是她决定卖可卡因,她要求被誉为有非法毒品的邻居向她提供可卡因,以便她转售,邻居同意并卖了这个女人一袋白粉.女方随后将白色粉末重新包装到更小的容器中,并卖给一名便衣警察,后者迅速逮捕了该妇女,该妇女立即供认并说其邻居是她的供货商.经检查,发现白粉不是可卡因或任何类型的非法物质。
ask: If the neighbor knew the white powder was not cocaine but the woman believed it was, which of the following is correct?
askZh: 如果邻居知道白粉不是可卡因,但女人相信,以下哪一个是正确的?

options.en: Both the neighbor and the woman are guilty of attempting to sell cocaine.
options.zh: 邻居和女人都曾企图卖可卡因

options.en: The neighbor is guilty of attempting to sell cocaine, but the woman is not.
options.zh: 邻居因企图贩卖可卡因而有罪,但女方没有.

options.en: The neighbor is not guilty of attempting to sell cocaine, but the woman is.
options.zh: 邻居没有试图出售可卡因的罪名,但女人是.

options.en: Neither the neighbor nor the woman is guilty of attempting to sell cocaine.
options.zh: 邻居和女人都没有试图出售可卡因的罪过。

explanation.en:
Defenses to attempt

Impossibility Legal – intended act would not be criminal if completed Factual (no defense) – unknown condition prevents completion of intended crime Abandonment Majority/common law (no defense) – attempt complete once overt act committed Minority/MPC – voluntary & complete withdrawal from crime MPC = Model Penal Code.

A defendant is guilty of an attempted crime if he/she had the specific intent to commit a crime, performed an act in furtherance of that crime, but did not complete it. This is true even when an unknown condition makes it factually impossible to complete the intended crime. Therefore, factual impossibility is never a defense to attempt.

Here, the neighbor did not have the specific intent to sell cocaine because he knew that the white powder was not cocaine. Therefore, he is not guilty of this attempted crime (Choices A & B). In contrast, the woman believed that the white powder was cocaine when she repackaged it and sold some to an undercover police officer. And though it was factually impossible for her to actually sell cocaine, this is no defense to attempt. As a result, only the woman is guilty of attempting to sell cocaine (Choice D).

Educational objective:

Attempt requires proof that the defendant (1) had the specific intent to commit a crime, (2) performed an act in furtherance of that crime, but (3) did not complete it. And the defendant can be convicted of attempt even if it was factually impossible to complete the intended crime.

explanation.zh:
企图辩护

法律 -- -- 如果完成事实(无辩护) -- -- 未知条件阻止完成预期犯罪 -- -- 一旦公开实施了少数人/穆斯林文化中心 -- -- 自愿和完全退出犯罪 MPC = 示范刑法。

如果被告有实施犯罪的具体意图,为推进犯罪而实施的行为,但未完成,则被告犯有犯罪未遂罪。即使一个未知条件实际上无法完成预定犯罪,情况也是如此,因此,事实上不可能成为企图犯罪的理由。

在这里,邻居并没有出售可卡因的具体意图,因为他知道白粉不是可卡因。 因此,他没有犯下这一未遂罪行(Choices A & B)。与此相反,该妇女认为白粉是可卡因,当时她重新包装并卖给了一名卧底警官。 尽管事实上她不可能真正出售可卡因,但这并不能成为试图出售可卡因的辩护理由。因此,只有该妇女犯有试图出售可卡因的罪行(Choice D)。

学习要点：

企图要求证明被告(1)有实施犯罪的具体意图,(2) 实施某项行为以促进该犯罪,但(3) 没有完成。被告即使实际上不可能完成预定犯罪,也可以被判未遂罪。

stem:
A man was engaged to marry a woman. One evening, the man became enraged at the comments of the woman's eight-year-old daughter, who was complaining, in her usual fashion, that she did not want her mother to marry the man. The man, who had had too much to drink, began beating the daughter. The daughter suffered some bruises and a broken arm. The woman took her daughter to the hospital, and the police were notified by the hospital staff.

The man was indicted for felony child abuse. He pleaded with the woman to forgive him and to run away with him. She agreed. They moved out of state and took the daughter with them. Without the testimony of the child, the prosecution was forced to dismiss the case. Some time later, the woman returned for a visit with her family and was arrested and indicted as an accessory after the fact to child abuse.
stemZh:
男方订婚娶女方,一天晚上,男方对女方八岁女儿的评论感到愤怒,女方以平常的方式抱怨她不希望母亲嫁给男方.这名喝多了酒的男子开始殴打女儿,女儿受到一些瘀伤和手臂断裂,女子将女儿带到医院,医院工作人员通知警察.

这名男子因严重虐待儿童而被起诉,他恳请该女子原谅他,并与他私奔,她同意,他们搬离了州,带走了女儿,没有孩子的证词,检方被迫驳回此案.一段时间后,该妇女回到家中探亲,在被虐待儿童之后被逮捕并被作为从犯起诉。
ask: At the woman's trial, how should the court proceed?
askZh: 女子审判时,法庭应如何进行?

options.en: Dismiss the charge, because the evidence shows that any aid the woman rendered occurred after the crime was completed.
options.zh: 驳回指控,因为证据表明,该妇女提供的任何援助发生在犯罪结束后。

options.en: Dismiss the charge, because the man had not been convicted.
options.zh: 驳回指控,因为此人没有被定罪。

options.en: Submit the case to the jury, on an instruction to convict only if the woman knew the man had been indicted.
options.zh: 将案件提交陪审团,根据一项指示,只有在妇女知道该男子已被起诉的情况下才能定罪。

options.en: Submit the case to the jury, on an instruction to convict only if the woman's purpose in moving was to help the man avoid conviction.
options.zh: 将案件提交陪审团,只有在妇女迁移的目的是帮助男子避免定罪的情况下,才指示定罪。

explanation.en:
Parties to a crime

Modern view

Common law

Definition Liability

Principal Principal

(first degree)

Performs criminal act with requisite intent or uses innocent agent to commit criminal act

Target & foreseeable crimes

Accomplice Principal

(second degree)

Present at crime & aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime

Accessory

before the fact*

Not present at crime but aids/encourages principal with intent that principal commit crime

Accessory

after the fact

Knows principal has committed felony & helps principal avoid arrest or conviction

Independent crime

*Common law liability requires conviction of principal.

A person is an accessory after the fact if he/she:

knew that the principal had committed a felony aided or assisted the principal after the felony was complete and did so for the purpose of helping the principal avoid apprehension or conviction. Although the accessory after the fact is not liable for the principal's crime, the accessory is liable for a separate crime—often "harboring a fugitive" or "obstructing justice".

Here, the man was indicted for felony child abuse after beating the woman's daughter. Although the woman was aware of this crime, she moved out of state with the man and her daughter. This move helped the man avoid conviction since the daughter's unavailability to testify forced the state to dismiss his case. But the jury should only convict the woman as an accessory after the fact if her purpose in moving was to help the man avoid conviction.

(Choice A) The evidence that the woman aided the man after the crime was completed supports her liability as an accessory after the fact—not a dismissal of the charge.

(Choice B) A person can be convicted as an accessory after the fact even if the principal has not been prosecuted for, or convicted of, the completed felony.

(Choice C) An accessory after the fact must know that the principal has committed a felony but need not know that the principal has been indicted for that crime.

Educational objective:

An accessory after the fact (1) knows that the principal has committed a felony, (2) aids or assists the principal after the felony is complete, and (3) does so to help the principal avoid apprehension or conviction.

explanation.zh:
犯罪的当事方

现代视图

普通法

定义 赔偿责任

校长

(一级)

有必要意图实施犯罪行为或利用无辜代理人实施犯罪行为

目标罪行和可预见的罪行

校长

(二级)

参加犯罪和协助/鼓励主犯,意图是主犯犯罪情况

附属

事实之前 *

不在犯罪现场,而是协助/鼓励主犯意图使其犯罪

附属

事后

明知校长犯下重罪,帮助校长避免逮捕或定罪

独立犯罪

* 共同法责任要求确定本金。

如果一个人:

明知主犯在重罪完成后犯下了协助主犯或协助主犯的重罪,而且这样做是为了帮助主犯避免被捕或定罪。虽然事后的从犯对主犯的罪行不负赔偿责任,但从犯对单独的犯罪——往往是"骚扰逃犯"或"妨碍司法"——负有赔偿责任.

在这里,这名男子在殴打该女子的女儿后因严重虐待儿童而被起诉,虽然该女子知道这一罪行,但她与该男子和她的女儿一起搬离了国家。这一举动有助于男子避免定罪,因为女儿无法出庭作证迫使国家驳回他的案件。 但是,如果该女子搬家的目的是帮助男子避免定罪,陪审团只应在事后判定该女子为从犯。

(Choice A) 犯罪结束后妇女协助男子的证据证明她作为事后从犯的责任,而不是驳回指控。

(Choice B)即使主犯没有因完成的重罪受到起诉或定罪,在事实发生后,也可以作为从犯定罪。

(C) 事后的从犯必须知道主犯犯下了重罪,但不必知道主犯因这一罪行被起诉。

学习要点：

事后从犯(1)知道主犯犯下重罪,(2)在重罪完成后协助或协助主犯,(3)帮助主犯避免被捕或定罪。

stem:
A man was convicted of possession of a controlled substance with the intent to distribute and sentenced to 20 years confinement in a state prison. Five years into the man's confinement, prison officials began to suspect that the man was distributing drugs inside the prison. One day, the man was removed from his cell and taken to the prison dentist for what the guards told him was a "routine checkup." After the man exited the cell, guards entered and told the man's cellmate that they were going to search the cell. The cellmate did not object. The guards searched the cell without a warrant and found several grams of heroin hidden in a locked box under the man's bed.

The man was charged with distribution of a controlled substance within a secure facility and, under the state's three-strikes rule, faces life in prison. The man has moved to suppress the heroin.
stemZh:
一名男子因持有受管制物质而被定罪,意图分发毒品并被判处监禁20年。该男子被禁闭五年后,监狱官员开始怀疑该男子正在监狱内分发毒品.一天,这名男子被从牢房中带走,并被带到监狱牙医那里,因为看守告诉他这是一次"例行检查",在男子离开牢房后,警卫进入,并告诉此人的狱友,他们将搜查牢房。狱友没有表示反对,狱警在没有搜查证的情况下搜查了牢房,发现有几克海洛因藏在男子床下的锁箱中。

此人被控在安全设施内分发受管制物质,在州三击的统治下,面临终身监禁,他动身镇压海洛因.
ask: Should the man's motion to suppress be granted?
askZh: 男人的镇压动议应该得到批准吗?

options.en: No, because the cellmate impliedly consented to the search of the cell.
options.zh: 不,因为狱友默示同意搜查牢房。

options.en: No, because the man had no reasonable expectation of privacy in his cell or items therein.
options.zh: 没有,因为此人对牢房或牢房里的物品没有合理的隐私期望。

options.en: Yes, because the heroin was not in plain view when the guards searched the cell.
options.zh: 是的,因为当警卫搜查牢房时, 海洛因并不清晰。

options.en: Yes, because the locked box was a constitutionally protected area that required a warrant.
options.zh: 是的,因为锁着的盒子 是一个宪法保护的区域, 需要搜查令。

explanation.en:
Common items & areas

with no reasonable expectation of privacy

Bank records Things exposed to public view (eg, open fields, abandoned property) Physical characteristics (eg, handwriting, vocal sound) Conversations with undercover officers & informants Pen registers (ie, records of dialed telephone numbers) Smells emanating from cars & other items Prison inmate's cell Automobile's vehicle identification number (VIN) The Fourth Amendment is violated when the government conducts an unreasonable search or seizure—ie, when police act without a warrant and no exception applies. A Fourth Amendment search occurs if one of the following tests is met:

Physical trespass test – the government physically intrudes upon a constitutionally protected area to obtain information Reasonable expectation of privacy test – the government invades a person's subjective expectation of privacy that society would find objectively reasonable In Hudson v. Palmer, the Supreme Court held that inmates have no privacy interest in their cells and no possessory interest in their items therein (eg, the locked box) that would entitle them to Fourth Amendment protections (Choice D). Therefore, the guards' search of the man's cell did not violate the Fourth Amendment, and the court should deny his motion to suppress.

(Choice A) Third parties (eg, a suspect's roommate) may consent to a warrantless search of property over which the third party had joint control and access. Here, the man's cellmate did not object to the search of the cell—ie, he impliedly consented. But since inmates have no reasonable expectation of privacy in their cells, the cellmate's consent was unnecessary.

(Choice C) Under the plain-view exception to the warrant requirement, officers may seize an item if (1) the item is in plain view, (2) it is immediately apparent that the item is contraband, and (3) the officer is lawfully in the area. But since prisoners have no reasonable expectation of privacy in their cells, reliance on the plain-view exception is unnecessary.

Educational objective:

Inmates have no privacy interest in their prison cells or possessory interest in the items therein that would entitle them to Fourth Amendment protections. Therefore, officials may search an inmate's cell without implicating the Fourth Amendment.

References

Hudson v. Palmer, 468 U.S. 517, 522–24 (1984) (holding that inmates hold no reasonable expectation of privacy in prison cells).

Wayne R. LaFave, 1 Search and Seizure 167; 2.4(d) (6th ed. 2020) (discussing privacy interests in detention facilities).

共同项目和领域

不合理期待隐私

银行记录 公众视野暴露的东西(如:开阔的田野,废弃的房产) 物理特征(如:笔迹,声响) 与卧底官员的交谈和线人 笔记(即:拨号记录) 气息来自监狱囚犯的囚室汽车车辆识别号码(VIN) 第四修正案在政府进行不合理的搜查或扣押时,即当警察无证行事时,即无例外。如果满足下列测试之一,则进行第四修正案搜索:

人身侵入测试——政府实际侵入宪法保护的地区获取信息 合理期待隐私测试 — 政府入侵一个人的社会客观上对隐私的主观期望在Hudson诉Palmer案中,最高法院认为,囚犯在牢房中没有隐私,对牢房内的物品(例如锁箱)没有占有性权益,因此他们有权获得第四修正案的保护(Choice D)。因此,看守对男囚牢房的搜查没有违反第四修正案,法院应当驳回他的镇压动议.

(Choice A)第三方(例如嫌疑人的室友)可以同意对第三方共同控制和进入的财产进行无证搜查,在这方面,此人的狱友不反对搜查牢房——他默示同意。但是,由于囚犯对牢房中的隐私没有合理的期望,因此囚犯不必同意。

(选择C)根据对搜查令要求的简单例外,如果(1) 物品在明显可见的情况下,(2) 物品立即明显是违禁品,(3) 该官员合法在该地区,警官可以扣押物品。但是,由于囚犯对牢房中的隐私没有合理的期望,依赖平视例外是不必要的.

学习要点：

囚犯在囚室中没有隐私,对牢房中的物品没有占有权。这将使他们有权获得第四修正案的保护。因此,官员可以搜查囚犯的牢房,而不涉及《第四修正案》。

Wayne R. LaFave, 1 Search and Capition 167; 2.4(d) (第6版,2020年)(讨论拘留设施中的隐私利益).
